Chapter 20: Part Twenty: The Covert
Chapter Summary

"Tell Paz Vizsla that I received his message." He stated simply, voice rising to carry
beyond the street and up into the buildings.

In the distance you could hear what sounded like a flare, the ignition of something as it
lifted and quickly drew closer to the three of you. You craned your head to scan the
interspersed walkways above you, finally spotting a silhouette as it descended down into
the street a ways ahead of you three.

The man from the holo-message was even broader in person. A prickle of intimidation
ran through you, yet you remained sure-footed as you looked out at the warrior who had
come to greet you.

"Djarin." The man spoke, though by his tone it sounded less a greeting and more a
challenge. "You dare bring an outsider here?"

Chapter Notes

TW at the end for referenced child death

See the end of the chapter for more notes

The journey to Coruscant was longer than you had anticipated.

It was a symptom of your inexperience in space travel, having lived your entire life on a
single planet. For much of the trip you peppered Din with questions about hyperdrives, nav
computers, and lightspeed travel. Every new fact you managed to grasp was both fascinating
and yet terrifying. The dangers of light speed were incalculable, and you quickly learned it
took an experienced pilot to chart a course through the infinite number of nebulas, asteroid
fields, supernovas, and dead star systems that stood between you and your destination. It lent
you a newfound respect for your companion, who appeared to have been self-taught in many
of his skills as a pilot.

In the end it took no less than five jumps, two tolls (which Din paid begrudgingly), a fueling
stop, and three days in hyperspace to reach your destination. Even though you were traveling
fast than the speed of light the distance from the Outer Rim to the galaxy's core was
enormous. Every hour you expected the ship's navi-computer to beep a warning that you



were exiting into the hyperlane above the densely urban planet, only to be met with the low
constant thrum of the engines instead.

Even though the distance to Coruscant seemed endless, the space between you and Din had
shrunk following your reconciliation.

The Mando no longer ignored you, yet he didn't offer to begin conversations as often as he
had before either. You didn't truly hold it against him, happy to at least put his attempts at
cold shouldering you in the past. You tried to allow him space as he needed it, knowing that
in some ways he was still trapped in his thoughts and trying to sort whatever conflicted
feelings he had about the relationship between you both. Even so, Din made it a point in
joining you and the child eating, teaching you more about the ship, and sometimes simply
being nearby without speaking as he enjoyed your company.

It was odd, in many ways, to return to this level of easy companionship between you both.
You were certainly glad that the Din was no longer ignoring you and enjoyed the sense of
comfort his constant nearby presence brought. Yet there remained an air of awkwardness
between you two, one neither of you wanted to truly breach. Often your thoughts lingered on
the moment in the cockpit, with his gloved hands sliding up your exposed arms, reaching up
to your shoulders and further to your face. The thought made goosebumps raise on your skin
every time you indulged in it. It had been the closest you had ever come to the Mandalorian
and resided in your thoughts just the same as Din remained a constant presence. A part of you
couldn’t help but imagine what would have happened had you two not been interrupted, if
maybe Din would have found a way to remove his helmet and lean down to-

That was for another time.

In the meantime, Din had become...closer. Though difficult to describe, you felt it
nonetheless. It was in the way he would gently lay a hand on your waist as he scooted past
you in the hold, would come closer and let his footsteps announce his presence rather than
calling to you from afar. It was in the way he was almost less afraid to touch you, his hands
ever gentle and hesitant in their contact. To you it felt as if he was treating you like glass,
purposeful yet delicate and ever careful of his movements. More than once he had grown
close enough for you to hear the steady, restrained breathing under his helmet, feeling your
own exhales slowly come into sync alongside his own.

You didn't know what to call this strange understanding you two had both come to. Since
admitting your own feelings, and beginning to understand his, you found yourself ever
mindful of his presence. You couldn't help it, letting your eyes linger on him when his head
was turned, doing your tasks a little quieter to hear him speak to the child. You knew he did
the same, as if both of you stealing silent glances and listening to each other's soft voices
could somehow resolve the wavering tension between you. It was a perfectly orchestrated
dance that you and Din had created, both of you following the other's improvised and
uncoordinated steps with fluent accuracy.

The closest you had felt to him within the days in the blue light of hyperspace was when you
had gently asked Mando about the planet you were traveling to, about the man in the
message, about his own covert. Though hesitant, he told you what he was willing to. His
voice was soft then, not in the way that it was gentle. Instead, it was cautious, solemn in a



way that spoke of regret, a grief you couldn't completely see. That fact that he replied to you
at all spoke volumes in how much his trust of you had grown since your original meeting
now months ago.

Slowly, over the course of those three days, you learned what had happened on Nevarro. Din
had mentioned before that he had rescued the child, but never before had he mentioned that in
the face of certain destruction the Covert had come to his aid, allowing him and the child to
escape. Hearing from the man who called himself Paz Vizsla was the first time he had
received contact from any members of the covert. There were rumors of what had happened
after his departure, ones he had heard from a now dead huntress on Tatooine. Yet the clan's
vow of secrecy, of silence had prevented him from hearing more.

It made sense then, why he had wanted to travel to Coruscant. It was not only to join forces
with the members of his covert, but to hopefully learn more about what had happened that
day after he left. He needed to know, though you knew he wouldn’t admit it. Likely Din felt a
sense of responsibility, of guilt for whatever fate the covert had come to as a result of his own
actions.

The same thought occurred to you now as you gazed out of the cockpit's viewfinder at the
massive planet before you, taking up almost every inch of your sight through the glass. The
dark surface of Coruscant was etched with geometric patterns of lights, each pinprick a
massive building spiraling high up into the sky to knock against the heavens. The 'ring'
around the planet you had originally assumed to be a collection of debris and space dust was
in fact thousands of spaceships constantly coming in and out of the space ports. Despite
hearing many times of the planet at beating heart of the galaxy, nothing could have prepared
you for the sheer size of the ecumenopolis.

You couldn't quite understand how, but the world before you felt heavy, like a marble
dropped into a taut fabric, sinking, and letting the space around it cave into its gravity. Even
in the dead silence of space you could feel it. The closer you traveled to the planet's surface
the more you felt a creeping sense of dread rub raw at your nerves and stifle the air in your
chest. The planet seemed to have a shadow you couldn't see, a presence beyond your
comprehension made from eons passed that whispered darkly against your senses.

"Razorcrest this is Galactic Market Sector Tower Five." A voice garbled over the
communications board. "Please state the purpose of your visit."

Din reached for the button to respond, pausing for a moment before replying dryly: "Visiting
family."

You contained a snort from your position behind the pilot's seat, and Din glanced at you for a
moment before leaning back to the console. You wanted to imagine a sarcastic smile under
his helmet.

There was a brief crackle over the comms before a tired voice answered. "Confirmed. Please
route to Spaceport Cresh docking bay five and present registration and papers for
authentication."



You frowned, fidgeting anxiously. You didn't have papers, and in all likelihood neither did
Din or the Child. To arrive in an unregistered ship with no papers meant instant questioning,
which would probably increase the chance of being detected by any bounty hunters or
Imperial spies on the planet.

"Copy." Din muttered, and at your concerned glance gave a small shake of his head. "Don't
worry." He told you softly. "We're headed somewhere else."

You tilted your head, blinking at him. "Wouldn't they send out a search party?"

Din made a small sound, something almost akin to a scoff. "If Coruscant were still the
capital, they might get around to it. Since the Empire was defeated and the Republic moved
to Chandrila however, flagging ships in is just a pretense." Gently, he angled the ship in a soft
descent towards the surface. "Besides, they won't find us where we're headed."

You remained silent, instead looking outside the ship at the distant tips of skyscrapers
growing ever closer. The glowing circles of the planet, built around the infinite skyline of the
city planet, receded into arches of light that curved beyond the scope of your vision. You
looked out, completely enraptured by the endless scope of city before you. There wasn't an
ounce of green on the entire planet, every inch sleek durasteel structures and glittering lights.
It was as beautiful as it was unsettling, the presence of any and all organic matter stripped
bare from the surface leaving an odd heaviness in your stomach.

In the seat behind you, the child whined uncomfortably. You turned, finding his small face
scrunched in what looked to be an expression fear. His small ears drooped as you looked at
him in confusion, uncertain of where this sudden fright had come from. So instead, you
scooped him into your arms, bouncing him slightly against your shoulder, where he snuggled
into the junction between your neck and collar bone.

"What is it?" You asked softly so that only he could hear. "What's got you so anxious?"

The toddler whined again, his tiny hands clutching the fabric of your shirt tight in his grasp.
You felt your brow furrow. It was a rare occurrence to see the little one so disturbed by
something, and the fact that there was no clear indication as to his fright left you puzzled. A
part of you wondered if he too, felt the odd clench in your stomach as you gazed out at the
sprawling city-planet.

Before you could try to understand the reason behind the infant's distress, however, you felt
your eyelids suddenly grow heavy. All at once the sounds of the ship were sucked into
nothingness. Though the floor dropped out from under you, you didn’t sink. Instead you felt
as if your body floated, cradled in the vast expanse of stars beyond the hull of the ship. The
weight of the child in your arms was the only anchor to the abrupt and startling absence of
sound and light, the gravity of the planet under you suddenly deepening into an endless void
that threatened to suck you down, down further into the unknown.

You could feel the distress of the child wash over you, and with it came sounds, images of a
time past. Laughter, voices, brightly lit corridors, and wise smiles filtered through your mind.
Like windchimes each note held for less than a breath before vanishing once more. Yet in the
next heartbeat the warmth of the visions blazed into a scorching heat, one that licked at your



skin and threatened to burn you from the inside out just like the dream where you were a
flame in an infinite inferno-

"Hey."

You blinked several times, trying to regain your bearings as Din's familiar voice summoned
you. The deep hum of the Razorcrest’s engines and roar of traffic returned to you, and as you
looked down you could see Din halfway turned to you from the pilot's seat expectantly.

You swallowed, throat suddenly dry. "I-huh?"

Din tilted his head at you, studying your suddenly bewildered features. In your chest you
could feel your heart suddenly hammer against your ribcage, the vision fading but leaving
behind a horrid sense of dread.

"You okay?" He asked, and you found it within yourself to nod.

"Yeah." You breathed. "I-I'm fine. The kid...he...he's scared, I think." As you spoke the child
made a small snort, tucking himself smaller against your chest. You let your hand rest gently
on the back of his wrinkled head, both to calm him and to reassure yourself.

Din turned his gaze to the child, and as you watched he reached out with a single finger and
gently stroked one of the infant's large green ears. You could see the toddler ease into the
touch, turning his head and looking at Din with a soft coo. A warmth that flooded your chest
and tugged at your lips, a reminder of how profoundly affectionate you were of their
relationship.

"We'll be there soon." Din murmured gently, and it felt as if he was speaking to you as well as
the infant in his care. "You'll be safe then."

"We're already safe." You wanted to tell him, but you knew the words need not be said. "Safe
because we're with you."

---

If you though Coruscant was vast from the surface, the underground was something else
entirely. It amazed you to think that all these buildings were somehow connected, stacking on
top of each other endlessly in a bid to tower closer to the sky. Yet the further down Din
piloted the Razorcrest, the less you could see the pale sky of the cosmopolitan world. A dark
part of you wondered just how deep it went. Din had mentioned before the vast underbelly of
Coruscant, places so deep that there were creatures there who had evolved to avoid any trace
of sunlight. There were things miles beneath the surface that had stopped being human long
ago.

The thought sent a shudder through you, one that hadn't seemed to stop ever since you
arrived in orbit around the planet. Despite its glittering skyline, Coruscant’s shadow cast deep
into its core and silently across your senses.



Eventually Din was able to pilot the ship into a jetty deep into one of the bored holes of the
planet designed for freight ships and the like. It was empty save for a few residents who
scattered as the ship descended, blowing bits of debris and paper in its wake. As you stepped
out onto the ramp and looked up, you could barely see a faint halo of sky far above. You
couldn’t help but wonder just how far you had descended, likely miles beneath the artificial
surface of the planet.

"Stay close." Din murmured as he passed you, one hand on the small of your back gently
guiding you downwards onto the docking platform. "It isn't safe here."

You cast him a dubious glance. "I thought this was still Republic territory?" You asked,
hoisting the kid a little higher on your shoulder underneath the hooded shawl the Mando had
mentioned you should wear. It obscured your face, but more importantly it hid the child in
your arms beneath the woven fabric.

The Mando shook his head only once. "This is gang territory now." He warned, voice low.
"The Empire abandoning this planet left a power vacuum that the local gang lords are
fighting over."

You suppressed a shiver, the memory of the gangs on Kaddack an all too familiar one. You
had seen firsthand what a pair of rival gangs could do to a city, much less and entire planet.
Why there was a Mandalorian covert here in a violent part of the planet was beyond you. Yet
you followed closely behind Din as he navigated the neon lit streets and walkways of the
Coruscant underworld, keeping you ever close to his side. You could feel him angle his body
to obstruct the view of you from any passerby, though the point was moot since most of them
let their gazes linger on Din's shiny beskar cuirass.

The streets were crowded, filled with every species you had seen and some of those you
hadn’t. It wasn’t just the difference in races, but their status as well. You passed a Nautolan
who appeared to be a bouncer for the entrance of a cantina, then past him a pair of slender
Twi-lek dancers. Beyond and further down a flight of stairs you could see a group of young
male Togruta idling outside the entrance of an apartment complex. All of them gave a side-
long glance to the man at your side, eyeing his armor and your form beside him.

The farther you walked the more the crowds around you began to thin, slowly tapering off
into a few stragglers. The streets around you slowly became less clean, trash debris scattered
in corners and Tookas fighting over bits of leftover food. Instinctively you pressed yourself
close to Din, knowing if you did so even more you'd be practically glued to his side with
every step. In your arms the constant rocking movement of you keeping pace at Din’s side
had slowly lulled the child to sleep. If you listened you could hear his steady, even breathing.

Din, for what he was worth, didn't flinch from the increasingly rough surroundings. You got
the impression that he was at least somewhat familiar with these streets, likely having hunted
quarry down here before. It did a bit to ease your discomfort at the dark pit in your stomach,
knowing that the Mando beside you had traveled here before. Yet the streets of Coruscant
were sinisterly unfamiliar, deep and dim in a way that you hadn’t seen before. Your part of
Kaddak was urban, yes, but at least you could see the sun wherever you were. Here on
Coruscant it was dark, shadowy, dimly lit and oddly ominous.



"Up ahead." Din told you, and you glanced up to follow his gloved finger pointing at the side
of a wall in the distance. The streets around you had emptied now, devoid of passerby as you
three ventured further, deeper into the streets of an abandoned district. You could feel your
feet ache with how long you had been walking, and your arms begin to hurt as you carried
the child tight in your hold. You had to squint, trying to see exactly what Din was referring to
amidst the graffiti laden surface. There, an odd symbol gazed back at you with bone-hollow
eyes.

"What is it?" You asked, voice soft as if the creature painted there could hunt you still.

"A mythosaur." Din replied, matching your tone. "We're close."

No sooner had he spoken than a shadow darted across the edge of your vision. You spun, the
motion startling the child under your poncho, letting out a little gasp of surprise and startling
him from where he dozed against your breast. Din remained motionless at your side, though
you knew he too had seen the figure. When you turned back to him, however, you could feel
the distinct impression of being watched by multiple eyes.

You weren’t alone.

"They're here." He spoke, voice low in warning.

Din remained still, and you tried to mimic his unbothered stance despite the sudden rapid
flutter in your chest. You couldn't help but feel like prey to multiple predators, all vying for a
chance to pounce on you as you squirmed in fear. Instinctively you held the bundled toddler
in your arms a little closer, widened your stance just a little more in preparation.

"Tion'cuy?!" A voice barked in the distance, and if you strained your ears you could hear the
same helmeted filter as Din's voice. "Meg cuyir gar aliit?!"

Din didn't reply to whatever question was posited at him, remaining perfectly still even as he
subtly shifted his gaze to locate the source of the hidden voices.

"Jorhaa'ir!" The voice called out again, rising and cracking like a whip. You flinched at its
severity, feeling Din tense beside you.

As the echo faded you felt Din draw himself up, looking up at a walkway above you.

"Tell Paz Vizsla that I received his message." He stated simply, voice rising to carry beyond
the street and up into the buildings. He was met instantly with a hard silence. You felt the
seconds go by, the only sound this far down into the streets the wind blowing loose pieces of
trash against the sidewalk.

Then, in the distance you could hear what sounded like a flare, the ignition of something as it
lifted and quickly drew closer to the three of you. You craned your head to scan the
interspersed walkways above you, finally spotting a silhouette as it descended down into the
street a ways ahead of you three.



The man from the holo-message was even broader in person. His heavy infantry cuirass
added to his height and width, and you for a moment felt as if you were staring down a Dire-
Cat rather than a person. You thought Din was tall, but the Mando before you easily dwarfed
his size. A prickle of intimidation ran through you, yet you remained sure-footed as you
looked out at the warrior who had come to greet you.

"Djarin." The man spoke, though by his tone it sounded less a greeting and more a challenge.
"You dare bring an outsider here?"

The visor in Paz Vizsla’s helmet bore down on you. You couldn't help but frown a little under
the stare, suddenly self-conscious of your position as anything but Mandalorian.

Din shifted, taking a single step just enough so that he partially shielded you from Vizsla's
pointed glare.

"These two are under my protection." He returned, voice even but not backing down from the
other Mandalorian's hostile tone.

"Two?" Paz echoed, tilting his head in sudden curiosity.

As if summoned, the toddler in your arms squirmed so that his wrinkled green head poked
from under your shawl. His large brown eyes gazed out at the other Mandalorian with a
curious coo.

"The child." Paz breathed, and oddly the hostility in his voice ebbed, ending with a
confounded snort of disbelief. Whatever tension had begun to build evaporated in an instant
as the larger Mando let his eyes rest on the small creature in your arms. For a moment, his
gaze flicked up to your face, looking upon your open expression of concern and
bewilderment.

Paz let his stare rest on you for a few extra moments, enough so that you shifted a little self-
consciously at the attention. Then, as if coming to an unsaid conclusion, he nodded to
himself.

"Shield your eyes, stranger. We don't reveal the location of our covert to outsiders." He spoke
directly to you, and you blinked several times before tilting your head in confusion. Paz
didn't elaborate, instead turning heel and waiting for you and Din to follow.

You looked to your companion for explanation, but he merely shrugged.

"Close your eyes." He told you, softly so Paz couldn't hear. "I'll guide you."

You nodded after a moment’s hesitation, closing your eyes and letting darkness wash over
your sight. In the same heartbeat you felt the child gently lifted from your arms, the absence
of his weight both a concern and a relief. Then, delicately, your hand was lifted into a gloved
touch, escorting you forward as you blindly followed.

Even without your vision you were able to follow closely behind Din. Unable to see, your
other senses began to compensate. As you walked you began to hear the sounds of footsteps



beside your own, including Din's and Paz's ahead of you. The sound of rustling clothes, of
clinking armor yielded the image of other Mandalorians beginning to follow behind you, Din,
and the child. Their added presence caused Din to give your hand a small firm grasp of
reassurance.

The sound of traffic had faded now, the constant drone of air speeders a distant murmur
against your ears. Instead, there were only footsteps, the sound of a breeze blowing loose
debris, and your steady heartbeat to fill the silence. You don't know how long you walked,
following closely behind your friend as you three were escorted deeper into the heart of the
Coruscanti streets.

Finally, Din halted. It took you a split second to not crash into his back, automatically
opening your eyes to reveal the secret location that you had been led to.

A tunnel. The entrance of which stood a Mandalorian on either side, staring at both you and
Din. Their armors differed, and as you turned your head you found that the warriors who had
fallen in step behind you had variously colored armors as well. There were roughly six of
them in total, including the two before you. Between them stood Paz Vizsla, half turned to
you as he motioned you forward.

"You will have questions, I assume." He spoke, voice deep and graveled. "There will be time
to answer them. First let me show you to the rest of the covert." With that he began to walk
once more. Din followed, and even as you expected him to drop your hand now that you
could see, he didn't. It took you a moment to join him, eyes trained instead atop the tunnel on
the metal depiction of the same symbol you had seen graffitied onto the wall of the street. A
mythosaur, Din had said. You let the word run over your tongue, relishing in the sound.

Paz led you three into what looked like a warehouse, one that appeared at first glance to be
abandoned. However, upon entering into building you discovered it to be decently lit and
furnished with various trappings of chairs, tables, mats, and what appeared to be makeshift
hallways and corridors. Though the walls were old, dusty, and the floors marred, it appeared
as though great care had been taken into trying to make the space as clean and organized as
possible. The storage crates that must have taken up much of the room in the warehouse had
been neatly stacked into the back of the main space, towards what looked like a freight
elevator to an upper level.

The ‘hallways’ that had been created by stacking and securing smaller crates to create make-
shift walls led off into the back of the warehouse, down actual corridors to where you
supposed sleeping quarters were. On your right a larger doorway opened up to a smaller
space, and as you glanced over you could smell some form of food being prepared. A kitchen
of sorts, you supposed. Though where the food came from you had no idea.

The warehouse wasn’t unpopulated either, with as many as half a dozen Mandalorians
looking up upon hearing you and Din escorted inside. You blinked, not expecting so few to
greet you. When Din had mentioned the covert, he had made it sound as if their numbers
were easily 50 or so strong. Yet combining the warriors at the door, the covert before you
seemed to be less than half that number.



No sooner had you exited the tunnel did several cries go up, making you tense automatically.
However, the sight that greeted you was not one of terror, but joy.

You felt your jaw drop as several children, all wearing helmets, surged forward towards Paz.
They shrieked with delight upon seeing him, an older boy going as far as to hurl himself at
Paz's middle and attempt to wrap his arms around him. The warrior didn't even budge despite
the force of the boy's embrace, instead lifting a hand and gently setting it down atop the
child's helmet.

"Welcome back!" The boy spoke, voice surging with happiness. "Are you hurt?"

Paz shook his head, and before your eyes the foreboding persona of a warrior seemed to fade
into that of an affectionate guardian. The boy turned his face to you and Din, tilting his head
upon seeing you partially obscured by your Mando's figure.

"Who are they?" He asked, tilting his head up so the chin rested against the larger
Mandalorian’s stomach.

A small huff of laughter escaped from under Paz's helmet. "You remember Djarin, don't
you?" He asked, and the child nodded. However, as Paz's gaze stopped on you, he paused,
then looked to the Mando beside you in a silent question.

"My partner." Din answered, along with your name, and you felt your eyebrows raise in
surprise. "Who I owe my life."

It took you a moment to process his words, but when you did a flush of warmth rose in your
chest. You couldn't help the broad smile that played out on your lips and had to duck your
head to hide it as Paz's gaze rested on your once more.

The warrior crossed his arms over his chest, tilting his head at you with interest now. It felt
like he had looked at you for the first time, now appraising you less as a stranger and more as
an ally. The child at his side seemed to be satisfied with the answer and wandered off once
more with the rest of his playmates.

"I'd like to hear that story." Paz replied at last, and again it felt as if that apprehensive
demeanor from your first introduction had eased from his body language. Then he turned
once more, waving a hand for you to follow. “Come.”

You expected Paz to lead you towards the back of the warehouse, where you assumed the
sleeping quarters to be. Instead, he turned, traversing through the main area towards a small,
seated area obscured from the main area by a tattered hanging curtain. As he did, you
observed the covert members you passed, and in turn they observed you. Their helmeted
gazes followed you as you walked, likely perplexed by the presence of an outsider to their
hidden hideout.

The covert seemed to be comprised mostly of children, from what you could tell. The few
women you saw were in various states of armor as well, ranging from full cuirasses to just a
chest plate and greaves. A small group of them, about three, stood off to the side of the main
area, and as you passed you could hear their whispered voices beneath their helmets. You



avoided their eyes, glancing over to the same group of children that had come to greet Paz,
now engaged in a game of wrestling. Without fail every member of the tribe had a helmet
obscuring their face. It shocked you to see so many children compared to the scarce number
of warriors present. Yet before you could ask Paz gestured to inside the curtained area, and
you gratefully accepted his offer of having a seat.

Din scooted into the booth after you, placing the child on the table so he could see Paz. The
Warrior let the curtain drape closed behind him, choosing to sit across from you three. A
small grunt escaped Paz as he sat, and now at this close distance you could see a bandage
wrapped around his upper arm. You eyed it curiously but decided to let the Mandalorian
speak before you proffered any questions.

"After aiding in your escape, we knew the Empire would come back with force to attack us."
Paz told you two at last. Beside you, Din clenched his fist on his knee. "The Armorer sent
myself and several other warriors to evacuate the children and the foundlings before that
could happen."

"The Armorer?" You asked Din softly, and he bent his head towards you to reply.

"The leader of our covert." He explained, trying to quiet his voice so as to not interrupt Paz.
"She forges the armor we wear and is greatly respected by the tribe."

"She stayed behind." Paz commented upon hearing you both. "With the other members of the
clan, to shield our escape."

You were momentarily distracted by the green toddler in your care trying to waddle across
the table towards the larger Mando, reaching out and scooting him backwards like a naughty
kitten. He grunted in dismay, but otherwise sat still as you and Din focused back on Paz.

"Is she alive?" Din asked abruptly, and you blinked at the sudden dry crack in his voice. Paz's
shoulders sank at the question.

"I...am unsure." The warrior replied, voice uncertain and tinted with a sense of grief. “I tried
to have her join us, but she refused. I wanted to stay and fight, but she spoke on no uncertain
terms that I was to take as many children as possible and leave at once. I do not know what
happened to the rest of the Covert after that.”

A long silence followed, and in it you could feel the anxiety, the grief that remained
unspoken at the uncertain fate of the two warriors’ tribe members. Gently, you rested your
hand on top of Din’s under the table, feeling an iota of relief in the way he relaxed under your
touch. Finally, you volunteered your voice.

"Why Coruscant?" You asked, and Paz turned his helmeted gaze to regard you. "There's so
many planets out there, many of them peaceful. Why here?"

Paz lifted his head, seemingly in thought. When he spoke you could hear the indication of a
smile in his voice.

"It's the last place the Empire would ever look."



You and Din shared a glance, and the Mando gave a small nod of assent at his comrade’s
words. If you were being honest, you had to agree as well. Based on what little you knew of
the world, you doubted any Imperial Remnants would want to do a full sweep of the planet
scale metropolis to find a few adversaries, much less ones who were of a breed designed to
fight and destroy.

“In your message, you mentioned that you were under attack.” Din stated, drawing your
attention back to the conversation. He shifted, leaning an elbow onto the table. “I doubt the
Empire has found you yet, so who?”

Paz sighed a long-suffering sound and eased back into his seat. “When we arrived, we
thought that this section of Coruscant was abandoned.” You watched as he spread his arms
across the back of the seat, blinking at the way it broadened his shoulders. “Little did we
know that the Black Sun had already staked a claim on this territory. They’ve been trying to
reclaim it ever since.”

Din nodded to the bandage on Paz’s right bicep. “A gift, then?”

Paz chuckled mirthlessly. “‘Gift’ is a strong word.” He replied, lowering his voice into a
near-growl with his next words. “They attempted to raid this warehouse several days ago, and
unfortunately one of the foundlings was caught in the crossfire.”

You felt Din tense beside you, his entire body going rigid. You looked to him, seeing his
muscles coil underneath his armor. Beside you the child made a small sound of concern,
likely picking up on his guardian’s sudden animosity.

“What happened?” Din asked, and you suppressed a shudder at the deep, murderous tone of
his voice.

Paz looked at you both, letting his gaze weigh on each of you before speaking in a solemn,
low tone:

“He’s dead.” Paz confessed, hands clenching so that his leather gloves squeaked in his grasp.
“They killed him.”

Chapter End Notes

Chapter 21: Part Twenty-one: Midnight
Chapter Summary

"Look at me."

You blinked, gaze still on your bare feet. Yet the gentle, encouraging tone of Din's voice
prompted you to look up at him bashfully through your lashes. His head was bent to
observe you, shoulders as tight as yours but hands loose at his sides.

"What happened?" Din asked, and though it was less a question and more a demand, the
touch of warmth in his voice made you let out the breath you didn't know you had been
holding.

"I...couldn't sleep" You confessed at last in reply, voice fragile. "I had that nightmare
again."

Chapter Notes

TW for child death. Explicit/descriptive paragraphs are marked with a * at the beginning

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Din could hardly listen to the rest of the conversation that followed.

"He's dead. They killed him."

The words tumbled endlessly in his thoughts, bouncing in a catastrophic echo against the
walls of his mind. A sick, stomach turning emotion had begun to fester deep in his stomach at
the news, gouging him from the inside out as you and Paz continued to talk in now solemn,
hushed voices. The shadow of guilt drew darkly across his vision, all logic fleeing as a single
phrase resounded in a whispered refrain.

This was all his fault.

Were it not for Din, the covert would still be safely encamped on Nevarro, living safely in
secrecy. It was only at his need that the covert did reveal themselves, coming to his aid as he
tried to save the child. He didn't regret that part, the knowledge of what they would have
done to the kid far worse than the idea of the covert relocating.

Yet the knowledge that an innocent, a foundling, had perished in the string of consequences
that had led to this scenario-



The infinite maw of the boreholes leading down into the Coruscanti depths seemed not deep
enough to swallow Din's guilt.

*He could picture it, the moment at which the unnamed foundling had been lost. As blaster
shots rained down like hellfire on the compound, Din could see in his mind's eye a young
form attempt to race to safety, cowering with his helmeted head tucked down into his arms.
His feet hit the floor in long strides, like a deer fleeing into the woods. Just before he was out
of range, a gang member would turn, lay his sights on the child's back as he pressed down on
the trigger-

A soft, gentle touch atop his clenched fist drew Din back. A stifled, sorrowful gaze turned to
your smaller form beside him. Your upturned face too had the expression of a silent misery at
the foundling's fate, tears brimming hot against the corners of your eyes. That sight alone
plucked at Din’s heart more so than the vision he had conjured. For the briefest of moments
Din wished he could take you into his arms, let your soft sobs echo against his beskar chest
plate as he drowned himself in your mutual touch.

"Djarin."

There would come a time for that later.

Din swallowed hard, turning back to his brother in arms across the table who regarded him
with a silent gaze. In the vacuum that the grief and guilt had occupied Din now found a new
emotion surging through him. This one started at the tips of his white-knuckled fingers, a
heated flush spreading up to his arms and shoulders, setting fire coursing through his veins.
His breath was harsh against the inside of his helmet, the rage at the audacity, the crime, the
violation of an outsider taking the life of one of the clan's beloved children-

"So, it's war then." Din spoke, and in his voice he could hear the flames of wrath. He didn't
miss the way you stiffened, shivered beside him at the pure bloodlust in his tone.

Paz's gaze bore down on him for a moment longer, as if weighing Din's reaction. Then, he
returned with a slow, solemn nod as if accepting the inevitability of the battle that was to
come.

"It's war." Paz echoed, voice deep and heavy with intent.

The deafening silence that followed spoke volumes. With it came the serious, weighted pause
that occurred only before a battle to be fought, a duel to be declared. Din felt it settle into his
bones, harden there like his beskar cuirass.

Paz stood abruptly.

"Come." He spoke, gesturing for you three to follow him. "There will be time for tactics. Let
me show you to your bunks."

Din felt a part of him ease into a modicum of relief, something almost akin to happiness. The
idea of a bunk waiting for him within the confines of the covert eased the despair and fury
building in his chest. To again be surrounded by Mandalorians, by the covert, by his clan- it



brought an easiness that came with the concept of family, of belonging. A black sheep as he
was to the Covert, they were the closest thing he had to a home.

Din nodded, rising after the larger warrior and waiting for you to slip out of the booth behind
him. Paz drew the curtain open, ushering the two of you out before letting it drape closed
once more.

Paz led you three past the common area, down past one of the makeshift hallways and up
onto a lift that led to the second level. There lay an open space, what looked to be a floor
used for storage. The crates that would have occupied much of the space had been cleared,
either pushed to one side or discarded of. Instead, much of the room had been sectioned off
with welded scrap metal walls and tattered fabric curtains. On either side the large loading
doors that would have been used to transport largo cargo remained shut, leaving the room
securely enclosed. The high, overhead ceiling lights lit the space with a dim yellow light,
casting a hazy glow off the reflective scrap metal of the bunks.

Upon the lift's rise into the area Din could see several curious heads turn their way. The
smallest children of the covert were gathered on this level, carefully guarded by a slender
Mandalorian who Din recognized as one of the recently trained warriors. The children, most
of whom appeared to be roughly the same age, were playing some type of game involving a
mouse droid that skirted around the floor constantly out of reach. They paid no attention to
Din and the others as they entered, too occupied with their play time. Their bubbling laughter
indicated the resilience that only a child could bear, taking joy in the fleeting moments they
were allowed without the grief of their lost friend.

Paz gave the Mando watching over the children a small nod, and the soldier returned the
gesture. Then, after walking past several curtained bunks, he halted at a space off to the side
of the haphazardly decorated area.

"Here."

Din watched as Paz pushed aside a tattered curtain, revealing a small bunk in the converted
space he had led the three of you to. Din caught your glance at him, a momentary hesitation
of unfamiliarity at the situation. Din offered you a small nod, to which your shoulders sank in
relief and you continued forward. As you ducked under Paz's arm, crossing the threshold into
the small room, Din made to follow.

A hand on his chest plate stopped him, and Din turned to meet the visored gaze of the
broader Mando in front of him.

"Male bunks are on the first floor." Paz intoned, and Din stiffened at the flat, unbudging
inflection of his voice.

Of course. As was custom, only married couples were allowed to bunk together. On Nevarro
that privilege was extended to only a meager handful of warriors who had recited their vows
before the Armorer.

A flustered blush rose to Din's face under his helmet. He had been so used to having you and
the child close by that it hadn't occurred to him that you would be bunking separately for the



duration of your stay. Yet the unspoken insinuation left by his attempt to follow you left a
resounding silence between him and Paz. Din could only imagine the other warrior's arched
eyebrows and intent, curious gaze under his visor.

"I'll only be a moment." Din managed at last, thanking the stars that his voice remained
unwavering.

Paz regarded Din for a moment longer, as if scrutinizing him. At last he nodded, stepping
aside to allow space for the leaner Mandalorian to pass.

"Come find me in the strategy area below. I'll be waiting," To which Din nodded with a dry
swallow before easing past Paz into the bunk. He waited a moment longer for the older
warrior's footsteps to fade before he turned to you.

Your back was turned to him, taking in the small, spartan bunk before you. The child that had
previously been in your arms now toddled around the small area, inspecting its meager
furnishings. A bed roll sat off to one side, a single blanket atop it. A crate with a small bowl
full of water atop it sat next to the cot, and beside it a small lantern which offered little light
in the already dim space.

"It's more than I expected." You spoke faintly, eyes looking up to where the draped ceiling
met the forged metal panels. "But are you sure we can't sleep on the Razorcrest?"

Din grimaced beneath his helmet, easily detecting the hesitation of unfamiliarity in your
voice.

"It's safer here." He offered. "You'll be protected."

"We were already protected." You answered softly, turning to him with a soft, concerned
gaze. Yet your words were not a protest, not spoken in a tone meant to debate or argue.
Instead, it was a soft confession, a plea for reassurance.

Din felt himself soften at your gaze, a familiar rise of easiness at your presence washing away
the tension left by his brief exchange with Paz. He shifted forward, subtly closing the
distance between you two and watching your disconcerted eyes all the while.

"I can protect you better here." Din spoke, reiterating himself. "With the other Mandalorians
nearby I can focus on aiding Paz Vizsla and the other warriors."

Your eyes shifted down, an empty hand catching your opposite arm almost uncomfortably.
Din wanted to reach out, warm the exposed skin of your forearms beneath his gloves. Yet he
remained still with uncertainty, swallowing as he watched you.

"Is that what you plan to do?" You asked, voice small.

Din hesitated, noticing the way you stiffened at your own question, the way you drew your
eyes away from his gaze.

What are you so afraid of, Cuyan? He wondered silently to himself. I'm right here.



"Yes." He answered instead, and the word came out flat, forced. When you didn't answer,
sucking on the inside of your lip in worry, he went on.

"The Covert...it was because of me that they had to relocate. Had it not been for me, they
would still be on Nevarro. I...can't leave it like this."

He thought the words would reassure you, but instead they served to only make you shrink
further into yourself. The corners on your lips dipped into a tight frown, brow wrinkling in a
mixture of anxiety and dismay. Your reaction puzzled Din, considering your original response
to the news of the foundling's death. Simply sitting beside you he felt the wave of nausea, of
fear and grief wash over you despite you never having met the child.

"I see." Was all you replied with, and the soft, resigned tone of your voice made Din shift
from foot to foot in uneasiness.

He didn’t understand. Did you not approve of him aiding in avenging his fellow foundling?
Of fighting alongside his brothers and sisters on behalf of their children? Of defending the
covert?

Din knew that wasn't the case, but the idea of your discontent with his mission made his brow
draw and jaw set in an idling sense of frustration. When you didn't speak further to try and
explain yourself he turned sharply back towards the entrance of the bunk.

"Din, wait-"

He paused, turning his head so he looked at you over his shoulder.

For the briefest of moments your eyes raised towards him, absent of the anxiety you had felt
only moments ago. Instead, you gazed forward with certainty, eyes clear and focused directly
on his own.

"It wasn't your fault." You spoke, and this time your tone didn't waver.

Din felt his lips part, eyes flickering with a silent light of recognition for a heartbeat before
darkening once more. Instead of a reply he only nodded once, gravely, before turning once
more and letting the curtain fall behind him.

---

Hot.

An unbearable heat, one that seemed to carve inside of you and devour you from the inside
out. Worse than fire, louder than an inferno, the roar of the blaze consumed every fiber of
your being. With it came screams, shouts, the rain of blaster bolts pinging off ancient
corridors and solemn statues.

You tried to scream, but the sound was silent against the endless chorus of anguish that
surrounded you. Blindly, you reached out for something, anything to anchor yourself to.
Instead, you were met only with a catastrophic absence, a darkness across your vision that
you sank into seemingly without end.



Why? You had never done anything worthy of this pain, this infinite chaos. Your days had
been peaceful ones, surrounded by your friends and allies. Even the darkest hours with them
had passed like a gentle rolling thunderstorm, with soft sunlight spilling through darkened
rainclouds after. None of it should have earned you the horrific soul defying grief that you
felt as another shot rang out, cutting off a sharp scream of terror.

You tried to run, tried to move forward and away from the unseen danger that lay before you.
Yet even then as you turned in the darkness another voice called desperately for you,
shrieking your name as you backed away, feet teetering on the precipice of a pitch-black
void.

Again, your name, louder than any sound you had ever heard, echoed forth in the voice of a
child. The force of it knocked you backwards, and at once you were falling, falling, the heat
rising as you yourself screamed without sound and the inferno blazed from somewhere
below-

"No!"

You gasped, bolting upright as your body reacted before your mind could fully process.
Limbs flailing, you knocked over your shoes on the crate beside you in a blind attempt to
grasp onto something, anything to anchor yourself from the nightmare. Chest heaving
desperately for air, you tried to swallow enough oxygen to let your brain catch up to your
movements. Yet even then it didn't stop the cold sweat, the deep tremble set in your limbs.
The blaze from your dream seemed to chase you into wakefulness, and it was only once you
tossed off the blanket pooled in your lap that you were able to feel the rush of frigid air
present in the Mandalorian enclave envelop you.

Upon seeing the dim, yellow glow of the lantern beside you, the stale air in your chest
seemed to finally fill your lungs. The soft, comforting light drew you for a moment like a
moth to flame, holding you gently against the creeping darkness. Your hand automatically
reached against it, the pads of your fingers barely brushing the hot surface of the glass before
drawing back.

"Just a dream." You spoke, breath still coming in stuttering, uneven exhales. "Just a dream."

Yet it didn't feel like a dream. It was too familiar, too detailed for it to be a dream. Still, you
couldn't recall having experienced anything as equally horrific as the scenario inside the
vision. Even now you could hear the screams of those around you desperately trying to flee
that which was unseen, that void-like darkness that lurked within the confines of your
thoughts.

A shiver ran through you, leaving goosebumps in its wake. In the silence of your bunk your
hammering heartbeat seemed loud enough to rattle the core of Coruscant itself.

As long as it took you to finally collect yourself, it took a moment longer to realize that you
were no longer aboard the Razorcrest. The humming engines, the whir of the ship's systems
were strangely absent from your surroundings. Instead, if you listened, you could hear the
subtle shifting of others in their beds, of soft snores from children as they slept. More than



that, you couldn't hear the familiar murmur of Din and the child conversing in words you
couldn't make out from your bunk behind the cockpit.

Right. You were alone. Din was sleeping in the men's corridor, resting with the child who he
had insisted on taking with him to allow you some proper rest.

The chill of his absence left you oddly empty, and even as you lay down once more and
tugged the blanket around you, you couldn't quell the odd clench inside your chest. Din's
words from earlier tugged at you, settling in your stomach anxiously.

"I...can't leave it like this."

You squirmed beneath your covering, grasping the blanket tighter around you. Din's reaction
to your dismay at his newfound mission only served to deepen the concern gnawing inside
you. The way he had stiffened, turned so sharply to leave and later in the day had been so
short with you- it haunted you almost as much as the nightmare still slinking through your
thoughts.

It wasn't as if you disapproved of him aiding the Covert. Rather, you were compelled at the
opportunity to learn more about him, his background, his culture, and the place where he
belonged. To find yourself in such a vastly different culture than the place you had grown up
in lift you brimming with excitement. No. It wasn't that.

Nor was it the mission itself. You yourself felt a dark urge to commit your abilities to the
battle ahead, the death of an innocent weighing heavily against your conscience. For such a
young life to be stolen away in such a way, it left an unabating ager creeping like a shadow in
your heart.

Rather, it was the fact that it was Din committing himself to such a violent struggle. It was
Din who was marching off to war with a faction known for their brutality and swift
vengeance.

You knew you shouldn't worry. Din had more than proven himself on more than one occasion
to be completely capable of dealing with adversaries. He had saved your life and the child's
more times than you cared to count by this point. His tenacity to do whatever it took to keep
you three safe spoke for itself.

And yet...

The deep breath you had been holding spilled forth in a quiet sigh against the otherwise silent
bunk. You shouldn't be thinking about this, instead trying to focus on getting back to sleep so
you could face tomorrow with better judgement.

Even so, the conspicuous absence of Din's nearby presence in the cockpit or walking across
the hold left you empty. The gap left by the silence devoid of the child's soft breathy snores
allowed sleep to dance nimbly out of your grasp.

An idea occurred to you, and as much as you tried to chase it away, the temptation of relief
from your insomnia whispered to you enticingly.



So finally, you rose from your bunk. Standing with the cool floor under your bare feet, you
took your blanket tightly against your chest as you cautiously ventured beyond the confines
of your bunk.

To your relief there were no other occupants in the communal area beyond the curtained
doorways of the enclosed rooms. No one to witness or hinder your midnight journey to your
destination on the floor below. The overhead lights were thankfully off, casting your form
into shadow as you padded carefully across the open area.

You would wake up the entire covert if you took the elevator, so instead you opted for the
ramp leading down behind the bunks into the makeshift training area. There, you briefly
ducked behind a crate as a warrior on night duty passed you by. His footsteps faded as he
walked past you towards the back entrance near the loading platform. It was only after he had
crossed the threshold that you darted forward, silence lent to you by the years on Kaddak
streets scrounging as a thief to survive.

"Third door on the left." You silently reminded yourself as you crept forward into the men's
corridor. Somehow it was even more silent than the women and children's corridor, each
warrior only barely resting in case they needed to be called to arms at a moment's notice. It
made your journey a difficult one, each step placed like a Canto-Bight dancer crossing
elegantly across the ballroom floor.

The male dormitories were actually separated into rooms rather than bunks. It looked to be
some type of converted office space, with enclosed cubicles offering a modicum of privacy.
Why the men managed to get more privacy than you and the children's corridor made little
sense, you thought derisively. Even so, you were grateful for the walls, as they allowed your
next movement to be obscured by any curious gazes that would have peeked outside
curtained doorways.

With a gentle, almost not there rap on the doorway, you called out in a whisper:

"Din?"

No response.

So, you tried again, voice the same volume. Even then there wasn't any indication of the
room's occupants stirring to answer your call.

You felt yourself deflate, disappointment sitting bitterly in your stomach. You should have
expected this. The Mando was likely exhausted after a week of barely sleeping on the
Razorcrest, always on the lookout for would-be interceptors.

Yet as you turned, hugging your blanket tight to your chest, you heard a soft shuffle inside.
You paused, listening to what sounded like a whispered curse followed by movement until-

The door slid open with a soft squeak, revealing a helmeted Din.

A helmeted Din...in pants but with no shirt.



You were grateful for the darkness of the hallway, allowing you to see Din but hiding your
suddenly wide eyes and raised eyebrows quickly vanishing into your hairline.

"Cuyan?" Din asked, voice soft with sleep but concerned nonetheless. "What?”

You swallowed hard, trying desperately to avert your eyes from the Mandalorian's bare torso.
You had always imagined him to be muscular (as much as you were embarrassed to admit
you imagined him at all) but the actuality of his exposed form left your mouth suddenly dry.

Din didn't have the washboard abdominal muscles you had originally envisioned, nor was he
nearly as broad as he looked in his armor. Yet he was muscular in the way that he was lean,
with a narrow waist and the faint outline of abdominal muscles below his diaphragm. A trail
of dark hair angled downwards towards the hem of his pants, and you had to keep your eyes
from descending too low to follow it.

"I-" You spoke, whispered voice cracking, jerking your eyes up to his helmet. "I-I'm sorry, I
didn't- this was a mistake. I should go-"

You turned abruptly, eyes wide and practically tripping over yourself as you averted your
gaze and started back towards your bunk.

Instead, your bicep was caught in a firm but gentle grasp.

You spun your gaze back to the hand's owner, lips parted in surprise. Din didn't speak, barely
breathed. For a heartbeat you were both caught in a teetering balance, neither willing to draw
closer or farther away from the other.

At last you saw Din loosen, one hand still caught on your arm and the other braced on the
frame of the doorway. He drew back into the room, not releasing his grip and gently guiding
you with him. You allowed yourself to be carefully escorted beyond the barrier of the
doorway, where Din let go of you and slid the door shut behind you.

He let his hands settle on the door handle for a moment longer, pausing to look and listen for
any potential prying eyes. When he turned to you, you squirmed under his gaze. The lit
lantern in his quarters allowed you to see the details of his figure more acutely now, and your
curious gaze roved from his stomach up to his shoulders and then down to his muscular arms.
You wanted to gaze openly, but you forced your eyes down to your feet instead.

"What is it?" Din asked, voice a touch louder in the confines of the room. "Did something
happen?"

The heat on your face was unbearable, ashamed of your boldness in coming to Din in the
middle of the night and too embarrassed to admit the reason. You shivered, not from the cold
of the warehouse but from the concept of suddenly being so exposed.

"Sorry." You muttered at last, eyes stubbornly fixed on the floor. You drew your shoulders
tight, tension radiating from your posture. "I...it's silly. I should go."



Din shifted from foot to foot, as if weighing whether or not he should let you leave. He
seemed uncomfortable at first, likely by your mere presence in his bunk. Yet in his next
words he spoke softly, encouraging you to draw your gaze upwards.

"Look at me."

You blinked, gaze still on your bare feet. Yet the gentle, encouraging tone of Din's voice
prompted you to look up at him bashfully through your lashes. His head was bent to observe
you, shoulders as tight as yours but hands loose at his sides.

"What happened?" Din asked, and though it was less a question and more a demand, the
touch of warmth in his voice made you let out the breath you didn't know you had been
holding.

"I...couldn't sleep" You confessed at last in reply, voice fragile. "I had that nightmare again."

Din tilted his head at you, visored gaze remaining on your form.

"' 'That' nightmare?" He echoed, and you blinked, realizing. You had never told him about
your consistent dream, about the screaming, the chaos, the fire-

You shuddered, and the motion prompted Din to take a small step forward towards you, then
pause as if awaiting your invitation.

"I-" You started, voice cracking. You wanted to tell him, to explain the horror that had
plagued you since childhood and had been written anew after meeting him and the child. You
wished you could close the distance between you both, tuck yourself against his form and
gasp out the fear, the terror that gripped you in the hours between sleep and wakefulness. Yet
the night was dark, the shadows too long for you to confess your horrid recurring dream, and
you were so tired.

"I don't want to talk about it." You replied at last, tucking into yourself protectively.
"Can...can I just...stay here? I-I don't want to be alone."

You saw the way Din stiffened, the way he drew up a little higher in automatic response. To
you it signaled a line you had crossed too soon, a discomfort at the idea of mutually agreeing
to spend the night in each other's presence. When Din moved, you expected it to be to open
the door once more, to wait for you to leave and close it behind you. What happened instead
left you wide-eyed with shock.

Din scooted past you, sitting himself down on the bedroll beside the child's closed carrier and
motioning for you to lay down beside him.

You shifted from foot to foot for a moment before obliging. Gingerly, you arranged yourself
so that your head was on the top of the mat opposite where Din sat. The small pillow there
was soft under your head, sinking under your weight. With the bassinet beside you, you could
hear the child's soft snores undisturbed by your midnight conversation.

Somehow you managed to tuck yourself so that Din had space at the bottom of the pad to sit
upright with his back against the wall. You wondered if that was uncomfortable for him but



felt as if you had already toed the silent boundary between you enough for one night. There
was plenty of room for you both, but perhaps Din felt an obligation to allow you the pad
before he himself took use of it. It reminded you of his awkward attempts at being a
gentleman when he had accidentally stumbled upon you bathing in the lagoon.

Despite the awkward air between you both, Din's mere presence did much to soothe your
frayed nerves. You didn't know when it had happened, but the simple act of having him close
by had long since begun to be a great comfort to you. Simply knowing he was nearby, ready
to defend, to fight, to talk, to simply be close allowed your eyes to slowly drift close.

Yet even then you didn't fall asleep. Even with your blanket it was colder on the first floor,
and no matter how you wiggled deeper into the material you couldn't seem to summon
enough warmth to get comfortable.

Your shiver must have alerted Din, because in the dark silence he gently asked. "You okay?"

"It's cold." You muttered back, eyes opening to peer down the length of the sleeping pad at
him. "Dunno how you don't need a blanket."

Din shrugged at first to your response, the motion tight despite its nonchalant nature. Upon
realizing the level of your discomfort, however, he stiffened even further. You assumed he
would remain silent and tried once again to force your eyes closed. Then, cautiously, Din
began to move.

In that way where he treated you like fragile glass, Din's hands gently scooted you, so you
balanced on the edge of the pad. You looked up to comment but silenced yourself upon
watching him insert himself in between you and the wall that the mat was pressed against.
You were so shocked that you didn't even flinch when he let an arm settle over you, the touch
at first hesitant and awkward and the settling loosely against your frame.

"Is this okay? I-I can sit up."

You didn't breathe, didn't move, feeling like your heartbeat would pause as well if you didn't
let go of the breath you had been holding.

He was warm. The heat from his torso carried the same radiant heat as afternoon sunlight
against slightly chilled skin. You were so cold that you automatically curled into it, pressing
your back against his chest and shivering. Din tensed, but when you settled he too relaxed,
allowing your gentle shifting in a bid to get comfortable.

"I-it's nice." You admitted, the warmth flushing across your skin doing more to chase away
the chill than Din's bodily heat itself. "Thank you."

Din hummed a small sound, something akin to a sleepy assent.

It was nice, if you were being honest with yourself. If it was enough simply having Din
nearby to chase away any rogue nightmares, the security that you felt pressed against him
with one arm gently draped over you was immeasurable. A flood of affection ran through
you, remembering the way his gloved hands had grazed your arms in the cockpit moments



before Paz's message, how he had held you on Hypori as you teetered on succumbing to the
Trandoshan poison.

This was different. This touch was born out of reassurance, yes, but it wasn't concerned,
fleeting. Instead, it was the embrace not of a protector, but of a friend. Perhaps, if you let
your heart truly hope, it was even more than that.

Your blossoming feelings for Din did not rise hot in your chest. Instead, the comfort of his
body pressed to yours in the darkness of night allowed a sigh of relief to bubble up your
throat, as if you had just come home from an awfully long journey. Your affection for the
Mandalorian did not race through you and cause your heart like a caged bird. Instead, it
settled over you like a veil, beautiful and intimately woven with your own heartstrings as
threads.

If you could stay like this, with no nightmares, no war, no pursuit from the Guild or Empire,
nothing except you, Din, and the gentle snores of the child beside you, then you would be
happy for all eternity.

You were finally comfortable, finally safe from the horrid dreams that threatened to haunt
you. Yet there remained a conspicuous gnawing sensation inside your chest, one unrelated to
just how close you had pressed yourself against your protector, the newfound experience of
being in his arms out of your own accord.

"Din." You spoke, and the Mandalorian behind you made a small, sleepy sound of
recognition.

You let the words settle in your chest before speaking, whispering them as a soft confession
in the silence of the Coruscanti midnight.

"Whatever happens with you and the Covert...promise me you'll come back to us when it's all
over."

Din didn't respond, and you assumed that he had drifted off without hearing your final plea.
Even so, it was enough for you to voice it aloud. You let the spoken words carry the anxiety
out of your chest and into the chilled twilight, watched them evaporate into nothingness with
naught but the sound lingering against your senses. It was only then that your eyes closed,
and the blissful relief of sleep embraced you as gentle as Din's comforting touch.

And as wakefulness faded at last, you heard the words:

"I promise."
