Chapter 22: Part Twenty-two: The Incident
Chapter Summary

"Nothing." Din answered quickly, and the sudden short cut of his voice was less a
response and more a warning to you to be still. Even so, even with the potential
consequences of being caught, you couldn't help but bite back a small, sly grin at the
circumstances. The idea of Paz cracking open the door to reveal you sitting cross-legged
on Din’s sleeping mat, watching him get dressed with bright eyes was dangerous and
exhilarating at the same time. You almost wished it would happen, just to see Paz’s
reaction and imagine the scandalized expression under his helmet.

You barely contained a snort of amusement as Din struggled to yank the flight suit up to
his waist, shimmying into the fabric with one leg held aloft as he balanced. The Mando
seemed less than amused, and even without seeing his face the expression he gave you
as you glanced over your shoulder spoke of a dry annoyance at the mischief in your
eyes.

Yet both of you stopped at the questioning tone of Paz outside the door.

"Is there someone in there?"

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

It wasn't the soft hum of the Razorcrest's engines that awoke you the next morning, soft and
steady against the back of your mind. Nor was it the quiet voices speaking from the cockpit
as Din made small conversation with the youngster in his care, listening to his small baby
babbling. Instead, there was a soft, fleeting touch against your face, cool against your skin
and gentle against your sleepy senses.

"Din?" You thought hazily, mind drawing back to the hand that had gently brushed your hair
from your face while you dozed, that had eased the nightmares in the inn on Rishi.

When your eyes fluttered open, however, it wasn't the helmeted gaze of your protector. You
had expected to see the unmistakable T-shaped visor belonging to your Mandalorian. Instead
as your vision came into focus you were greeted by a bright, curious brown stare complete
with long green ears and a wrinkled forehead.

The child tilted his head at you, one hand still smushed gently against your cheek. He cooed
softly, as if trying not to awaken the sleeping Mando behind you.

Any remaining grogginess fled you instantly upon remembering the happenings of last night.
Slowly the memory filtered back to you through your sleep addled thoughts; of how you had



snuck down to Din's bunk in the male corridors after awakening from your dreaded
nightmare. The image of Din in his nightclothes answering the door in the hallway darkened
by midnight drowned out any other thought, making your heart beat a little faster in your
chest.

Reflexively, you caught your breath upon realizing just how bold your actions were the night
prior. Sneaking into the men's dorms was one thing, but knocking at midnight on the door of
the same man who had spoken to you in a low, affectionate tone aboard the Razorcrest? The
same one who had been slowly drifting closer to you over the past weeks, going as far as to
hint at his feelings for you? All while you were dressed only in your loose sleeping clothes?

The heart fluttering feeling that should have come to you last night now beat against your
chest with your realization. You didn't move, didn't breathe a word, afraid of awakening the
Mandalorian as he slept beside you.

Even now you could hear the soft snores from under Din's bucket behind you. In his sleep he
had somehow dragged you even closer to him, one arms wrapped securely around your waist.
Your entire back was pressed flush against his front, and you could feel the soft rise and fall
of his chest as he slept. It was almost as if he was clinging to you in sleep.

You didn't bother to hide the grin that spread across your face, eyes twinkling at the light
flutter in your chest. The fact that Din had become so comfortable around you in the course
of your travels together, enough so that he had agreed to spend the night on the same cot as
you, drew forth a profound joy in your chest. It traveled up your throat and threatened to
escape as a bubbling laugh. Your own developing feelings for the Mando let loose from your
lips with a contented sigh, eyes closing in momentary bliss at your soft awakening.

It was so comfortable like this. You knew you had to get up and some point to take care of
the child, and to figure out a way to sneak out of the dormitories unsuspected, but for now
you wanted to just stay like this in Din’s arms. You wished for nothing else than to doze with
Din beside you, peaceful and content, hoping that morning would wait just a little longer.
Silently, you gently wiggled yourself farther into Din's hold, trying to memorize the way his
body curved around you, how tightly his arm held you around your waist.

Din shifted, and you stilled. However, he only mumbled something to himself before settling
once more. You breathed a sigh of relief, not wanting him to wake up just yet so you could
enjoy your time with him a little longer. Likely he’d find a way to instantly distance himself
from you in the small space when he did open his eyes, much to your potential dismay. Din's
propensity to draw back as soon as you two got too close bothered you, and you didn't want
his sudden reflexively distancing to ruin this soft moment you found yourself in. Instead, you
closed your eyes, trying to ingrain every feeling, sense, and sound into your soul as the
morning dawned with a gentle beckoning.

That was, until-

Heavy footsteps sounded at the end of the corridor, rapidly coming closer. Your eyes shot
open, body tensing automatically in preparation. The motion caused Din to stir once more, as
he made a small grumble of awakening behind you. Before he could fully grasp you still in
his arms, the footsteps stopped at the door and a deep tenor voice rang out.



"Djarin." Paz called out from beyond the door. "How long are you planning to sleep? You
were supposed to be in the training area 5 minutes ago."

Neither of you responded, and you could tell by Din's sudden stillness and silence that he was
still processing the current situation. You suspected that if you were able to see his face his
wide-eyed expression would look like a bordok in the headlights.

Upon not receiving a response the Mandalorian at the door knocked again. "Vod?"

"I'm awake." Din responded at last, and your eyes widened upon hearing the rough treble of
his voice, gravelly with awakening. "Give me a minute."

With that Din began to detach himself from you, and you let out a small grumble of protest in
response, lips turning down in a frown of displeasure. He froze, as if suddenly understanding
that you were awake as well. You shifted, rolling slightly to face him. With one arm propped
under him, Din's helmet was practically nose to nose with you as you looked up at him.
Breath catching, you swore you could see past the black of his visor for just a moment, to
where a pair of wide eyes gazed at you from underneath-

"You fall asleep again?"

Both of you startled, and the sudden jolt from you accidentally knocked your forehead into
Din's beskar helmet with a dull thunk.

"No." Din answered flatly, glancing quickly at the door before turning back to you.

"Ow ow ow-" You hissed under your breath, reaching up to gently pat the sudden tender area
of your forehead with the flat of your palm.

"You okay?" Din asked softly, voice tinting with concern, and you gave him a quick
reassuring smile in response. Truly, you would have laughed at the humor of the entire
situation, with Din still only half clothed, the baby beside you whining at your sudden
discomfort and everything else if it weren't for the Mando still standing right outside the very
flimsy sliding door.

"I'm fine." You reassured him in a quick whisper, motioning with your other hand for him to
get up and start getting dressed. With some carefully extraction and a few mumbles, Din was
able to get over you to the armor leaning against the wall on the other side of the room. Even
with the lantern off, the light of the hallway managed to seep in and illuminate his bare torso.

You quickly averted your eyes from his exposed form, a warm flush rising to your face and
making it hot to the touch. Even so, your eyes couldn't help but wander back to Din's muscled
shoulders and arms as they yanked over his undershirt over his head. The outline of his
biceps was much more predominant in the early morning light, flexing as he raised his arms.
The Mando turned to reach for his folded flight suit, stopping when he noticed your eyes on
him.

The warmth on your face was nothing compare to the sudden full-body flush you felt at being
caught peeking. Lifting yourself up, you quickly tried to swivel your body to face the wall in



a sit, giving Din the privacy he needed. Your abrupt, sloppy motion knocked the crate beside
you, causing the unlit lantern there to wobble and tilt off onto the floor with a loud clatter.

"Kriff.” You couldn't help but curse, your hand slapping over your mouth not even a
heartbeat after the sound left you. You glanced sharply at din, eyes wide with surprise. The
Mandalorian paused his movement, watching the lantern roll to the feet of the toddler beside
you.

"What was that?" The muffled voice outside the door asked, deep voice rising with curiosity.

"Nothing." Din answered quickly, and the sudden short cut of his voice was less a response
and more a warning to you to be still. Even so, even with the potential consequences of being
caught, you couldn't help but bite back a small, sly grin at the circumstances. The idea of Paz
cracking open the door to reveal you sitting cross-legged on Din’s sleeping mat, watching
him get dressed with bright eyes was dangerous and exhilarating at the same time. You
almost wished it would happen, just to see Paz’s reaction and imagine the scandalized
expression under his helmet.

You barely contained a snort of amusement as Din struggled to yank the flight suit up to his
waist, shimmying into the fabric with one leg held aloft as he balanced. The Mando seemed
less than amused, and even without seeing his face the expression he gave you as you
glanced over your shoulder spoke of a dry annoyance at the mischief in your eyes.

"Is there someone in there?" Paz asked, voice dipping down an octave in suspicion.

Both of you froze, and the humor in your smile evaporated in an instant. In your silent
conversation the child between you glanced back and forth at your faces, voicing a small,
baby-ish 'ehh?' in concern.

"Just the kid." Din answered, without breaking eye contact with you. His stare bore into your
own, hinting dangerously to cease your silent antics. "He's being a little womp-rat."

The child made a small snort of indignancy, to which you covered your mouth as you held
back a huff of laughter.

You managed to stay still and quiet as Din donned the rest of his armor, finally standing in
full beskar at the doorway. The dim light from outside managed to catch the shiny metal,
casting a brief glare against the walls of the room.

With his hand outstretched to the handle he turned to you and the child behind him. You
straightened a little under his stare, looking up sheepishly from your spot on the bed mat. You
offered him an apologetic smile, noticing the way his hand loosened a little on the door.

"Stay out of trouble." He spoke, as if reprimanding the child, yet his eyes remained locked on
you. You nodded earnestly, mussed bed-hair bouncing with the motion.

Then Din's voice softened, his tone easing into something more affectionate, something
gentle like the way he had held you asleep in his arms.



"I'll...see you soon."

With a lingering glance Din swiftly slipped out the door, not allowing Paz outside to get even
a peek into the room.

You could hear muffled conversation as they departed, with Paz sounding curious and Din
feinting fatigue in his voice. Their voices grew distant as they left, headed towards the
training area as Paz had mentioned.

It wasn't until two pairs of footsteps echoed down the hallway that you finally let out the
breath you'd been holding with a soft woosh. The brown eyed toddler next to you looked up
into your face as you did, again making a small whine for attention. You offered him a soft,
apologetic smile.

"I think that was the easy part, bud." You murmured quietly. Now alone, you let yourself
stretch out, a small groan escaping you as the sleepiness left your limbs. With a sigh you
turned your eyes back to the child, an eyebrow arched in mischief.

"Getting out of here is going to be tricky even for me."

-----

With Din's departure, having been summoned to a war council headed by Paz, you and the
child were left to your own devices.

You started by waiting for the perfect moment to sneak from Din's bunk, managing to get all
the way out of the male dormitories before stumbling into one of the younger Mandos. You
managed an excuse about not being able to find the bathrooms, hinting at a fake urgency that
allowed you to escape without any further questioning and ignoring his continued gaze on
you as you slipped around a corner.

After getting you and the child back to your bunk, washing up in the wash bin, and getting
dressed, you went in search of some type of breakfast. Fortunately finding the kitchen was
fairly easy. The moment you stepped into the communal area on the first floor you were able
to follow the smell of cooking food to an area off to the side of the warehouse filled with
light chatter and small wisps of cooking smoke.

The kitchen seemed to be some former maintenance area, with several of the obsolete
machines used for scraps in making several stoves, ovens, and flat cooking surfaces. It wasn’t
ideal by any means, but it was functional and allowed the two Mandos there to cook enough
food to offer the Covert. As a mechanic you found yourself once again impressed by how
much the Covert had been able to salvage from the old warehouse and then convert in
functioning technology for everyday needs. Your idea of volunteering as someone who could
help with construction and repairs seemed a little redundant with just how much they'd been
able to create from nothing.

The two Mandalorians in the kitchen eyed you curiously upon your entry, but otherwise
remained silent as you snagged what looked to be some type of starch and stew for you and
the kid. The soup was a little watery, the meat within it scarce and slightly overcooked, but



you couldn't really complain. It was better than the endless supply of ration bars and freeze-
dried meals that Din kept stored on the Razorcrest. Besides, the child seemed to like it well
enough, having downed a second bowl before you had even finished your first.

Yet as you sat in a far corner of the kitchen during your meal you could feel the continuous
stare of the kitchen's occupants, none of them bothering to hide their visored gazes observing
you and your tiny companion. The undeniable sensation of being watched soured the flavor
of the food in your mouth somewhat. Every time you looked up to meet the gazes of the two
in the cooking area they turned their backs, eyes averting just a moment too late from your
form.

You were able to read Din fairly well at this point despite his ever-present helmeted
expression, but in the presence of these new Mandalorians you couldn't help but flounder a
little. In Din’s presence the trademark Mandalorian helmet was his face rather than being a
threatening mask. Yet now, with the blank visored gazes of other Mandos around you, the
original purpose of intimidation had become quite clear.

The other Mandos weren't hostile, per say. Rather, they had all been fairly courteous so far.
Yet the scant interactions you had with them had informed you of their attempts to remain
distant, not bothering to go as far as to learn your name or story besides your connection to
Din. Though no direct action had been taken to inform you of your role as an outsider, the
signal was clear enough from the short conversations and deliberately brief dialogue that had
been given to you.

Paz’s words upon your first meeting echoed back to you. ”How dare you bring an outsider
here?” You knew the Mandalorians were a tightly woven community and given the recent
events they had every right to be suspicious of outsiders. Yet your dismay at being watched
with caution weighed on you, sinking your shoulders with every passing stare.

Even now, as you watched the kid finish his now third bowl of stew, you could hear low
whispers from another pair of male Mandos near the doorway to the kitchen. They were
careful not to raise their voices enough for you to hear them, but it was clear from the glances
tossed your way that you were the object of their conversation. For what you didn't know, but
the fact alone left your face hot with a sense of self consciousness.

A burp beside you drew your attention to the child, who smiled up at you with post-meal
contentment. You smiled in return, feeling your heart fill with affection as your concerns
about being gossiped about faded. Instead, you focused on the child, who waved his spoon at
you with a sound of delight.

The kid really was adorable in many ways. With his oversized ears and huge, curious gaze
you couldn't help but find him utterly charming. His propensity for endearing mischief and
sweet nature made it pretty easy to be enchanted with the little guy. Yet even without those
things you could still feel your chest surge with warmth at his presence close to you, drawing
upon an invisible connection that had been forged long ago. If reincarnation did exist, then
perhaps you knew the child from another lifetime.

"All done?" You asked him, and the kid made a small gurgle of agreement.



It was remarkable how much the kid was able to understand despite his age. Even though he
was so young he seemed to be able to keep up with your and Din's conversations fairly easily.
Despite being able to contribute little other than small baby gibberish, he was expressive
enough to signal his agreement or displeasure at whatever you spoke to him. It spoke of an
emotional and logical intelligence beyond his years.

A bark of laughter from the other side of the room made you glance to the two Mandalorians
at the door, who quickly silenced themselves as your gaze drew over towards them. They
stared back at you silently, the blank stares of their helmets expressionless. You managed to
tear your gaze from them before you frowned into your half-empty soup bowl, its meager
contents reflecting back your uncomfortable expression.

"Let's go find your dad, shall we?" You asked the toddler beside you, feigning brightness. He
gave you a toothy smile in reply.

After cleaning up after yourself, you hoisted the child into your arms, making you way past
the two Mandos at the door with your eyes turned down and cheeks warm with self-
consciousness.

The communal area was bustling with activity, with several younglings playing what seemed
to be a game of tag. The boy who had greeted you, Paz and Din yesterday noticed your
entrance and left the others, jogging over to you.

"Hey! Cuyan!"

You turned, blinking at the Mando'a nickname. The older boy skidded to a halt in front of
you, but before he could say whatever it was he was meant to you blurted out:

"How did you know that name?"

The kid tilted his head at you, as if confused. "I heard Din call you that name yesterday.” He
supplied. “I thought it was kinda funny since I've never heard anyone with that name before,
but you smiled when he called you that so-" He shook his head, the slightly too large helmet
rattling on his head.

"Oh! But he- Din, that is, he told me to tell you that Paz told him- or wait, did he tell Paz?"
He glanced briefly down in thought, one hand scratching the top of his helmet where his hair
would have been.

"Right! They're going out to move the ship- I think it was called the Razorcrest. Is that
right?"

You nodded, feeling a small smile tug at your lips as you witnessed the boy's bubbly but
rambling manner of speaking.

"Anyways, he said he'd be back later, and that I should let you know. Oh, and my name is
Umos, by the way." Umos finished with a little shrug, tilting his head back to fully look up at
your face.



Your eyes softened, looking kindly down at the boy. You wished you could see his face,
could commit his smile to memory as the only person who had been so kind to you in the
covert, with his rambunctious energy and youthful excitement. A part of you wondered if Din
too, had been louder, happier at Umos' age.

"Thank you, Umos." You replied sweetly.

The boy nodded enthusiastically, but before he could continue the conversation one of his
playmates called out across the room, beckoning him back into their game. Umos glanced
over his shoulder to look at the source of the sound, a younger girl with only a single black
visor band at the level of her eyes. A tell-tale braid escaped from under her helmet, brown
and frayed slightly at its tail.

"Your friends are calling you." You told your new friend, who turned back to face you. He
nodded, taking a step towards the group before pausing, looking at the child in your arms.

"Can he play too?"

Reflexively, you held the child a little tighter, not meeting his upturned eyes on you. The
thought of being left completely alone while Din was gone, of being left in a covert that
didn't particularly favor your presence unsettled you.

"No, I don't think so." You answered shyly, and Umos' shoulders fell a little in dejection
before you added: "Maybe next time."

That seemed to be enough for the boy, who straightened a little and nodded at you before
joining his friends once more.

You watched them as the group trotted around a corner and out of sight, feeling a little pang
of jealousy in your chest. Not for the first time you wished you had what they did as a child.
Friends, protectors, a place to sleep in the knowledge that the older members of your clan
would fight until their last breath to keep you safe. The idea brought forth a familiar ache
inside you, your smile still present but eyes softening with a grief that only orphans such as
yourself knew.

The child in your arms made a small babbling sound, trying to begin with the first syllable of
your name. You looked down at him, noticing one had trying to reach up and touch your face.
With a sigh, you adjusted him so he could see you better.

"Just you and me, little guy. I think I have an idea how to spend our time, though."

-o-o-o-o-o-

"Kriff."

You watched as the bolt from your blaster dinged off a piece of scrap metal just to the left of
your set target, bouncing off and leaving a smoking scorch mark on the alleyway wall behind
it.



Your next shot hit roughly in the same place, even as you tried to correct your aim. The sharp
pew of the blaster echoed off the walls of the alleyway a short distance away from the covert.
Within the relative quiet of the abandoned district, each sound seemed loud enough to rattle
the ground under your feet. Had you not warned the guards outside the entrance to the
enclave ahead of time of your practice, you were sure that you would have long since been
surrounded by a squad of helmeted warriors.

After being left to your own devices in the covert, you had decided to spend your time the
best way you knew how- by making yourself useful. Having been cooped up on the
Razorcrest for a week prior to your arrival, you couldn’t miss the opportunity to improve
your blaster skills. Even though you and the child would remain within the safety of the
enclave as Din and Paz marched off to war, you refused to allow yourself to become
complacent. You had become spoiled, in some ways, by not constantly being on watch while
Din was away. Relying on Din and the covert to protect you felt wrong, in some ways. He
had spent so much time protecting you that it was only fair you attempt to return the favor.

Secretly you harbored the hope that you would be able to be by his side whenever the battle
did come, able to watch his back and ensure he arrived back to the child safely. Yet you
couldn’t do that at your current skill level, at least not yet. Doing so would take many more
hours of practice, hence your current standing in a trashed alleyway holding the blaster Din
had lent you.

Your next shot was merely an inch off its mark, to which you smiled with a subtle
satisfaction.

The kid was seated off to one side, safe in his carrier behind you and away from the line of
fire. As you practiced your blaster skills he had occupied himself with the metal ball from the
Razorcrest's controls, turning it over in his tiny hands and lifting it so that it reflected what
little light that managed to filter down from the upper levels.

Since your exit out onto the streets the little fellow had become increasingly quiet, even
somewhat withdrawn. You could hardly blame him, feeling the ever-creeping wariness of
being within the deep confines of Coruscant. The air seemed a little staler outside the
Mandalorian enclave, the temperature a touch cooler. Your senses prickled with alertness, and
more than once you had caught yourself looking over your shoulder for ghosts that weren't
there.

You chalked it up to the fact that you were still in gang territory despite your relative
proximity to the Covert. After all, there had been a raid not even a week prior, one that had
injured several warriors and taken the life of a foundling. You had made sure to not go so far
that any Mandalorians on patrol wouldn't hear your scream for help.

Even so, there was a part of you that couldn't attribute the dark, luring sensation in your
stomach to that of the Black Sun or any other potential enemies nearby. The full-body shiver
that had wracked you more than once seemed to originate not from the streets, but the planet
itself. You had felt it as soon as you had exited into orbit above Coruscant. A sinister shadow
had drawn across your senses the moment you had seen the planet, felt it weigh heavy against
your mind. No doubt the child could sense it as well.



Coruscant smelled like death.

There was no other way to describe it. You could never forget the smell even if you tried, the
acrid, cold scent of iron and rot that permeated every living fiber of your being. You couldn't
recall when exactly you had been able to recognize it, having been able to recognize the scent
since long ago. Death was not uncommon on Kaddak, but even there it was a passing event
as opposed to the constant shroud that had draped itself over the ecumenopolis. If you
paused, stopped to let yourself sink into the low hum of the planet you felt as if you'd be
sucked all the way down into the core itself, burned alive at the molten fireworks beneath the
surface.

Perhaps it was the lingering traces of the Empire that had once held the planet, a regime
soaked so deeply in blood that it followed the survivors and exiles years into the future. Yet
the ache in your chest spoke of something deeper, something tat resounded like a clarion
inside your soul.

The memories long since passed of your childhood on Kaddak were easily summoned by the
violent nature of the Coruscanti streets. It didn’t take much notice of your surroundings for
you to recall the cold dark nights alone in a part of the outer-rim city you thought was safe,
sleeping with one eye open for those who might wish you harm. The presence of the gangs
made it even more so, and you could remember the predatory smiles, the deceiving offers of
protection and shelter from other rival syndicates. You had been lucky, able to complete your
assigned errands for the gang leaders and avoid potential consequences until your adulthood.
Yet even then you had been caught in a snare, with a bloodthirsty Trandoshan darkening the
doorway of your workshop.

Whatever it was that left your senses tingling with danger, it left a shiver in your skin and a
tremble in your hands that you couldn't shake. As you raised your blaster once more the
shake of your grip caused your aim to tilt slightly. You managed to correct yourself, and with
your next shot you hit the target dead on.

"HA!" You exclaimed triumphantly, punching one hand into the air in celebration. To your
small, green companion you said "Did you see that bud? Not bad, right?"

You turned to the carrier, only to find it conspicuously empty. The soft interior with its
blanket met your gaze devoid of its occupant.

Brow wrinkling in confusion, you turned further to scan for the toddler.

"Kid?"

Yet the alleyway was empty, and your call was met only by the soft rustle of trash debris in
the occasional undercity breeze. Even as you called there was no gurgle, no 'Patoo' in
response to your voice.

The shroud of darkness that remained omnipresent on Coruscant lent itself to you, allowing
panic to mount rapidly inside your chest at the disappearance of the infant. Forgetting the
bassinet behind, you holstered the blaster at your side and paced quickly to the alleyway



entrance. Even then there was no sign of the child. You called out once more, voice rising and
bordering on shrill.

“Hey, kid, where are you?”

Silence.

"It's okay." You spoke to yourself quietly in an attempt at reassurance. "He probably just
started back towards the compound."

Yet your voice trembled as you said the words, and as you trotted back in the direction of the
Covert there were no signs of the small green toddler. You passed by several alleyways and
sheltered doorways, none of which revealed the toddler to you. By the time you reached the
small entrance leading towards the tunnel guarded by two Mandalorians, you felt your lungs
quickly constrict for air. The two warriors at the entrance regarded you as you trotted up,
exchanging a small glance at the panic written clearly across your face.

"Th-The kid." You asked breathlessly, hands shaking. "Have you seen him?"

Again, the two glanced at each other, returning your question with silent shakes of dissent.

You felt the blood drain from your face, vision becoming hazy as panic began to take hold of
you. Without another word you spun, launching back in the direction from where you came
even as one of the warriors called after you. You ignored them, legs pumping under you as
you raced to try and find the child.

The words from Paz haunted you as you ran, boots hitting the durasteel sidewalks of the
street, breath quickly devolving into hyperventilation.

"He's dead. They killed him."

A foundling, one much older than the youngster in your care, had been shot dead in this place
not even a moon ago. Now the tiny helpless toddler you had been charged with protecting
had vanished right under your nose and into some of the most dangerous streets in the known
galaxy. The word 'terror' could not begin to describe the horrific sinking feeling that
threatened to swallow you whole if you didn't locate the child.

You raised your voice to call for him, listening to it echo off the empty walls of the
abandoned district. The sound of traffic far above the overhead walkways and metal exteriors
of the buildings was deafened by the rapid stutter of your heartbeat in your chest. Your eyes
were wild, terrified as the minutes ticked by with no response, no sign, no indication of the
child that had vanished.

Minutes stretched on as you expanded your search range, trotting down a set of stairs further
away from the covert territory. Several residents noticed your frantic calls, quickly easing
themselves into the shadows as you passed and shielding themselves away from your notice.

If you had been paying attention to your surroundings you would have noticed the streets
growing less familiar, the shadows at the edge of your vision drawing closer. Under your



increasingly loud yells for the child perhaps you would have heard the low voices speaking,
the rustle of debris as you bolted past an open alleyway. You were being followed, but the
panic of having lost the toddler in your care dulled your senses to the keen eyes watching you
from the shadows.

Yet you didn't take note. You couldn't think past the all-consuming dread of the child's
absence in the city of trillions, so large that there was a possibility you might never see him
again. Imaginary scenarios of what could have happened to him drowned out any other
rational thought. Din’s mentions of the monsters that lurked far beneath the undercity and
ventured upwards in search of prey haunted you, with the thought of the child caught in the
claws of a horrific creature.

Finally, out of breath, you trotted to a halt under the sharp illumination of a cracked
streetlamp. Doubled over, your chest desperately heaved for air. Throat burning, you braced
your hands on your knees as you tried to catch your breath. Your pounding heartbeat covered
the electric crackle of the flickering light above you, white noise to your hysteria.

Din would be horrified to learn what had happened, probably more so than yourself. The
mental image of his shoulders stiffening, of him whipping around to face you when you
confessed what had happened haunted you. It was your duty to take care of the child, and you
had failed. Even as guilt drained into your stomach you could only imagine the horrific
feeling of Din’s frustration and disappointment.

"This yours?"

You whipped around at the voice, pupils blown wide and body tensing on instinct. You could
feel your muscles coil before your mind fully caught up to the sight before you, your sixth
sense immediately sensing the danger present. Still, nothing could have prepared you for the
sight of a large figure raising an object up for you to see.

As the Pantoran stepped into the sharp, artificial glow of the streetlight you were finally able
to see what he held in his knuckled grasp.

The child.

Your lips parted in a silent gasp, breath sucked sharply into your chest at the sight of the
toddler being held by the back of his shirt, ears drooped fearfully as he looked up at you with
stricken brown eyes.

Yet it wasn't the sight of the child held captive in the alien's grasp that made your heart stutter
in your chest. No, it was the distinct marking on the blue skin of the Pantoran's bicep on the
arm he held aloft, the tattoo unmistakable.

The signet of the Black Sun.

Whatever fear you felt as the child being held captive doubled tenfold upon recognizing the
symbol. Though the Black Sun wasn't predominant on Kaddak, you didn't live long in the
Outer-Rim without being able to distinguish syndicate symbols from each other. The only
time you had ever seen that symbol was painted on the burning wreckage of a building,



graffitied and smeared with the blood of whoever there had tried to cross the gang. You could
still smell the stench of death, almost as if it originated from the faded tattoo itself.

The terror of your face must have shown, because the Pantoran grinned. He lifted the child a
little higher, causing the toddler to whine in distress.

"Wait." You spoke, voice suddenly hoarse with fear. "Don't hurt him- we didn't mean to
wander in, we-we can just go, please-" You hated how fearful you sounded, how your voice
cracked as you spoke. If it were just you, you wouldn't have let the horror seep into your
tone, would let your hands shake as you beckoned him to please, please don't hurt him-

The Pantoran didn't even move, didn't bother to reply to your stuttering words. Instead, his
eyes flicked past you, giving a small nod to something you didn't see.

You felt the hairs on the back of your neck raise automatically, and you spun to face whatever
it was behind you.

You only caught a glimpse of a dark shadow before something came down with force on your
head, knocking you to the ground with a sickening thud.

Before you could cry out in pain darkness flooded your senses, and your body collapsed
under the pressure of unconsciousness.

Chapter 23: Part Twenty-three: The Duel
Chapter Summary

"The covert." Din growled against Paz’s ear, the sound dangerous with pure intent.
"Have you and the other warriors. Those two-" and he grunted as Paz again tried to free
himself, to no avail. "Only have me."

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

The air on the Razorcrest was stale. Din could taste it even from under his helmet.

It was in the way Paz studied him from behind his back as Din handled the pre-flight check,
the older Mandalorian’s eyes boring into the back of his helmet. Din knew the warrior had
questions, questions about where Din had been, about who you were, about the nature of the
relationship between you and him. He was considering his words carefully, weighing each
question in his mind as Din made his way through his check, pointedly ignoring the way
Paz’s gaze lingered on him.

The walk back to the Razorcrest hadn't been a particularly long trek. Yet to reach the craft
Din and Paz were forced to cross into a busier part of the sector, where the eyes of bar
visitors and idling passerby lingered on the pair's heavy beskar cuirasses. Din was acutely
aware that in the crowd of wandering residents and drunken stragglers that an eye for the
Black Sun was keeping the gang appraised of the two men’s whereabouts. The idea made
Din's jaw set a little harder, his hand drifting closer to his holster the entire journey towards
the ship docks.

He could tell Paz felt it as well, the increased scrutiny weighing heavily on his back. The
presence of an experienced warrior at his side didn't avail Din of the shadow of anxiety cast
across his senses. If anything, Din felt that Paz keeping pace with him made the two of them
even more of a target to any gang members who might attempt to ambush them. The beskar
that composed their armor was priceless, and Din didn’t miss the murmurs of passerby
muttering over how much the cuirass would fetch for a fair price.

“When you walk the path of The Mandalore, you are both hunter and prey.” The Armorer
had said. Din hadn’t fully understood her words at the time. Now, as he and Paz had walked
through enemy territory with targets on the back of their helmets, he finally comprehended
her meaning.

Din counted himself lucky that he was fully rested enough to take on any potential
opponents, the result of an exceptionally long and comfortable night’s sleep. Truly, he didn’t
think he had slept that well since Sorgan. There, he had rested peacefully with the knowledge



that even if he was resting, Cara was keeping watch over the village perimeter. He almost
wished he were back in bed, held aloft by the cradle of a gentle morning complete with your
soft, slumbering figure still in his arms, his helmet tucked up against your hair.

When was the last time he had felt so relaxed? So open and vulnerable? What was it about
you that disarmed him so gently and yet with such heart stammering force?

When you had appeared to him the night prior, with your sleeping clothes askew and hair
mussed from sleep, he didn’t originally understand your presence. Yet the anxiety, the
uncertainty in your gaze, followed by your eyes going wide upon realizing Din’s own state of
undress had done things to him that Din still couldn’t fully comprehend. He hadn’t missed the
way your eyes had roved over him, taking in the skin you never saw and the outline of
muscle there. A dark part of Din’s mind had wandered back to the exposed form he had seen
on Rishi, with your naked shoulders and hair curling at the nape of your bare neck. That same
thought briefly wondered what your exposed form looked like under the dim light of his
rooms, skin lit only by the warm glow of the lantern at his bedside. For the briefest of
moments Din let his mind overtake him, hoping to the stars that perhaps you were there for
exactly that purpose.

So, when you had stammered an excuse, trying to escape, Din didn’t let you. Yet at the same
time when you had spoken with a trembling voice and downcast eyes, he had listened. Din
didn’t question you over your ‘nightmare’ that you had spoken of. Instead, he shortly found
himself cradling your back to his torso, trying to control his breathing so you didn’t hear the
shortness of breath inside his chest. He took comfort in just how soft you were against his
arms, holding himself back from letting his hands wander and hoping you wouldn’t hear the
resounding drum of his heartbeat against his ribs.

He didn’t know if this was wrong or not, to hold you in his arms like that and feel the weight
of you against his side. The line between you two had become far too blurred, washed away
by the gentle tide of your circling orbits, complete with lingering glances and lasting touches.
The gravitational pull between you had set you both on a crash course, bound for an
inevitable shattering of the walls you both had constructed. If Din admitted the truth to
himself, it would be that he did want this, did want the comfort of your presence beside him.
He wanted the hold you, to allow himself to breathe in your scent, listen to the soft sounds
you made in your sleep and let your voice be the final thing he heard before the velvet
comfort of night closed the curtain over his eyes.

He wanted you. He did. He knew that now. Yet to allow himself that much…he wasn’t sure if
he could do that yet.

And as if sensing the object of his thoughts, Paz finally spoke from the threshold of the
cockpit doorway.

"Your partner. Tell me about her."

Din felt his shoulders hike up an inch, a result of the guardedness that came with discussing
the unspoken tension between him and you. Ultimately Din forced himself to not indicate any
discomfort to the larger Mandalorian. Still, he couldn't deny the spike of self-aware heat that
rose to his face, glad that Paz couldn't see his reddened cheeks under his helmet.



"What about her?" Din replied, careful to keep his voice even. Yet Paz didn't reply, remaining
silent in hopes that Din would continue.

When it became clear Paz wouldn't clarify his question, Din sighed.

"She's...a friend." He confessed at last, voice softening in the way that it did whenever he
spoke to you. "Someone I've met who...has earned her keep many times over."

Paz hummed in thought, the sound low in his chest.

"How did you two meet, exactly?"

Din paused, one hand hovering above the controls before pushing the button for the engine
flaps. The memory of your face, smeared with the red dirt of Kaddak and eyes wide as the
moons above Tatooine, looking up at him after he had uncovered your hiding place in the
cargo hold, appeared to him instantly. You had looked terrified beyond all measure, voice
cracking as you desperately tried to bargain for your safety. The thought of such fear from
you now made an uncomfortable weight settle in Din's stomach.

"I...met her on a waystation in the Outer Rim." Din lied, the idea of admitting to Paz that he
had almost killed you upon your original meeting making the bashful blush on his face
deepen with shame. "She protected the child from bounty hunters."

Paz huffed behind him, as if Din's answer was somehow amusing.

"She sounds brave." He commented, watching as Din deftly piloted the Razorcrest down into
a narrow passageway that led to the lower levels. “All by herself?”

Din nodded to confirm Paz’s question. "Cuyan is...fearless." He replied, voice dipping into a
low tone. His words were careful, halting as he tried to measure them before admitting too
much to his Vod. "She-"

" 'Cuyan?' " Paz asked incredulously, and there was laughter in his voice. "As in 'survivor'?
That's hardly romantic, Djarin."

Din spluttered under his helmet, caught entirely off guard by Paz's comment. Forgetting the
controls for a moment, he spun in his chair to face the other warrior. He was grateful Paz
couldn’t see his face, with his widened eyes and deep-set flush across his cheeks.

"That's- No, I-" He tried, only for Paz to cut him off once more.

Paz barked a laugh, the sound rich and deep in his chest.

"Don't lie, Vod.” He interjected gleefully, as if he were taking pleasure in Din’s awkward
discomfort. “It's clear as daylight that you have feelings for her. Oritsir, I can see that she
feels the same just by the way she looks at you." Din could almost see the knowing smirk on
Paz's lips, and Din couldn’t understand how he found the situation so karking funny.

Din didn't answer, staring at Paz for a moment longer before spinning back around towards
the controls. His refusal to address Paz only made the other warrior chuckle again.



"I assume that she and you aren't officially courting yet, then?"

Din groaned, letting his helmet thunk on the headrest of his chair and desperately wishing
Paz would just drop the subject already. "No." He replied definitively. "She and I are
not...'courting'."

Paz nodded, adjusting so he was leaning on the door with his arms crossed.

"Perhaps that's for the best then." He supplied with a sigh, adjusting so that he balanced more
easily as the ship banked left. "I doubt she'd be keen on our traditions or be willing to swear
by the Resol'nare. "

Din scowled, stopping just short of sending Paz a displeased look from beneath his helmet.
Yet even if he didn't want to admit it, Paz was right. You didn’t know the tenants of his
culture, didn’t understand the traditions and customs that came with it. You weren't
Mandalorian.

All Din's life he had been raised expecting that if he did ever settle down, it would be with a
member of the covert, someone who already knew The Way. Whoever his partner was, it
would be someone who was a warrior like himself, who could train whatever children or
foundlings Din found within his care according to the tenants of Mandalorian culture; To
wear the bes'kar, to know the language of Mando'a, to defend oneself and their family, to
raise warriors, contribute to the clan, and to rally to their Mand'alor when called upon.

And yet...

Truly, in some ways you had already fulfilled those tenants. You had proven on more than
one occasion your willingness to claw your way to survival, mirroring the warrior spirit of
Mandalorian culture. Your determination in protecting the child and yourself was one of the
qualities Din truly respected in you. Plus, you had sought to prove yourself in your skills,
fixing the ship, attempting to prepare food, ensuring that the child was taken care of, and
going so far as to save Din's life back on Rishi. Though you didn't wear the armor, nor did
you speak the language, in some ways your current willingness to serve and protect did not
venture far from the core ideas of the Resol’nare.

Before he could stop himself, Din let his mind stray farther. It was true that you didn’t swear
by the creed, but maybe that might change, especially considering how it aligned closely to
your own ideals. Perhaps, after you and the child were safe from the Empire, and the covert
had settled itself once more, and if you decided to stay with Din, then maybe...

Din shook his head, blinking away the thought. It was much too soon to think about that.
Besides, he still had the bounties hanging over your and the child's head to concern himself
with. Not to mention that there was a war to fight to ensure to safety of the covert.

Even so, your words of finding yourself on a peaceful planet far away from the conflicts of
the galaxy beckoned to him like a soft summer breeze. If Din still found himself by your side
when that happened, then...



"You shouldn't underestimate her." Din forced himself at last in response to Paz. "She's far
more capable than you know."

Paz remained silent, and if Din turned he would have seen the way the larger Mando tilted his
helmet at him in curiosity. If Paz had a reply he didn't speak it, as if weighing Din's words
silently in his thoughts. Yet Din knew that his words had struck an interest in Paz, one that he
filed away for later study.

Soon enough Din could see the landing platform adjacent to the warehouse below,
maneuvering the ship deftly out of traffic and downwards at an angle. The landing gear
deployed with a soft hiss, the ship lurching in a familiar thunk as it came to rest on the
landing dock.

Once the ship was landed, Din stood and made his way towards the ladder. However, Paz's
larger figure remained in the doorway, thick arms crossed, and visor tilted at Din.

Din expected him to wait a moment and then move, posturing for the sake of some sort of
entitled control. Yet when Paz spoke Din felt an irritated itch pass over his skin.

“Be careful not to get too distracted, Vod.” Paz warned, voice lowering as if others might be
listening. “The clan comes first.”

Din leveled his stare hard at the other warrior, taking a moment to let the gaze sink in before
shouldering past Paz and making his way down the ladder into the hold. Paz followed behind
him, footsteps heavy on the floor above.

No sooner had Din opened the ramp and stepped out onto the loading dock did he spot the
small crowd waiting just beyond the loading bay doors. It seemed to be comprised mostly of
children coming to look at the spaceship that had landed next to their temporary home,
peering out from behind the safety of the steel shutters with several quiet murmurs and
curious stares.

It was at that moment that one of the younger warriors pushed past the gaggle of children,
barking at them in Mando'a to get back inside and away from the entrance. The children
scattered, leaving behind their older counterpart as he jogged forward to meet Din and Paz
halfway across the platform.

"Vizsla." He spoke breathlessly in reference to the older Mando. "We have a problem."

Din stiffened automatically, eyes still scanning beyond the loading dock entryway for your
familiar figure. When you didn't appear, he turned his attention back to the younger
Mandalorian at hand.

"What's happened?" Paz demanded, tone easily shifting into that of a soldier, a commander.

"The woman-" The younger warrior paused, nodding to Din. "Your partner. She-"

He didn't get to finish. In a heartbeat Din had closed the distance between him and the other
warrior, grabbing his by the lip of his helmet to force his eyes upwards.



Din could feel his heart rate spike, hands tightening into fists. His blood rushed hot in his
veins, muscles coiling in readiness. Staring own at the younger soldier Din's eyes darkened
under his helmet upon realizing that something was terribly, terribly wrong. Instinctively he
could feel his spine straighten, fists clench in readiness.

"Where is she?" He growled, feeling the reverberation of the words deep in his throat. Like a
Loth-wolf his lips drew back, teeth bared in a predator's snarl as he jerked the younger
warrior's helmet a little higher.

The teenager grasped a gloved hand onto Din's bracer, trying to free himself. Din could feel
his stammering heartbeat under his helmet, thrumming against his fist.

"She-she's gone!" He choked out. "We tried to find her, but she was so fast! she-"

"Slow down." Paz demanded of the boy, one hand also descending heavily on Din's bracer.
"Start from the beginning."

Turning to Din, Paz tightened his hand on the bracer under his grip, forcing Din to loosen his
hold on the younger soldier. Din could feel the silent warning ripple between them, promising
violence if Din did not let the boy go.

Din forced himself to release the younger Mandalorian, who at once tumble several steps
backwards and away from the furious Mando. After a small splutter and a jerk to resettle his
helmet, he spoke again. His rush to explain had him tripping over his words, a nervous tick as
a result of intimidation by his older counterpart.

"Your partner, she ventured just outside the covert. She said something about target practice.
When she came back she was beside herself, babbling about how she couldn't find the child.
She ran off again before we could stop her."

"And you let her go alone?" Din snarled. "Into Black Sun territory? By herself?"

The warrior took another step back, startled by the pure menace in Din's tone. Instinctively,
he let one hand drift towards his sheathed vibroblade, likely anticipating a brawl.

"We thought she would be back!" He answered, trying to keep his tone even despite his voice
cracking. "She didn't go far, we could hear her practicing, so we figured-"

Din took a step forward, blood spiking with fury. Before he could make another move Paz
had intercepted him, standing halfway between Din and the younger warrior. Din could see
the rigid outlines of Paz's shoulders under his armor, held taut in preparation of Din trying to
force his way forward. This close Din could see his reflection in Paz's visor as the older
warrior leveled a hard, warning glare at him.

Though he kept his eyes trained on Din, Paz directed his voice to the Mandalorian behind
him.

"Have we found a trail? Do you know where she could have gone?"

Again, the younger warrior faltered, visor jerking to Din's wrathful stare.



"We think the Black Sun may have taken her, along with the child."

The sound around Din seemed to suck into silence, leaving only the stuttering staccato of his
heartbeat behind. If he didn't know better Din would have assumed he had been shot, the
empty hollow pain in his chest stealing the breath from his lungs and making the ground drop
out from under him. Whatever fury had taken hold of him moments prior fled, leaving the icy
grip of fear in its place.

Even through that, the words he had spoken only that morning appeared back to him
unbidden.

"I'll...see you soon."

With it came the image of your shy, smiling face. With your hair still mussed from sleep,
nightshirt dipping slightly off your shoulder and cheeks flushed with a mixture of affectionate
warmth and embarrassment. Beside you the child looked at him with sleep bleary eyes, gaze
wide and trusting that his caretaker would return shortly. Din had felt his heart surge at the
sight, enough so to let the image imprint on his thoughts even as he and Paz made their way
to the training grounds. He had never imagined that such a sight could be the last time he
ever saw you both.

Din's shocked silence caused the air to still, the hum of air traffic above indiscernible from
his own thrumming heartbeat. Under his visor Din's lips had parted in a silent gape, eyes
wide and pupils blown in fear and disbelief.

Paz regarded Din for a moment as the bounty hunter struggled to process what he had just
heard. In the absence of Din's response, he nodded at the younger Mandalorian who had
preferred the message, and after a moment the teenager gratefully fled back into the confines
of the warehouse.

Din's thoughts tumbled ceaselessly, a mixture of shock, anger, and guilt colliding into a
hailstorm of fear that threatened to drown out all his other senses.

He should have never left your side.

The feeling of your form still cradled in the grip of his arms seemed a distant memory now.
He had wanted to stay there, within the soft embrace of a restful sleep breathing in your scent
and listening to the steady rise and fall of your chest. Now...

Din startled to, eyes blinking back into focus. He was moving before his mind fully caught
up, body instinctively stalking forward with deadly intent. He didn't make it a full step before
Paz's hand landed on his pauldron, the older warrior halting him mid-stride.

"Djarin." Paz spoke, his voice low in a firm warning. Din didn't stop, shoving Paz's hand off
his pauldron and continued to stalk forward towards the warehouse and further towards the
street entrance. Paz faded behind him, the graveled sigh in his throat tapering off as Din
quickly put distance between himself and his Vod.



The second he set foot into the warehouse, into the open area cleared for training and
sparring, Din saw the gaggle of children from before rush to cover, peeking out from behind
crates at the hunter on a blood quest. Din hardly noticed, intent on marching on a war path
towards the heart of Black Sun territory, to where you had likely been taken.

He'd kill them, Din thought. The scum who had dared try and take you and the child. He had
already planned on it, with the image of a foundling killed too soon by the blaster of an
enemy warring over meager territory rights.

But now...

Din didn't consider himself to be a violent man by any means. Efficient, deadly even, yes.
But unnecessarily violent? Taking pleasure in killing? He was not those things that some
other bounty hunters were or claimed to be. Yet the idea of the damage you and the child
could possibly suffer at the hands of the Black Sun made him deeply reconsider that moral.

He could feel his blood boiling, teeth bared under his helmet and eyes alight with fire at the
thought of you and the child taken from him. Taken, and by the same low life scum that had
taken the life of a foundling not a moon prior. He could feel the lightning in his veins crackle
deadly under the heat of his skin, fists clenched and steps heavy as he made his way to the
entrance of the covert.

The two Mandalorians on guard there parted easily, sensing the bloodlust bubbling like the
fires of Coruscant molten core under Din's palms. Din could feel their stares on him as he
passed, ignoring the way they stiffened upon seeing the predatory roll of his shoulders, the
way his hand never left his holster.

He was only steps beyond them when a voice called out from behind him.

"Djarin!"

Din ignored it, knowing the words Paz would speak before they left his lips. He knew it made
no strategic sense to march into enemy territory, not when he was facing down an entire
syndicate as opposed to a squad of stormtroopers. Paz wanted him here, defending the covert
and the other foundlings before racing off to rescue you. If Din put himself in Paz's shoes, he
couldn't blame him. Yet Din wouldn't let that stop him from marching headfirst into enemy
territory, Black Sun be damned.

"Djarin!" Paz repeated, and again Din didn't answer to the call. That was until Paz's voice
rose and cracked like a whip, his shout echoing and bouncing off the metal exteriors of the
alleyway.

"DJARIN!!"

This time, Paz’s shout came with a fierce grip onto Din’s shoulder, spinning him halfway
before Din tore himself from the grasp with a snarl. Yet instead of backing off Paz only tried
once more, reaching forward and then recoiling to block the strike Din hurled at him.



Within an instant the tense but allied camaraderie that had built between Din and Paz
vanished, leaving behind the sneering hostility and animosity that came with being rivals.

Paz drew his vibroblade with a growl to rival that of a Nexu, taking advantage of Din’s
sloppily thrown punch to sidestep him. Despite having an opening to do so, he didn’t slice
down Din’s shoulder, instead securing Din’s attacking arm between his elbow and side. The
motion threw Din off balance, allowing Paz to drag Din closer to him and seize the hunter by
the nape of his neck. He was still trying to rein him in like a misbehaving pup, a fact that
made the light in Din’s eyes flicker with rage.

Din felt his blood pressure spike, and with a grunt he threw his head forward, connecting the
beskar helmet with the crown of Paz’s own helm, causing Paz to loosen his grip enough for
Din to retreat with his arm. Paz took a small stumble backwards, rattled by the force of
Kov’nyn strike. In the time that it took him to shake his head clear of the ringing sound left by
the metal collision, Din had drawn his own vibroblade.

There was an audience growing now at the mouth of the tunnel underneath the Mythosaur
mantle. Comprised mainly of other warriors, Din could hear the hushed murmur of surprise
and interest at the unfolding duel. Between the legs of the adults several of the foundlings
watched curiously.

Din and Paz circled each other like opposing predators, with bright eyes, and bared teeth. The
hum of the vibroblade sang in a low tune within Din’s grasp, reaching out to harmonize with
the weapon across from it. Din knew how painful the slice of Paz’s blade could be, with
small scrapes and bruises all over from his previous spars with the warrior. Yet this wasn’t a
duel to kill, it wasn’t even a duel to maim. This was about making a point in the way that
only warriors understood.

Din sank low into his stance, recounting the number of spars he had dueled with Paz before.
Though Paz had the advantage of height, weight, and strength, Din that the advantage of
being faster, nimbler on his feet. His reaction time was quicker compared to the heavy
infantry Mando, his lighter stature allowing him to move with increased speed and agility.
Which meant that this brawl became less one of strength, and one of endurance, with Din
wearing down his opponent and waiting for the perfect moment to strike.

"Vod." Paz spoke again from across the space between them. His voice was low, but not
threatening. Instead, it was a request, a firm plea for Din to reconsider. "Don't do this."

Din didn’t answer, instead feinting left and jabbing forward with his right hand, swinging a
broad strike across Paz’s chest plate that left sparks in its wake. He didn’t expect Paz to take
advantage of the opening, his gloved hand reaching out and grabbing Din by his belt. Din
managed to keep his footing as the stronger warrior dragged him forward into grappling
range, landing a precise blow on the inside of Paz’s elbow that broke his hold.

Yet even then he wasn’t free, as Paz struggled to keep Din in close range an overwhelm him
with his superior strength. He blocked the next swing of Din’s blade with the inside of his
bracer, the weapon singing loudly as it vibrated against the beskar. With his other hand Paz
drew up his own blade towards Din’s chest plate, only for Din to catch him by the wrist. They
remained locked, each trying to deflect and attack simultaneously. A ripple ran through the



witnessing crowd, some warriors bending helmets to speak in low voices as they observed
the altercation.

"We need you here, defending the covert and the other foundlings.” Paz grunted, voice tight
with concentration and effort. “You're itching to get yourself killed, marching off to war by
yourself.”

"I won't leave them." Din snapped back, eyes flashing dangerously. Sweat was now beading
on his forehead, skin flushed with the adrenaline that came with anger. "I swore to protect
them."

In an attempt at surprise, Din dropped the blade in his hand, letting the sound of it clattering
against the pavement distract Paz momentarily. Then, using Paz’s own momentum, Din let
the warrior lurch forward. Grabbing Paz’s helmet, Din brought it down on his knee. He
expected the warrior to reel backwards, teetering and allowing Din to take down to the
ground. Yet Paz seemed to think ahead, and in a mere heartbeat Din found the world spin,
ending with himself with his stomach on the ground. Paz’s weight settled on him pinning him
down and keeping him from rising.

"You swore first to the covert." Paz's barked next to his ear, and Din swore he saw red at the
outrage of Paz’s words and at being subdued. "Would you really choose them over your own
clan? Again?"

"I said those two are under my protection." Din snarled, twisting so he managed to get at least
one hand free from Paz’s pin on him, the other still yanked behind his back. "I swore to
protect the child on Nevarro, then to protect Cuyan, my partner after she had saved the child's
life. I will not abandon them."

Paz grunted as Din thrashed, not noticing the creep of Din’s hand outwards. Din disguised it
as trying to use his free arm to push himself upwards in an attempt to throw Paz off, to no
avail. Yet Paz didn’t let up despite having Din pressed against the pavement, forcing him to
listen as he continued.

"The covert, your aliit, is your priority." He growled, the sound deep in his chest. When Din
let loose a grunt, trying desperately to free his pinned arm, Paz’s grip tightened painfully in a
warning. "Trust me when I say there will be time to find your friend. When we attack the
Black Sun, then you can look for her, but right now we need you here."

There.

Paz noticed Din’s fingers grasping the handle of his dropped blade a moment too late,
tumbling off Din in attempt to avoid the backwards stab aimed directly at his hip. The second
Paz’s weight left his body Din shot to his feet, using his momentum to kick Paz square in the
chest as he was still rising. The strike forced Paz to momentarily lose him balance, one knee
folding. A hand reached for his own dropped vibroblade, only to have Din kick it away. Din
surged forward, not allowing Paz even a moment to recover.

Rather than kick him again and risk Paz seizing his leg, Din skidded to Paz’s level on the
ground. With speed greater than the heavy infantry Mando, Din managed to wrap one arm



around Paz’s neck, hauling him to the side and letting his other hand press the vibroblade into
the junction under his helmet between his chin and throat. The other Mando managed to
wedge a hand between Din’s bracer and his neck, keeping Din from choking him but pinning
his hand in the process. Paz attempted to jerk Din off, only for Din to reach and secure Paz’s
remaining free arm under his calf.

"The covert." Din growled against Paz’s ear, the sound dangerous with pure intent. "Have
you and the other warriors. Those two-" and he grunted as Paz again tried to free himself, to
no avail. "Only have me."

Paz paused, and Din for a moment thought that the warrior was thinking, considering another
way out of Din’s hold. What came next, however, wasn’t another surge of effort to free
himself. Instead, Paz let out a grunt before tapping Din’s calf twice in the signal of surrender.

Din was hesitant, but after a moment let loose Paz from his hold. The warrior slackened
under him, both Mandalorians breathing heavy from the brawl. The onlooking crowd
murmured, some of its members dispersing now that the struggle was over. Din and Paz both
took a moment to collect themselves, heart beats evening out and air collecting once more in
their chests.

It was Paz who stood first, pushing up from his elbows and towering over Din’s form still on
the ground. Din could still see the tension in his shoulders, the sting of being bested smarting
against his skin. Yet even so he turned, offering his Vod a hand and hauling him upwards
when Din accepted.

They stood apart from each other, chests still heaving and eyes flashing despite the brawl
having ended.

Now mostly alone, Din regarded Paz with a hard stare. He half expected Paz to deny him
leave to go pursue you even after he had bested the other warrior, not that Din truly needed it.
He was going whether Paz would allow him or not. He wouldn’t abandon you.

Paz seemed to sense this, as if nothing he did or said would dissuade Din from his current
course. He chose his next words carefully, speaking at last after a long-suffering sigh.

“I’m coming with you.”

Din blinked, despite not showing any other outward reaction. Out of all the things Paz could
have said, an offer to come with him was not something that Din had expected.

“The covert-“ Din started, only to be cut off.

“Can handle themselves for a single day.” Paz shot back, voice biting with irritation. “I’m not
the only capable warrior here by any means. However-“ and Paz stepped a touch closer,
causing Din to crane his head back briefly to make eye contact with the warrior’s visor. “We
do this quietly. I won’t have the whole of Black Sun raining hell down on us because you
decided get payback for what happened, you understand?”



Din stiffened, gaze darkening. His fists clenched at his side, the worn leather of his gloves
squeaking in his grip. Paz was trying to cower him, keep him in line as Din had allowed him
to do so for the years of their training together. Din hadn’t bothered to challenge him, more
focused on developing his skills than picking a fight with a member of a well-established
clan. That fact alone had only fueled Paz as a younger man, assuming his superiority over
Din due to their differences as a born Mandalorian and a mere foundling. Now, however…

“Fine.” Din bit back, voice low at the back of his throat and refusing to back down even an
inch. “But you don’t give me orders, Vizsla. You may be Mand’alor here, but I don’t answer
to you.”

Paz regarded him with a hard stare, helmet pressed close enough so that the metal nearly
scraped against Din’s. Yet Din refused to flinch, to back down. He had experienced enough of
Paz tossing his weight around, not when it concerned two beings that if, had they belonged to
any clan at all, belonged to Din’s. Had anyone still been watching, they might have assumed
that the two warriors were about to draw blades once more.

Paz was the first to step away, brushing past Din so he knocked shoulders with the smaller
warrior.

“Get what you need.” He shot sharply over his shoulder, stalking forward like the commander
that he was. “We’re leaving. Now.”
