Chapter 24: Part Twenty-four: The Escape
Chapter Summary

"And then what?" The wolf-man carrying you asked, grunting as he adjusted you
uncomfortably on his shoulder. You bit back a grunt, keeping quiet as you listened to
their current conversation.

"Then we attack, show them the full power of the Black Sun!"

Oh good, you realized belatedly. They were idiots.

If they thought they could attack an entire covert of Mandalorians and win, then they
had to be stupid. From what you could tell the covert had already fended them off once,
enough so that the gang was forced to retreat and recoup their numbers. Unless they had
some superior advantage, the Black Sun's attack would in all likelihood turn out to be
unsuccessful.

Although, you supposed that's where you and the kid came in.

Chapter Notes

General chapter warning for fear of heights, injury, and child endangerment. Please
practice self care.

See the end of the chapter for more notes

You could hear a voice.

Calling out to you over and over again, verging on tears as it echoed your name, the sound
echoed more familiar to you than any other word. It was quiet, pleading, as if afraid to speak.
Yet this wasn't the voice from your dreams, the one that cried out to you in horror and
desperation. This was softer, but no less afraid.

You knew this voice.

The first thing you noticed upon stirring towards wakefulness was the motion of your body,
rocking back and forth jerkily as air moved past your face. It didn't take long for you to
realize that you were moving, but any idea as to your destination remained absent. It was
almost comfortable, like being cradled. Yet your senses urged you to regain awareness,
combined with the desperate tone of the voice calling your name.



Your eyes fluttered open, vision beginning to clear from unconsciousness. Yet as it did a pain
drew low across the back of your head, making you stifle a groan. A sharp ache blossomed at
the base of your skull, crawling up and over your temples like a crown of thorns digging into
your muscles.

It took you more than a moment to realize what had taken you out in the first place, as well as
to try and figure out exactly where you were. Your thoughts were clouded by the haze of pain
across your skull, and even as you tried to clear them the echoing sound of your name
remained present.

"I'm awake, stop." You thought back, surprised to find that the constant drum of your name
ceased almost instantly. In its place came a small whimper, a sound of fear and uncertainty.

Yet in the silence that followed came a new sound, a voice that remained unfamiliar to you.

"Are you sure this is the same one you saw with the Mandalorian?"

The voice's owner was close enough that you could hear the deep timbre in their chest as they
spoke, voice several octaves too deep for that of a typical human. In fact, as the world slowly
began to make itself clear to you, you realized the person speaking was close enough to
touch.

"Yes, I'm sure. That's the third time you've asked me."

You were being carried, you realized. The conversation didn't dawn on you, not yet. Instead,
you tried to make sense of your surroundings, failing to reconcile the words spoken with why
exactly you were being transported, or to exactly where.

Slowly, you began to recall the events prior to your unconsciousness.

You had been searching for the kid after he had wandered off, with your heart in your throat
and eyes wild with fear. How far you yourself had ventured from the covert you did not
know. All you remembered was the streets getting darker, deeper into the underbelly of the
sector as your feet carried you to where you prayed the child was.

Then, held aloft by a tightly curled fist, you had found him.

You could recall the memory now, that of the fear and heart stopping panic upon seeing the
tattoo of the Black sun emblazoned across the Pantoran's bicep. You had watched his eyes
trace something behind your back, turning a moment too late to face whatever threat lay
beyond your sight.

Then, darkness.

The cold, tight grip of terror seized you upon realizing that you were captured. Though not by
the Imperial remnants, or by bounty hunters, the fact remained that you had been forcibly
detained by someone who you considered to be an enemy.

That same fear that you had felt back on Kaddak as you desperately fled the Trandoshan
hunter for the gang there now rose unabated in your chest. You couldn't hold it back, brain



conjuring impossible images of being held, tortured, made an example of, killed-

You didn't have Mando to aid you the way he had on Hypori and Rishi. Everything had
happened so fast, you weren't even sure if he was back yet from his errand with Paz. He
would notice your absence, but would it be too late before that happened?

"We should be able to get some information out of her once she wakes up."

The second voice spoke again, and as your senses cleared you began to realize there was
distance between you and them. You opened your eyes once more, peering through your
eyelashes to see the cracked pavement of Coruscant moving past you as you hung...upside
down? That would explain why your head hurt so badly, with all the blood rushing
downwards with the force of gravity. What was more, your hands had been bound in front of
you as you lay on your stomach across the alien's broad shoulder, leaving very little room for
you to try and wiggle free.

What surprised you more than that was staring down the large furry back of whoever had you
slung over their shoulder. As they walked you could see their feet far under you, complete
with hackled legs and claws longer than your fingers. You suppressed a shiver, trying not to
imagine one of the blade-sharp nails catching across your skin.

"Like what?" The voice of the one carrying you asked, and now you had enough to guess that
it was some type of wolf-man alien variety, complete with sharp fangs and a deep growl in
his chest.

"Like where exactly they're hiding, you moron." The other voice answered from somewhere
in front of your captor. You began to recognize the voice of the Pantoran who had seized the
child and distracted you, though the realization made your blood flush hot with anger.

Immediately your thoughts raced back to Din. There was no way he didn't notice your and
the child's absence. It could be he was on his way right now, tracking the sleemo who had
taken you both into custody. For a moment you couldn't help but pity the poor souls,
remembering the events that had occurred on Hypori.

The memory of the bloodbath that had taken place there made you shiver internally. You
didn't see Mando's face when he saw your poisoned, injured and collapsed form on the ramp
to the Razorcrest, but you didn't need to. The stance he had taken, the way he gripped his
blaster and had snarled that sound in Mando'a that you still didn't understand had spoken for
itself. Then the chaos that had followed...

You wanted to be far, far away with the kid when Din exacted his revenge.

"We know which sector they're in, but we still haven't been able to pin down where exactly
they are. She should be able to lead us to them." The Pantoran continued, and it seemed
neither he nor his companion carrying you seemed to realize that you had stirred awake.

His words, of course, led to your own questions. Where the hell were you being taken?
Obviously back to some type of safehouse or headquarters, but where exactly? It had to be
deep enough into the Black Sun territory that it had taken them some time to notice the



Mandalorian Covert setting up at the edge of their sector. If you could figure out exactly
where, then maybe, maybe you could begin to orient yourself and chart a path back towards
where you thought the warehouse was. You could at least try and shorten the distance
between yourself and Din, who would inevitably follow you both into the gangland. That
way he wouldn’t be forced to fight his way through the thick of Black Sun territory to get to
you and the child.

Yet the further you walked, the less sure of that plan you became. You had no idea how long
you had been walking, or if perhaps you had been walking the entire time at all. For all you
knew you could be on the other side of the planet at a different sector controlled by the
syndicate, far removed from the scarce number of familiar streets you had encountered.

"And then what?" The wolf-man carrying you asked, grunting as he adjusted you
uncomfortably on his shoulder. You bit back a grunt, keeping quiet as you listened to their
current conversation.

"Then we attack, show them the full power of the Black Sun!"

Oh good, you realized belatedly. They were idiots.

If they thought they could attack an entire covert of Mandalorians and win, then they had to
be stupid. From what you could tell the covert had already fended them off once, enough so
that the gang was forced to retreat and recoup their numbers. Unless they had some superior
advantage, the Black Sun's attack would in all likelihood turn out to be unsuccessful.

Although, you supposed that's where you and the kid came in.

"What if she doesn't want to tell us?" The one holding you still on his shoulder asked, and
you would have laughed at the odd tint of concern in his voice if it wasn't for the fact that he
had just knocked you out and kidnapped you.

"Well then we force it out of her!"

The thought made you grimace, trying not to imagine all the techniques that could be used on
you to extract information that you didn't possess. After all, the Mandalorians had been
suspicious of you as an outsider, revealing very little except the bare minimum needed to
safely navigate the boundaries of the covert's meager territory. You hadn't been present at the
war council with Paz discussing numbers, ammunition, defenses, and the like. You didn't
know exactly what information the Pantoran thought you might have, but you could almost
guarantee that you didn't have it.

"How do we force it out of her?" The wolfman asked, and this time when he spoke you could
hear what sounded like a Correlian drawl to his voice.

"Is there even a brain in that gigantic furry head of yours?" His smaller friend snapped back
irritably. "Like using the thing I'm holding, for example" and suddenly you heard the distinct
sound of the child letting out a sharp whine of distress.



It took everything in you to not kick and shout as you tried to free yourself. You were barely
able to not draw in a sharp gasp at the wave of concern that washed over you upon hearing
the child's voice. You tried desperately to breathe as if you were still unconscious, retaining
your element of surprise for whenever you did try to break free. Yet that didn't quell the panic
in your chest at the thought of nefarious gang members hurting the child to try and extract
information that you didn't have.

One thing became very clear, very quickly, however.

You couldn't wait for Din to come find you. You had to get out of here.

"What even is this weird green thing anyways?" The Pantoran asked, as if he was holding the
child up for a closer inspection. The kid snorted at him in what seemed like a mixture of
indignation and disgust at his captor.

"I don't know, a pet maybe?" The wolf-man carrying you answered. "I think he's kind of
cute."

"He?" The Pantoran questioned, voice tinting sardonically.

You could feel your captor shrug, the motion lifting you up on his shoulder. "Yeah, just seems
like a 'he' to me."

The child snorted again, making a small sound of discomfort which was promptly ignored by
both men.

You wished you could hold him, as if the mere gesture of cradling him in your arms could
make him safe. Even if you were still held captive, if you could at least hold him then you
could make sure no harm came to him. You felt the urge draw hollow in your chest, wishing
desperately that you could just see the child and make sure he was unharmed.

There would be time for that later. For now, you had to figure out a way to escape.

You couldn't see much from your position, limp atop the back of the furry beast under you. If
you opened your eyes you could see the ground pass under you, count the steps in between it
took for your handler to reach the seams in the sidewalk. The ever-present sounds of traffic
had faded to a low hum in the distance, signaling that you and the child had been taken
deeper, further into the underbelly of the sector and away from the shantytown where at least
some light filtered downwards from the planet's surface.

You were alone, it seemed. The streets were empty as far as you were aware, no other
footsteps present except for the two who held you and the child captive. Perhaps there were
those that loitered outside your vision, but in order to see them you would have to move and
alert the wolf-man carrying you that you were no longer unconscious.

If only you could get your hands free. As smart as the Pantoran seemed to think of himself,
he didn't bother to bind your hands behind your back. Not that you were complaining, truly. It
made your job of escaping much easier with your hands in front of you. Even if your hands
were bound you could still use them to some extent. The thought of reaching down and



ripping the fur from the alien's back occurred to you, though truly it might only make him
angry as opposed to actually injuring him.

You could try and kick your way free, trying to tumble off the creature's back. Though if the
Pantoran was still holding onto the child, he could easily threaten him and subdue you once
more. There had to be a way to distract him long enough to grab the child and make a break
for it. If you had your blaster you could do it, but you couldn't feel the weight of it in its
holster at your side, likely confiscated along with what little else you had on your person.

"Even if we can't get any info out of her, that Mando's sure as hell going to come looking for
her. We might be able to get something out of him if we use her as bait." The Pantoran mused
aloud, and you almost stiffened at the thought, muscles coiling in panic. You forced yourself
to breathe, to keep your body limp in the wolf-man's hold. Yet inside your heart drummed
louder in your chest, blood rushing in your ears and breath short in your lungs.

Trying to use you as bait to get Din's attention was a fool's errand. Din wouldn't stand to be
manipulated, especially by those who had already killed a foundling of his creed. The one
bounty hunter who had tried to extort him using you had failed, and now lay deep in the
jungle dirt on Rishi.

Still, the thought of Din being trapped after coming to your rescue had you panicking. If
somehow they lured Din into an ambush he couldn't handle, you would be helpless as he
fended off attackers, knowing that even if you tried to intervene, doing so would risk the
child you had sworn to protect.

You couldn't help the fearful despair that threatened to cloud out your other thoughts. You
had to escape. Not only for yourself and the child, but for Din as well. He was always coming
to your rescue, always defending you and trying to protect you. Now, with the single mistake
of turning your attention for a moment too long, you had potentially put him in terrible
danger. If the worse came to pass and Din was defeated, you didn't know how you could ever
live with yourself.

Then again, if your escape attempt failed, if somehow you managed to get free but not
retrieve the child in the process, you doubted you'd ever be able to face Din again. Your one
job of ensuring that the kid wasn't harmed would have failed, and whatever trust you had
sought to build with the Mandalorian would be broken.

Would he even bother to come looking for you if that happened?

A crease furrow drew across your brow, one you quickly brushed away. Thinking about such
a scenario didn't help your current situation. You only had one shot at this, and it had to go
exactly right, or you wouldn't have anything to worry about because you'd be dead, lying cold
against the durasteel walkway of the Coruscant underworld, and the child would be stolen.

No sooner had you begun to resolve yourself did your two captors suddenly halt. There was a
small shuffle and a grunt from the Pantoran, followed by another whine from the child. You
had all of a moment to blink in surprise before you were being hauled off the wolfman's
shoulder by his large furry arm.



Instinctively, you yelped in surprise, startling both yourself and the beast holding you. Yet
before he could speak you felt yourself unceremoniously dumped downwards, your butt
hitting the worn cushions of some type of air speeder. With your legs sprawled over the back
seat, hands bound in front of you, you turned your gaze upwards to look into the face of your
captor.

"What the?" The Pantoran asked, and you jerked your head to the side, watching as he paused
halfway into the front seat of the speeder. "How long were you awake?"

Your eyes darted wildly, breath frozen in your throat as your mind worked into overdrive. On
the seat that the gang member was climbing into you saw the kid, swaddled tightly in some
type of cloth to prevent him from squirming. For a heartbeat his eyes looked at you,
establishing some unspoken connection of understanding.

Then your eyes jerked past the wolfman, with his dingy brown fur and sharp canines to a spot
just over his massive shoulder. There your gaze widened, a hopeful light dancing off your
irises as you raised your hands to wave.

"Mando!" You yelped, voice as loud as you could make it. "Over here!"

"What-?!" The Lupine yelped, twisting to gaze over his shoulder at the rescuer who wasn't
there.

In the moment he was distracted you lunged for the controls, tumbling over the back of the
front seat. In doing so you accidentally kicked the Pantoran across the head with your boot,
inadvertently but successfully disorienting him. He grunted, faltering over the gap between
the mounting platform and the speeder.

In the time it took for the wolfman to turn back and realize his companion was now in danger
of falling, you wiggled your foot towards the pedals of the speeder, one hand shaking and
fumbling for the ignition. Sprawled sideways now in the front seat, your head whipped to
your right to see the Pantoran trying to tumble into the speeder, with his Shistavanen sidekick
now trying to aid him in getting back into the speeder to try and stop you. Locking eyes with
you for the briefest of moments, you could see the confused look on his face sharpen into a
predatory growl, making the blood drain from your expression with fear.

The sound of the engine sputtering to life was the most beautiful sound you had ever heard.
The speeder lifted up, the repulsors fully activating and keeping the hovercraft buoyant in the
air.

"Hang on, kid!" You yelled, voice echoing off the alleyway walls.

Just as the Pantoran tumbled head over heels into the passenger seat you shoved your foot
down on what you prayed was the accelerator. The craft jerked forward with a splutter,
shooting off just as the Shistavanen tried to dive for you on your other side. His extended
claws missed you by a hair breadth, then screeched as they failed to catch on the metal
exterior of the speeder. In an instant he was left behind, and you were trying desperately to
pilot the blasted thing as it hurtled down the street.



With the air rushing past your ears and whipping through your hair, you struggled to keep
your hands on the controls and straighten yourself in the seat at the same time. The street in
front of you was, gratefully, empty as the speeder zig zagged its way low across the metal
walkway. You couldn’t seem to keep it straight, correcting over correcting amateurly. No
wonder Din didn't let you anywhere near the controls of the Razorcrest. Although, you
thought irritably, maybe if he had you wouldn't be trying to steer a speeder with exactly zero
experience.

With the metal exteriors of apartments and building on your left, and the thin guardrail
holding you back against the vast expanse of emptiness leading further down into the
undercity on your right, keeping a straight course was vital to your survival. That wasn't
aided, of course, by the Pantoran struggling to straighten himself in the seat beside you, head
down on the floor and being jerked back and forth as a result of your sloppy steering; A fact
that wasn't aided by your hands still bound together in front of you. Your fingers managed to
grasp onto the steering wheel with a white-knuckle grip, each shake of your hands driving the
speeder a little closer to the ledge of the street.

Now straight in your seat, you braced a knee on the steering and raised your wrists to your
face, using your teeth to try and tug the bindings free from your hands. As you did, you
jerked your knee to the right, crashing into a pile of crates. You ducked just in time, avoiding
the supplies that crashed onto and over the zooming speeder. The Pantoran, who had just
begun to right himself, was struck low across the brow by a flying piece of debris, rendering
him limp across the passenger seat as he tried to cradle the oozing blue gash in his forehead.

With a mighty tug, you managed to get one of your hands free from the ropes, and now with
two hands available you took full control of the steering once more.

Movement ahead caught your eye, and as you swept your gaze forward you watched in
horror as a small group of bedraggled residents peered from an apartment building doorway,
some leaning into the street to see the cause of the commotion in your direction. Their
smaller forms grew in size rapidly, and in a panic you jerked the speeder to the right, feeling
your heart drop to your stomach as you careened out into the open air.

Neon lights decorated the boundaries of the massive expanse, glowing in the darkness that
came with night. The dizzying colors and flashing signs made it all the more difficult as you
tried to gain your bearings. A crisscrossing network of walkways intersected far under you,
and if you paused to look you could see the stares of passerby craning their heads to see the
out-of-control speeder far above them.

The sounds of traffic quickly became clear to you, even as you tried to contain a scream at
the terror of being so high up and suspended in midair with only the speeder's repulsors to
keep you there. Ahead and above you, a lane of traffic whooshed by with a number of
speeders. You tried to avoid it, but ultimately ran through, with several drivers honking at you
as you caused them to swerve around you in midair.

"Are you out of your karking mind?!" The Pantoran screamed, having finally righted himself
as he now leaned across the front seat and fumbled for the controls. "You're going to get all of
us killed, including yourself!"



You didn't answer, eyes wild and hair whipping across your face. Instead of replying you
reached for the child in between you and the gang member, grasping the edge of his swaddle
and tugging him into your lap with a brief heartbeat of relief.

That relief vanished as your former captor and now adversary snarled, lunging, and snaking
one hand around the steering. Yelling in surprise and fear, you struck wildly at him, one hand
catching the gash on his forehead and smearing your fist with blue blood.

The alien roared, reeling back but refusing to let go of the speeder steering. In doing so, he
jerked the speeder hard enough to make it tilt dangerously to the right. You screamed as you
began to slide in your seat, one arm reaching and holding desperately onto the edge of the
craft behind you, the other snatching the kid into your grip and keeping him from tumbling
off and into the void below. Your feet struggled to find purchase, keeping you from sliding
down the seat and towards the gaping expanse of air that lurked under you.

"Let go!" You screamed, voice shrill and at a note you'd never heard yourself shriek before.

Yet the Black Sun member didn't relent, even as the speeder tilted dangerously further into
capsizing. Instead, the Pantoran reached with his other hand down to his belt, and you
watched in blind horror as his hand drifted to the blaster at his side.

Your body moved before your mind could catch up. Now sideways in the front seat, you
brought your leg up to your chest, and with a great cry launched it forwards so that it struck
the Pantoran square in his chest. You weren't expecting it to have as much force as it did, as
your opponent was launched backwards.

As if in slow motion, you watched as his back hit the side of the seat, arching over the edge
as he recoiled from pain. You could see the realization, the terror pass over his eyes as the
speeder continued to tilt. His lips parted, as if to beg for help before you blinked, and he
tumbled over the side into the endless expanse below. His terrified scream echoed in your
ears, ringing in a high note as you gazed down in disbelief, holding the child tight to your
chest with one arm.

Chest heaving in a vain attempt to control your breath, you looked around wildly. The
speeder was out of control now, tilted far enough that you couldn't reach for the controls
without letting go and falling or releasing the terrified child in your arms.

Yet as if fate intervened, you could see a walkway ahead, the passersby on it pausing to look
curiously at the vessel before scattering with a series of screams. The engine of the speeder
was whining now, a horrible screeching sound as it tried and failed to balance itself. You
watched the walkway draw ever closer, seeing the details of advertisement boards and trash
piles come into place.

You were going to have to bail, you realized. Drop down onto the walkway as the speeder
passed over it. If you stayed in the speeder with no way to right it you would crash, and the
impact would jerk you and the child into falling endlessly towards the void-like bottom of the
sector. With the speed at which you were flying, you were going to have only one chance. If
you missed, you would end up plunging into the great chasm below you like your captor,
falling to a deadly and inevitable fate.



"Whatever gods are up there." You gasped, readying yourself as the walkway grew in size.
"For force's sake, don't let me miss."

The child in your arms hiccupped, and you felt the gasp of fear in your own chest holding
tightly to the air in your lungs. Holding your breath, you kept your eyes wide open as you
tensed, held the kid tight-

And let go.

For a moment you were suspended in air on all sides, hair and clothes fluttering as you
descended. With the neon lights of the city all around you, and the air rushing past you as you
seemed to take flight, you surrendered yourself. In that briefest of moments, holding the kid
suffocatingly tight to your chest and hearing the wind harmonize with the blood rushing in
your ears, you felt as if you were weightless, held aloft by an invisible tether in the cradle of
flashing light, sound and movement that composed the aria of Coruscant's anthem.

Then the ground came rushing up far too quickly, the grey durasteel blurring as it flew closer
to your vision. You tried to twist in mid-air as you fell, holding the kid and praying that he
wouldn't be hurt-

The impact drew whatever air was left in your body from your lungs. Something in your
shoulder made a distinct ‘pop’. You let out a broken cry as you tumbled, managing to keep a
grip on the toddler as you rolled, crashing into a pile of trash debris and eventually coming to
a stop.

The air settled around you, several pieces of paper fluttering and coming to rest on your limp
form. You could hear the sound of the speeder, with its horrible engine scream, fade into the
distance. After several moments there was a loud bang, then silence.

You stayed there on the ground for some time, winded, bruised, and disoriented. Yet the first
thought that entered into mind wasn't that of the pain or the terror of your ordeal, but the
simple, overwhelming gratitude of being alive. Somehow, against the overwhelming odds,
you had survived.

Your body ached from head to toe, and you could feel a sharp, unrelenting pain on the side
you had landed on, whimpering when you attempted to shift. The pain dug deeper into your
side, curling up under your arm and etching along your ribs. It was an indication of your
survival, and you thanked whatever superior power lived above that you were only injured,
not dead or falling to your doom far far below.

Yet from within your arms came a distressed whine, and every injury that you suffered was
forgotten in an instant. You drew the child away from your chest, eyes wide and breath
hitching in your throat.

"Kid!" You gasped, feeling the air flood back into your lungs. From the confines of the dingy
swaddled blanket the child looked up at you with peering eyes, as if he were too scared to
open them in case your landing had only been a figment of his imagination.



Upon realizing that you had both survived the ordeal, however, the toddler's little green
forehead wrinkled. His eyes became glassy with tears, and with a hiccup, he began to sob in a
mixture of being completely overwhelmed and terribly afraid. You could feel his entire body
jolt with the cries, the sounds echoing in your own chest.

As if hearing the child's sobs opened a floodgate, you too felt your throat choke. Unwillingly,
a gasp escaped you. Within seconds you felt the hot trail of tears spilling down your cheeks
as you held the kid close, curling around him comfortingly as you cried in tandem at the
horror of your ordeal and the gratitude at having survived.

"Hey!" A voice called, and despite your eyes still blurry with tears your head jerked up. You
jolted to a sit, whining in pain at the sharp pierce that ran across your side, stealing the breath
from your lungs. Yet your eyes looked up even as you wrapped both arms around the kid's
swaddle.

A female Quarren stood a ways away from you, stance low as if ready to run. She looked
directly at you and the kid, then glanced behind her at a small crowd of residents who had
their gazes locked on you.

"Are you okay?" She asked, voice concerned. "Do I need to call the police?"

Whatever relief you felt in your system now drew hard and cold as realization. The police
would only ask questions. You and Din had entered the planet under the radar, and you had
no papers with which to present yourself. Plus the image of having jumped from a speeder
while holding a baby would immediately cast you into doubt. You couldn't let the police
officers find you, couldn't let them take away the kid. You had to go, you had to run.

Pushing yourself so that you tucked your knee under you, you grit your teeth against
whatever horrible pain inflamed your side. It took a moment, but soon enough you wobbled
to a stand, turning from the growing crowd, and limping quickly in the other direction. The
woman called after you, but you ignored her voice, focused only on trying to get somewhere
where you wouldn’t be noticed.

The child in your arms was still crying, still sobbing against your chest. You could feel your
own tears still hot against your face as you quickly put distance in between yourself and the
crowd, pushing your way past those still on the walkway and towards the outline of shops
and buildings at the far end. The few Coruscanti citizens who hadn’t been on the bridge
during your jump made way for you. You could hear their confused and curious whispers as
you stumbled towards the shadows of the shops.

There, you ducked into an alleyway, collapsing into the shadows. The moment your back hit
the wall and your feet slid out from under you a broken gasp let loose from your throat, one
born from the intense pain that flooded your veins. This seemed to only further distress the
child, who cried louder with a high-pitched whine and shaking breaths. You tried to hush the
kid, reassuring him, and unbundling him from the swaddle. As soon as you did his tiny hands
reached for you, face scrunched miserably.

"Are you hurt?" You asked, and the kid didn't answer, instead curling into your chest. There
his cries quieted, as if the touch of being against your body comforted him. As you gently



examined him it seemed that you had absorbed the brunt of the impact. He whimpered as you
poked and prodded him but didn’t let loose any cries of pain or discomfort. You breathed a
huge sigh of relief, muscles loosening. The kid seemed a little bruised, but otherwise in one
piece and thankfully okay.

"It's okay." You spoke to the child, one hand brushing lightly against the back of his head.
The motion caused him to snuggle farther against you, a stray hiccup tearing from his throat.
Yet at your words he eased into your touch, sniffling but no longer sobbing.

"We'll be okay." You said again to yourself, looking up at the endless expanse of the
Coruscant underworld. The narrow frame of the alleyway walls allowed the hanging
buildings of the planet’s artificial shell to peek through. There the dizzying neon lights of the
city twinkled down at you, casting bright colors over your anxious face and reflecting in the
stray tears that still escaped the corners of your eyes.

Somehow, your thoughts drifted back to Din. You prayed to the stars he was looking for you,
that he had somehow already caught your scent. If that were so then maybe you could hold
on, could make it until morning so you could find him and be safe in his hold once more. The
thought brought forth a new choking sensation to your throat, and you swallowed back an
overwhelmed sob of fear and desperation. Instead, you spoke, words curling up above you
and, you prayed, floating to the place where Din was.

"We'll be okay."

Chapter 25: Part Twenty-five: The Ambush
Chapter Summary

Before Din could deflate in relief the wolf man huffed a laugh under his breath, causing
Din's eyes to shoot back towards him.

"What?" He asked sharply, and the wolf-man smirked.

"It crashed." The Black Sun member spoke, voice sinister. "My buddy was still in there
when she took off. He must have done something because the speeder crashed lower in
the sector.” He sneered, white canines colored red with blood. “They found his body on
a walkway a couple levels down and the wreck somewhere in the market area. Your
friends? They're both dead, pal."

Chapter Notes

Warnings for this chapter:

Descriptive violence, fair amount of death mention, mentions of gore, passing mention
of child trafficking (no trafficking takes place), graphic description of injury, just overall
a fairly violent chapter as the result of two Mandos raining hell on some kidnappers.

In addition this chapter is the longest one I've written, clocking in at 7.7k words. So if
you have a drink or a snack, I recommend it while you're reading.

 

Also I'm so sorry

See the end of the chapter for more notes

The windstorm that had engulfed the upper altitudes of Coruscant had begun to waft
downwards towards the lower levels and into the Black Sun Sector. Din could feel the breeze
ripple the cape across his back as he lay flat on a rooftop overlooking the darkened side street
where he had located the Black Sun hideout to be. Night had engulfed the sector as he and
Paz had tracked prints back to the small outpost, the neon lights slowly flickering to life
amidst the darkness.

The three Black Sun members that lingered outside the awned doorway of the hideout
seemed not to notice the change in weather, the wind rolling in hot just as Din's anger seemed
to pulse under his skin. If Din strained his ears then he could hear the low promise of thunder



in the distance, obstructed by the hum of air traffic. With it came the promise of a storm, one
that would shower the upper levels of Coruscant but rain hell down on the Black Sun hideout
Din and Paz were surveying.

"You're certain?" Paz spoke, and Din briefly glanced at the warrior next to him, who too was
laid flat against the durasteel surface of the abandoned apartment exterior. The neon lights
from the walkways above cast dimly against the heavy infantry’s helmet with bright colors.
Din gave the other Mando a single, purposeful nod.

"The tracks I picked up where her and the kid's leave off lead to here." Din returned, careful
to keep his voice low. They were high up enough for the guards not to notice their forms
hunched over the edge, looking down into the side street. Yet Din remained quiet all the
same, a habit born from years of experience as a bounty hunter.

"One of them, at least." Paz noted, and Din didn't respond, raising a gloved hand to the side
of his helmet, zooming in on one of the guards. The Duros Black Sun member was seated on
a crate just outside the entrance, chatting casually with the two other guards while idly
twisting a vibroblade in his hand. With no response from his Vod Paz continued: "You said
the other set of tracks stopped where we saw the speeders."

Din didn't miss the insinuation that Paz left unspoken, yet it lingered all the same. That
perhaps you and the kid weren't in the hideout at all, that you had been taken somewhere else.
Din knew he shouldn't get his hopes up that you were in there, but his mind continued to
offer images of your and the child's terrified but relieved faces when he and Paz got inside
and dealt with the ge'hutuun that had taken you both. The feeling of your form in his arms the
night before haunted him, and in that fantasy of rescue Din imagined the weight of you in his
hold once more, safe.

"Even if they aren't there." He eventually returned to Paz, turning on his side to face the
warrior. "One of these scumbags will have a lead we can go off of."

Again, Paz nodded, this time his head bobbing in thought as he weighed Din's words.

"Good." He conceded at last, angling himself once more to gaze at the trio of criminals seated
outside the outpost. "How many inside?"

Din pushed another button in the side of his helmet, night vision flickering to the
kaleidoscopic colors of infrared. Flicking his gaze past the entrance, Din squinted in an
attempt to see the other figures waiting inside the hideout.

"Three more in the main area." He reported softly to his Vod next to him. "More in the back, I
can't tell. Wait-" Din stopped abruptly, zooming in on a figure different from the too bright or
cool colors of the aliens inside the hideout. There, a figure tucked up in a side room, huddled
tightly in a corner. Waiting.

"It's her." His mind whispered.

"I may have something." Din spoke, voice softening a fraction. "On the left-hand side of the
main area. Be careful to check your fire when we come in."



"Is it your partner? Or the baby?" Paz asked, and Din gave a small shake of his head, unsure.

"Hard to tell. The kid isn't in the main area, but he might be in the back where I can't see."

As much as he shouldn't have let himself, Din could feel his heart rise into his throat. If it was
you, if it was your form huddled in the corner, then-

The thought of what the scum could have done to you remained unspoken between the two
warriors, but inside Din's thought images of your bruised and beaten form made his skin run
hot under his flight suit, making his hand tighten against his helmet. His anger from earlier
had not entirely dissipated, remaining dulled by his hunter’s instincts as he tracked you, but
now it reared back into full force. The fact that you and the kid had been taken by itself was
enough to charge his bloodlust with lightning fire, but the idea that they had hurt you, had so
much as touched you-

"Let's go." He spoke, turning to slide down the angled roof. He had to get in there. Even if the
kid wasn’t there, even if they had separated you both, at least he could get one of you, could
make sure those lowlifes never touched you again, or anyone for that matter. He would break
their hands before they ever got the chance, kill them if he had to. He had to go, had to get in
there-

"Vod." Paz spoke, one hand descending on Din's pauldron to halt his movements. It was
careful this time, not heavy handed in the way he had attempted before outside the covert that
had led to the duel. Instead, it was gentle, yet Paz's voice remained firm in reminder.

"Discreet." Was all the older warrior spoke, the single word conveying sentences of meaning.

Din paused, hearing Paz's warning and letting it sink past the panic and ire building in his
veins. He forced himself to breathe, to feel the air tickle his face inside his helmet. The hot
flush of fury in his veins remained present, but Din could feel it cool, hardened into that
battle worn focus he wore during his hunts. That same concentration he felt on Rishi, on
Hypori and beyond even then, to the days before you, weighed down on him like a second set
of armor.

"Discreet." He agreed, letting the cold calculation of a hunter overtake the flush of fear that
his mind summoned at the thought of you inside and subject to whatever treatments the Black
Sun had decided to inflict on you.

Paz gave his pauldron a pat, and Din frowned not in determination or fury, but mild
annoyance at the vaguely condescending gesture.

"The first three come quietly." Paz spoke, and even though Din agreed with the instruction he
could feel a prickle of irritation at Paz issuing orders. "I'll drop down and take one, you flank
the other two."

Din nodded, skidding down the rooftop to circle around like Paz had suggested. Or at least he
hoped he had suggested, instead of barking orders at him like some young verd'ika. That was
a matter for later.



Instead, Din's feet hit the street, form hunched low to stay in the shadows. There were very
few passersby in this sector, and even fewer in the cold silence of night, but Din felt his
experience creeping up into his bones and taking hold. It allowed him to ease into the
darkness, careful to skirt around the corner and into the alleyway.

The years of his Mandalorian training clung to him like a second skin, as close to his flesh as
the beskar itself. Within it boiled a silent fury, an undeniable anger at the crime that had taken
place, one he could have prevented if he hadn’t left your side. If you were truly in the
hideout, if it was you in there, then he would slaughter every criminal in his path to get to
you and hold you tight once more.

Above the incoming thunderstorm rumbled threateningly, dark clouds roiling like ink across
the night sky and blocking out the artificial haze of the Coruscanti underworld that reflected
off Din’s cuirass. What little light remained seemed to dance off his form like smoke,
wavering along with his heartbeat thudding in a steady rhythm between his ribs.

Up above he could see Paz's helmet peeking from over the rooftop, then vanish again back
into the shadows. Din needn’t give the other Mando a signal, knowing fully well that the
warrior would be ready the second Din decided to strike. Obscuring himself from the soft
flickering glow of a streetlight, Din crept up to his hiding place behind a stack of empty
crates, watching the three guards continue to talk in soft voices. One of the three raised a
hand, looking to the heavens as if he could gauge exactly when the storm would break. None
had an inkling as to the predator that lurked behind them.

Din waited, letting his breath even out despite the itch in his palms, the desire to feel the
crack of bone under his grasp at the ones who had taken you, had hurt you.

And as he did, the rain began to fall.

In a single breath Din launched his whipcord, watching as the weighted end wrapped itself
around the arm of one of the guards. Feeling the weight of his target pull it taut on the other
end, Din drew himself backwards, using all his strength to pull. His victim didn't have a
moment to yelp before Din was yanking him backwards into the shadows, his form sliding on
the smooth surface of the slickening street. The other two guards stood, eyes widening as the
hunter’s blade descended before the man could scream for help.

In the moment it took the other two to react, a large figure dropped down behind the Duros
seated on the crate. The alien turned at the sound, wrist holding the vibroblade slackening in
surprise. The white-hot fire of Paz’s jetpack flames flickered off the weapon. Just as the alien
opened his mouth to call for help, Paz wrapped a hand around the alien's face, bracing them
both before launching himself skyward once more with the red flare of his jetpack. The
muffled scream of the Duros followed him, note rising high in surprise and fear. The rockets
blazed briefly, but before they could reach a fever pitch Paz had vanished into the rooftops
above.

Din was stalking forward before Paz had even descended, eyes never leaving the third guard
who reached for his rifle propped against the doorway, wheeling to try and face the phantoms
that had taken his associates. He never got the chance. As he turned Din could see the flicker
of panic in his eyes. Yet the hunter barely regarded it, instead burying his blade deep into the



man's back. The knife drove up under the Black Sun member’s ribs, and the man let out a
choked sound as Din twisted.

Whatever sound the man tried to make was muffled by Din's glove. Din could feel the
criminal slump against him, and knew that if the scum wasn't dead already, that he would be
soon. He let the body go slack, drawing back his blade and lowering the man against the
pavement with hardly a sound.

The laughter from inside died with the brief commotion Din and Paz had caused. Din felt
himself tense, then roll and duck behind the crate as a chair scraped against the floor and a
gang member ventured towards the open doorway.

The moment he stepped outside Din heard the sound of a jetpack, looking up as Paz came
crashing down once more. The warrior’s large figure descended rapidly, Paz using his broad
frame and weight to crush the man under his foot, slamming his head down against the
concrete and keeping him there as he fired a single shot into his spine.

Then he looked at Din, offering a single nod. Din rose to join him, blaster drawn as both
Mandos stalked into the hideout.

Din felt the remaining criminals before he saw them, a blaster bolt dinging off of his armor as
he and Paz swept inside. Din fired back past the red blaze of blaster fire, hearing one yelp as
his aim hit his mark. Yet even despite one down the rain of red plasma continued, obscuring
his vision and forcing him to duck behind a closed doorway. Din peered carefully out from
behind the door frame, noting the double barrel blaster favored by most Black Sun members.
The weapon allowed five men to feel like ten, with the blaster bolts scorching the other side
of the wall he had ducked behind.

It was chaos now, with several of the gangsters yelling and trying to be heard above the
blaster fire that deflected off of the metal walls of the hideout. Din could hear answering calls
from further down a hallway, evidence that there were indeed more gangsters than he had
originally hoped. Yet they remained pinned. At this close range Beskar could only protect
them so much, with an errant or poorly aimed blaster bolt ripping through flesh not covered
by armor.

Paz remained across from him, trying to tuck as much of himself against the wall as possible.
Din noted that the heavy infantry Mandalorian hadn't yet drawn his cannon blaster, likely
remembering Din's warning about discrepant fire possibly wounding those they were there to
rescue. Paz seemed to notice Din's gaze despite the raining bolts, nodding as if Din had
somehow communicated something to him.

Before Din could mentally question whatever Paz had seen in his glance, the warrior stepped
forward. With a precise roll of his wrist that, if Din listened above the blaster fire, he could
hear a low whine of activation. In the moment that several bolts pinged off his chest plate the
warrior braced, lifted his arm-

And let flames erupt from his gauntlet.



Din blinked, the orange haze of heat casting shadows brightly on his helmet. Even with his
armor on he could feel the bite from the scorching eruption heating his beskar. Yet it wasn't
flames like Din's own vambraces, instead the heat that poured forth from Paz's own bracer
was that of plasma.

The glowing, orange arc reached over the inner threshold of the hideout, extending to the
table where the thugs had been seated. The sound was catastrophic, erupting like magma in a
volcanic explosion on the planet Mustafar. Over the roar Din could hear frantic screams
rising in pitch as the lava shot forward, hitting its intended marks and scorching the furniture
nearby.

"So much for discreet." Din thought to himself with a tight frown. “Showoff.”

It lasted all of a heartbeat, and the second that Paz switched the weapon off the magma fell to
the ground, catching on the furniture and floor. It sizzled upon contact, the color fading from
an almost sickening orange to black as Din watched.

Din's body moved automatically, firing two shots at the Black Sun members who were
already screaming in pain at molten flesh and burning clothing. Their screams silenced
quickly, bodies hitting the floor with a 'thud' that spoke of finality. Din almost considered it a
mercy upon seeing the gore of melted skin and burnt clothing fused with their flesh.

Yet it wasn't over. Din could hear yelling in the back rooms as the remaining (and likely
sleeping) Black Sun members were startled into action. He braced, readying his own
vambraces and raising his blaster to train on the doorway leading further into the Black Sun
outpost. Yet a gesture from Paz stopped him.

"I'll take care of this." Paz barked, nodding to the hallway leading off further into the hideout.
"Go find your partner."

Din nodded, eyes already scanning the room past the collapsed forms of the gang members,
past the still smoking molten furniture. As Paz continued into the hallway, his heavy
footsteps soon followed by a rapid series of shots and returning fire, Din walked further into
a side room, eyes searching desperately for the form he knew to be yours.

You had to be here. You had to. Paz would find the kid somewhere in the back room,
frightened but safe, and you would simply be restrained in a corner, otherwise untouched and
unharmed. That had to be the case, and if it were, it meant that Din could touch you both,
gloved fingers checking and skimming over your faces to remind himself that you were both
okay, that you were alive-

There.

He almost missed it at first, the shape huddled into the corner shielded under a torn blanket.
In the dimly lit room it looked like a heap of trash or some type of debris. Yet when Din's
eyes passed over it the figure underneath shuddered, the motion rippling against the fabric.

Din took two steps forward, immediately holstering his blaster and reaching a hand to tear the
blanket off of the person underneath.



And stopped dead in his tracks.

Where he was expecting to find your frightened but relieved gaze, eyes wide like the time he
had discovered you aboard his ship, he instead found something entirely different.

The eyes underneath were less frightened and more terrified, gazing up at Din in the darkness
and partially shielded by an arm lifted in defense. Past the hand that obstructed his view Din
could see the tell-tale, childlike roundness of an adolescent face, sweaty hair plastered against
a brow wrinkled with distress.

A child.

Yet not a young one. No, Din guessed that the boy was likely not even into his formative
years, only slightly older than Din himself had been when he was taken in by the
Mandalorians.

"Don't!" The kid cried, wincing as Din recoiled in surprise. "Wait, please!"

It was clear the poor boy was terrified, hands held out in an effort to protect himself from
what Din likely appeared to him as: an attacker. With his Mandalorian armor and intimidating
visored gaze, Din couldn’t exactly blame him. He even felt a pang of sorrow for the kid, in
some ways recognizing a flash of himself when he had been rescued by the covert as a child.

Yet he could feel his thoughts racing to understand, to process the presence of a child in a
location of such debauchery and filth. Had he been trafficked? If so, why wasn't he bound?
Why just him? The collection of various fabrics under the kid seemed to almost be a bed of
some sort, and the blanket draped over him meant that the kid was there of his own free will,
perhaps even looked after. The idea made Din’s mind short circuit, trying to reconcile what
little he could gather about the boy with what he knew of the Black Sun.

Still trying to understand, Din eased backwards, making it a point to move slowly so as to not
startle the boy. Then, still moving very gently, he extended his hands in a motion of peace.
Din lowered himself down, tucking one knee under him as he came to rest at the boy’s eye
level.

"Hey, it's okay." He reassured him, voice softening. "You're safe now."

Past the arm still lifted as the boy attempted to shield himself, Din could see a flicker of
doubt, then confusion. Din didn't fully understand either, yet even so he made a point of
keeping his hands up, showing his empty grasp free of weapons.

"What are you doing here?" Din asked, confusion and curiosity tinting his voice.

Slowly, the boy lowered his arms, gaze still fearful yet eyes flickering in confusion. His lips
parted once, twice before he finally summoned the words in a quivering voice.

"I...I'm a messenger." He spoke, but even in his voice Din could sense the unease, the
curiosity but fear at facing someone in a mask.



Din's thoughts flickered in recognition, some part of him summoning the memory of the
background you had divulged about yourself. You had mentioned your entanglement with a
gang on Kaddak when you were younger. An errand runner, you had said? A messenger, a
gopher for packages and information. Someone young, someone seemingly abandoned who
would go unnoticed on harsh streets filled with shady characters. Likely this boy was the
same, seizing a less than ideal opportunity in a simple bid to survive the harsh environment
of Coruscant’s underworld.

Din felt himself grimace at the thought, an odd weight settling in his stomach.

"You don't have to be afraid." He instead spoke, offering a hand in a silent gesture of aid.
“You can come with us, you can be safe.”

The boy eyed Din’s open palm, still keeping his own hands tight to his chest. Now that they
weren’t obstructing his face Din could properly see him. He was Twi’lek, Din realized, with
dark blue adult coloring fading in with blotchy splashes all over his face and lekku. He
couldn’t have been more than 14, but with the lack of proper food he appeared almost as
young as 12. The desire to bring the child back to the covert, to help him escape the Black
Sun outpost drew tight in Din’s chest.

For a moment it seemed like the boy would take Din’s hand, might reach out and let himself
be aided by the hunter.

and then as Din blinked, the kid vanished, springing from his hiding spot and leaping towards
the door.

"Wait!" Din called after him, but it was too late. He could hear the kid scramble to avoid the
still sizzling magma on the floor of the main room, skidding against the ground of the
entryway in his bid to escape. Even when Din raced to the entryway he could see the dimly
lit figure of the child racing down the side street, off into the night.

Din sighed, the breath rattling in the inside of his helmet. The bitter sting of regret filled his
mouth for all of a moment before the commotion of a fight in the back rooms brought him
back to reality.

He turned back to the inside of the hideout, passing the scorched main area to the hallway
Paz had vanished down. As he did the other Mando appeared, a section of his shoulder plate
still smoking with blaster fire.

"Did you find her?" He asked, nodding to the room the boy had come from.

"No.” Din replied, unable to hide the grimace of disappointment and frustration in his voice.
“It was a kid. The gang was using him as a messenger."

Paz tilted to look past Din, visored gaze roaming the hideout and finding it empty of the boy
Din had mentioned.

"You let him go?” He asked, voice low but incredulous. “That's going to cause problems for
us later. He could inform their reinforcements."



"I'd rather deal with whatever comes next than deal with the aftereffects of killing a kid" Din
snapped back, hackles raising.

"Didn't say I disagree." Paz remarked dryly, following Din and nodding towards the room he
had just come from. “I’d rather bring him back to the covert with us until this is all over.”

Din sighed in conjunction, closing his eyes once more in frustration. Opening them, he turned
to Paz once more.

“Did you find-?”

“No.” Came Paz’s immediate reply, and the disappointment seemed to sink even deeper in
Din’s chest.

So, you and the kid weren’t here after all. It was a dead end.

Din felt his jaw set in a hard grimace under his helmet. Even after finding your tracks and
following them, he still had no clue where you or the child were. He couldn’t stop the shake
in his arms, the way his fists clenched at his sides. Wherever you were, you both were surely
terrified and likely struggling to find a way back to him. The thought seemed to fracture
Din’s heart, breath stuttering as he held back the urge to tear off his helmet so he could
breathe, could compose himself.

“However…” Paz ventured, and Din wheeled on him instantly. “There is someone I think
you might want to meet.”

With that he pushed past Din, shouldering aside the Mando’s smaller form as he made his
way further down the hallway. There, Paz paused at a broken door, inclining his head inside.
As Din neared he could smell the burning after-taste of blaster smoke and scorched skin.

It seemed Paz had managed to contain the remaining Black Sun members before they had
even fully equipped themselves. Din tried not to count the number of bodies in the room,
noting some of the few there hadn’t even left their bunks. Yet in the middle of the scene Paz
had wreaked havoc upon, a single gang member sat braced against an overturned table,
raising his head as Din’s shadow fell over him.

A Shistavanen, Din noted. Known for their acute tracking abilities and wolf-like qualities.
This one was colored a dark grey, the blood oozing from his wounds caking against his fur as
dark as onyx. It was only the single ceiling light above that let the fluid tinge crimson at the
edges. Din wasn’t sure exactly what Paz had wrought upon the criminal, but it was enough to
tell that the Black Sun member would not be long for this world without help.

Yet that wasn’t what caught Din’s attention, nor was it the feral glint in the beast-man’s eyes
as Din towered over his collapsed form. No, Din let his gaze trace down from the alien’s
muzzle, past his gashed chest and to his feet.

The tracks. He realized. The ones he had traced back to the hideout from the moment he had
found them where yours stopped. They were the same.



This was the one who had taken you and the child.

The disappointment that had carved a hollow inside Din’s chest fell away like shattered glass,
only to be replaced by a bubbling anger as dark as the Shistavanen’s blood. It coiled in his
gut, building heat beneath his skin like magma.

Paz stood behind him, and as if sensing Din’s growing ire, turned his head to face away.

Din took a single step forward.

“What do you know?” He asked, voice dipping dangerously low and leaving no question as
to the threat there.

“I don’t know anything.” The gang member spat, lips curling back to reveal his sharp
canines.

“Try again.” Din returned, one hand reaching down to caress the handle of his blaster. The
alien only barked a broken laugh at him.

“Go to hell, Mandalorian.”

Din felt his rage boil over, breathing quickly becoming unsteady with fear and frustration. He
unholstered his blaster, keeping his finger off the trigger but feeling the whites of his
knuckles wrap the weapon tightly in his grasp.

Yet before he could raise the blaster to level between the thug’s eyes he felt his eyes drawn to
something in the corner of his vision. Almost like a whisper, Din turned his head to find the
source of the sudden distraction. It took him a moment, but Din’s eyes traced over a nearby
bunk, towards something partially obscured by a ragged blanket. He didn't know how he
spotted it, but suddenly Din’s gaze grew wide as he recognized the glint of a familiar object.

Ignoring Paz's curious stare, Din paced to the bunk, withdrawing the sleek, well maintained
handle of a blaster.

The blaster he had given you.

"Where did you get this?" Din growled, one hand tight against the handle of the blaster, the
other pointing his own weapon dead center against the skull of the Shistavanen. When the
wolf man didn't answer, remaining silent with only a grimace plastered across his face, Din
felt his jaw draw tight and hard as he gripped the blaster he had given you.

"Where." He tried again, and this time his voice dipped low, unmistakable with deadly intent.
"Did you get this?"

When the alien still refused to answer Din remained silent, perfectly still as he weighed his
options. Then, with practiced precision, he lowered his aim to the beast man's foot, firing off
a single shot that was deafened by the wolf-man's roar of pain. The sound was inhuman,
almost unlike anything Din had ever heard, more animal than man, curling up past the ceiling
into the stormy clouds of Coruscant’s skies.



"KARKING-!!" He yelped, raised hands instantly reaching down to cradle the injury and
forgetting the blaster trained on him. When the blaster clicked, recalibrating, his eyes shot up
to look at the Mandalorian standing over him. Din pointed his blaster at the other foot, yet he
didn’t fire. Instead, he kept his eyes locked on the Black Sun member, gaze heavy with intent.

"Fine!" The Shistavanen growled, one hand raising placatingly. In it Din could see a barely-
there tremble.

"I got it off some chic- she had a kid with her.” Din’s captive continued. “We saw her walk
into the sector with you, we thought we could ransom her or use her as bait."

"Where is she?" And even Paz turned his head at the tone in Din’s voice, dark and furious yet
restrained in a way that spoke of the dark temptation inside his thoughts to leave this man to
die a gruesome death.

"She got away!” He gasped, still clutching his foot. “Stole a speeder right out from under us,
took the kid with her."

At that Din felt his shoulders drop in relief, and it took a moment of composure for him to not
drop his weapon back to his side, his relieved breath rattling in the inside of his helmet.

You had gotten away. Both of you.

As concerned as he was for your safety, Din couldn’t help but feel the rigid steel of fear in his
bones collapse with solace at the fact that neither of you remained in Black Sun custody. His
nightmares at the pain the criminal syndicate could have done to you eased from haunting
specters into flickering shadows.

Yet more than that he was proud. He was so immensely proud of your drive, your ingenuity
and perseverance to survive and protect the child. Even if you were still lost to him the fact
that you had managed to escape on your own volition brought the Mando an immense pride
and satisfaction.

Before Din could deflate in relief the wolf man huffed a laugh under his breath, causing Din's
eyes to shoot back towards him.

"What?" He asked sharply, and the wolf-man smirked.

"It crashed." The Black Sun member spoke, voice sinister. "My buddy was still in there when
she took off. He must have done something because the speeder crashed lower in the sector.”
He sneered, white canines colored red with blood. “They found his body on a walkway a
couple levels down and the wreck somewhere in the market area. Your friends? They're both
dead, pal."

It took a moment for Din to process the words spoken to him, expression briefly clouding
with confusion. When he did understand, it felt as though he were the one falling, pushed off
the edge by an invisible hand and plunging down into oblivion. The icy cold wash of dread
froze the previous hot fire of anger in his veins, lips parting in silent shock at what he had just
heard.



No. That…that wasn’t right. There was no way you both had just…left like that. Your flames
were too bright to be extinguished that easily. Yet the possibility of it scared him in that
moment more than anything else, more than breaking his creed, more than the possibility of
becoming dar’manda.

“You’re wrong.” Din spoke, but his voice was choked, unsure.

The thug seemed to easily notice his captor’s distress, laughing until something wet bubbled
in his throat. He spluttered for a moment, voice choked with both laughter and blood.

Before the Black Sun member could speak, however, Din felt a presence grow behind him.

“Vod…” Paz spoke, voice soft and regretful. Din almost turned to him, eyes wide and
disbelieving under his helmet. Yet he didn’t, keeping his gaze locked on the criminal below
him.

“You’re wrong.” He spoke again, and even with his added conviction he could still hear the
tint of despair in his voice. “They’re alive.”

There was no way you both weren’t alive. With your white-knuckle grip on survival and the
child’s abilities, there wasn’t any scenario where you weren’t alive. Yet the shadow of doubt
lurked dark across his thoughts, whispering to him in sinister tongues he couldn’t decipher.

"It won't matter anyways,” The Shistavanen laughed, coughing. “You'll never get to see her
or the kid ever again even if they did survive. You'll be dead before then."

As if to punctuate his words, the thunder overhead rumbled dark and stormy against the night
sky. If Din had been paying attention, he would have noticed the odd mechanical grumble
that came with it, and would have felt the slightest tremor in the floor beneath his feet.

"What does that mean?" He asked instead, feeling Paz’s hand vanish from his pauldron. He
stepped forward again, shoving the barrel of his blaster closer to the Black Sun member’s
head. The Shistavanen only glared up at him, the fight slowly leaving his eyes as he began to
succumb to his wounds. Din could feel a well of emotions rise within him, overwhelmed
briefly by the grief, the anger, the confusion the criminal’s words had wrought upon him. He
spoke again, voice rising with each word.

"What do you know!?"

“Vod.” Paz greeted from behind him, and Din glanced over his shoulder at the heavy infantry
Mando. When he gave no indication he was listening to Paz’s words, however, the warrior
repeated himself, voice hinting urgently. “Djarin. We need to go.”

The wolf-man spluttered once more, one clawed hand raising to his throat. He grinned up at
the two men, teeth bared.

“You and your covert are going to die. Just like everyone else who…dares to challenge...the
Black Sun.”

He wheezed once, twice, then fell still, hand dropping limply to the floor next to him.



Din didn’t have any time to fully process the man’s death before Paz was taking advantage of
his shocked expression, hauling him backwards down the hallway he had come from.

“They’ve summoned reinforcements.” He barked over his shoulder as Din began to follow.
“We have what we came for. We need to leave.”

Din nodded numbly, mind still racing to understand what he had just heard about you, the
child, the covert, the speeder crash, all of the information the Shistavanen had supplied.

He didn’t have any time to fully consider it, however, as he and Paz burst out of the entrance
to the hideout and into the narrow side street outside.

As soon as they did Din could hear the rumble more clearly now, low but different than the
thunder overhead. The rain was pouring down now, soaking everything in its path and
streaming down the sides of the buildings on either side of them. Yet in between the tall
structures that enclosed the street Din could make out a shape slowly defining itself from
behind the sheet of rain and lit by the flickering glow of the single streetlamp.

He didn’t have much time to fully see the vehicle that was parked at the entrance to the street,
peering from behind his visor as the low rumbled began to rise in pitch, humming low and
rising as a muzzle flashed in the darkness.

Paz spoke, voice tinting sardonically a second before the whine of the turret reached a fever
pitch.

"I have a bad feeling about this."

The turret opened fire, and Din instantly flattened himself against the entrance to avoid the
hellfire of blaster bolts that rained down upon them both. The sound was deafening, each shot
hitting the slick durasteel walkway with an explosive metal thunk. That alone was indication
of the turret being more than just a plasma repeating blaster. No, the rounds in the weapon
were designed to explode on impact. One shot from such a cannon would be enough to down
even the most battle hardened Mando.

They couldn’t stay put like this, crammed against the inside of the entrance. The turret would
eventually roll forwards and tear both him and Paz to pieces. Yet the second they tried to
escape, tried to run the superior range on the weapon would shred them alive as well.

Din glanced behind him, into the warehouse, trying to remember if he had seen a back door
to the hideout. All the while he kept his bracers up, trying to avoid any shrapnel flying at his
helmet and visor.

Yet before he could formulate a battle plan he felt the solid grip of his Vod next to him. Din’s
gaze spun to face Paz, who too had one bracer up to avoid the worst of the flying bits of
metal from the canisters exploding on the street before them.

“Hold on!” He yelled over the turret fire, wrapping one hand tightly around Din’s smaller
frame and securing him fast to his chest. Din was too shocked to squirm away, the surprise of



Paz’s action making his brain go empty with a screeching halt. It wasn’t helped at all when
Paz took a step forward, crouching low and forcing Din to follow his motions.

The second Din put his hands down to try and remove Paz’s forearm wrapped around him the
ground jolted under his feet. Before Din could stop him, Paz’s jetpack roared and launched
them both upwards towards the rooftops. The world spun as the ground vanished under Din’s
feet, held aloft in the air only by Paz’s tight grip.

It seemed like they were going to make it, even if Paz’s hold on Din was as ungraceful as it
was uncomfortable. Yet Din could hear the turret stop, then whine as they ascended. Glancing
down, he saw the barrel of the weapon raise to aim at them, the whine of it charging again
rising in pitch.

“Look out!” Din grunted, jostling his shoulder into Paz. The motion threw the warrior off
balance for a moment, making him hover in flight as he tried to readjust his grip and keep
Din from falling.

That was all it took.

Din didn’t hear the weapon fire, but the impact it made against Paz’s beskar seemed loud
enough to rattle the core of the planet itself. All at once Paz was descending, knocked straight
backwards by the shell exploding against him. Din didn’t have time to take stock of the
shrapnel embedded in the arm closest to Paz’s chest plate because he too was falling, falling,
plummeting down to the street below as Paz’s jetpack failed without control.

Somehow, Din was able to angle them both so that their bodies didn’t collide catastrophically
with the metal walkway, shattering bones upon impact. Instead they landed into a debris pile
that managed to cushion their fall despite the bits of discarded metal and plastoid amongst the
softer trash.

The impact left Din gasping for air, lungs expanding dramatically in a bid for oxygen. The
world around him spun, and for a moment he couldn’t decipher which way was up or down.
Yet his body was already moving despite the rush of blood in his ears, the roar of pain in his
left arm at the slices of metal gouged past his flight suit. A glance back up the side street
proved that they were beyond the turret’s range. Yet Din knew it wouldn’t stay that way for
long.

Paz remained limp beside him, alive but barely conscious after the planet shattering impact of
the ballistic. Din could see the blue paint of the heavy infantry Mando’s armor chipped and
stained black with ammunition smoke. No doubt the warrior had at least a fractured rib,
possibly even something more serious. Paz himself seemed alive, unconscious and blacked
out from the impact but otherwise still breathing.

Din had to get them both out of here. Now.

Ignoring his own injuries, Din wrapped his gloves around Paz’s uninjured shoulder, dragging
him backwards off the trash heap and around the side street corner. It wouldn’t last long, but
the position allowed them safety from the encroaching turret and the Black Sun force that
followed.



“Vizsla.” Din heaved, chest still rising as he tried to catch his breath from the fall’s impact.
“Vizsla!”

It took a moment, but suddenly the other Mando came to with a gasp, body briefly spasming
in reflex. Paz groaned, helmet lolling to face his Vod.

“Dank ferrick.” He muttered, and Din tried to take the curse as a positive indicator as to the
man’s injuries. “That hurts like a karking skug hole.”

“Get up.” Din commanded, not bothering to humor Paz’s comments. He chose to instead lift
up the warrior’s shoulder in an effort to encourage him. “We can’t stay here.”

Yet Paz remained on the ground, still trying to gather his bearings. Din could hear the low
drone of the speeder that the turret was mounted on growing in volume as it slowly made its
way down the side street. Again, he tried to rouse the other Mandalorian, with little success.
Paz was still semi-limp against Din’s touch, trying and failing to orient himself to his
surroundings.

“I can’t.” He croaked, and Din could hear the moment he seemed to recognize the extent of
his injuries. Yet Din didn’t allow him a moment longer to recover, shoving insistently at him.

“Paz.” He tried again, daring to use the warrior’s first name. “We have to go. Now.”

“Go then.” Paz spoke, voice hoarse, and Din stopped.

“What are you-“

“Go.” Paz repeated, interrupting the younger Mando. He swallowed, helmet tilting to gaze at
the younger Mando.

“You have to warn the covert.” He warned. “You know what that weapon could do to our
people.”

Din did know. If that weapon was unleashed against the covert, the remaining warriors would
strive to overcome it, but many would be lost in the process. If they failed, the covert’s
children, the foundlings would come next.

“We can warn the covert.” Din gritted, trying once more to haul Paz upwards. “Get. Up.”

Yet even as Paz tried to assist, he remained nearly limp despite his effort. When it was clear
he couldn’t rise, the warrior found Din’s wrist and grasped onto it, hold lacking its usual
strength.

“Go, Din.” He spoke, voice tight with pain.

“I’m not leaving you.” Din snapped, muscles straining to lift the other Mando so maybe he
might carry him, hobble their way to safety-

“You will.” Paz returned, voice rising in urgency. “That’s an order.”



Din huffed, managing to get Paz to a knee with the larger Mando’s arm thrown across his
shoulder.

“I thought I told you-“ He spoke, voice straining with effort. “-that I don’t take orders from
you.”

Paz made no effort to assist his Vod, instead lowering his voice so Din could hear the words
he spoke clearly.

“You’ll take this one.”

Din stopped, muscles stiffening as he realized that Paz was being extremely serious. The hum
of the turret was drawing closer now, imminent in its arrival as the two men still knelt on the
street just around the corner.

“I’m not leaving you to die.” Din tried, not caring at the hint of despair in his voice becoming
apparent. Yet Paz merely scoffed.

“You think this is enough to kill me?” He asked, but his voice was tired, strained. “I may
need to take you a few rounds at sparring to remind you who you’re talking to.”

Din didn’t smile at Paz’s jovial tone, feeling a grimace tighten across his face.

He couldn’t leave him.

Yet if he did, they’d both die. You, the child, the covert would all be at risk from an enemy
Din couldn’t stop because his body would be laying on the cold, wet backstreets of the
Coruscant underworld.

But his Vod…

“Go.” Paz’s voice encouraged him, and this time the warrior’s voice was resigned, accepting.

Din hesitated once more. Yet after a moment he felt his chest seize with the undeniable
burden of the decision he was about to make.

He stood, letting Paz’s arm slide from his shoulders. The warrior seemed to almost breathe a
sigh of relief. Yet to Din it sounded like a wheeze of fear.

He reached down, forward to Paz’s kneeling figure, securing the other Mando’s hand to his
bracer and doing the same for him in traditional Mando fashion. Yet the motion itself made
Din’s face fall, made his chest seize in emotion. This man, this soldier he had grown
alongside, had challenged, and become rivals with, to leave him like this- to leave him to a
fate of dying alone at the hands of a lesser enemy. It wasn’t right. Yet there was nothing he
could do.

“K'oyacyi.” Din spoke, voice cracking as he emphasized the words in Mando’a. “Stay alive.”

“K'oyacyi.” Paz returned, squeezing Din’s bracer. Yet it lacked its original strength.



“Go. Warn the covert. Find your partner and your son.”

Din could feel his eyes grow hot but forced himself to let go, feeling Paz’s grip slide from his
bracer. Rising, he took several steps forward, turning one more time to glance at the warrior
who had led the covert’s children to safety, and had rescued the future of their clan. Paz
regarded him as he lay splayed on his side, the hand Din had just let go held to his beskar
chest plate.

With a choked swallow Din turned, forcing himself to look away and flee.
