Chapter 26: Part Twenty-six: The Chase
Chapter Summary

The sound of cans cluttering down the alleyway startled you abruptly from your
thoughts. Instantly, your head jerked to the side, briefly making your vision spin from
the ache still present at the base of your skull. The backstreet was empty at first glance,
the only motion being the remnant breeze fluttering loose pieces of flimsy against the
ground. Still, you couldn't ignore the sudden prickle of awareness, the instinct that you
were being watched.

It took a moment to get the kid settled into his make-shift carrier, and even longer for
you to haul yourself once again to a stand despite your protesting limbs. As you did you
glanced one more back to the origin of the noise.

And watched as a broad, dark figure emerged from the shadows.

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

You were lost.

You were horribly, dreadfully, irretrievably lost.

You had been wandering for most of the night, trying to stay away from the main roads to
avoid the police and Black Sun spotters, and yet trying your best to sneak through side streets
and alleyways to bypass any shady characters that might obstruct your path. It was no easy
feat, made all the more difficult by your injuries.

Your shoulder was busted. You didn't know how, exactly, but the pain when you attempted to
lift it burned through your muscles like scorching fire. There was an odd, uncomfortable
crick in your knee that kept you from traveling any faster than a power-walk, and even that
threatened to shoot a sharp ache through your hip and up your spine. The twinge in your
chest made it difficult to breathe at times, and when you lifted your shirt you could see a dark
bruise blossoming along the underside of one of your ribs. On top of everything else the dull,
ringing pain at the base of your skull made you dizzy and slightly lightheaded, sending a
throb through your temples up towards the crown of your head.

All in all, you felt like shit.

The kid seemed to be doing okay, having since calmed down from his crying fit after your
escape. Not that you blamed him, really. He was likely traumatized, afraid, confused, and
wanting nothing more than to be held in comfort. You were barely keeping it together
yourself, lost, hurt, fearful, and desperate to find the covert and the Mando there waiting for



you. The mere thought of being safe, of feeling Din's arms around you again threatened to
crack the sob in your throat.

At one point you were forced to stop your journey as a thunderstorm broke high above on the
upper levels, sending rain trickling down into the underworld and splattering against the
streets and rooftops. In some small semblance of grace, you had managed to find shelter for
you and the kid before the rain came pouring down like a torrent. In the hour or two it took
for the storm to subside you had tried to rest, to close your eyes and attempt to sleep. Yet
every time you had begun to drift off a noise had caught your attention, a clatter of trash that
could have been an attacker, a pursuer. That or the kid was whining, scared by the deep
rumble of thunder above.

The kid seemed to take note of your steely courage in the face of adversity, and you noticed
his attempts at being quiet, at being still so he didn't jostle you much as you walked. Yet he
was still a child, and like yourself when you were young he whimpered at shuddered at the
dark threatening boom of lightning far above you both. At some point he had drifted off,
tucked impossibly close to your chest in a bid for both warmth and comfort. It hurt your heart
to see him like that but gave you the determination needed to push onwards towards finding
your way home.

You had given up trying to sleep by the time the storm ended. Yet by that time you had found
a strip of fabric in the debris close to your hiding spot that you could fashion into a carrier of
sorts of the kid, slung over your good shoulder and allowing you to balance the kid on the hip
that didn't twinge when you walked.

Even with these small blessings though, you were nearing your limit. The storm had ended
hours ago, and at some point the foot traffic had picked up again in a sign of the morning
rush hour. The increase in passerby made keeping out of sight more difficult. With your lack
of sleep, and the adrenaline from your escape having long since worn off, you could quickly
feel yourself tiring.

You were exhausted, hungry, sore, and on top of that badly injured. More than anything, more
than the temptation of collapsing into sleep, you just wanted Din to miraculously find you, to
hold you and take you back to the Razorcrest, to let you collapse onto his bunk for a long
well-earned rest. The thought of being safe, fed, warm and protected once more made your
legs go limp with relief. Even that, the thought of simply making it back to Din with both you
and the kid in one piece made your heart ache with longing. You summoned what you could
of that thought to push you onwards, hopefully back towards where you hoped the Covert
would be.

It was all you could do to hold yourself together by the threadbare seams. You had to, you
had no choice. If you broke down now in desperation verging on hysteria, you wouldn't be
able to keep moving. Even if it felt terrible, you needed to cling onto that bit of hope that
you'd find your way back to the covert, or that Din would find you. Not only for yourself, but
for the kid as well.

So, you did exactly that, pacing yourself and walking ever further into the Coruscant
underworld. You knew you had fallen several levels whilst on the stolen speeder, so your plan
was to find a way back up towards the upper part of the sector. Even if you had been



transported far away, just being on the same level as the Covert would give you a huge
advantage in trying to find them, and Din.

At some point you could no longer ignore the sharp tug of hunger in your gut and knew that
the toddler in your care almost certainly felt it even worse. With his voracious appetite, going
so long without a meal was definitely taxing on him.

So, you had made your way back to the main road, being extremely careful to avoid anyone
who looked like they'd give you trouble. Even then you had waited in an alleyway for some
time, looking for the perfect moment to ease out into the flow of foot traffic unnoticed.

The kid at your side was whining now, hungry, and tired with the constant movement. You
gave him a half-hearted pat, knowing whatever comfort you could offer him was lackluster
compared to finding him something halfway decent to eat.

You didn't have any credits to buy anything from a street vendor. Resorting to pleading for a
portion would only arouse suspicion. By doing so you risked said vendor calling the cops on
you for soliciting. If that happened it meant ending up in police custody and the chance of
being separated from the kid. Not to mention the fact that the Black Sun may have very well
bought off members of the police force, in which case your grand escape would be useless.

With that in mind, you made a decision for your and the kid's survival.

Stealing wasn't an easy feat. It required perfect timing, confidence, and nerves of steel. You
had honed those skills over the course of a childhood, perfected them through trail of fire
with little room for mistake. A single misstep meant being chased down through the busy
market streets, sometimes as a moving target for a blaster barrel. You had the advantage of
being smaller then, quick on your feet and lean enough to squeeze through the narrow gaps
between stalls and alleyways. Now? Older, larger, and injured? You'd have to be extremely
careful, else it wouldn't just your life you'd be risking.

Whatever it was that the vendor you were about to pass was selling, it smelled absolutely
decadent. The scent of warm spices and cooking oil was so overwhelming that, for a moment,
you nearly forgot what you were there for. The kid seemed to smell it too, and he wiggled at
your side as he tried to get free of his carrier. A small pat of reassurance on his head and a
cautionary glance settled him once more.

Then, you turned your attention to the booth.

You had always been good at this. For some reason, the ability to tell exactly when the
vendor would turn their head or back just long enough for you to sneak something came
naturally to you. It was almost like a sixth sense, allowing you time your stealing swipe just
perfectly so as to not be noticed. If you did this right, the lady tending the market stall would
never even see your face.

You waited just short of the stall, leaned up against the wall beside casually as if stopping to
fix your boot. The motion made you wince, a sharp jap of pain racing from your knee to your
hip as you did so. Yet you didn't have to wait long, as the merchant overseeing the counter
where the food was on display turned to tend to her stove. In an instant you had grabbed as



many skewers could fit in one hand, feeling your blood pressure spike at the adrenaline of
taking what wasn't yours. Then, to the best of your ability, you bolted.

It took a solid ten steps for the vendor to notice, but by that point you were already around
the corner and tucked into an alleyway. You could feel your chest heave in a combination of
exhilaration and anxiety. Yet you kept calm as the vendor yelled down the street, raising her
voice to call out in frustration at the thief she couldn't see.

You kept your head down as you walked further into the alleyway, tucking the skewers into a
pocket of your pants out of the way. As much as your stomach growled at you, you couldn't
indulge just yet. You were too close to the stall, even if you were in the safety of the
alleyway.

Yet as the minutes passed and it became apparent that you were not being pursued, you took
one last look over your shoulder, and heaved a sigh of relief.

The kid was babbling at your side now, tiny hands reaching up from his carrier towards the
pocket you had stashed the food in. You reached down to take him into your good arm,
letting your back hit the cool metal of the wall behind you and sliding down to sit on the
ground beneath. The motion made all your limbs loosen, stress oozing from your aching
joints and tired muscles. You hadn't realized just how exhausted you were, and as you sat you
could feel your legs go limp now that you were finally able to rest.

The kid was already two steps ahead of you, reaching for and trying to dig into the pocket
where his meal ticket was stashed. With a weary smile you extracted the still slightly sticky
meat from your pocket, offering a skewer to the child first before trying any yourself. The kid
took it gratefully, chowing down with his tiny toddler mouth and letting forth a series of
satisfied grunts and babbles.

You yourself dug in too, letting the flavor of the meat pool over your tongue. It was still
slightly warm, sweet and a tad spicy. Whatever it had been seasoned with was just hot
enough to make you wish you had some water too to wash down the slight burn on your taste
buds. Yet you didn't find yourself minding, instead grateful at the weight that settled in your
stomach as you ate.

It was gone all too soon, with part of your share offered to the kid, who devoured it happily.
Yet it was enough to quell the rumble in your stomach, and that's all you could have asked
for.

Fed, sore, and exhausted, you could feel your body loosening in a semblance of relaxation.
You couldn't entirely relax, not with the knowledge that you two were still unsafe territory.
Yet you could feel your body protest at the thought of standing and moving on again, having
finally decided enough was enough and that you needed to rest. As anxious as you were, you
couldn't help but feel grateful for the break.

The kid had finished his meal, and now used the opportunity to stretch his tiny legs. You
watched as he scooted off your lap down to the ground, waddling about and inspecting your
surroundings. You kept a keen eye on him, making sure he didn't wander too far. After all, his
misadventures in exploring were what had gotten you into this situation in the first place.



You let your head fall back against the alleyway wall, a deep sigh passing your lips as you
took a moment to let it all sink in. Your thoughts wandered as you kept one eye on the kid
and another on the alleyway junction you were seated next to, making sure no strangers
crossed your path.

This was...familiar, you couldn't help but think. You had been here before, in this exact
scenario many times. On the run, not sure who to trust, living hand to mouth and only having
yourself to depend on. The streets of Kaddak were not kind in general, but they were
particularly vicious towards children. If you didn't have a way to earn a living, you had to
depend on the kindness of others to make sure you survived. That kindness was scarce on a
crime filled planet like Kaddak.

There were people who would take sympathy on you sometimes, giving you a fruit or piece
of bread when you needed it the most. They were the ones that always seem to appear when
you were in your worst moments, having not eaten for days or being weak with sickness. As
if some higher force beckoned them, their graciousness allowed you to teeter back from the
brink of hunger and illness each time it occurred. Their unexpected kindness always caught
you by surprise, giving you mercy from a wretched fate that awaited many of the kids you
had seen perish over the years.

Yet even then, it was up to you to find your own survival. Stealing, running, hiding, they
were all things that you had perfected to an art form when you were younger. The other kids
that found themselves in similar circumstances did the same, even at the cost of pushing their
peers into harm’s way to save themselves. You had been on the receiving end of that more
than once, a stretch from the reaching hand of an angry gangster or infuriated trader who they
had stolen from and pinned the blame on you.

So you had adapted, training yourself to be faster, smarter than even the oldest of your peers.
Soon you became known for being the one who could vanish into crowds, who could scale
rooftops and swipe a Jogan fruit right from under the nose of a market worker. Your speed,
agility, and ability to easily conceal your presence drastically increased your chances of
survival, but they didn’t ensure it.

When you finally had been noticed by the gang that controlled the city you were in, they had
found your tenacity and determination useful enough to recruit you. It wasn't a choice you
made yourself, it was one that had been made for you. To refuse meant starving in the streets,
being picked off by a bored and vicious mercenary, or even worse.

In was in the interest of your own survival that you had started running errands, belaying
messages on foot, and carrying packages with unknown contents to mysterious recipients.
You told yourself it wasn't permanent, and in the end it wasn't. The time you would have
spent scavenging you instead used to tinker, to watch the mechanics work on bikes and
communicators, to pick up skills you knew you could survive with.

The gang on Kaddak may have taken care of you, but they weren't your family. It was a
temporary arrangement for mutual benefit. You knew this even as a kid. They saw promise in
you, and you saw temporary safety in them. You could have belonged there, could have
settled for a life of crime and extortion, but that wasn't what you wanted. Even if you tried,
you weren't them.



So, when the chance came to separate yourself, to sweet-talk the gang leader, Graac, into
lending you some cash to find your own place and start your own business, you jumped
headfirst. For a while, you were happy. The work was hard, the hours long, but you were
content. You had your own place, could afford to buy your food rather than steal it, and there
was a deep satisfaction to seeing the fruits of your own labor unfold in front of you.

Yet even then, there was a part of you that was missing. In the quiet hours where you'd settle
in your kitchen with a drink, washing dishes or tinkering with a project to pass the time, the
house felt empty. The hum of the city would die as evening crept in, and you would sit by
yourself simply waiting for the next day to start only to awake alone once more. Despite
having everything you ever dreamed of, there was a loneliness you couldn't ignore, one that
settled into your bones and let a sad smile creep across your face.

It wasn't until a week of being aboard the Razorcrest on that forgotten moon where you three
had first laid low that you realized that empty part of you was gone. When you woke, it
wasn't to the cracked heat of your home planet or the silence of your small apartment above
your workshop. Instead, you could feel the warmth of a place lived in, one cared for by its
owner along with the presence of him and his charge. The void that you had felt in the place
where you lived had suddenly been filled with the presence of your two companions.

And slowly, over the weeks that had turned into months, you felt that now filled part of you
grow. Like a cup spilling over, your love for both Din and the kid had increased with each
passing day. Even with the Imperial bounty over your head, even being on the run from other
bounty hunters and encountering strange and dangerous circumstances, you felt that change
deep in your soul. It lay in the kid’s desire to be close to you, to reach up to your face with
tiny hands and babble happily at your smile. It lay in the quiet, subtle affirmations Din
offered on your work aboard the ship and the softer, more romantic moments in between.
That emptiness that had been inside you for so long overflowed with the joy of being with
two people you had grown to adore with all your heart.

At last, with them, you belonged.

And now, you would do whatever it took to see Din again and reunite the three of you once
more.

The sound of cans cluttering down the alleyway startled you abruptly from your thoughts.
Instantly, your head jerked to the side, briefly making your vision spin from the ache still
present at the base of your skull. The backstreet was empty at first glance, the only motion
being the remnant breeze fluttering loose pieces of flimsy against the ground. Still, you
couldn't ignore the sudden prickle of awareness, the instinct that you were being watched.

"Hey, kid." You muttered, gaining the attention of your small green friend. He turned to you
with a small 'awah?', and upon seeing the wary look on your face, toddled back towards you
with a small whine.

"I think it's time to get moving again, bud." You warned him, nervously glancing back to the
spot where you had heard the noises. The kid made a small whine once more, uneager to
climb back into the carrier you had fashioned for him. It took a moment to get him settled,



and even longer for you to haul yourself once again to a stand despite your protesting limbs.
As you did you glanced one more back to the origin of the noise.

And watched as a broad, dark figure emerged from the shadows.

You turned quickly on your heel, beginning to walk in the opposite direction. You tried to
keep your pace steady despite the shudder of fear that rippled through you. If you kept calm,
exuded confidence, perhaps the person would assume you were simply one of the many
vagrants in the sector and well enough leave you alone.

Yet you were tired, and despite your short rest you could feel the weight of exhaustion bear
down on your body. You thought that perhaps taking a break would re-energize you, but
instead it had signaled to you exactly how weak you were, deprived of sleep and any type of
medical treatment. It hurt to even walk, let along try and outpace a potential pursuer.

You thought at first that perhaps the person didn't notice you trudging along ahead of them, as
they seemed to hesitate behind you. Yet after a moment they regained themselves, and you
could hear the stranger begin to pace after you with slow, deliberate steps.

The light feeling that followed the instinct to flee, to run, buoyed you for a moment as you
tried to regain control over your quickly stuttering heartbeat. The kid had gone quiet now, as
if sensing your fear and keeping still so as not be noticed. You couldn’t help but glance down
at him, to meet his wide brown gaze with your own pupils blown wide with fright. Still, as a
flash of concern washed over his expression, you closed your eyes and tried once again to
focus.

They were just headed the same direction as you. One you hit another junction in the
backstreets you'd go one way, and they would go the other. Sleep deprivation and being on
your own with the kid for too long had made you paranoid. Not every shadow was the same
darkness as the Black Sun. Some things were just coincidences.

Yet tried as you may to tell yourself that, you couldn't shake the feeling of a pair of eyes
locked onto your back, boring holes into the nape of your neck. The idea that this was simply
someone passing you seemed to erode with each minute of their slow, deliberate foot falls
behind you.

As you turned a corner onto an empty side-street you prayed the person would go the other
direction and leave both you and the kid alone. However, after about twenty steps you heard
them pause at the junction, then resume their walk behind you. A sick, dark uncertainty
twisted your gut and made the strength momentarily ease from your grip on the sling holding
the toddler.

You were being followed.

It was undeniable at this point. Yet you didn't dare turn around to confront your pursuer. The
moment you did they might charge you, might come at you with a weapon or attempt to
attack you or steal the kid. No, the most important goal was to get away, to lose them and
hide somewhere until it was safe. You knew this ritual, having practiced it for years as a
child. Escape, survival; These were elements that you had claimed as your own years ago.



You used that thought to steady yourself, let it weigh in your lungs as you inhaled, then
exhaled deeply as you centered and regained your focus. They had made a mistake by trying
to tail you. Even injured, unarmed, and without allies, this was a test to your own strengths.
You knew this game, one of survival that you couldn't afford to lose.

So, as you passed another side street you ducked quickly into the shadows, hurrying your gait
to a limping trot to try and outpace the one chasing you. To their credit, they seemed to catch
one quickly, hurrying their own steps to try and catch up. Even then they were slow, and by
the time they reached the passage you had darted down you were beyond their sight.

You veered left at the next intersection, then cut a path past some garbage bags up a small
alleyway. All the while you grit your teeth, ignoring the sharp jabbing pain of your leg injury
racing up to your hip and leaving a crick in your step. Yet even as you tried to ignore it, the
pressure of pursuit wore down on the injury, making your senses alight with pain.

The person behind you, slow as they were, didn't let go of your trail easily. Almost as if they
could see your footprints, you could hear them round each corner and shuffle through piles of
debris to follow you.

You didn't know how they could do it, how they could pick up your scent so easily. It didn't
matter. It was clear now that you were the target they were after. What remained to be seen
was if they were Black Sun, Police, an Imperial agent, or just some wandering criminal who
saw you and the kid as an easy target. Either way the fright of being pursued or being chased
by an unknown predator, one who you couldn't lose despite the number of senseless turns and
winding movements you used to confuse them, heightened all your senses with terror.

Yet it was exactly those twisting paths that eventually confused you instead. These weren't
the streets of Kaddak that you had memorized by heart, the same ones that had sheltered you
in their shadows and hid you from danger. This was Coruscant, the endless city that never
sleeps. In trying more and more desperately to lose the person following you, you had
unwittingly woven a web for you yourself to be ensnared in.

So, when you round a corner, only to be met with a dead-end, you knew it was over.

The impregnable, towering durasteel wall loomed over you, casting you in its shadow void of
the flashing colorful lights of the neon walkways high above. For a moment you could help
but stare up into the endless void of the Coruscant underworld, as if falling upwards into the
luminous abyss.

Then you came crashing back down, pulled back by the gravity of the situation you found
yourself in. Now cornered, unarmed, injured, and out of options, you spun towards the
entrance of the dead-end you had entered. The footsteps echoed clearly beyond the faint din
of traffic above, heavy and intent on finding the place you had scurried to.

Thinking quickly, you knelt as much as you could to carefully help the kid out of his carrier.
The toddler looked up at you, his little green brow wrinkling in distress. You suspected your
face looked much the same, lips tight in concern and determination. Still, you tried to
summon a smile to reassure the kid.



"Listen." You spoke quickly, voice soft for only him to hear. "I'm going to get us both out of
this. But if something happens, if you see the chance, you run. Okay?" You didn’t miss the
crack of fear in your voice despite your attempt at speaking calmly, and watched as the light
of fear flashed across the kid’s eyes.

Again, the kid whined. Instead of running to hide, however, he simply clung to your shin with
tiny green claws, burrowing his face into your pants leg.

You felt your heart crack.

There wasn't any time to comfort him, however. Instead, you dug into your pocket for the
metal skewers of the food you had stolen, gripping them in between your knuckles in a
desperate attempt for a weapon. Then, you turned your attention to the mouth of the
alleyway, face hard and stance ready.

You didn't have to wait long.

The hulking shadow from earlier appeared. First, the stranger's hand braced on the corner of
the alleyway, slowly pulling the rest of his broad figure into view. In the darkness cast by the
shadow of the building behind you it was hard to make out anything other than his figure.
You could see his height, his wide shoulders, and a glance of his equipment. He easily
dwarfed you, a fact that made your blood run cold at the thought of trying to physically
overpower such an opponent.

Yet as he continued forward, you could sense something wasn't right.

His breathing was ragged, torn in his chest. The hand you had seen at first was now used to
prop himself against the wall of the alleyway, figure hunched as if he was trying to summon
oxygen into his rasping lungs. When he saw you his steps stuttered, feet briefly tripping over
each other in his attempt to reach you.

Your first thought was that the man was a drunk, or perhaps a vagrant who had fallen too
deep into the spice dens for his own good. Yet as your eyes grew accustomed to the darkness,
senses heightening with adrenaline, you could begin to make out other features.

Pauldrons adorned his shoulders, and as you looked closer you could see a chest plate, and
beyond that, armor. Yet the thing that made your eyes go wide and your jaw go slack wasn't
any of that.

It was the T-shaped visor, tinted dark as the void between stars and glinting with the neon
lights above.

You felt your stance ease. Not with relief, but shock and confusion. The man, no, the Mando
before you, wheezing and weak as he was, looked to you with a ragged breath rattling his
chest.

You blinked twice, still unable to process what you were seeing. Still, you took a single step
forward, arms gently raising up as if to help him as you offered a name.



"...Paz?"

The Mando looked up at you, silhouette hunched over with trembling legs. You could hear
him inhale, could hear the oxygen scrape the hard inside of his lungs.

"C-Cuyan." He spoke, the Mando'a name cracked with pain.

Then promptly collapsed in on himself, hand slipping from the wall as he fell onto the hard
concrete and crumpled into stillness.

Chapter End Notes

HA. You didn't really think I was going to kill Paz so easily, did you? No, of course not.
Paz is now exactly where he needs to be in this story, though he is in pretty bad shape.

Chapter 27: Part Twenty-Seven: An Ally
Chapter Summary

Somehow, you struggled to your feet, standing over Paz so that you blocked him with
your body. Though you didn’t truly have anything to defend yourself or him with, and
on top of that struggled to even remain standing as a result of your battered and bruised
limbs, you braced yourself, nonetheless. Eyes blazing, drawing yourself up to your full
height, hands held in front of you, you directed your attention to the alleyway entrance,
ready for a fight.

Yet it never came. The footsteps you heard only moment ago crept closer, slowing and
placing themselves delicately against the pavement so as to not attract attention. With
every heartbeat you could hear boots slide against the slick concrete, dust and grime
crunching under them as they drew closer still. With your focus held rapt by the pursuer,
you could hear every shuffle and step as they slowly sidled up to the corner.

There, they peeked around the corner, and upon seeing your hostile stance and
malevolent stare, quickly ducked back out of sight.

“Who are you?!” You barked, voice hoarse. “Come out!”

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

"Oh stars."

The words whispered past your lips, intended as a gasp of fear, and now coming as a sigh of
relief and bewilderment. The man who you were so afraid had tracked you and the child to
take you as Black Sun hostages, to attack you, or even worse, had ended up being an ally. Yet
your relief was short lived, as the Mandalorian before you collapsed and curled in on himself
due to the weight of his injuries. Even steps away the acrid, sour smell of blood flooded
through your nostrils.

Paz lay face down in the alleyway at your feet, one gloved hand still clutched to his side as he
remained crumpled and still. You could see a section of his chest plate scorched black by
some type of ammunition, more than likely cracking a rib and causing him great pain.
Underneath, his flight suit was stained a blotchy wet red in sections, shrapnel embedded in
his right shoulder. Yet despite his wounds you could hear him wheeze a heavy breath under
his helmet, an indication that he was alive, if only just barely.

Yet your mind was focused less on his state of injury and more on one overshadowing
question.



What had happened?

A thousand possibilities raced through your thoughts, each as terrifying as the last. The
Covert had been attacked while you were gone, Paz was one of the few survivors. Or
somehow, he had followed you into the lower levels but had been caught by the Black Sun.
Maybe he was patrolling and was ambushed, cornered, and forced to leave his patrol group
behind. Each scenario ended with him dying at your feet, unable to care for himself due to his
grievous wounds.

That only left one question.

Where was Din?

Was he not far behind? Searching for Paz just as he was searching for you and the child? Or
perhaps he too had been injured and was forced to hide in the lower levels like his comrade.
Maybe he had been forced to retreat to the covert and abandon his mission of searching for
you both.

Or, in the worst case...

You shook your head, damp hair flying in your face. The motion alone made your vision
spin, your earlier head injury dizzying your sight. Now wasn't the time to panic. You couldn't.
Paz was gravely injured and you needed to help.

You took several rushed steps forward, falling to your knees in front of Paz and stifling a
shiver of pain that the motion brought forth to your own injuries. Your crooked knee seized
for a moment before settling once more, aching muscles jostled by you rushing towards the
Mandalorian.

"Paz." You spoke, voice suddenly hoarse with fear. You reached out your hands hesitantly
before splaying your fingers over his armor, pushing him just enough for him to roll over
onto his back. Yet that didn't stir him, the hand that had clutched his side now falling limp
next to him.

You felt a cold ball of fear settle in your stomach, swallowing reflexively as your eyes
flickered to his limp arm. Yet again, you tried to rouse the warrior, shaking him by his chest
plate.

As you did that the sound of distant debris clutter greeted your ears, and your head whipped
towards the noise, trying to peer around the dark of the alleyway entrance.

You weren’t alone.

"Paz!" You tried again, turning back to the Mando with your voice becoming desperate. "Paz,
please, wake up!"

Yet the Mando remained still, and as you bent your head to listen to the heartbeat echoing
past his armor you could hear his breath strained in his chest, choked like a broken exhaust
pipe.



You sat up abruptly, hands shaking now. His injuries were clearly worse than you had
thought. What you assumed were exterior wounds penetrated deeper. Something had broken
inside him, and you had no way to tell, no way to stem the pain or the blood.

You could hear footsteps now, and you turned once more, where a shadow fell against the
grime-streaked wall, leaning towards you and the fallen Mando you knelt beside.

“Who’s there!?” You called, hating the way your voice wavered in fear. You straightened,
trying to peer through the shadows at the silhouette of the figure who crept closer to your
hiding place. With your hands bracing yourself delicately on Paz’s chest, you arched to look
at whatever potential assailant lurked in the darkness.

He had been followed, you realized belatedly. By whom, you did not know. Yet something,
someone had pursued him through the dark streets to where he had fallen here beside you.
The possibilities of this realization made your muscles go taut with fear, eyes wide and body
bracing for an incoming attack.

Somehow, you struggled to your feet, standing over Paz so that you blocked him with your
body. Though you didn’t truly have anything to defend yourself or him with, and on top of
that struggled to even remain standing as a result of your battered and bruised limbs, you
braced yourself, nonetheless. Eyes blazing, drawing yourself up to your full height, hands
held in front of you, you directed your attention to the alleyway entrance, ready for a fight.

Yet it never came. The footsteps you heard only moment ago crept closer, slowing and
placing themselves delicately against the pavement so as to not attract attention. With every
heartbeat you could hear boots slide against the slick concrete, dust and grime crunching
under them as they drew closer still. With your focus held rapt by the pursuer, you could hear
every shuffle and step as they slowly sidled up to the corner.

There, they peeked around the corner, and upon seeing your hostile stance and malevolent
stare, quickly ducked back out of sight. There they remained, pausing there as they tried to
consider their options. You only received a glimpse of their face, eyes flashing in the
darkness for the briefest of moments. They vanished just as quickly, and had you blinked you
would have never seen them at all. You could feel your shoulders tremble, both from the
stress of potential confrontation and strain on your fatigued, sleep deprived body.

“Who are you?!” You barked, voice hoarse. “Come out!”

The person didn’t respond, shadowing themselves in the dark of the alleyway out of sight.
You half expected them to respond, or even call out back to you. Yet instead they did neither,
and all at once you heard them bolt from their hiding place, steps fading. After moment of
surprise, you bolted after them, skidding to a stop in front of the alleyway entrance and
narrowly avoiding a pile of trash debris. There you saw the figure race out of sight, ducking
around a corner and out of your line of sight.

The air in your lungs released with a loud whoosh, straining the injury there cracked against
your ribs but loosening your shoulders in the act.



Whoever they were, you had no doubt that they’d be back, likely with whoever they were
running back to. What that meant for you, you could only begin to guess. It wouldn’t be
pleasant, which meant you had to get out of here as soon as possible, with Paz and the child
in tow.

You turned your gaze back to the Mando, only to find that his chest was rising shallowly, his
breath stuck somewhere in his chest and clogged with a damp, wet sound. Instantly you felt
the fear in your blood spike once more, eyes wide and veins freezing with the icy grip of
terror. In a heartbeat you were back at Paz’s side, hands grasping the edges of his chest plate
in an effort to rouse him.

"Paz!" You gasped, trying once more to shake him, to no avail. Your voice was high in your
throat now, choked with terror at the idea that this man would die right in front of your eyes,
and that you'd be unable to prevent it.

You didn't know what to do, terror quickly engulfing your sense of logic with dark shadows
and making your desperate voice seem like the only one in the whole universe. Paz was
going to die, his final words the name Din had bestowed upon you. You didn't deserve them,
not when you had barely known him and had yet to learn anything about him.

It took you a moment, your own breath rising quickly into stuttering gasps of fear, but
eventually you managed to drag yourself back from full-fledged panic with clawing hands.

You had to do something, anything more than simply vainly trying to shake him awake as his
heartbeat dipped low in his chest. Even if you failed, the fact that you tried meant that
perhaps you'd be able to forgive yourself for not doing enough.

With your fingers now curled against his beskar cuirass, you forced the air in your throat to
even out, closed your eyes as you recentered yourself.

First things first. You had to get his armor off to survey the full damage of his external
injuries. Slowly, your fingers began searching along the sides of his chest plate for the
grooves leading towards the clasps. Sure enough, you found the buckles situated at his
shoulders, and quickly your shaking hands reached to undo them. From there you were
somehow able to shimmy the plating away from Paz's body and remove the pieces of his
armor atop his chest and stomach to reveal his flight suit.

There, you froze, breath catching as your eyes fell upon the wide dark stain that began at his
right shoulder and bled down towards his stomach.

There was so much blood.

Scarlet seeped past the pale fabric of Paz's flight suit, so dark it was nearly black in places.
Like a map it chartered a course from his shrapnel laden shoulder down past his sternum and
towards his ribs. A glance down at your hands proved that it was stained as well, and the
sight alone nearly overwhelmed you.

"By the stars." You heard yourself mutter, but even then it felt as if your voice was light years
away, muffled by the rapid staccato of your heartbeat.



Again, your thoughts strayed, teetering on the cliff of overwhelming panic at the thought that
Din too had suffered such injuries, or possibly even worse. Yet even so you managed to
swallow back the lump of fear in your throat, trying to focus even as your thoughts grew hazy
with frantic terror at the edges.

Your hands instead reached for the section of the flight suit torn by the shrapnel in Paz's
shoulder, and with a tough tug and a rip you exposed the flesh underneath. Past the mar of
blood you could make out silvery scars from battles past laced across a dark shoulder, taut
muscle now limp as Paz remained still. You could feel the wetness on your fingers as you
traced the wounds in the dim light, trying to remove what larger shards you could.

Yet as you did you could feel blood gush gently force once more, staining your hands a deep
red and catching on your clothes. Now feeling the mocking laughter of death whisper in your
ears, you desperately tried to stem the flow from the gashes in Paz's shoulder, still feeling the
blood ooze between your fingers. Paz's rattling breath under his helmet had ceased to a dull
shiver now, and despite the warm scarlet between your hands he felt oddly cool to the touch.

"No." You croaked, eyes wide and frantic. "No, no no no no please, Paz, wake up! Paz,
please, please-" You babbled, feeling your eyes grow hot with tears.

"Not like this." You thought desperately. "Please, not this."

You didn't notice the figure that had toddled to your side as soon as you collapsed to your
knees next to Paz. So focused were you on trying something, anything to help the Mando that
you failed to recognize the worried sounds of the child at witnessing your distress and Paz's
bruised and broken figure. Yet now that same small figure reached out, straining to reach
your hands pushing down on the blood flow against Paz's shoulder.

Your concentration was broken upon seeing the child rest his small, three clawed hand atop
yours, his hand too, coming away red. For a moment you tried to shoo him, not wanting him
to see such a horrid, gruesome scene. Except then you caught his gaze, breath pausing in your
throat as you saw the fear fade from his expression, eyes closing in a strange serenity as his
hand connected with yours.

The moment you felt his touch, it was as if the sound around you had been sucked into
silence, like the vacuum of space swallowing all noise and light. Time seemed to slow, and
the heartbeat beneath Paz's chest and the thrum of Coruscant evened out, drawing long and
deep against your senses. The air around you hummed with energy, and for a moment you
felt almost weightless, like you could float upwards into the sky far far above you three, body
cradled by the atmosphere and hovering in the clouds between the planet's artificial surface
and the void of space.

And somehow, the thrum of Paz's life beneath your fingers and the drum of Coruscant began
to synchronize, their sounds intertwining and singing a soft, winding tune against the dark
heavens and twinkling stars high above. You could feel your own heartbeat rushing in your
ears, but the sound was slow like ocean waves crashing against a gentle shore.

The fear that had gripped you so ferociously now faded with a distant sigh, falling away like
a veil lifted away from your face. In its place there was peace, harmony, a balance between



the terrible fate that beckoned Paz and the two hands that held him back from it's inevitable
grasp. You could feel that balance engulf you, could feel it tap into a part of yourself you
didn't know existed, strengthen the sinew of your muscles and the marrow in your bones.

It lay in the child too. If you were a bright beam, glowing from the essence that had washed
over you, then the child was a supernova, all-consuming and casting your own glow in
shadow compared to his radiance. There was a vibration in his presence that, if you focused
on it, threatened to drown you with its force.

And if you extended your senses, reached out, you could feel that essence channeled through
you, beginning in a low hum and climbing with each note, weaving a symphony of light and
energy that sang trough your veins and past your fingertips, down into the thick ooze of blood
that coated your palm. There it spread across Paz's skin, down into his chest where it wove an
impossible tapestry, threading together the brokenness into something whole once more.

How, you did not know. Yet you could feel it, could feel the stem of blood ease and shrink
backwards, the grooves of ripped flesh mend under the pads of your fingers. That energy that
had begun as a low hum, a breathy sigh now increased, notes rising as you strained to listen,
trying to understand the voiceless words spoken therein.

Yet before you could begin to comprehend, could feel the beautiful yet inexplicable harmony
that flowed from the child through you to Paz, it sang a final, high dazzling note before
fading into silence.

In the brief moment before the sound and weight of the Coruscant underworld came crashing
back into you, you swore you could hear an unknown but familiar name echo out against the
quiet.

It was gone before you could grasp it, fading like smoke through your touch.

Then, as if you had been dropped off the side of a building, the silence came to a deafening
end as sound and the gravity of your surroundings crashed back into your senses.

You fell backwards onto your rear as if you had been shocked, chest heaving with the breath
you didn't know you had been holding. Eyes wide, you looked first down at your hand, still
dyed red, then to Paz's form. There you could see the now steady, even rise of his chest, fed
by whatever energy you had just felt course through you. As your eyes lingered on him you
heard a broken groan, followed by a gentle stir of his head.

Your eyes then shot to the smaller figure next to him, slumped by his side with exhaustion.

The child's ears drooped low, head bent in fatigue as if he hadn't slept for days. You picked
yourself up, scooting quickly over to him just as he slumped forward, a small whine of
weariness echoing forth from his tiny form. You caught him as he did so, feeling the weight
of his tiny body sag into your lap.

A brief flash of fear ran through you, but as you turned the child over to examine him, you
could tell that he was uninjured. Instead, the child seemed to be simply at rest, dozing into



your arms as if he had tired himself playing. As if sensing your hold on him, he snuggled into
your arms, a small sound of sleep murmured into your ears.

You looked at him in wonder, lips parted in awe at what you had just experienced.

Never in your life had you seen or felt anything remotely similar to what had happened.

It was as if some power had been laying dormant within the child's tiny body all this time,
and with a single touch it had exploded into existence, weaving an energy through your body
and into Paz's, mending the things that were broken and strengthening the damage there.

You couldn't comprehend how such a massive power could manifest itself in a being so
small, so delicate and helpless. As if he could channel the radiance of the stars the child had
reached out and healed Paz, and in doing so had seemingly mended your injuries as well.
How, you could only begin to guess.

Your thoughts were interrupted by a stiff groan beside you, and you turned to see Paz stir, the
hand that had previously lain limp now raising itself to where the previous injury had been.
There, it groped for the pain that had been present until only moments ago. When it became
clear to him that his armor, and what was more, the source of his hurt was gone, he lifted his
head from the ground, and in the motion caught your wide-eyed gaze.

"Wha-" He started, voice still hoarse and uncomprehending. "You...Cuyan?"

You felt the breath you had been holding whoosh past your lips in a huge sigh of relief.

"Paz." You spoke, and your voice felt dry in your throat, cracked from the fear that had held it
so tight.

Paz continued to hold your gaze, and you were sure that beneath his visor he was struggling
to understand what had just happened, same as you.

"Did-" He began, but his voice too, was strained. He paused, swallowing before continuing.
"That...did you you...?"

You understood his question even if the words weren’t clear. So, you shook your head in
reply, feeling water flick away from your wet strands.

"No." You returned, still holding the child against your chest. You turned your gaze to him,
adjusted him ever so slightly so as to not disturb his slumber. "It...it was him."

Paz followed your gaze, and he too paused there, asking of himself the same questions that
had occurred to you. How did something so helpless manage to accomplish something so
grand, so mysterious and strange?

"The child?" He asked, and you nodded without breaking your gaze upon the toddler's dozing
face. "How?"

Again, you shook your head. "I...don't know." You confessed. "I've...never seen or felt
anything like it before."



You let your fingers trace the child's wrinkled forehead, touching the soft skin there and
soothing any would-be nightmares.

You had so many questions. Was this something that beings only in this child’s unknown
species was able to do? If he could accomplish such feats as a mere toddler, what else might
he be able to accomplish as he grew? How had he known to do such a thing despite his young
age?

…Who was he?

Yet eventually your previous thoughts resumed once more, and you turned again to Paz in
wide eyed fright.

"Din." You spoke, voice breathless and oddly hopeful. "Is he...?"

Paz regarded you for a moment, as if he were engaged in a one-sided conversation by
himself. With each passing moment you felt your chest seize, the clench of fear bubble up
your throat with an all-encompassing panic.

Finally, Paz seemed to come to a conclusion, leaning up and eventually bracing himself on an
elbow to better face you.

"We were separated." He spoke, and you watched him with an expression full of concern.
"We were searching for you and the child, and were ambushed by the Black Sun. I told him
to leave me behind, and he escaped."

You felt he air in your chest seize, a hesitant hope blooming there as you processed Paz's
words.

"So, he's...alive?" You asked, voice barely above a murmur, as if daring to speak the sentence
aloud would make it not come true.

Paz nodded.

Something broke inside of you then, and instead of a soft sigh it felt as if you had dropped
something delicate, listened to it shatter on the floor. The fear, the panic and terror that you
had held so close to your heart broke apart into pieces, making it fracture into a sob within
your throat. Before you could stop them, wet heavy tears grew in the corner of your eyes.
Without warning they spilled down your cheeks, streaking the dust that had collected there
from your journey in the underground. Several caught on your chin, dripping onto the child’s
clothes. When they did, coloring several wet droplets against his rough-hewn garments, you
curled around him as if doing so could protect him, and comfort yourself.

You tried to hold the tears back, embarrassed that you would lose your composure in front of
the battle hardened Mando. Yet the more you tried the more the sob cracked in your throat,
escaping as a weak sound against the hum of Coruscant. It was as if the stress, the fear, the
panic, and despair of your circumstances had finally shattered something inside of you,
breaking your will and momentarily manifesting as the sounds of your cries against a
dawning sky.



As ashamed as you were to break down in front of Paz, you couldn't help but feel an
overwhelming relief at this news and consequent turn of events.

Din was alive. You knew that now. He was alive, he was looking for you, he was determined
to find you. His brother already had, and now that he was here you three could finally orient
yourself and find a way back to the surface towards the covert once more. There you would
reunite you and the child with Din, feel his warm embrace one more, and hold him fast as
though all the power in the galaxy could never separate you again.

Paz sat silently to your side, and as you began to collect yourself again you glanced at him,
finding that he had averted his gaze awkwardly to allow you a little privacy. In the time it
took you to empty yourself of your cries he had gathered the chest plate you had taken,
fingers absently fastening it back onto his broad front.

"Sorry." You muttered at last, using the back of your hand to wipe your face. It was wet,
messy and thick with tears. For a moment you wished you could wash your grimy hands,
splash water onto your hot eyes and warm cheeks.

"No apologies needed." Was Paz's only answer, voice deeper now that he too had collected
himself in recovering from his injuries. You couldn’t help but feel a small, grateful smile tug
at the corner of your mouth, even though Paz refused to look at you just yet.

 

Wiping the remainder of your tears, you finally turned to face Paz properly. Then, he too sat
to face you, and for a moment you felt a ripple of discomfort that came with unfamiliarity
cross the space between you.

Just as you began to speak, Paz's voice interrupted you.

"The thug in the hideout." He spoke, voice rumbling in his chest. "He said you stole a
speeder, that it crashed somewhere in the lower levels."

You blinked, understanding the unspoken question in his words, the same as the one you had
for him. How did you get away?

"I managed to grab the controls but-" A warm blush crawled across your face. "I...don't know
how to pilot and it spun out of control. I managed to jump with the kid onto a walkway and
got pretty beat up in the process. I've been down here ever since, lost and trying to find a way
back."

Paz nodded, head tilting as he considered your words. In his next words you felt your eyes
flash to him, wide and startled.

"The man you were with, the one who kidnapped you, did you kill him?"

The question caught you off guard, shoulders hiking up in a flinch under Paz's heavy stare.
Yet soon you averted your gaze, grimacing at the memory.



You hadn't...truly meant to kill the man. The only person you had ever killed was the
Clawdite on Rishi, and that was in a moment of panicked self-defense and a desperate bid to
save Din's life.

Yet the image of the Pantoran's eyes, wide and flashing with a horrifying moment of
understanding, haunted the back of your thoughts. When you had kicked him, it was merely
to get him away from the controls. Yet instead he had careened over the side, back bowing as
he hit the edge of the speeder and arm still reaching out as he fell in the abyss.

You let your eyes close for a moment, hearing the man's cry fade into the deafening current of
traffic before opening them again to level your gaze at Paz.

"Yes."

Paz let his stare weigh on you, and you noticed that not for the first time, he seemed to be
weighing you in his thoughts, trying to come to conclusions based off your answers and the
way you carried yourself. To what ends you didn't know, but being the subject of his scrutiny
made you squirm a little under his gaze.

"Good." He concluded after a moment, and if you listened carefully you could almost hear a
modicum of respect in his voice.

"And you?" You questioned, to which Paz responded with a tired sigh under his helmet.

"I don't remember much." He replied, shifting so he sat and propped up his knee in front of
him to rest his arm, his other leg stretched out and opposite hand balancing his weight. You
could see him flex his hand, trying to regain the feeling there.

"Djarin left me beside a trash heap. In trying to escape I fell into it, and some of the debris
fell on me. It must have kept me hidden from the other Black Sun members, because when I
woke up they were gone. After that..." He waved a hand. "It becomes hard to remember. I
was trying to retrace my steps to the covert, but in doing so managed to get even further
down into the lower levels. I suspect the blood loss had something to do with my poor
judgement."

You listened with rapt attention, trying to focus on Paz's words and extract any detail you
could that might help you three back to the covert.

"I tried to hide once foot traffic picked up, knowing I'd be an easy target for any wandering
gang members. That's when I saw you, but I was too weak to call out." He went on, then let
his voice trail off.

You blinked at him, trying to understand what had distracted him, until-

"I apologize for scaring you." He spoke, and this time his voice was softer, regretful even.
The unexpected gentleness of it surprised you. "It must have been terrifying to be chased the
way I pursued you."

You felt your lip’s part in astonishment, but then summoned a small, bashful smile.



"No apologies needed." You returned, repeating the words he had offered you a few minutes
before. Paz huffed a laugh, and the lightness in your chest seemed to grow with the sound.

The feeling of relief swelled once more in your chest, and for a moment your previous fears
of not being able to reunite with Din, of failing to protect the child, and of not being able to
survive this turn of events yourself were forgotten. Your circumstances were still not ideal,
lost and within enemy territory.

But now? You had someone Din trusted, another Mandalorian to help make your path clear.
Now that Paz was no longer injured as a result of the child's mysterious powers, he could
help guide you three out of the underworld and back to the person who had grown to be your
home.

"What now?" You asked, feeling your chest lightened with the buoyant feeling of optimism.

Yet all at once you remembered the strange figure hovering at the edge of the alleyway, the
one who had vanished like smoke when you had noticed their presence. Whoever they were,
it was clear they had followed Paz, and that in the Mando’s distorted mind sickened by his
wounds that Paz hadn’t noticed them.

“Wait. There’s something you should know.” You spoke, the glint of hope in your eyes
dulling to a sharp focus, training in on the ‘T’ of Paz’s visor. Paz’s head turned towards once
more, averting his gaze from observing the dank corners of the alleyway.

You swallowed, the anxiety in your throat settling in your stomach before you continued.
“You were followed.”

Instantly Paz’s shoulders tightened, the hand splayed across his knee curling into a fist. Yet
he listened as you went on.

“Someone was tailing you. I…don’t know who it was, but I have a feeling they were with the
Black Sun.” For a moment you were distracted by a small slumbering murmur from the child
in your arms, and you held him a little tighter as you continued. “They ducked out of sight as
soon as they saw me, and when I tried to confront them, they ran.”

Paz hummed after a moment, the sound more akin to a growl than anything else.

“An informant.” He spoke, voicing your own suspicions. “They’ll be back, with more to
follow.”

Then, with a small grunt, the Mandalorian warrior rocked to his feet. He took a moment to
take stock of himself, observing the disappearance of his injuries and casting another,
lingering glance at the toddler asleep in your arms. As he silently considered your words his
fingers fidgeted with the clasps of his armor. From where you were seated Paz appeared as
giant as a Bantha, towering above you. You thought Mando was a little tall, but next to Paz
he seemed about as short as an Ewok. You had to tilt your head up to look at him.

Yet you didn’t feel scared. More than that, you felt an odd sense of comfort at being close to
someone who you had formed a sense of trust with, an ally who would prove capable in



helping you back home.

"There's going to be a lot of Black Sun members in between us and the Covert." Paz spoke,
voice low in warning. His eyes focused back on you. "Can you fight?"

You gave Paz a grim nod, holding the sleeping child in your arms with a delicacy contrasted
to your serious expression.

Paz let his gaze weigh heavy on you, the black of his visor reflecting the neon lights from
above. Then, he offered a hand to you to help you stand. You blinked at it for a moment, a
little surprised at the gesture before taking it. Paz hauled you to your feet, and with his next
words he spoke low, voice rumbling in his chest.

"Then we fight our way out."
