Chapter 28: Part Twenty-Eight: The Underground
Chapter Summary

"Do you trust me?" Paz asked, voice dipping low for you to hear. The sound was
practically a growl in his chest, demanding an answer as the enemies around you closed
in.

Time seemed to slow, each moment passing by in a sudden absence of the space around
you, narrowing in only on Paz’s t-shaped visor. Your heart fluttered in your chest, up
into your throat where it threatened to break look with a whimper of fear. You forced it
down, felt it sour in your stomach. Yet you looked up at Paz, seeing your own frightened
gaze reflected back at you, then hardened into an attempt at courage.

"Yes."

Chapter Notes

See end notes for special announcement

Warnings for being shot at, fear of heights, fear of falling, and mild claustrophobia

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Paz had been right.

The scout that had tailed him into the alleyway had indeed come back with company, and
now a torrent of gang members were raining hell down on you both. The sounds of blaster
fire seemed to make the ground beneath you tremble, sending shockwaves through your feet
and all the way down to the molten heart of Coruscant itself. You could barely hear yourself
think, let alone breath in the never-ending destruction that fell all around you.

It had all happened so quickly.

You and Paz had been trying to figure out exactly which level you were on, which may have
given you a clue as to how far you needed to ascend to get back to the Covert. In the maze of
the underworld, it was entirely possible to climb too far and ascend past the compound
without knowing it. Doing so would mean running the risk of exposing yourselves to the eyes
of the Coruscant authorities. Without papers or any type of identification, you, the child, and
Paz would find yourselves quickly out of options and possibly in the scrutiny of anyone with
ties to the Imperial Remnants. Yet any violence you perpetuated towards the police in trying



to free yourselves would not only garner more attention, it would also mean drawing prying
eyes back to the covert, making the other Mandalorians there a target. Which meant, despite
its dangers, the underground was safer than the surface.

Yet between the piles of debris, the graffitied walls, winding pathways, and blocked streets, it
had become increasingly difficult to navigate the underworld. It seemed every set of stairs
you climbed seemed to invert itself, leading you further, deeper into the intestines of the
ecumenopolis. The residents who had traveled the streets beside you aimlessly seemed to
evaporate like ghosts the farther you traveled, vanishing away into the shadows like mist.
There they watched you three pass by with weary gazes that had never seen the stars from the
endless depths of the planet. You wondered if some of them had ever seen the sun at all. You
could tell they were there, lurking, but every glance would make shapes dart out of the corner
of your eyes as if you were seeing things.

The child had continued to rest, exhausted by the great feat of healing both you and Paz.
Though neither of your injuries had been completely recovered, it had been enough to give
you both the strength to continue onwards in a chance to escape the shadows of the
underworld. You switched between carrying the child and tucking him against your chest in
the carrier, making sure he was soft and comfortable against you while he slumbered so that
you could focus on the path ahead.

So, you walked for what seemed like a full rotation, following behind Paz's broad back as he
marched forward relentlessly. As impressed as you were with his stamina, you had more than
once asked to take a moment to rest. He didn't speak much, offering only the bare minimum
of what needed to be said as he relented. Yet you noticed the way he did stand guard while
you caught your breath, resting your arms from carrying the child and switching the make-
shift carrier from one shoulder to the other. Despite the situation, you took great comfort in
knowing that you had an ally to keep watch while you collected yourself.

Yet one fact remained, and that was that Paz didn't trust you. He put his faith in you enough
to watch his back as you both continued onwards, and extended the same courtesy to you, but
made it a point not to make any more conversation than strictly necessary. In a way you
couldn’t really blame him. After all, to him you were a stranger, and worse than that, an
outsider. Your unfamiliarity with the ways of Mandalorians meant that Paz's confidence in
you only ran so far.

Yet there had been a moment, back when you both had crouched in the alleyway where he
had collapsed, where you could feel his eyes boring into you from under his visor, as if he
could somehow discern your nature based on appearances alone. Whatever he had found
there seemed to satisfy him enough to form a tenuous partnership with you, and for that you
were grateful.

There was so much you still wanted to know. You wanted to ask about the Covert, about
Mandalorian culture, about the pieces of your own Mando that you couldn't quite grasp due
to your lack of knowledge. You tried to push them down, reminding yourself that this wasn't
the time, but the queries weighed on you as you walked, your softer footsteps following
closely behind Paz's larger ones.



Yet just as Paz's gloved hand had traced the faded numbers of '1313' on a graffitied wall,
shouts and the sound of rapid footsteps had echoed down the street from the three of you. In a
blink you and Paz were sheltered behind a mountain of debris as what seemed like a dozen
Black Sun members converged to bombard your hiding place.

You held the kid tight in your arms, his still slumbering, pliant body soft against your chest. It
was all you could do to tuck yourself smaller around him, trying to shield him from what
seemed like an unending hail of blaster fire that rang forth from somewhere behind you. You
couldn't see where the shots were coming from, and even if you could, your blaster was long
gone, lost in the hands of one of the Black Sun members who had kidnapped you and the
child.

So, it was all you could do to sit tight and hold the kid fast in your embrace, head down as
Paz tried to return fire.

The Mando was trying to do all he could, but his munitions were limited, having abandoned
his semi-automatic cannon somewhere in the upper levels so he could travel faster. A blaster
pistol was all he had left aside from his vambraces, which seemed to be of little use in this
situation.

"We need to get out of here." Paz called to you over the cacophony. "If we stay, they'll circle
around and close in."

You nodded at him, trying to quell your rushing heartbeat and wild eyes. Despite your panic,
the instinct to survive held fast to your thoughts. Find an escape route. That you were good
at. You could manage that much.

"Go!" Paz barked at you, visor whipping to face you. "I'll be right behind you."

You sprang forth from your hiding spot like a bird in flight, legs unfolding under you and
allowing you to sprint forward beyond the range of the blaster fire. Like prey fleeing through
the woods, you zig zagged beyond the reach of the blaster shots, the bits of debris and grime
crunching under your feet with every heavy footfall. When you reached the end of the street
you skidded around a corner, sending one final glance back towards Paz, who had moved to
follow you, setting the debris pile aflame to cover his tracks.

You resumed your path, scanning your surroundings, looking for the path of least resistance
to continue forward. Like a long-forgotten dance, you felt your senses expanding, growing to
encompass the entire maze of broken streets and cluttered back roads before you. The
labyrinth was a deadly one, each turn a potential dead end that could have fatal consequences
if the Black Sun caught you there.

In your arms the child made a small sound, teetering on the edge of wakefulness and trying to
discern why you were hurling yourself forward, trying desperately to escape the danger he
couldn't see. You wished you could will him back to sleep so he wouldn’t wake up to the
scene of violence around him. All the while your eyes roamed frantically over the broken
streets and alleyways that could offer sanctuary, escape.



There. You would have missed it if your eyes hadn't landed exactly on it. A tunnel, one that
quickly vanished into darkness. If you and Paz hid within it you would be able to not only
lose the Black Sun behind you, but route yourselves to safety within the confines of its
shadows.

You bolted right, nearly tripping in your haste to reach the asylum. You used a hand to right
yourself, just barely avoiding crashing onto the rough cracked walkway. Then, somehow, you
were able to scoot yourself past the trash piles, weaving through and over the litter towards
the empty stretch of road ahead that led to safety.

A rapid series of blaster fire shots told you Paz was not far behind you, likely tracking your
movements via your footprints. You wanted to look behind you, to make sure he was close
by, but knew that your own task was to make sure that the way forward was clear. So, you
continued onwards, legs pumping under you and chest cramping in lack of oxygen.

Yet when you were about a dozen paces away from the tunnel the light illuminated the inside
just enough to see the wall just beyond the entrance, blocking the way.

Then you saw there was no floor.

With a yell of surprise, you skid to a stop just short of the shaft, dust spilling over the edge
and into the tunnel of darkness below you. You couldn't see the bottom save from a dim
orange haze that cast menacing shadows across your expression of despair. The breeze that
hit your face from below stank of rot, an organic waste long since forgotten by the rest of the
planet's inhabitants. A scant few lights flickered, casting hazy shadows down into a never-
ending metal abyss.

Down, deep into the maw of Coruscant.

You teetered away from the edge, nearly landing on your backside as you tried to quickly
back away from the depths. Yet it seemed like the void grabbed at you, trying to sink you
further, deeper into the planet. Even as you stumbled backwards you could still feel the too-
hot wind, smell the horrid stench that poured out from below. You had to find another path,
had to find another way to get away, even as the whisper of whatever lurked below the depths
beckoned to you with a sinister grasp, making it feel as if you dragged forward, downward,
falling endlessly-

Before it could, the world around you seemed to rock with the roar of an explosion behind
you, shattering whatever had tried to ensnare you. You whipped your head towards the sound,
hair flying as you looked with wild eyes. There, you watched as fire curled over the rooftops
of the shantytown like a supernova, the orange combustion spiraling upwards and dissipating.

"Cuyan!"

The shout echoed somewhere behind you, and you turned in full to see the shadow of Paz's
larger form stumbling through the trash in an attempt to reach you. Several shouts echoed
behind him, and you ducked as a red blaster bolt came whizzing over his pauldron. The shot
hit the wall of the abandoned elevator shaft behind you with a resounding clang.



"It's a dead end!" You yelled back to him, trying to ward him away. "We can't!"

Paz didn't respond, fighting his way past the remainder of the debris before jogging over to
you, halfway turned back the way he came to face any incoming attackers.

"What is it?" He asked, and in his voice you could hear the breathlessness, the concentration
of a battle worn soldier.

You gulped, looking up at his large form. "It's...it's an elevator shaft, but it doesn't go up, it
only goes down." Your voice trembled as you spoke, eyes flickering back to where shadows
collected beyond the littered alleyway.

That made Paz turn to you, his focus now on your startled face. You could see him pause,
freeze, consider. Though you couldn't see his expression, you tried to imagine the tight frown
on his lips before he finally spoke.

"Then we go down."

You blinked, expression fading from concern to confusion as you tried to dissuade him.
"Wha- w-wait, HEY!"

Paz bent just long enough to loop one of your arms across the back of his neck, and despite
your protests, then proceeded to lift you from the back of your knees into his hold. Now
carried aloft in his arms, you held the kid tight with the one arm now splayed across the
Mando's nape. Though Paz made a small grunt, he didn't complain about your weight, instead
marching forward towards the gaping entrance of the depths below.

"Hold tight!" He spoke, voice low and tight in his chest.

"Are you sure?!" You practically yelled, holding yourself a little tighter to Paz's broad form
despite your protest at being carried. Your attempts at trying to squirm away ceased as Paz
stopped just short of the edge, the toes of his boots hanging over as the maw glared up at you
with a sinister orange-red mist. You tried to suppress a shiver of fear, wanting nothing more
than to scramble away from the edge.

Yet the shouts of the Black Sun members were getting closer, the sound of breaking glass and
debris reaching your ears as they clambered over the same trash pile you and Paz had passed.

"Do you trust me?" Paz asked, voice dipping low for you to hear. The sound was practically a
growl in his chest, demanding an answer as the enemies around you closed in.

Time seemed to slow, each moment passing by in a sudden absence of the space around you,
narrowing in only on Paz’s t-shaped visor. Your heart fluttered in your chest, up into your
throat where it threatened to break look with a whimper of fear. You forced it down, felt it
sour in your stomach. Yet you looked up at Paz, seeing your own frightened gaze reflected
back at you, then hardened into an attempt at courage.

"Yes." You replied, voice attempting to be firm despite the tremor in your words.



Paz nodded, and if you could have seen past the helmet covering his face, you would have
seen a smile tug at his lips.

"Good."

With that, Paz tucked you tighter against his chest as you did the same to the child in your
arms. He gave a small ‘hup!’ as he jumped. Then you were falling, descending, the torrid
wind whipping your hair and clothes, air rushing deafeningly past your ears. You muffled a
scream, but you were sure that even if it had escaped you, it would be silenced by the gale
around you. Then, over the turbulence, you could hear the sound of something igniting. There
was a small lurch, but soon your speed had reduced to a slow descent as Paz's jetpack flared
to life.

After a moment you opened your eyes, staring up at the ledge you had just leapt from as
several figures leaned over, trying to find your forms in the mist that had enveloped you both.

"Leave them!' You heard a voice call from above, frustrated yet still sinister. "The cthons will
get them."

You couldn't question what exactly the syndicate members referred to as you still clung
tightly to both Paz and the child, sinking further into the abyss. Nor did you want to, fearful
of what horrors lurked well below even the deepest parts of Coruscant you had travelled to so
far. You shut your eyes against the thought, as if removing your sight would also remove their
potential existence.

The aging lights along the wall lit the shaft around you, growing dimmer the further you fell
into the red mist. Whatever had tried to make you teeter over the edge now seemed to
envelop your entire being, calling out with what seemed like a voice that rose and fell with
every unknown word.

Yet the lights slowly began to grow fainter, every moment becoming darker. A horrible part
of you wondered if you'd be sinking forever, that soon enough whatever shadows lurked
around you would swallow you whole, trapping you in the underground so you could never
see the light from the sun again. The blazing sun of Rishi, of Hypori, of the forgotten moon
and even Kaddack seemed a distant memory, flitting across the back of your eyelids with
vague shapes of a time you'd never see again.

Yet you felt Paz's grip on you tighten once more, and though you didn't open your eyes, you
felt him shift, widen his stance as you slowly came to a stop, ground under your feet once
more with a lurch.

You kept yourself curled against Paz's chest, protests against being carried long forgotten.
You tried to imagine it was Din that held you so close, voice murmuring reassurances against
the things you couldn't see. Your arms were shaking. From holding Paz and the child so
tightly, or from fear, you didn't know. So, when Paz released his hold on you, gently
depositing you onto solid ground once more, you tried to catch the shaky gasp of fright that
crawled up your throat with little success. Instead, you stood, holding both the child and
yourself against the smell of organic rot and decay that filled your nose.



"You should see this." Paz murmured, not touching you but remaining still beside you as if
his presence might lend you some type of comfort.

Despite not wanting to see, you allowed one eye to slowly open, gaze then shooting open at
what you saw.

Where you had expected a never-ending corridor of darkness, beasts and unknown creatures
lurking in the shadows, you instead found a startling sight.

The walls were...glowing.

No, it wasn't the walls themselves. It was a collection of tiny, microscopic fungi that grew
from the cracked pipes and up from the deteriorating trash in the tunnel before you, casting
the entire space in a strange orange and red haze. What you had originally mistaken as some
type of toxic mist was in fact the bioluminescence from the fungus. They formed spiraling
patterns against the walls, tiny nodes reaching out and upward like mossy tendrils grasping
for tree-trunks. It was...otherworldly, beautiful and impossibly strange at the same time.

Still, cognizant of the spores they could possibly produce, you tried to cover your nose, using
the fabric of the make-shift carrier to cover the child's face as well.

"They aren't harmful." Paz's voice intoned beside you, and you glanced at him to find his
gaze trained upwards, looking up to a pinprick of light at the ledge you two had come from.
“They eat metal and industrial waste, but they aren’t toxic to other organics.”

Slowly, you lowered your hand from your nose, taking a cautious step close to examine the
strange growth. It pulsed with a faint light from within, remaining still but with the
appearance that somehow it was pushed by an invisible current. Odd, yet strangely
fascinating. For a moment, your fear was forgotten, instead rapt with wonder at another sight
you had never seen before. Like a small flame, the orange glow flickered, casting brightness
against your irises.

"We should get moving." Paz concluded at last, breaking your trance. You glanced at him to
find his gaze return to you. "They'll be guarding that entrance to make sure we don't come
back up."

With that, he brushed past you, boots splashing into puddles that had partially submerged the
grates that paved the walkway ahead. You followed hesitantly, eyes still roaming the tunnel
walls.

"How deep are we?" You wondered aloud, voice echoing slightly in the near empty space.

"Too deep." Paz's grumbled response came from ahead. "We likely fell a dozen levels or so,
we're at or below level 1000."

"Level...1000?" You echoed, turning to cock your head at the back of Paz's helmet.

Paz huffed, and you couldn't tell if his mild frustration was with your lack of knowledge or
with the circumstances in general.



"Coruscant has close to 5000 levels." He explained. "The lower the level, the closer it is to
the galactic core. You probably saw level 5121 when you first arrived. It's the closest thing
Coruscant has to a surface."

You nodded, mulling Paz's explanation over in your thoughts while avoiding a particularly
deep puddle.

"Where is the covert?" You asked and watched as Paz's shoulder sank an inch.

"Level 1325."

You felt a weight drop into your stomach, pulling towards the floor with the heaviness of it.
The fall alone to this level had seemed like an infinity. To think that there was nearly ten
times that much in between you and the covert, between you and Din…

"That's...a very long climb." You replied at last, unable to hide the dejection in your voice.
The child in your arms shifted in his sleep, letting out a small mumble before again growing
still.

"All the more reason to continue forward." Paz returned easily.

You nodded silently from behind him, following the Mando's dimly lit form deeper into the
unknown.

For a while the glow of the strange fungi on the wall continued to light your path, the cracked
and burst lanterns on the wall having long since lost their batteries. Yet soon even they began
to grow dim, plunging you three into even further darkness. Here, miles and miles beneath
the artificial surface of the world, sunlight had stopped reaching this level eons before you
were even a concept in the grand scheme of the universe. The thought made you shudder, the
concept of what darkness lurked below the never ending city a terrifying one.

Paz paused to switch on a light atop his helmet, lighting the path ahead of him. You used the
pause to place yourself beside him, the tunnel having since widened enough to fit you both.
Yet your new pace at his side did nothing to alleviate the odd, heavy silence that fell between
you, filled only by your footsteps across a rugged grate and organic pathway. You scrambled
to try and find a conversation topic, the absence of noise between you unbearable. Yet it
ended up being Paz who spoke first.

"Din said he met you on a waystation in the Kaddak sector."

You glanced at the Mando beside you, having to slightly crane your head to look up at him.
The question caught you somewhat off-guard, mainly for Paz's sudden attempt at
conversation, but also for Din's odd recounting of your meeting to his comrade.

"No-" You started, then bit your tongue remembering the details of your first encounter. The
image of Din, backlit by the cargo lights inside the hold of the Razorcrest, standing
menacingly over you resurfaced in your thoughts. You didn't know how kindly Paz would
take to your explanation of the circumstances that led to your meeting, considering he was
already wary of you. "Well...yes."



Paz leveled a hard, inquiring glance at you, and you averted your own gaze a bit bashfully.

"I actually....was a stowaway on the Razorcrest." You finally admitted aloud after what
seemed like several minutes of silence. "I lived on Kaddak, but got into some trouble with a
gang there, so had to jump planet to avoid getting killed."

"What exactly did you do?" And there was an accusatory tone there, Paz's hackles rising in
automated self-defense. You were almost offended that he assumed you must have done some
terrible misdeed to offend the gang, considering his current experience with their vicious
nature. Yet again, you reminded yourself that it was exactly for that reason, and others, that
Paz likely didn't trust strangers.

"Nothing!" You exclaimed, shooting him a dirty glance, which then sank to look at your feet.
"Well, mostly nothing. I was an errand runner for them up until I became a teenager, and then
I took out some money to start a workshop. When I didn't pay it back on time...they sent a
hunter after me."

You shivered at the recollection of the Trandoshan hunter who chased you through the
market, wounding you and smearing his venomous blood against your scraped skin. "I got on
the first ship I saw taking off, and it just happened to be his."

Paz hummed, sounding almost amused, if not somewhat intrigued. "And Djarin just...let you
accompany him?" He asked, the doubt in his voice clear.

You huffed a sardonic laugh. "Not exactly." The memory of Din shooing you off the
Razorcrest at the way station seemed almost comical in retrospect. Yet you could still
remember the small medpac he tossed you, how the weight of it in your hands made you
smile in relief.

"Odd." Paz mumbled, yet at your confused look he offered no further explanation.

The silence resumed, with little sound in the abandoned corridor save from your footsteps
against the grates and decaying gravel, occasionally splashing into still, dripping pools of
water. The air was damp down here, you noticed. Warm, wet, dark. You wondered that if
somehow there wasn't a scenario that you made it out, if falling asleep forever here would
feel like returning to the womb, ensconced forever in a stillness that you didn't understand.

You gave a small shake of your head, trying to dispel the thought. After all, you were going
to make it out, it was only a matter of time before you got back to Din. That thought alone
made your thoughts begin to churn, looking for something to hold onto in the bitter silence
that fell between you three.

"Din said that he was a foundling." You spoke, attempting to fill the void of sound with a
subject lighter than thoughts of being trapped alive in the underground. "Are you also a
foundling?"

Paz made a small 'pfft' sound, which surprised you, and almost made a smile crawl onto your
lips with how much it seemed out of his character.



"No, I'm of clan Vizsla." He replied, and there was a shift in his voice, less suspicious, more
prideful. "One of the few of my line left."

"Clan?" You echoed, and this time Paz did look at you, studying your face open with
curiosity. The brightness from the light atop his helmet made you blink and squint, to which
he resumed looking forward to the path in front of you.

Paz nodded with a small sound of affirmation. "Different than a house, of which Vizsla is as
well. Mandalorian society is built of them."

This time you couldn't help but let a small smile tug at the corner of your mouth, noticing the
way Paz's demeanor had changed, the way he now spoke with ease of his heritage.

"Can you tell me more?" You asked, and again Paz turned, whipping his head to face you,
only for you to hiss at the glaring brightness of the flashlight.

"Ah, sorry." He mumbled, and the sudden soft, apologetic tone caught halfway in your throat,
sitting there as you mulled over the subtleties of the man who had become your current
companion.

As you continued on, Paz began to explain the answer to your question in detail, voice
amiable and hands loose at his sides. You listened intently, a half-smile on your lips, eyes
tired but friendly as you listened to Paz's commentary on Mandalorian houses, clans,
bloodlines, and the culture that tied them all together like an abstract tapestry. His voice
shifted slowly from serious and suspicious to a soft-spoken enthusiasm that quickly became
contagious.

Your interest in what Paz had to say was spurred on by the fact that Din spoke little of his
culture other than what was strictly necessary. The society of fighting for honor, of claiming
glory, of protecting one's family and passing on skills to the next generation resonate deeply
with what you knew of Din and his commitment to you and the child. Not to mention that
belief extended to others as well, as was seen by his dedication towards locating and rescuing
the village children on Rishi, and then to readily answer Paz's call for him to come to
Coruscant.

You continued to pepper Paz with questions about his heritage, to which he responded with a
subtle but beaming reverence. If it weren’t for the darkness you would have seen the way he
carried himself higher, the way his chest puffed with pride at offering his voice on topics such
as Mandalorian armor, the creed, and even at some points referencing his own clan as being
integral to the history of Mandalore itself. The wary, suspicious and serious Paz from earlier
had faded, replaced by one that radiated admiration for his own culture.

However, like a whisper of something foul against your senses, you heard something that
made you pause. Soon, you stopped, feeling as if…something was wrong. Your sudden halt
in footsteps caused Paz to pause as well, and as he turned to you, his voice trailed off as well.
Upon his glance at your startled, albeit confused face, he shut the light off and plunged you
both into total darkness.



Yet it wasn't as dark as you imagined, and soon your eyes were drawn down a tunnel to your
right, where a warm orange haze flickered at the end of it.

There, cast in horrid shadow against the curved metal wall, lay a lurking figure shuffling in
the darkness.

You felt your stomach seize at the sight. Even despite not being able to see it clearly at a
distance, you could tell that the thing was...wrong. Deformed, changed. With its back
hunched well over its body, pale slimy skin reflecting what small light there was at the end of
the tunnel, and vertebrae clear under its stretched flesh, the thing hissed lowly, head sweeping
towards you.

It had no eyes.

That fact alone made you nearly squeak with fear, but you caught yourself, knowing that
making a single sound might alert the creature to your presence. So, with one of Paz's arms in
front of you, trying to control the shake in your hands, you clamped a palm over your mouth
to stifle any noise that might escape you.

Whatever it was, the strange thing hissed lowly once more, scenting the air before making a
strange clicking sound and vanishing around a corner, ambling on deformed hands and legs.

It wasn't until it was well clear that you turned to Paz, the question in your eyes clear despite
your silence.

"A cthon." He supplied, voice quiet in a warning. "Something that stopped being human eons
ago."

You shivered, following Paz's lead as he crept forward, body low and ready for an attack
from the shadows.

"It's gone. It can't see, so it didn't notice us." He offered at last, keeping his voice low. "Stay
close."

You continued to walk in silence, each step sounding too loud against the void-like silence of
the tunnels. Yet as you pressed onwards, the darkness began to ease, and soon you found
yourself peering into the aging lights of some type of service corridor. Inwardly you breathed
a sigh of relief. Despite enemies still possibly lurking nearby, the presence of man-made
passageways was a small reassurance that you were headed in the right direction.

With the previous conversation abruptly squashed, you blindly attempted to fill the void.

"Do you think the covert is okay?" You asked after what seemed like an hour of silence,
voice still quiet but clear.

Paz took a moment, but ultimately nodded. "I try to think so." He answered. "Between Djarin
and the other warriors, they'll be able to hold off until we arrive."

Then, surprising you, Paz spoke again, his voice a touch softer. "Djarin may be a fool
sometimes, but he's clever, smart. The covert will be fine." In his words he offered his



reassurances to you, but by the sound it almost seemed as if he was speaking to himself,
reminding himself of his trust in the comrade he had sought out the aid of.

You weren't sure if you should be pleasantly surprised or mildly offended on Din's behalf.
Paz's backhanded compliment did, however, make you wonder exactly how much the Mando
knew about your self-proclaimed partner.

"Din isn't a fool." You mumbled, sounding a bit petulant. Yet that only made Paz fail to
contain a small snort of laughter.

"That man is a complete fool.” He replied, bemused. You shot him a small glare, which he
pointedly ignored, continuing. "When you and the child went missing, I had to wrestle him to
not go marching headfirst into Black Sun territory and get himself killed. If that isn’t
foolishness, I’m not sure what is."

You blinked, nearly stopping in your tracks at the image of Din trying to race off in the
direction he had lost you, marching like a one-man army to come find you and the child. The
concept made your chest ache, and for a moment your eyes turned sad as you imagined what
he could possibly be feeling right now, wanting but unable to come find you, and even then
not knowing where to start. If it felt anything like what you currently felt…

Stars, you hoped he was okay.

"He's even more of a fool for being so thick-skulled with how he feels about you."

That made your head snap to Paz's, and in the growing light of the tunnels he too turned
towards you, watching your face momentarily go blank with surprise.

Before you could ask, Paz continued. "It's clear he has feelings for you that go beyond your
'partnership. Yet by the sounds of it that or'dinii doesn't act on it as he should, likely leaving
you wondering about his intentions."

Damn his perceptiveness, you thought sardonically. Still, Paz was right. Din's emotional
wherewithal was frankly...lacking at best. The memories of Din's actions contrasting against
his small moments of vulnerability left a puzzling trail of how he felt about you. From Din's
conflicted emotions after your time on Rishi, of him withdrawing himself rather than face his
growing feelings for you, to him telling you his name and then almost wishing he hadn't, to
his denial that he saved you on Hypori for anything less than a mutual agreement, all of it
coalesced into one large lingering question as to his potentially romantic interactions with
you. Every time you thought you understood, Din would draw himself away, almost as if he
was afraid to admit and act on his feelings towards you.

"Din can be a fool sometimes." You spoke, voice low yet affectionate and breaking the
building gap in conversation. "But he's a good man. He's smart, capable, strong, clever, and
more than that he's...kind."

At those last words you felt a familiar blushing warmth against your chest, mind recalling the
soft moments of Din before he woke the morning after you arrived at his room in the middle
of the night. With his arms wrapped around you, holding you close in his embrace, body



coiled in sleep beside you, the fear of never seeing him again seemed bittersweet. He was so
far away, distanced by miles of winding interconnected levels, hidden pipes, durasteel walls,
streets and abandoned elevator shafts. Yet in your heart he was still just as close, and for a
moment you almost felt as if, through that memory, he was lending you some of his strength
to continue on.

You opened your eyes to see Paz staring at you, observing your gentle smile and hopeful
eyes.

"Never said I disagreed." He concluded at last, then turning to a ladder you hadn't seen until
he had moved. Before you could puzzle the ladder’s odd location in the winding wet tunnels,
Paz climbed to the top to unscrew the hatch there. You stood at the bottom, peering up as Paz
pushed the thing open.

At once a cool blast of air hit your face and hair, ruffling your clothes and making you hold a
hand to look up where Paz had begun to climb through. You had to squint, as suddenly there
was a bright light that framed the Mando's helmet almost like a halo. Once he had climbed
past the hatch, Paz turned to offer you a hand as you too, began to climb after him.

Once there, kneeling before Paz as he did the same for you, he spoke, voice raising above the
sudden gale of wind that muffled the sound.

"You will see him again, of that I can assure you."

With that he stood, pacing past you to the opening of the tunnel. There, endless air spanned
between you and the other side of a grand entrance to the lower depths, one of the boreholes
you and Din had originally traveled to in order to reach the covert. You followed Paz,
footsteps inaudible against the roar of air that rushed past and around you.

Then, as you stepped out of the shadows and looked up, you had to cover your eyes. For
there, at the top of the endless bore hole, was sunlight.

Chapter End Notes

I'm back to a semi-regular updating schedule!

This will be subject to change, however. I'm moving at the end of the months and then
traveling again soon afterwards, so August may be a little iffy in terms of updates.

I've also now moved update days to Sundays, which better fits my schedule.

With all that being said, I want to address some things:

I'm very glad everyone is enjoying this story. I work extremely hard on it, putting up to
8-10 hours in each week to write everything, edit, edit again, and polish it before
posting. I do this because I have fun doing so, and working hard on something that turns
out really well is a very nice feeling.

However, that becomes less so when folks pressure me for updates. This hasn't become



a huge problem yet, but I've noticed a little bit of it and want to nip it in the bud before it
develops further.

It's perfectly fine to say 'I can't wait to see what happens next!' or 'I'm on the edge of my
seat!' It makes me very pleased to see folks are really enjoying this story. But comments
such as 'great, now do the reunion' or 'You aren't updating on time' are stressful to read,
put pressure on me and put a damper on something that is supposed to be enjoyable and
are frankly...a little rude.

I just want to remind everyone that this story, which is now well over the word count of
some well-known fiction books out there, has been written entirely for free and on my
own time. To make demands on it is impolite at best, entitled at worst. I know none of
these comments come from a place of hostility, but it is important to keep these things in
mind before posting stuff like that. If you've done this, I'm not mad, I just ask you to not
do this in the future.

On to more positive things: I hope everyone enjoyed this little world-building detour!
It's so fun to explore the full environment of Coruscant and get a chance to develop Paz
and Cuyan's relationship as well! He's a good big bro, I promise, he's just a little iffy
with strangers. It was pretty tough to get the conversation between him and Cuyan right,
so I hope it turned out well!

A reminder, if you want more detailed updates on when I plan to add a new chapter, you
can follow me at sprout-fics.tumblr.com!

Okay, that was a really long A/N. But! Thank you all again for staying with this story.
Every comment, kudos, bookmark, and view really means a lot to me, and encourages
me to eventually work on my own original series.

See you next weekend!



Chapter 29: Part Twenty-nine: To Forget
Chapter Summary

"Djarin told me in the hours before you went missing that I should not underestimate
you." Paz finally offered, tentatively. "I will admit that upon our first meeting I didn't
understand his enthrallment with you. An outsider, not a Mandalorian, and by
appearances someone who did not hold a warrior's heart."

You frowned, but before you could take full offense Paz interjected once more.

"I see now that I was wrong. I still won't claim to understand you completely, but now I
know why he gave you the name he did."

That made you soften, your heart full in your chest for a moment upon remembering
Din's soft words in the Razorcrest after you had taken off from Hypori.

"Survivor." You spoke, voice deeply affectionate and warm. Your words echoed Din's,
tone similar and yet now built off an entirely different circumstance. "It means
survivor."

Chapter Notes

TW for violence. The first section of italicized material is graphic, but I suggest at least
skimming it to understand the full context of what is described.

See the end of the chapter for more notes

"This seems like a good place to rest."

Your legs nearly crumpled under you before Paz had finished speaking, muscles buckling
involuntarily at the promise of a recess from the endless climb and following hike towards
level 1325. Automatically, your back hit the grimy wall of the empty walkway you and Paz
had clambered up onto, sliding until your sat in a collapsed heap of exhaustion on the ground.

The day wore heavy on your shoulders, feeling like the legends of a god who carries the
weight of the stars upon his back. A deep, permeating ache clung to your body, holding fast
to your arms and legs. You thought that the chance to sit and simply breathe would allow the
hurt to abate, but instead it seemed to briefly intensify, as if your movement had prevented
you from acknowledging the full scale of it.



The climb from the service corridor had been absolutely brutal. Paz had taken the child to
lighten the load on you, but even then you had to climb up a ladder at least a dozen stories
with the threat of falling forever into the abyss of the planet looming dark against the bit of
courage you had mustered. When you finally had ascended to a platform, your muscles had
begun to spasm with the combination of wearing adrenaline and fatigue. Yet even then you
and Paz hadn't stopped, pushing onwards past the sector of The Works towards the district
where the covert lay.

You couldn't remember the last time you pushed yourself this hard. It had to have been the
better part of a week that you had been on the run, each day a struggle to remain standing, to
keep moving forward. Any potential of being able to relax with the added safety of another
person was squashed by Paz's insistence on a consistently grueling pace. That, combined with
the little food and nourishment you had scraped together along the way, the stress of being
chased, and the overwhelming concern for Din and the covert meant you could probably fall
asleep right here, in the middle of the urban Coruscant underground, and remain asleep for
several rotations.

Now, darkness had again begun to shroud the streets. Though you were closer to the surface,
the sky was still not visible here. Despite that, a scant few remnants of sunlight managed to
alight the streets during the brightest parts of the day. Now they had faded, and in their place
streetlights and bright flashing signs had taken their place. They cast dim shadows on the
forms of you, Paz, and the child, dancing and flickering across your weary figures.

The walkway you and Paz had clambered onto was a safe vantage point overlooking a small,
littered square. Though it had taken the last of your strength to climb up, the safety and
shelter it offered allowed you to finally relax after the day's toil. Now hidden within the
shadows of the overlook, you could fully observe your surroundings and the place Paz had
led you to.

The durasteel walkways surrounding the square dipped down into a small park of sorts,
though void of any organic matter. Instead, a drained fountain sat in the middle, a small sign
of the area's former prestige. Greyed and rusted statues stood as silent sentinels at the edge of
the area. You briefly wondered if perhaps this area had used to be some type of memorial.
Maybe before your time, perhaps even before the clone wars. Now it lay partially desecrated,
one of the statues burnt and damaged, with others graffitied or draped in trash. You tried to
imagine what this place could have looked like before, when it still stood in its glory, and
somehow your chest twinged with a bit of regret, of a feeling that you couldn't fully
understand. Something akin to familiarity.

A heavy sigh escaped past your lips before you could stop it, head lolling down toward your
chest. There, the kid looked up at you with large brown eyes, making a small coo at you,
placing a tiny hand against your dirt-streaked face. You summoned a weary smile, one hand
coming to rest atop the kid's head and stroke his long green ears.

The youngster had fared rather well for the continued stress of your journey. A part of you
assumed it was a child’s naiveté, not knowing the true extent of what was occurring around
him, knowing only that he had protectors to keep him safe. Yet You knew better. Though the



child was only a toddler, he was wise in a way that you didn’t exactly understand, almost as if
he had seen even more than you in his lifetime.

It was the source of a perpetual curiosity and bewilderment for you. He had to only be several
years old, not even able to create actual words beyond baby-ish babble and the occasional
trademark ‘patoo.’

Yet he had managed to heal Paz, and you as well, bringing the Mando back from the brink of
death with a strange ability you couldn’t comprehend. On top of that he seemed to sometimes
recognize things on your journey, of being able to understand the conversations and feelings
of those around him. Beyond all of that, one great mystery still remained.

How did he know your name?

Of course, you adored the child, but that fact alone made you look at him with different eyes.
Curiosity, but also wariness, even a trace of fear. How he knew you defied all logic. You had
never met him, and you hadn’t even spoken your name in front of him before he had echoed
it through you somehow, letting it ring forth without his voice but in a way you could still
hear it. There were times that, as much as you cared for him, that you looked at the child as if
you didn’t know him at all, as if he was a stranger.

Your thoughts were interrupted by the Mando next to you. With a grunt, Paz slid down beside
you, using one hand to brace himself as he sat. You cast a glance at him as he did so, taking
note of the sudden looseness of his legs and arms. He must be tired too, you realized. No
doubt he was pushing even himself to keep going, trying to get back to the covert as quickly
as possible to ascertain the welfare of the clan. You could relate, wanting little more than to
finally get back and collapse into the comfort and safety of Din's arms.

"How much farther?" You asked the Mando beside you, voice hoarse.

Paz heaved a sigh. "Another day. If we keep the same pace, we should make it by tomorrow
afternoon."

You felt your body fall limp at the prospect. It was so close, considering all that you had
already gone through, but the idea of one more day maintaining your current pace seemed
unimaginable.

Placing the child beside you, you curled your knees up to your chest and buried your head in
your arms. You were so, so tired. You were sure that the fatigue was playing tricks on your
brain by this point, every street corner, every ramp looking as though you had passed it
before, an echo of the past. It was the fact that you had traveled for so long that the street
styles and architecture were beginning to blur. At least you thought so.

A large, awkward hand descended softly on your shoulder. You looked up to see Paz's visor
turned towards you, shoulders eased and body language a little slack.

"Soon." Was all he offered, but the word alone made you give him a hopeful, tired smile in
return.



"Soon." You echoed, and as you did a small 'Patoo' came from between you two. You looked
down to see the child beside you, mimicking Paz in laying a hand on you as well. You huffed
a small laugh, straightening out your legs so the kid could clamber up onto them and into
your lap.

"You holding up okay?" You asked the toddler, who cooed, showing his small baby teeth in
reply.

"What...is he, exactly?" Paz ventured, trying to sound tactful despite his curiosity.

You shook your head. "I honestly have no clue." You offered in reply. "I've never seen
another species like him before."

Paz nodded absently, eyes turning to look back over the square watchfully. A long silence fell
between you two, occupied only by the distant sounds of traffic and loose pieces of debris in
the wind. You felt it hum against your senses, offering a soft, rocking vibration to which you
felt yourself easing into.

"Back there-" Paz started, and your drooping eyes looked back to him. "What he did, how he
healed me, you, I-" Paz's voice sounded oddly strained, as if he were coming to terms with
what he was about to say. "I...would have died without it."

The sudden vulnerability in his voice surprised you, and the lingering thought of sleep now
seemed distant in his confession. You gazed up at him, lips slightly parted but remaining
silent for him to speak.

"I'm not afraid of a warrior's death." He went on, fist clenching atop his bent knee. "But to die
when I still have yet to ensure the clan's safety, it's not something I can accept. My soul
would be restless, unable to move on to the Manda."

You nodded, turning and focusing on your hands in your lap. You understood what Paz
meant. For him, his goal was to the covert, to his clan. To Din, it was to the child, to see him
safe and protected. For you...

You weren't sure. For so long you thought your goal was to live simply, safely in the core
worlds. Yet the longer you traveled with Din on his adventures, the more that thought seemed
like a silly fantasy, that your true purpose lay elsewhere.

"The Covert is lucky to have you." You offered at last, pushing aside the thought to address
Paz. The warrior hummed, the sound low in his chest.

The silence stretched on between you two again, and you looked to the child, who, now
rested from his long slumber, had begun to explore the area around you. You kept a close eye
on him, making sure he didn't wander too close to the edge of the platform. Yet the child
instead eventually wandered over to Paz's feet, staring past them and up at the large warrior
with a small tilt of his head. Paz chuckled, clearly amused by the toddler's antics.

You felt yourself smile at the sound, remembering how the persona of a clan leader and
strong Mandalorian warrior had faded upon your original arrival into the covert when Paz



had attracted the attention of the group of children there. Umos, the boy who had launched
himself at Paz’s waist, his hands barely spanning the width of Paz’s waist, had spoken to him
with such reverence and adoration. You knew it came from a place of respect, but also a
mutual affection shared with the warrior.

"You seem to like kids." You offered a little awkwardly. Paz huffed a small laugh.

"They are the future." He responded, lifting a gloved hand and offering it for the child to
inspect with tiny green claws. "Children are one of the foundations of Mandalorian society.
Without them, the battles we fight and glory we succeed in do not matter as they won't be
passed to the next generation."

You nodded in agreement. "I can tell Din feels very strongly about that." You spoke, voice
quiet. "On Rishi, he went out of his way to rescue children of a Rishii village that were about
to be sold into the slave trade."

Paz turned to you, even as the child peered into his empty hand with a small whine of
disappointment.

"Your travels." He spoke, voice suddenly distinct. "Tell me about them."

Despite the promise of sleep, you felt yourself brighten and begin to slowly unravel to Paz
the full tale of Din and your adventures.

The Mando listened intently, nodding, asking questions, and clearly being engaged by your
recounting of your journey thus far. All the while he tried to entertain the youngster who had
developed an interest in him, patiently allowing the toddler to clamber onto him, inspect the
battle-worn grooves on his cuirass, and place small hands against the black of his visor. For a
moment, the unease of being on the run, the fatigue, the concern and desperation of your
journey back to the covert was forgotten. In its place, the easy, buoyant light of a developing
friendship allowed the weight from your shoulders to lift up and beyond you, into the
darkening night sky of the never-ending city.

Eventually your tale caught up to the moment you had arrived at the covert with Din, the one
where Paz had descended from the rooftops and ensued a tense confrontation with Din. You
didn't mention as much, letting your voice quiet rather than admit your feelings on the matter.
Yet it remained unspoken between you two, hovering just like the thought of the day ahead
tomorrow.

"Djarin told me in the hours before you went missing that I should not underestimate you."
Paz finally offered, tentatively. "I will admit that upon our first meeting I didn't understand
his enthrallment with you. An outsider, not a Mandalorian, and by appearances someone who
did not hold a warrior's heart."

You frowned, but before you could take full offense Paz interjected once more.

"I see now that I was wrong. I still won't claim to understand you completely, but now I know
why he gave you the name he did."



That made you soften, your heart full in your chest for a moment upon remembering Din's
soft words in the Razorcrest after you had taken off from Hypori.

"Survivor." You spoke, voice deeply affectionate and warm. Your words echoed Din's, tone
similar and yet now built off an entirely different circumstance. "It means survivor."

Paz nodded slowly, letting the same thought weigh on him as well. The silence that followed
was comfortable, as if you both had come to a mutual understanding that while it wasn't
clearly friendship, it was something that was not dissimilar.

And so, you felt your head beginning to drop, eyes half-lidded now as you took comfort in
the relaxed atmosphere between you both. You tried to resist long enough to make sure the
child would sleep as well, but the toddler's suddenly limitless energy was beyond what you
could manage.

"Sleep." Paz offered at last, softly. You were so tired at that point that you didn't bother to
open your eyes to look at him. "I'll keep watch. You'll need your strength."

You managed a single murmur of agreement, too tired to protest, head dropping to your chest.
Body slackening, you finally allowed the comfort of sleep to take you into its guarding
embrace.

---

No.

You know it before you feel it, the familiar and horrible heat of the flames licking and burning
at your ankles, the edges of your clothes, your hair and the boundaries of your senses. Heat,
the scorch of it threatening to devour you whole. With it comes the great roar of an
uncontrolled blaze, a world-ravaging inferno that wishes to take you and burn you to ash.

The scene unfolds as it has a thousand times before, a tragedy that is inescapable, imminent
and inevitable in its horror. The dream, the nightmare, creating a great outcry in your soul
that even in slumber you cannot voice. All around you the screams of those hurt, those
shrieking for aid, the whimpers of the dying coalesce into a bloody shriek that seems to shake
the stars themselves.

And you, you stand in the middle of it all. Frozen in terror as the flames creep closer, the
blaster shots ring out, the ancient pillars crack and tumble downwards. Your world is
crumbling in a great, unstoppable catastrophe, and you stand as a single reed bending in the
gale, unable to save yourself.

There's nothing you can do.

Yet you still scream, knowing that this is only a dream, it's only the nightmare that still haunts
you despite the years that have passed. Powerless to stop it, you scream until your voice
grows hoarse, cracks in the scorching heat and burnt air. That person that had passed you a
thousand times does so once more, bloody hand leaving the same handprint on your clothes
as they stagger forward towards a certain doom. You want to turn, to grab the edge of their



tattered hem, but when you do your hand passes through them like they are a ghost. Maybe
they really are one.

The dreams you had dreamt here in this place, of growing proud and strong alongside the
other children, of becoming something greater than what you are now are all in vain. They
too push past you, blurry and hazy shapes. Their faces are hazy, forgotten. When you try to
recall a pain too great to bear claws at the inside of your chest like a parasite, thirsting for
blood.

How did it come to this? Those days of exhausting yourself alongside your playmates, of
wrestling and tumbling in the sunshine, of laughing and collapsing into giggling heaps
seemed like they had never happened in the face of the gore, the violence, the catastrophic
destiny of their fates.

You know what is out there, the way they all are running. You've never seen it, but you know.
The moment they step beyond your sight into the dark of night their lives would end, and you
are helpless to stop them against the wave of death that wants to drag you out to sea.

Yet with the fire, the all-consuming blaze at your back, you don't have a choice. For you too
continue forwards, fleeing this place that had been your home, a sanctuary, a monument to
you and your kind. You pass by the bloody, the broken, the desperate and the dying. When you
reach that entrance you hear the sounds, the screams, the silence, the blaze.

A single, small hand reaches out for you. Its owner screams your name, and in the moment it
feels like the only sound in the universe, exploding with the power of a supernova against the
depths of your being.

You scream back, reaching out your own tiny hand, but the voice is cut short, and then with a
single step forward you're falling, falling, hurtling downwards towards a cataclysmic end
with the flames licking at your form the entire time, crawling down your throat and burning
you from the inside out.

You want to forget, you want this to end, you want to never again see that scene of
unfathomable grief and destruction. You want to forget, to forget, to forget-

 

 

Silence.

When you open your eyes next, it isn't to the shroud of death bending over your form. No,
you're held buoyant, cradled like the child that you are in the gentle embrace of the universe.
There is no sound here, not even your own heartbeat. The vacuum of space is absolute,
consuming every thought, every waking dream and nightmare. You expect darkness to fill
your vision, yet instead it is a vast array of stars. Like a tapestry of light, they gaze down on
your face of despair, whispering a lullaby. Though they sing out to you in their grief, there is
an inevitability there, a peace that has known the dawn of ages and fall of empires.



Like a winding tune, they sing to you, each small pinprick of light a clarendon note, hanging
high in the heavens and echoing across the vastness of space. Together they weave a grand
orchestra of harmony, an aria devoted to the grief, the goodness, the gorgeousness of the
universe in its whole.

Beyond the rising and falling notes, each star blinking out and into existence somewhere new,
there is a sound.

You know this sound, as it calls out for you within time and space. The realization creates a
path before you, lighting the way forward with radiant colors dancing against the eternal
background. Each silent step you take causes a ripple onto a seamless surface, creates a note
of its own against the unending song of the stars themselves. With every motion forward you
can hear the call for you grow louder, clearer. To reach it is to accept all that has passed, to
take with you the grief, the hope, the despair, the lessons you had learned and the heartbreak
that came with.

But you cannot deny it any longer, and soon you are reaching out with your own hands, now
scarred by the sands of time as you touch the edge of what was known long ago-

---

You're standing when you come to, eyes fluttering open as the sounds of Coruscant slowly
ease back into focus. Why you are on your feet, you don't know, but the position seems to be
of less importance than the fading grasp of what lay beyond your dream. It was so close,
close enough for you to breathe in the smoke and blaster fire. The knowledge of what was,
what could have been whispers in the back of your mind in words you can no longer hear.
Like mist the epiphany slips through your fingers and beyond reach.

So instead, your vision shows you the scene before you.

You don't know how you got here, but you're standing somewhere open, the wind whipping
your hair back from your face. The ground under your feet is unfamiliar, foreign. You can tell
by the twinge in your soles and the ache in your legs that you had begun to walk at some
point while you were asleep, body unconsciously guiding you to somewhere that it needed to
be.

In the darkness it was hard to see, each form a stranger. Even your hand seemed to barely
catch your vision as you lifted it. Yet even without illumination you could discern the feeling
of stone walls around you, radiating a coldness that sank past your skin. You couldn't tell if
you were alone, if somehow you had walked her by yourself in your sleep. Where was the
child? Paz?

As if to answer you, the world around you began to brighten. Casting your eyes upwards, you
felt your face dissolve into an expression of awe. For there, high above the clouds, past the
upper echelons of the hazy atmosphere, you could see the stars.

Their brilliance was dimmed, however, in the light of Coruscant's moon, hanging heavy in the
sky. The crescent cast a beautiful, delicate blue glow down to you, grazing the edges of your



face with a soft kiss of radiance. It also cast illumination on the scene around you, and your
wide eyes began to take in the place that you had come to stand in.

Ruins.

You stood in the center of a wide, circular chamber. Above you, a glass dome had cracked
and splintered, allowing you a clear gaze up towards the sky. Within, the edges of the space
were decorated in intricately carved stone columns. They stood in some places, having fallen
and broken in others. Stone and masonry debris lay heaped throughout the chamber, piled
high towards the edges. The thunderstorm from days passed had deposited still, reflecting
pool of water throughout, the stars coming to rest on their surfaces. Beneath your feet, a
stone walkway lay caked in grime, its previous splendor forgotten. The particles of dust here
floated hazily in the beams of moonlight, held aloft by an invisible tether.

For a moment you forgot you were on Coruscant, your elegant but destroyed surroundings
standing in such contrast to the metal, towering durasteel buildings and littered walkways
you had traversed within the past few days. No, this place was older, stronger, and in a
way...ethereal.

The ruins spoke of a long, ancient history that remained unknown to you. It seemed sections
of the space had been touched by something else, a darkness that you couldn't understand. In
some of the columns and aged statues that adorned the great hall other architecture had
begun to take its place, brutal and dark and speaking of something almost primordial. It lay
incomplete, the entire chamber broken, repaired, and broken once more. Remnants of
shadows beckoned at your senses, humming low and dark against the back of your mind. Yet
beneath that there was a peace, an undeniable wholeness that refused to be erased. The
thought of what had happened here, the secrets that lay in the shadows here were well beyond
your comprehension.

And yet...

Yet even then you found your eyes drawn, gaze shifting to focus where the moonlight
streamed through the strongest. Like a benediction from the heavens, a single beam of
moonlight shone down like a spotlight, illuminating a single, tiny figure standing amongst the
desecrated temple.

Your eyes focused on his form, his head tilted to look up at the columns, the dome, the sky
beyond. His energy, his baby-ish excitement had faded, now replaced by a silent grief, the
feeling small in an overwhelmingly chaotic universe. As your eyes landed on him, he slowly
turned his head towards you. There, in his eyes, lay the proof of a wisdom beyond his age, a
memory of the things he had seen, the events of history he had watched unfold.

You watched him, but somehow he felt distant, suddenly untouchable in a way you didn't
understand. Your lips parted, and past them you spoke the sound of a name you had forgotten
long ago.

 

 



"...Grogu?"

Chapter 30: Part Thirty: Surrounded
Chapter Summary

"You can apologize later." The warrior returned quickly, and his voice was lower than
yours, tinted with urgency. "We need to leave. Right now."

You blinked, Paz's face only dimly illuminated by the back-glow of his headlamp. You
didn't understand. This place was abandoned, ruined and desecrated. There was no
reason for anyone to enter here-

A tumble of stone off behind you spoke otherwise, and as both you and Paz stilled you
could hear distant, hushed voices, movement around you on all sides.

The familiar prickle of fear began to sharpen your senses, coiling your muscles and
making your heart thrum loudly in your chest. All at once the dream, the child, Grogu,
became forgotten, and in its place came the razor-sharp awareness of being watched.

You weren't alone.

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

"...Grogu?"

The toddler blinked at you slowly, his eyes glinting in the darkness, and you felt your heart
drown in the sudden wave of uncertainty within your chest. For a moment it seemed like the
young one before you wasn't the same one who you had traveled with, who whined to get
into your lap and place his tiny palm against your cheek. No, this seemed to be someone else
entirely. For in the child's large brown eyes lay a wisdom beyond his years, a knowledge that
you yourself could brush against but not fully understand. He gazed into you as if you knew
the true meaning behind his stare, the peace, the resignation and acceptance there.

You could feel something within you call out to try and reach him, fingers outstretched as
they had been in your dream. The distant clarion song of starlit notes rang forth in your mind,
hanging in the night sky. The longer you met the child’s eyes the closer you could feel it pull
you, like looking into a mirror and seeing someone that was yourself, but someone entirely
different all at once.

Your lips parted, eyes wide and reflecting the hazy glow of Coruscant's full moon shining
down on your face. It felt as if you were still within that dreamscape, walking along an
illuminated path, each step balancing on the teetering edge of grief and ignorance. At the end,
sat atop the ruined pillar, bathed in moonlight, sat the child.



You tried to speak, but your voice was tight in your throat, constricted there by a sob or a
well of anxiety, you couldn't tell. Still, somehow, you managed to let the words pass your
lips, broken and hesitant.

"Who-"

"Cuyan!"

You whipped to the side at the voice, muscles tensing automatically at the sudden
interruption. As if on cue, the same moonlight vanished, plunging the ruins into darkness.
Your eyes tried to adjust, but all at once shadows consumed your vision, engulfing you in the
inky darkness of night. Yet even without your sight, you were able to tell where the voice had
come from, and who its owner was.

"Paz." You breathed, stretching out one hand cautiously in the direction you had heard him.
"Paz, I-I'm here-"

Footsteps, and soon you were blinded by the sudden onslaught of brightness as Paz turned on
the lamp on his viewfinder. You raised a hand to shield yourself from being blinded, and past
it you could see the broad outline of the Mando's form against the ruin's shadows.

When his eyes landed on your form, Paz stalked forward, boots heavy against the fallen stone
and marble of the ruined chamber. You were stammering out an apology before he could
reach you, hands shaking and voice trembling from the aftereffects of what you had just
witnessed, the dream you had.

"I-I'm sorry." You offered, hands reaching out to brush against him and ground yourself in the
darkness. "I-I didn't mean to wander off. I fell asleep and I-I think I was sleepwalking-"

Paz's hand grasped at your elbow, steadying you. The touch made you cut your voice off,
overwhelmed and confused and slightly afraid. Paz seemed to sense this, because he stilled,
trying to anchor you with a gentle grip.

"You can apologize later." He returned quickly, and his voice was lower than yours, tinted
with urgency. "We need to leave. Right now."

You blinked, Paz's face only dimly illuminated by the back-glow of his headlamp. You didn't
understand. This place was abandoned, ruined and desecrated. There was no reason for
anyone to enter here-

A tumble of stone off behind you spoke otherwise, and as both you and Paz stilled you could
hear distant, hushed voices, movement around you on all sides.

The familiar prickle of fear began to sharpen your senses, coiling your muscles and making
your heart thrum loudly in your chest. All at once the dream, the child, Grogu, became
forgotten, and in its place came the razor-sharp awareness of being watched.

You weren't alone.

"The kid." Paz hissed, the gentle hand on your elbow tightening in urgency. "Where is he?"



It took you a moment to process, but soon you were spinning, trying to orient yourself in the
darkness. The place where you thought the child had been obscured by shadow, causing you
to call out cautiously in fear:

"Grogu?!"

"Who?" Paz asked beside you, but you ignored him, feeling your blood turn cold in your
veins. In the darkness, with strangers on all sides, you stumbled forward blindly, hoping and
praying you could find your charge, could find the youngster you had been tasked with
protecting.

Yet you didn't have to go far, because after a moment you felt a small tug on your pants,
followed by a whine. A gasp of relief whooshed past your lungs, and you bent to safely scoop
the toddler into your protective hold. Yet that relief was short lived as you felt Paz press his
back against yours, sweeping the ruins with his light to uncover whoever stalked you three in
the darkness.

They were getting bolder now, like predators encircling prey, boldly whispering and
murmuring to each other. You could hear them moving, and as your eyes slowly adjusted to
the darkness, you could see shadows weaving between the ruins. They danced like spirits
against the walls, forms shifting in and out of focus hazily. Every moment you tried to track,
your eyes would flicker towards movement elsewhere. In the inky darkness of midnight, it
felt as if each shadow was ten men, and soon you, Paz, and Grogu were surrounded by what
seemed like hundreds.

"Don't leave my side." Paz growled to you, and you felt him shift as he withdrew his blaster
from its holster with one hand, the other readying his vambrace. You nodded, feet shifting
under you as you prepared to fight, to flee, of which you didn't know.

The child in your arms whined once more, and the strange persona that had previously
washed over him now vanished. Now came once more the personality of a child, a toddler
who was defenseless and yet keen to the danger around him.

"It's going to be fine." You whispered to him, even as more forms seemed to rise from the
shadows. Then, softer to yourself once more: "It's going to be fine."

As if the heartbeat of Coruscant itself heard you, the clouds that had obscured the blue light
of the moon parted once more. You had to blink several times to adjust, squeezing Grogu
tight to your chest as you did so.

You were surrounded.

It took you a moment to realize, but as the darkness was washed away by moonlight, your
situation became desperately apparent.

On all sides of you were dozens of various ruffians, all donned in singed clothing and dirtied
bandages. It seemed like they had been through quite a fight, with some of the wounded
barely able to hold a blaster. They were all perched at the periphery of the room, and as the
moonlight streamed through the broken dome several lamps began to light, their warm haze



contrasting with the watery blue glow of the heavens above. Yet despite the gentle misty
radiance of both the lanterns and the moon, every figure stood tense, taut, ready for a battle.

You didn't understand at first. Briefly, you assumed you had accidentally trespassed on a
refugee settlement, or something like it. After all, of those present, most were in bad shape
despite their numbers. Some still bore untreated wounds on their figures. Yet then your eyes
landed on the gaze of one Duros who was closer than the rest of her cohort, and your own
stare traced the tattoo over her right, red glowing eye.

The Black Sun.

The previous trepidation you felt now hardened like a blade against your throat, cold and
deadly. The thought that your situation had simply been one of misunderstanding, of
coincidence, shattered like the glass in the arched dome above you, raining down into
nothingness even as it twinkled beautifully in the light of the moon.

There were too many, and you were unarmed.

Paz didn't speak behind you, but you could tell from the tautness of his shoulders, the low but
present breathing in your ears that he too was watching, scanning, thinking desperately of a
way to escape. To fight meant a certain death, or perhaps even worse, to be captured and held
at ransom by the same enemies who had slaughtered a child for the simple crime of existing
on the syndicate's territory.

"Mandalorian."

Both you and Paz looked up, watching as a figure climbed atop one of the highest piles of
debris, standing atop and looking down on the three of you. Broad shoulders were tucked
under a strange vestment of sorts, folding over each other in multiple layers but leaving her
muscled arms bare. One foot was braced atop a piece of fallen, carved stone as she leaned
forward to examine you three.

She was...strangely beautiful, you realized. With her emerald green skin, and jet-black hair
emerged atop an otherwise bald head and coiled into a messy bun, she was an exotic beauty.
If you examined her closely you could see her jet-black locks fastened by a blade of sorts,
signifying that the second the style came loose it would free both her hair and her weapon. In
the odd lighting the alien's complexion seemed...strangely luminescent. Yet when her eyes
fixed on you, you felt that surprised admiration vanish into a startled surprise. For there, in
her eyes, lay the promise of a sadistic type of violence.

She smiled, the grin tugging lopsided at her lips as she tossed her head haughtily. The
overconfidence would have made you roll your eyes if it weren't for the venom in her own, a
stare that blazed alight with the threat of danger.

"You've saved us the trouble of finding your two friends there." She spoke, voice deep and
nodding to both you and Grogu. "Thought you had finally given my men the slip after
vanishing into The Works. Only for you to show up right at our doorstep."



You felt her eyes trace you, and in them there was a raw fascination, a hunger. You shivered
as her eyes raked you from toe to top, her voice a purr.

"Interesting."

Paz nudged you, if only just so. You jerked your head towards him, catching the profile of his
helmet in your periphery.

"Let me do the talking." Paz murmured low enough for only you to hear him and raising his
blaster near his helmet. The motion was met by the sounds of a dozen different blasters

You nodded, summoning a bit of courage despite the terrified flutter of your heartbeat. You

"Your men don't appear well." He noted, raising his voice to address their leader. "Either you

The gang leader sneered, revealing a row of sharp yellow teeth.

"Don't flatter yourself." She snapped, and if Falleen could spit venom, she would have. "One
Mandalorian can't stand against us all."

Paz scoffed, and you knew a part of his reaction was forced, trying to appear unbothered

"Even so, I'm pretty sure I can take out about a third of your men here before you take us

There was a small murmur in the shadowed figures that surrounded you, a subtle shift at

The Falleen smiled triumphantly, crossing her arms as she gazed down the bridge of her nose

"That's right." She crowed. "You didn't know that your friend there is wanted by the Empire,

"What is she talking about?" Paz asked you, and you felt your skin prickle in warning. "I

So why...?

Paz stilled beside you, and uncertainty settled deep inside your stomach. The possibility that

"Paz." You whispered, and in the sound even you could hear the fear, the sudden desperation

"No deal." Paz spoke at last, lifting his head to stare directly into the astonished eyes on the

Whereupon all hell did break loose.

With one arm, Paz tucked you further behind him, using his broad frame to shelter you. With

"Run!" Paz barked, and your feet carried you before you even finished processing the

The firefight that ensued was nothing less than catastrophic. The sounds of blasters ringing
