Yet despite Paz's hardened battle prowess, despite his finely tuned Mandalorian abilities, you
knew it was only a matter of time before he fell. He was outnumbered, outgunned, and the
discrepancy between his ammunition and the overwhelming firepower of his opponents was
too much to ignore. If he had his heavy repeating blaster, perhaps that fact would be different.
As it stood, the hope of him making it out alive seemed little to none. Soon enough a single
misstep would cause Paz to falter, to fall, and his body would be left here, in the shadows of
the ecumenopolis, never returned to his people.

You wouldn't stand for it.

Paz had earned your trust, and now the thought of being dragged from his fallen figure by
unknown hands even as you screamed for him to wake made the icy fear in your blood melt
and boil with an unobstructed anger. This entire time you had been trying to understand how
you could be less of a burden, how you could better protect yourself, Din, and the child. Now
your ally faced down an impossible enemy, and you hid meekly behind rubble hoping and
praying that his imminent death would not arrive. No, you had to act.

You were gentle in depositing Grogu on the ground, forcing a thought at him to stay put. In
his frightened state he seemed unable to do any less, staring up at you with wide fearful eyes
and making a small pleading babble for you to hold him once more. As much as it hurt your
heart to leave him, you knew that if you didn't act the fear of being handed over to the
Imperial Remnants would be far greater than being hidden safely away from the deafening
violence around you.

With that weighing heavy in your thoughts, you tried to summon every ounce of courage
within you, letting it settle heavy on your skin like beskar. The thought of Din’s cuirass



bearing down on your shoulders lifted you, and with it came the tenacity to step forward. You
would protect Grogu, you would help Paz, you would save yourself.

You launched yourself from your hiding place, past Paz and you vaulted over a nearby
section of debris. Paz's astonished shout echoed behind you, but you paid him no attention.
Instead, you focused not on the laser bolts that flew past you, or the sudden shouts and
barked orders to fire at you, but instead on the slumped figure of a Black Sun member just
out of reach.

You dove from him, narrowly missing a barrage of blaster fire. The shots pinged against the
stone beside you, whizzing overhead deafeningly. Your fingers landed on the still warm metal
of his blaster just as you collided with the ground beside his fallen figure. Somehow, you
were able to seize the heavy blaster off his body and tuck it tight to you. With your back flush
against the broken and rough stone, you could hear Paz yell for you, his voice raising
dangerously over the gunfire. Yet he was unable to come towards you, as his shout again
attracted the attention of those firing, drawing their focus away from you.

The breath you took settled in your chest, providing a gasp of air to your rapidly echoing
heartbeat. It took you another moment to regain yourself, but now you moved without
thinking, without fear. If you stopped even for a moment to consider your actions, to plan
your move, then the horror of what was happening around you would seize you by the throat
and drag you down to drown. To stay alive you needed to move, to run, to fight.

With that you popped your head above the section of rubble you had crouched behind, firing
indiscriminately at the source of the blaster fire aimed at Paz. Several surprised shouts rang
out as you did so, shocked to find their own weapon turned against them. It took them only a
moment to pinpoint you, and you ducked behind the fallen pillar again just in time to avoid a
volley of blaster fire.

Yet it worked, as the second they were distracted with you Paz managed to unload his own
blaster at them, taking out two of the Black Sun members as you hid from the plasma
scorching the other side of the rubble behind you.

"Cuyan!" Paz bellowed, voice dark and deep. You moved without stopping to consider,
launching your body back over the ruins and again towards your hiding spot. As soon as you
were within sight Paz spared you a glance, his tone verging between anger and disbelief.

"What were you thinking?!" He called out to you over the firefight, grunting as a blaster bolt
pinged off his chest plate. "You could have gotten yourself killed!"

"I'm not letting you fight alone!" You yelled back to the Mando, who spared you a glance of
what you assumed to be either shock or disbelief.

You crouched next to him, partially obscured by a pile of supply crates. Then you again
unloaded the blaster in your hands towards the opposite end of the chamber, the jolt of the
kickback tilting your aim but making your shots go wild. Yet your tactic seemed to work, as
the uncertainty of where your shots would land kept several gang members from rising to
return their own fire. You repeated this several times, trying harder and harder to see through



the dense smoke, where through the orange light lit by Paz's blaze, you could see the Black
Sun leader barking orders to her forces.

Yet there, to your right, you could see the darkened archway of where you had originally
entered beckon with a whisper of safety. Somehow, despite the odds, you and Paz had cleared
a path.

"Take the kid and go!" Paz roared at you, but you shook your head obstinately.

"I'm not leaving you!" You answered, raising your voice hoarsely over the catastrophic
orchestra of blaster fire.

Before Paz could insist, however, you heard the warrior cry out in surprise and jolt
backwards. Shocked, you watched as he stumbled, tried to return fire, and again was struck.

“Paz!” You screamed, the sound ripping your throat apart with the alarm and terror there. Yet
despite the two shots that he had received the Mando remained upright, launching his plasma
thrower once more in an attempt to create a barrier between you both and the oncoming
Black Sun forces. Yet then he slumped, and from somewhere on the other side of the
darkened chamber you heard the order to cease fire.

You didn’t waste a moment, for as soon as the voice rang out you dove for Paz, tucking one
of his thick arms over your shoulder and helping him stumble into the alcove where you had
stashed Grogu.

“Cuyan-“ Paz tried, grasping your arm, but you yanked it free and returned to the alcove
entrance to fire a volley of shots at the figures creeping over the ruins towards you three. Yet
soon you were forced to duck out of the way to avoid the incoming shots that were returned,
allowing the syndicate members to creep closer, slowly advancing on your sanctuary.

A voice called out in the silence that followed, void of blaster shots as a dozen gang members
encroached upon your position. Your eyes glanced back to Paz who had managed to right
himself and stood beside you to carefully peer out. Past him you could see the child, his eyes
reflecting the scant bit of light in the shade of your shelter. You gazed back at him, chest
heaving, eyes wild, hair mussed and clothes smelling of blaster smoke. Beyond, you could
hear the slow but steady creep of the Black Sun members drawing ever closer towards you,
towards your demise.

“Come on out, darling!” The Falleen leader cried out, on the edge of mania. “We promise it
will only hurt for just a while!”

“Kark off!” You yelled back, but the moment you tried to fire a volley from your spot you
were met by several rounds pinging the stone corner where you had been standing, forcing
you back once more. Out of options, out of escape routes, you could only look desperately at
Paz and the child, the inevitability of what was to come clear in your eyes.

It was over.



You had failed. Your instinct to protect the child, to save Paz had ultimately been your
downfall. You should have taken the opportunity to flee with Grogu when you could, and
now the three of you were cornered, pinned, prisoners of your own design. Yet you didn’t
regret it. You would have rather faced the Black Suns beside Paz than abandon him in his
time of need. Still, the bitterness of defeat soured deeply into your bones, and for a moment
you closed your eyes, as if you could somehow block out all that was to come.

Yet then, beyond the glass dome, a distant sound rang out.

It caused the Black Sun members to pause as well, and you could hear them mutter between
themselves as they tried to pinpoint the source, craning their heads up to where they assumed
the origin would be.

At first you thought it was a speeder, humming low with a distant flare of engines. Yet soon it
drew closer, and you realized that where you had assumed there was one sound there was
many, singing in harmony as they approached the domed ruins. When they grew close
enough the hum reached a nearly deafening pitch, whereupon you finally realized what, or
who had come to your aid.

The next sound came as a simple clatter, and as you peeked out your head you watched a
large capsule tumble down the stone sloped ruins and come to rest at the base of where the
Falleen leader had spoken. She gazed down at it, bewildered, mouth opening in a single
word:

“…Wait-“

BOOM-

All at once the room filled with light, and from your obscured hiding spot you were shielded
from the blinding brightness of it. Yet you could hear the startled shouts of those unlucky
enough to be staring directly at the bomb when it exploded, blinding them to the sudden
figures that crashed through the remainder of the dome.

Mandalorians. The Covert.

Relief bubbled up your throat into a desperate cry, ringing out against the sudden flashes of
blaster bolts and returned fire from the Black Suns. Where you had assumed your fate at
being handed over to Imperials, of witnessing Paz’s last moments, of being separated from
the child merely moments after you had recognized his name, destiny had intervened and
offered you one more chance.

The glass that rained down and landed with a delicate tinkle against the floor was overridden
by the sounds of jetpacks lowering into the chamber, followed once more by an outbreak of
blaster fire. The chamber exploded once more into a battle zone, with a barrage of ringing
blasters firing upon each other and the lights from each sparking like fireworks against a
luminescent sky. The previous catastrophic barrage of sound resumed once more, berating
your ear drums and shaking the stone under your feet. Yet this was different. Whereas you
had been firing indiscriminately, attempting to cover Paz as he selected targets, this battle
was over before it even started.



The Mandalorians moved as one body, each soldier a finely tuned weapon that turned against
the adversaries present with deadly force. All at once the ground beneath your feet shook
with the force of the explosions that followed, and the death cries that came with. Every
moment seemed to be consumed by the discharge of a fully loaded weapon, a charge
detonating somewhere beyond your sight. Carefully, cautiously, you peeked your head out to
witness the scene of vengeance that the Covert inflicted on the same ones who had dared to
try and cross them.

Using jetpacks, each Mandalorian managed to avoid the returning fire, unleashing hell of
their own upon their targets. You watched as one Mandalorian used her vambrace to set afire
a stack of supply crates, then landed to squarely kick a nearby Black Sun member into the
burning wreckage. Another flew over her, avoiding a volley of blaster shots, landing atop a
high broken column and letting forth a series of small missiles that landed precisely on their
targets. Yet even another landed in the thick of it all, calmly and assuredly pointing his blaster
at those who dared to approach him, not wasting more than a single fatal shot on each.

Through the chaos and the bloodshed, you could hear the distinctive whine and release of a
rifle, charging and unloading repeatedly. Each target it hit barely had time to scream, as their
body evaporated into dust and floated eerily in the moonlit beams.

You knew that blaster.

The memory of Rishi, of the moment that blaster had set Din in its sights, seemed to consume
every other sound in the galaxy for the briefest of moments. Here, now, in the utter chaos of
the room, you could hear it sing to you from afar, signaling to you that the one who wielded it
was safe, and was fighting his way towards you and his son.

Above it all you could hear the Black Sun leader screaming at her forces to retreat, to fall
back further within the temple. The shout was echoed, but as the calls rang out so did the
blaster shots, and the voices who commanded the order were cut short with a chorus of
pained screams. Still, the remaining members managed to withdraw, and with them so did the
sounds of battle. As they did, the Mandalorians pursued them, chasing them further within
before a shout echoed forth with the order to hold the positions they currently occupied.
There they paused, and eventually a tense quiet began to fall over the scorched and bloodied
ruins.

When it was finally silent you slowly crept from your hiding place. Each step seemed to take
a lifetime. Gingerly, afraid that your shadow would perhaps startle one of the warriors, you
tried your best to remain visible as you inched forward. The moon still managed to draw
across your face past the blaster smoke as you advanced, casting your features in a watery
blue haze. It was only once you were in full view of the dozen or so Mandalorians present
that you saw him.

There, illuminated by the moon and backlit by the orange haze of the embers still burning,
stood a single figure. He scanned the ruins, still holding the pulse rifle within his grip and his
eye leveled to the cope. At your hesitant steps forward, he turned sharply as if expecting an
enemy, and the blue haze of the heavens caught on his visored gaze as he stared at you.



Instantly upon seeing your figure his arms dropped to his sides, and he took an almost
disbelieving step forward. You too, froze in your steps, wide eyed in your doubt that it truly
was your Mando, that the man in front of you was very much alive, whole, here, just beyond
your grasp.

"I-It's you." He spoke, voice choked, and in it you could hear the same exhaustion you had
felt within the days spent from him. The emotion, so uncharacteristic of his tone, flooded
through the space between you both and seized the inside of your chest with a clenching grip.

Soon unbidden tears welled in your eyes, a desperate but impossibly relieved sob bubbling up
your throat. All at once the strain, the stress, the fear, the despair of the past week came
crashing down on you like the heavens falling inward. He was alive, here. Despite all the
odds he had found you and the child, had come back for you, and had protected you as he
promised he would.

”Din.” Your thoughts cried out, and you weren’t able to even speak the name past the relief,
the joy, the bliss at seeing him in front of you.

Without another sound you launched yourself forward, arms outstretched. Din skidded down
the rubble pile he stood on as well, bracing himself at the bottom as you rushed full force at
him. You made contact with him hard, hearing the whoosh of air leave his body as your arms
wrapped around the middle of your companion, your friend, your protector, your
Mandalorian. Instantly Din’s arms closed around you, securing you fast within his embrace.
There, he tucked his head against your hair, his hold tight enough to press a laughing,
wrecked sob from your throat. With tear-stained cheeks and a voice cracking with joy, you
were able to utter one beautiful, soul clenching word.

"Din."

Chapter 31: Part Thirty-one: Reunion
Chapter Summary

"I knew." Din spoke, and his voice was tight, failing to restrain the emotion underneath.
For a moment you thought he might break, trying and failing to hold back the fractures
of relief, the utter bliss at your reunion held tight in his chest. "I knew you were alive,
Cuyan."

Survivor.

Din's name for you had been born of your past, and yet it had continued to follow you
even now. You, against the impossible odds, had survived once again, fighting and
clawing your way back to him. Now safe in his arms, it was all you could do not to sob
at the name once more, feeling as though Din's title for you had been given as an
incredible blessing, a prophecy of who you were, how you would find him once again;
and silently to yourself you vowed that you always would, that you would always find
him, no matter what.

Chapter Notes

TW for injury, blaster fights, violence, explosions, and general badassery as well as
referenced child death once more

See the end of the chapter for more notes

"Din."

The words were choked, cracked in a stifled sob of relief as you clung to him, burying your
face against the beskar chest plate and feeling the heat of your brimming tears seep against
the metal. The weight of Din's arms around you seemed to be the only thing anchoring you,
keeping you from being lost in the tide of your blissful solace at once again being by his side,
here, with him, whole.

Din tightened his arms impossibly further around you, squeezing some of the air from your
lungs for a moment, which came out as a small whimper of reprieve. You could feel him tuck
his helmet against you, leaning it down as far as it would go into the crook of your neck.
There, you could hear the breath that rattled his lungs, tempting him to let out his own
choked sound of complete consolation at finding you. As if to pull yourself impossibly closer
you stretched up on your toes, hands fisting into the cape behind his back. It was only then



that you could no longer contain the sniffle and following stuttering exhale that warned of
oncoming tears.

"I knew." Din spoke, and his voice was tight, failing to restrain the emotion underneath. For a
moment you thought he might break, trying and failing to hold back the fractures of relief,
the utter bliss at your reunion held tight in his chest. "I knew you were alive, Cuyan."

Survivor.

Din's name for you had been born of your past, and yet it had continued to follow you even
now. You, against the impossible odds, had survived once again, fighting and clawing your
way back to him. Now safe in his arms, it was all you could do not to sob at the name once
more, feeling as though Din's title for you had been given as an incredible blessing, a
prophecy of who you were, how you would find him once again; and silently to yourself you
vowed that you always would, that you would always find him, no matter what.

"You're okay." You spoke, and your voice did nothing to hide the breathlessness there, chest
rising with a gasping inhale as you tried to not cry, to hold back the tears-

"When Paz told me you two had been ambushed...I-"

"Paz?" Din asked, and gently, as if he were afraid to break you, he separated himself from
you, holding you at arm's length as he looked down into your face. Your own eyes, reflecting
the Coruscant moon hanging heavy in the sky above, stared back at him.

You nodded, lips parting as you tried to understand his words past the emotional haze that
had taken hold of you. One of Din's hands came from your elbow to your face, hesitantly
cupping your cheek and smearing the tear that grew against the corner of your eye. It was all
you could do to not melt into his touch, a sigh pouring forth from your lips. That part of you
that had been missing ever since you had wandered outside the covert, since you had looked
hopelessly up into the abyss of the Coruscanti underworld with a crying child in your arms
now lay complete. In your chest that wholeness mended the ache there, and the trials and
tribulations of the past days felt like mere minutes now that Din was here, safe, alive.

Yet you nodded at last, a broad and overjoyed smile spreading across your face as you looked
up at your Mando.

"Paz." You repeated, and then turned to face the small shelter of debris you had crept from, to
find that the warrior himself had stepped into the light, and dwarfed in his arms was the child,
gazing out cautiously from the safety of Paz's hold.

Upon seeing Grogu your heart sang to even higher heights, and before you could stop
yourself you had taken one, two steps and trotted down the slight incline of rubble to meet
Paz halfway. Din's choked breath of surprise followed behind you, shocked to see his
comrade still alive and in one piece.

Grogu held out his arms to you, the fright in his large brown eyes fading to relief once more.
You lay one hand on Paz’s shoulder as you scooped the child into your other, holding him



against your chest as he curled there, a hand reaching and grasping the fabric of your shirt in
an attempt to comfort himself.

You gave Paz a smile, one perhaps a bit too bright for his injured state, but blissful
nonetheless at your unexpected rescue. Paz returned your gesture, letting the hand that didn't
clutch his side rest on your shoulder as well. There it stayed, as if you could both silently
communicate the mutual understanding of having survived an impossible encounter, and the
camaraderie, the friendship that came with. For a moment his visor lingered on you, and
though Paz didn't speak, you could understand the gaze there.

Then Paz turned to Din, who had followed several steps behind you. You turned as well, and
in doing so allowed Grogu's eyes to land on his paternal figure. The toddler stared in disbelief
for a moment, eyes wide and lips slightly parted. Then, his face scrunched miserably. All at
once the child began to cry, startling the three of you with the sudden intensity of his
outburst. The noise of his sobs bounced through the chamber, making several of the Mandos
maintaining their positions cast glances at your small group in curiosity. You rushed to shush
Grogu, trying to bounce him in your arms as he sobbed, to no avail. Yet after a mere moment,
Din's hands reached forward and grasped the toddler, taking him into his own arms and
holding him against his shoulder. There, the toddler instantly curled into his care-taker’s
pauldron, hiccupping.

You felt your heart melt as Din's shoulders relaxed, as one hand rested gently against the kid's
back, one of Grogu's large green ears squished against the edge of Din's helmet. Slowly, the
toddler's cries began to lessen into small sobs, whimpers muffled by the coarse material of
Din's cowl and cape. One he became quiet enough, Din sighed, the sound heavy and yet
utterly relieved. Tilting his head just slightly, he directed a quiet voice to the child in his
arms.

"You okay? Feel better now?"

After another sniffle and a sob, you heard Grogu let out a small noise in reply, one hand
tightening into the fabric of Din's cowl at his collarbone. You felt your heart rise to your
throat, fluttering there like a thing with wings, delicate and pure. A hand found its way to
your chest as if you could contain the feeling, a smile of utter happiness making your face
warm to the touch.

Unable to contain yourself any longer, you gently padded forward to Din's other side,
hovering until Din's hesitant arm reached around to your back and huddled you closer so that
he held both you and Grogu in an embrace. You tucked yourself into him, one hand reaching
up to cover Grogu's clutched against Din's cowl, the other wrapping around Din's back. Din
tucked his head against the child in his arms, and you felt rather than heard the deep sigh that
settled in his chest.

That moment you had longed for, when you had awoken to Din's arms around you while the
child awoke you with a gentle touch, the utter bliss of being together with both of them,
seemed to fill every fiber in your being. For a moment it seemed that the happiness between
the three of you, the love and the trust there could conquer anything, could light all the stars
in the sky themselves.



No words were needed between you, only the comfort of touch and the sound of three
heartbeats in sync.

Then Paz made a small noise, clearing his throat, and instantly your gaze shot back to him,
one hand still clutching his side.

"Oh kriff-" You involuntarily cursed, covering your mouth instantly and glancing at Grogu to
see if he had heard. Fortunately, he hadn't, but as you watched he moved past you as Din took
a few steps forward to greet his Vod.

He seemed at a loss for words for a moment, and you could practically feel the guilt roll off
of him at the memory of leaving his brother for dead. Paz seemed to notice too, because he
straightened and held out his arm in an offer of reconciliation. Din peered down at it as if it
were something foreign. Yet after a moment, hesitantly, he reached out and secured his arm
against Paz's in traditional Mandalorian fashion, turning his gaze to the other warrior.

"Su cuy'gar." Din managed at last, and Paz huffed a laugh.

"You're a fool if you thought I'd simply die like how you left me." Paz rumbled, and you
could hear the smile in his voice, contagious enough to broaden your own. You didn’t think
your heart could grow any fuller, but the sight of the two Mandos back together again made it
sing in a tune of ultimate elation.

Then Paz nodded to the toddler in Din's arms. "Your little one- he saved me. Saved both of
us."

Din glanced at the child still tucked against his shoulder, then turned his attention back to
Paz. "That's...a long story." He offered, then as you came up at his side once more, looked
between the two of you. "How did you find each other?"

"That's a long story too." Paz replied, and Din tucked his head a bit as if he were smiling.
Then Paz's heavy hand landed on your shoulder, causing you to look up at the Mando.

"All I can tell you is that I wouldn't have survived without your partner here." He concluded,
and you felt yourself grow an inch with pride, felt it lift you so that for a moment you felt
almost as tall as the warrior beside you. "She is deserving of the praise you have given her."

At this you blinked, turning to Din as if he could offer an explanation. Yet Din's visored stare
gazed back at you blankly, and you couldn't decipher the meaning there. Yet then he spoke,
his voice tinting in a tone you rarely heard.

"That she is."

You beamed at him, feeling like your smile could reach all the way up to your ears.

"Paz!"

"Vod, you're alive!"

"Osi'kyr! We thought you were dead!"



You blinked as the Mandos who had been stationed near the exit that the Black Suns retreated
to suddenly caught sight of Paz, some rushing forward to greet the warrior while others still
stood high on debris piles as lookouts. Yet all of them seemed to be delighted at the sudden
return of the Mando, shouting exclamations of surprise and relief at his appearance.

Paz took it in stride, grasping the arm of another Mando that you recognized as one of the
gateway guards, and turning to greet one of the female Mandalorians who you had seen
watch over some of the foundlings when you first arrived. Yet despite the joyous reunion, Paz
was again back in the role of commander, issuing greetings but surveying the damage from
the fight, asking about casualties, where the gang had escaped to, what their numbers were
like. A different, leaner Mando snuck up beside him and said some small words before
injecting him with a painkiller.

You turned towards Din once more, who too was watching over the scene. Grogu had since
settled his crying fit, following Din's gaze and then turning to you with a small series of soft
baby sounds.

"Are you hurt?" Din asked, tilting his visor towards you.

You paused, suddenly taking stock of yourself. You hadn't had a moment to do so since you
had originally fallen into that dreamscape that had lifted you upwards and made you travel
into the ruins.

The dream...

"Din." You said suddenly, eyes wide. "I have to tell you something-"

You stopped, ears tracking a distant sound.

While Din waited for you to continue, you listened, straining to hear the sound that had
caught your attention. Like a shadow flickering at the periphery of your sight you could hear
it, an ominous reverberation of something you couldn’t see yet. You could feel it, if ever so
slightly, a vibration that made the ground under you hum with energy. A distant rumble, a
far-off growl that promised danger.

"Something's coming." You whispered, turning to face the darkened corridor where the Black
Sun forces had retreated to. Your voice was small against the ruckus behind you. Din tensed
beside you, form readying and eyes drawing to where you peered into the darkness. As he did
the sound grew louder, rising from a low grumble to a singing hum of something large,
something terrifying.

The other Mandos noticed too, and quickly their raucousness at Paz's survival grew quiet.
Silently, several of the Mandos made themselves vanish back into the ruins, issuing hand
signals as they all placed themselves strategically to face whatever incoming threat emerged
from the darkness. Paz spoke some low words to those that remained, and soon they too were
igniting jetpacks, slipping away to set themselves as shadows against the night.

The ground under you began to tremble now, little bits of rocks and rubble shaking against
the ruined ornate floor. You tensed, drawing yourself up in preparation for the hulking black



shape that began to make itself known from the shadows. All around you the Mandos lay
silent, training their blasters and weapons on the thing that moved forward, out of the inky
blackness and into the clouded moonlight.

Din drew in a sharp breath beside you, and before you could ask he was suddenly grasping
your arm and dragging you to the side, uncaring about his sudden rough grip. You went
willingly, though confused as your eyes traced the barrel of a cannon pointed straight at you
both. Your eyes grew as large as the crescent moon, lips parting as you tried to speak.

"T-that's-"

BOOM

The sound of rock exploding was nearly simultaneous with the cannon fire that deafened
every other sound on Coruscant, and you screamed as Din hauled you to safety, covering
your head to avoid the debris that rained down on you both.

By the time your hearing resumed, ringing in your ears fading, the other Mandos were
yelling, barking orders over blaster fire as the regrouped Black Suns poured out from behind
the mounted gun, blaster bolts pinging off the walls and rubble.

"What the hell is that?" You yelled at Din over the chaos. Din at first didn't reply, putting
Grogu in your arms and withdrawing his pulse rifle from his back.

"A modified Imperial Troop Transport turret." Din called back, ignoring your blatant look of
confusion.

"A what?!"

"Bad news." Din replied, and this time you understood.

Din went through the motions of checking his munitions, hands flying over his armor to the
pouches on his hips and sliding over the well-maintained exterior of the rifle. Your mind
seemed to haze over as you fully processed the world around you. The Black Suns you had
assumed were defeated now poured like blood from a wound, spreading and festering from
their origin, from the weapon that had taken down Paz, and would now turn itself against
you, against Din and the other Mandos.

Din finished checking his munitions, nodding to himself and striding past you out towards the
chaos.

"Stay here." He barked over his shoulder.

Panic rapidly mounted in your chest, and before Din could take another step you lurched
forward to grasp his cape, causing him to turn as another explosion rattled the world around
you.

"No!" You yelped, and that anxiety, that fear at losing him again while you simply huddled on
the sidelines now roared back into full force. You had vowed yourself against this, this reason
why you had ventured from the covert in the first place, to better yourself so you could stand



beside, not behind him. The fear that you would have to resign yourself to watch as he stood
in harm’s way yet again bubbled in your chest, angry and desperate.

"I'm coming with you!" You declared loudly, much to Din’s surprise. It took him a moment to
process, but when he did he fully rounded on you, setting his stance wide against your
protest.

"What? No! Stay here, you'll be safe here." He argued, and you felt yourself grimace at his
tone. Yet you wouldn’t back down, not anymore.

"I'm not letting you fight alone!" You yelled back, and the hand on his cape tightened into a
white-knuckle grip. "Not anymore."

Before Din could protest you withdrew the blaster you had stolen off the Black Sun member
from your holster. Despite your shaky grip you set yourself, staring at Din with eyes hard as
beskar. You refused to let him go alone again. Not so soon after you had just reunited. You
refused to let him out of your sight. You wanted to protect him, wanted to keep him safe just
as he had done for you.

"We're in this together, remember?" This time your voice lowered, but the edge was still there,
sharp as steel and unrelenting in your determination.

And as Din watched, he could see the flame of courage, of conviction burn in your eyes. It
grew alight along with the smoldering embers of where the turret shells left their mark,
smoldering dark in the inky shadows of night. In his own he felt himself reflected, felt the
synchronous heart of a warrior burn alongside his own, refusing to back down, to give a
single inch.

It took his breath away.

"...Fine." He bit back at last, reluctant to agree but knowing that it was pointless to argue.
"But do NOT leave my side. If something happens, my priority is getting you and the kid to
safety, okay?"

You felt the breath you had been holding escape you in a gasp of relief, not wanting to anger
Din by choosing to ignore him should he have refused you. Then you turned around, facing
the child you had been protecting. Grogu stared up at you worriedly, raising his arms
plaintively to attempt his way back into your arms. You felt a piece of you break at the sight,
so instead you knelt down to his level.

"Grogu, you're going to have to stay here, bud. Stay here where you can be safe. We will
come back for you, I promise you. Do you understand? We aren't leaving you behind." Your
voice choked for a moment, but you swallowed it down, forcing yourself to swallow the
uncertainty there.

Grogu seemed to comprehend the meaning of your words, but even then he refused to lower
his arms, whining worriedly at you as you rose once more.



"Here." A voice to your right spoke, and you turned to see the same Mandalorian that had
treated Paz bent over one of his comrades, kneeling before him but turned halfway to you
with a beckoning hand. "Give him here. He'll be safe with the injured. You have my word."

You looked to Din for confirmation, casting eyes over your shoulder for his approval. When
he nodded, the grip on his rifle tightening, you turned back to the medic and muttered your
thanks, gently depositing Grogu beside him and turning before your heart could shatter at his
upset and panicked cry.

You watched Din's helmeted gaze flicker from Grogu to you, and for a moment you could
imagine his indecisiveness. The choice between escaping with you and the child, forcing
himself to abandon the covert once again, versus putting you in harm's way to help save them
was an impossible one. He couldn't make it on his own.

So, you decided for him.

"Hey." You spoke, and the sound was cut off by the dull think of another round firing and then
exploding into dissonance somewhere in front of you. Din pulled you down automatically, one
arm over your head as he sheltered you from whatever debris raining down from the cracked
ceiling. You waited a moment before grasping it, holding it off of you so you could look him
in the eyes as you spoke.

"We go together."

Din paused for a moment, as time seemed to inch forward, each heartbeat a small sound
against the cacophony of violence around you. Yet within it lay, just for a moment, only you
and him, tethered together by the promise you had just given him. There, in the single part of
space and time, you felt a part of yourself tied to him, anchoring him to you no matter how
far you would ever go, beyond the expanse of stars and space, to where he stood.

He felt it too, because the arm that you had grasped twisted in your hold so that his palms
cradled you elbow, bringing you just slightly closer to him and yet narrowing the space
between you more than you could have ever expected.

"Follow me." He spoke, and this time his voice was only for you to hear. "Have my back, and
I'll have yours."

And follow you did, through the hail of blaster fire, ducking past the broken and ruined walls
of the chamber, flattening yourself against metal and sandstone surfaces as you slowly-
achingly slowly- maneuvered your way towards the center of battle. You stayed on Din's heels
the entire time, ignoring the shouts and injured cries around you, focusing on Din's back as
he strode ever forward, unfazed by the battle.

At last, he scrambled up a few feet behind a pile of loose stone, sheltering behind the
fragment of what used to be a mural and propping his pulse rifle just over the top.

"Shoot when I shoot." He instructed, raising his voice to be heard over the discord. You
nodded grimly back at him, trying to stifle the shake in your hands. You looked down at it for
a moment, trying to force your nerves to calm themselves and for courage to replace the



tremor there. An involuntary shiver raced up your spine, leaving gooseflesh in its wake at just
what exactly you were doing, the gravity of the situation you had entered into willingly.

Din's hand came to cover yours holding the blaster, forcing you to look at him. In the chaos
around you couldn't hear him if you tried but watched as his hands withdrew and held the
rifle, glancing at you meaningfully as he leveled his sights.

"Remember to keep the front and the back of the gun level, otherwise you risk aiming too
high or low.

Din's voice filtered through your thoughts, blocking out the sounds of battle for the briefest of
moments as you felt the shake in your hands quell, felt your breathing even out, your eyes
close as you inhaled deeply. Then, eyes flashing open, you lifted your blaster above the wall,
sighting a nearby Black Sun member in your sights-

-and fired.

To your amazement the blaster shot caught the shoulder of the Rhodian you had aimed at, not
striking his center of mass but landing heavily enough to knock him off balance. The pulse
rifle whirred next to you for a moment before Din fired, and the Rhodian exploded into dust
before he could recover.

You felt the confidence from your success lift you, and the heavy oppressive weight of doubt
rise off your shoulders as you continued to search your sights for another Black Sun member.
After several missed attempts you managed to strike a Nautolan in the moment she popped
her head above her shelter, ignoring the way your guts heaved and soured at you taking
another life in order to defend your little family and Din's clan.

Beside you Din worked easily, focusing his fire on the mounted turret that had locked itself
into place just beyond the reach of most of the Mando's munitions. The operator was
sheltered behind some type of make-shift welded durasteel wall from which they aimed and
fired the weapon. It took some time to charge between firing, and as you listened you could
hear the sinister and imminent hum of it preparing another shell.

Din's attempts to try and stop the barrage had trivial effect, his rounds impacting but doing
little to slow the turret. He cursed beside you, ducking down as several Black Sun members
seemed to catch sight of you both, turning their blaster fire towards you. You followed him,
dodging just in time to avoid a blaster bolt that whizzed past where your head had been a
split-second prior. The narrow escape rattled you, and for a moment you were unable to
compartmentalize, weighing the oppressive the knowledge that at any moment a single
misstep would mean a bolt through your brains, body limp beside your partner, beside Din.

Din seemed to catch sight of your hesitation, one hand reaching over to jostle you back into
focus. You looked at him, breathing heavy as your sight narrowed down to his T-shaped visor.

"Concentrate." He barked, and even though his tone was rough the word was not unkind,
trying to way you back into that sense of bravery that you had shown him only minutes prior.
You nodded at him, swallowing thickly and trying to force down the horror at your situation
in favor of courage.



Din nodded back at you, raising himself up after a moment, picking the second in between
blaster fire to return a barrage of his own, the pulse rifle now switched to regular rifle
rounds. You quickly inhaled a few times, psyching yourself up before popping up beside him,
turning your own aim at an outcropped rubble where several Black Sun members sheltered.

That was, until the corner of your eyes caught the flash of a muzzle moving towards you.

Din saw it too, and in the space of a second tackled you down the slope of the rubble pile as
the cannon whirred to a fever pitch. You both tumbled out of reach just in time, the turret
firing off a single round which tore apart the perch you had both occupied only a moment
ago. The close proximity of the explosion rattled you, and you couldn't hear Din's shout at
you over the sudden catastrophic ringing in your ears. Instead of answering, you curled
beside him, eyes closed as he braced himself over you, kneeling upwards and firing back with
the pulse rifle.

Through closed eyes you could feel the world around you seem to shatter just as in your
nightmares, the fire of burst lanterns and exploding turret rounds searing heat across your
skin and lighting the blue moonlight haze into a destructive and all-consuming inferno,
flames dancing across Mandalorian visors and catching the bright shadows of Din's armor.
The air was rancid with blaster smoke and ash, sour with the scent of burnt stone and metal.
That horrible stench that seemed to wrap itself around Coruscant's underworld permeated
every fiber of your being, the rotten iron smell of death closing in over the space and
whispering between the broken bodies and wreckage of what used to be a place of peace, of
justice.

Then there was you, in the middle of it all, partially covered by Din's broad figure as he knelt
protectively over you, refusing to give an inch while you desperately tried to right yourself.
Again, the chaos, the death, the destruction he stayed by your side, steadfast and undeterred.
He danced in hazy shapes as your vision tried to clear itself, tried to reconcile your
consciousness with the world around you.

You wondered for a moment if this would be the last image you ever saw, of Din towering
over your sprawled figure, the bottomless black of his visor dancing with the light of the fire,
the back of the pulse rifle braced against his shoulder and hands tight around it. Though the
Mandalorians had easily pushed the Black Sun back before, now they barely held their
ground as the turret punctured holes in their defense, making the tiled floor beneath you lurch
with every canister fired and erupting on impact. If this continued it wouldn’t be long before
they were forced to retreat, to give ground with nowhere to go except up and out of the dome,
where they would be shot down like meteors burning up in the atmosphere. And Din, and you,
and Grogu would be stuck as the turret advanced forward, cornered you in what used to be a
place of tranquility, of justice and peace.

As the tragedy your fates began to be written across the stars Din remained. He never
flinched, never backed down for a moment even as the whims of the universe began to close
fast around you both.

You felt your lips part, as if you could tell him everything in these ultimate moments as the
blaster fire drew closer to him, as the Mandalorians behind him began to grow frantic in
their cries, and the essence of your being shook with another world-shattering explosion from



the turret. If only you could confess what you hadn’t yet told him, about the dream, about
Grogu’s name, about the great mystery surrounding you that even you yourself could not
understand. Maybe, somehow, if you told him, then everything would begin to make sense,
and the ghost of the person you used to know would finally show herself to you.

"Take cover!" A Mando to the front and right of you called, and you twisted to see, watched
as she reached back, spine arching as she motioned to throw something in her hand, arm
extending over her shoulder like a great wing unfurling.

Then, as if in slow motion, you watched as a single blaster shot ripped into her shoulder, and
her motion was cut off with a sickening jolt, body angling horribly, collapsing and falling
backwards as her hand opened...

…and a grenade fell beside her.

You could see the red blinking flash of the weapon, counting down the invaluable seconds
until its fiery destruction. The Mando's limp form lay beside it, her fingers just out of reach.

You moved before you realized what you were doing, scooting yourself out from under Din,
his surprised then terrified shout echoing behind you. Yet you didn't stop, scrambling over the
rubble, scraping your hands on sharp edges and clawing your way towards, instead of away,
from the grenade.

There was no time to think, no time to so much as breathe. The fallen Mando before you
gazed back at you with Din's visor in her place, body limp and still beside the rapidly
counting down weapon. If you didn't act she would die, and you would have merely stood
there, watching, waiting in the seconds that you could have acted, could have saved her.

Even as you saved yourself, you were never going to leave anyone behind, never again.

Blaster bullets whizzed past you as you scrambled for the grenade, whizzing just over your
skin but never touching you as an invisible forcefield of destiny, of purpose kept you safe. You
didn't look at the blaster fire, didn't even breathe as you lurched forward, your hands closing
around the grenade as it began to blink into its final stages. The red cast brightly against
your irises, reflecting the countdown of destruction against your sight. You could feel your
stomach turn, heave at the reality of what you were doing, the risk you were putting yourself
in. A part of you panicked then, but before the feeling could fully freeze over your blood,
could keep it held static, you pushed the feeling down with an enormous effort. Even then it
lingered, the thought that if you failed, if you waited-

With only a moment's thought to aid you, you held your breath, reached back as far as you
could-

and hurled the grenade at the turret with all your strength, feeling the moment the metal left
the pads of your fingers.

There it sailed across the front lines, past the Mandos already ducking down to avoid the
incoming blast. For a moment, the metal caught the pale moonlight, glinting like a falling
star as it began its descent.



For a moment it seemed like it would stop just short, the arch laying too low across the
broken glass ceiling. The world around you seemed to inch forward, the space between your
heart beats light years from each other. You could feel the world around you shrink as you
watched it descend too close, too soon, and you willed it further, just a few more steps. If only
it fell downward just a few feet more, then maybe, maybe…

Then as if hearing you-

It landed on the turret with a dull clang just barely audible over the chaos and anarchy of the
battlefield.

You had a split second to see it tumble to a stop atop the weapon before a force hurled into
you from the side, pushing you to the ground as the red blinked down to nothingness, as the
world roared, shook into fire, engulfed you in a horrifying blazing heat. All other sounds
shattered like glass as the explosion detonated, shaking the foundations of the planet itself.

You curled into yourself as the world shattered around you, anchored only by the weight
above you weighing you down and keeping you safe. You didn’t even have the breath to
scream, your eardrums punctured by the force of the shockwave, and even past closed eyes
you could feel the back of your eyelids brighten from the intensity of the detonation. The heat
rose hot against your skin, and you didn’t even have time to think that you had been too close,
that perhaps the blaze would only continue to grow and consume you from the inside out.

Yet in all of that you felt Din’s arms close fast around you, his entire body go rigid as you
both lay still, hoping that you were beyond the range of the blast radius, that somehow the
fire would pass over you, that the ground would stop quaking, that you would both be okay.

When the world stopped trembling at last, you felt your breath remain stuck in your chest. It
took a moment for you to free it, your throat blocked by both fear and an impossible hope that
slowly seemed to reconcile with reality. After what seemed like minutes, you finally permitted
yourself to peek open one eyelid, watching as your vision sluggishly faded from vague,
uncertain shapes to the outlines of solid objects once more. The ringing in your ears didn't
stop for several moments later, and even then there was a hum, a crackle that hadn't been
there before. Yet you were alive, untouched by the blaze that had curled its fingers towards
you but ultimately drew short.

It was only moments after you got your bearings that you craned your head, wincing as it
throbbed with the movement, and discovered the sound was not a product of your own
impaired hearing, but that of a massive burning heap where the mounted turret had been. The
entire chamber was cast aglow with a red-orange haze, the fire seeming otherworldly in a
mist of blaster smoke, glowing brightly in the fog.

The quiet that followed was filled only with the crackle of the surrounding smoldering fires,
and the burnt metal wreckage of the weapon that had been used against the Mandalorians in
your mix. Yet in it was the absence of blaster fire, of panicked shouts and relayed orders, jet
packs firing and flashing against the darkness. It was as if every soul still present in the
ruined chamber began to creep from their cover, to peek over decimated walls and buttresses
to examine the battle ground which had erupted into a terrifying cataclysm of fire and debris.



The weight atop you shifted, and as you turned your head back you saw the familiar
pauldrons of your own Mando sprawled over you.

"Din!" You breathed as the Mandalorian shifted with a small grunt, as he too was rattled by
the proximity of the explosion, just beyond danger but within the radius to be rocked by the
aftershock. As you observed he managed to tuck his knees under him, arms sliding to either
side of your shoulders. Slowly, he pushed himself off of you, only to hover his helmet close to
your face.

"Are you hurt?" He asked, and there was a strain there in his voice, the result of some type of
injury you couldn't see yet. Even so he sounded as if it wasn't serious, and the fact that he
could rise off of you was a positive indicator to his situation.

You nodded, arms still sprawled to either side of your shoulders and head, hair pushed away
from your face and falling onto the floor around you. The breath in your chest seemed to
catch as you began to process what had just happened, that you- that Din had-

Your thoughts were interrupted by a great cry, and you flinched at the sound. Yet when you
listened it wasn't that of pain, or anger, or sorrow. No, the shouts that rose from the rubble
around you carried to the ceiling, out into the Coruscant sky that had begun to streak with
the colors of dawn. It was the sound of triumph, of victory.

Din's head lifted to observe for a moment, taking note of the Mandos rising from their
perches and holding their arms aloft in celebration. Then his eyes swiveled to that of the
burnt, destroyed turret, laid to waste by the grenade you yourself had thrown with the last of
your hope. You expected his shoulders to slacken, for his head to droop, but instead Din's
helmet whipped back towards you, hovering inches from your face.

"What in the seven hells were you thinking?!" Din roared at you, and you flinched at his
suddenly booming voice mere inches from your face. "You could have gotten yourself killed!"

You blinked, unable to conjure a response to Din’s outrage. He had all the right to be furious
with the stunt you had pulled. If it were him you would have tackled him to the ground as
well, bent over him and let your voice rip from your throat in anger and desperation.

Yet the image of the female Mandalorian laying prone…of Din’s helmet instead of her own
staring back at you. You shouldn’t have done it, but you didn’t regret that you had. If it had
been him, you would have done it over again in a heartbeat.

Before you could respond Din's helmet fell to your chest, his heavy breath rattling from
within. The weight of it there seemed to jolt you back into reality, with your breath heaving
back into your lungs and body briefly spasming with the reality of what you had done, of the
physical aftershock of being so close to the eruption. Yet none of that mattered, because Din
was speaking words past his helmet that sounded less like anger and more of a deep, aching
grief for what could have transpired.

"I could have lost you...I..." He murmured, voice raw. His hands tightened on either side of
your head as he tried and failed to regain himself, no doubt the image of your destroyed
figure haunting him.



"If anything happened to you...Cuyan, I-I..."

You felt all the air in your lungs leave you, skin damp with sweat and muscles exhausted.
Your arms were heavy, and you slid them down, raised them to brace against the sides of his
helmet. There, you brought it closer to you, braced your forehead against the metal of his
helm and let your eyes close. Din nearly collapsed on top of you, his arms weakening as they
held him off of you. Yet you felt the desperation echo past his lips with his next breath, felt his
legs relax between yours as he forced a steadying breath through himself, finally speaking
low against you.

"Please...please never do anything like that again."

You nodded softly, breathing in the breath Din had just let go, holding it as you reminded
yourself that you were alive, you were okay, that Din was here with you, that Grogu was safe,
that you were all going to be fine.

"Okay. I promise." You whispered as your arms slid from his helmet to his shoulders, closed
around him, and Din slowly relaxed into your touch.

You stayed there for a moment longer, waiting and letting both of your bodies and minds
settle. The cries of victory around you had begun to quiet, and soon you could hear boots
beginning to march past you towards the burnt wreckage to look for enemy survivors. You
opened your eyes as Din lifted off of you, rocking back to kneel between your legs. Carefully,
you followed his motion, raising yourself off the brittle ground and wincing at the headache
that throbbed as you sat up.

Din’s gaze went past you, and you followed his gaze to where two other Mandos assisted the
Mando who had activated the grenade in standing. One of her arms was slung over another’s
shoulder, the other visible with a blaster wound. Yet she took a moment to make them pause,
to let her gaze linger on you for what seemed like a heartbeat too long. Then, as if reverently,
she nodded in your direction, and you blinked at the silent but meaningful recognition. With a
pat she signaled the one helping her to continue, and together they hobbled away.

“You.”

You whipped your head towards the source of the sound, feeling your vision tilt for a moment
at the motion. Yet the call wasn’t for you, hissed and furious with righteous anger. Instead,
you watched as a familiar blue beskar figure marched over towards the side of the burnt
turret, and in the hazy smoke that had begun to clear you watched as Paz used his good arm
to raise a lean figure off the ground, his entire body radiating violence.

“Child slayer.” He spat, and if the words could suck the life force out of the person he held,
you had no doubt they’d fall limp in his grip before he could finish uttering the sound. Your
shoulders tensed at the accusation, mind flashing back to his words about the origin of this
disaster, of how the Covert had been attacked, and in defending themselves had lost one of
their foundlings to the Black Sun. Now, Paz held that criminal within his grip, fist closed
tightly around the front of their shirt as they hovered several inches off the ground.



Before the person could respond you watched Paz take a step backwards, turn, and hurl them
to the ground. There they grunted weakly, but now that they were closer you could see the
green skin and unique features of the Falleen Black Sun leader come into focus through the
smoky haze. She seemed severely injured, her clothes still singed and smoking, torn in places
from being too close to the explosion. No doubt she had been on or near the turret when it
had exploded, body tossed and turned within the flames. In an attempt to raise herself off the
ground, the woman’s eyes flicked upwards, stopping when they met yours.

Her snarl at you was cut short when Paz strode forward once more, using his foot to turn her
over onto her back. She sneered up at him even as he withdrew his blaster.

“You. You’re the one who killed our foundling! I know your face now!” He boomed, and you
couldn’t help but shrink at the full force of Paz’s voice, thunderous and enraged. “I saw you
turn your blaster on him, scum.”

It was only then that the Faleen’s face flickered with fear, her hands coming to grasp the boot
that stayed atop her chest and forced the breath from her lungs.

“N-no, I-“ She tried, but Paz pressed down, and the remainder of her speech tapered off with
a wheeze.

Din was up on his feet in a heartbeat, taking a single step towards his Vod. Paz’s eyes shot to
Din before he could speak, reading his thoughts as only a brother could.

“If this was your foundling-“ The older warrior spat at the other Mandalorian. “If she had
killed the child, would you show mercy?”

Din faltered, but then you saw him drop his arms in a silent acknowledgement and let his
eyes train on the face of the Black Sun Leader.

The Falleen seemed to realize that Din would not aid her, and her eyes grew wide as she
stared back up at Paz, mouth opening and closing fruitlessly as she tried to summon a barter
for her life.

Even as the other Mandalorians closed ranks around Paz, watched in silence as he aimed his
pistol between the Black Sun leader’s eyes, Paz didn’t falter. Nor did he make a grand show,
letting his booming voice roll from deep within his chest. No, Paz was simple in that he
clicked the safety off the blaster, his fist clenching at his side and his shoulders trembling in
righteous rage.

“Those who kill children don’t deserve an honorable death.”

You closed your eyes and looked away as the Falleen woman’s voice rose for all of a second
before being cut off by the ringing out of a blaster bolt.

You didn’t look back in the silence that followed, only opening your eyes again when Paz
finally raised his voice, letting it ring forth and upwards into the ceiling, echoing into the
oncoming dawn.



“Oya!”

“Oya!” The Mandos around him echoed with a great cheer, quickly dissolving into cries of
exultation and victory. Yet in your chest it felt bittersweet, the product of several casualties
from the Mandos in the Covert’s ranks, and beyond that, the smile of a child that you’d never
get to see.

Din turned back to you, and you lifted your eyes to him as he stood over you, offering a hand
to help you stand. You smiled up at him, finally letting your shoulders droop and muscles
unwind now that the battle was well and truly over, now that you could return home to the
Razorcrest with Grogu, safe and whole once more. At least now, you were together once
more.

You used his grip to rock to a stand, only to find the ground sway beneath you severely. For a
moment you thought the ground had been rocked by another explosion, but instead this time
there was no sound except you falling to your knees in a daze.

"Cuyan!" Din hissed, immediately following you to the floor, where he kneeled beside you,
one hand bracing your back. You felt the world spin for a moment, settling only after you had
centered yourself with a hand to the floor.

"I-I'm alright." You managed, voice cracked and casting Din a slightly embarrassed look.
"I'm pretty dizzy, I think I might have hit my head."

Really it was more than that, it was pouring every ounce of your being into the fight after just
having survived the previous one, after barely getting any rest following a grueling day or
clawing your way back to the surface from the bowels of Coruscant, of even before then
having fought with barely any sleep for days prior.

You were spent.

There wasn't an ounce of energy left within you and having finally acknowledged that fact,
your body had succumbed to the bone breaking fatigue left behind. Your legs couldn't carry
you a step further, something that made you feel a little chagrin to admit.

"Sorry Din." You offered with a conciliatory smile. "I-I...don't think I can stand."

Yet even if you could, your body would refuse to stay upright for long, because even now you
could feel a heavy, oppressive presence of sleep, of rest now that you were safe, beckon for
you. Despite your vain attempts to ignore it, it called to you with the imminent whisper of true
rest, of surrendering completely and totally now that you were safe. The velvet touch of
slumber reached to embrace you, and you found that you went willingly.

"In fact...I'm...I'm going to rest now if that's okay. I'm fine, I'm not hurt, I just...really need to
sleep." You spoke, voice softer now, eyelids growing heavy. The muscles in your body
automatically began to loosen, and you found yourself leaning into Din’s hand at your back,
head lolling to the side and soon being braced against his chest plate.



Din nodded, and the hand at your back unfurled as he realized you weren't in any danger,
that you were here, with him, but drifting away for only a little bit before you came back to
him.

"Will you be here when I wake up?" You asked, and a flash of wakefulness washed over you
as you tried to keep your eyes open long enough for him to answer. The thought that he would
once again be gone when you did ease back into wakefulness haunted you, but Din’s gentle
voice spoke, erasing your fears and lulling you to sleep.

"I'll try my best." He replied softly. "But if I'm not, I promise you- "

"No matter what, if you call for me, I'll come.”

much braver and more sure of herself, how she's finally settled into her feelings for Din,
how her relationship with Grogu has improved, and how she's finally getting that
warrior spirit that I truly envision for her. Though I write a lot of Cuyan's reactions from
my perspective, she's really become her own strong character in this, and I hope that a
lot of you can relate to her instinct for survival along with her kind heart and
courageousness.



Thank you so much for continuing to follow this fic, for all your lovely comments and
kudos, and for staying with me on this incredible crazy journey it has been writing this
series. Thank you!

I'll see you in the next arc: The Prisoner



Chapter 32: Part Thirty Two: Realization
Chapter Summary

You were alive. You were alive, whole, and though you had not escaped from the ordeal
unscathed, you had clawed your way back to Din, fighting tooth and nail to survive. Din
would have been impressed if he wasn't struck by the strength sapping relief of your
expression slackening into slumber, lips barely apart with the softest of breaths as you
dozed.

For a moment Din was struck by how your now peaceful face contrasted with the
ferocious determination, the fear and the bravery that so often held your expression. The
beauty of your suddenly vulnerable visage startled him in some ways, strange to him
and yet not unwelcome by any means. With several strands of hair falling into your face,
eyes still and body completely limp in his hold, the urge to hold you closer, to never let
you go again seemed to overwhelm him, and Din was held fast by the force of it.

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

Din watched as your eyes lowered peacefully, fluttering shut in a beautiful, blissful slumber.
Your breathing began to even out, head drooping as you finally gave into the insistent grasp
of sleep after your ordeal. With your body slack, Din let his arms cradle you against his chest
plate, shoulders scrunched up near your face, arms limp on your side and legs splayed out
past his lap.

Din had forgotten how many days it had been since you had been taken, but he was sure that
it was close to a full week. Nearly seven days. Seven days of longing of desperation, of
hoping and praying against all odds that somehow, you had made it through unscathed. The
persistent clench in his chest even now had yet to completely abate, clinging tight to his ribs
and restricting the breath of relief held there.

All that time Din had struggled to focus on what he thought was Paz's dying wish, to save the
covert, to destroy the Black Sun, to make a place for them in a galaxy that had tried to steal
everything from them. All the while Din could feel his chest seize at the thought of you and
the child somewhere, waiting for him. In his mind you were exhausted, pursued, weak with
hunger and fatigue while trying to keep you and the toddler alive.

In the darkness of the Coruscant night, when the neon lights of the underground glittered like
strange constellations, the image of your despairing face haunted him. Despite his efforts,
Din hadn't slept for more than a few hours each night, and each blink of sleep had been
cursed with images of you calling for him, obscured by an ominous shadow that dimmed the
light of fight in your eyes.



When dawn came, it was only the work of routing the disjointed Black Sun forces that kept
him occupied. Each breath was spent trying to navigate the underground with the other
warriors or being bent over a map trying to pinpoint the enemy forces and drive them from
the area surrounding the covert. It was only the instinctive, muscle memory driven pursuit of
battle that kept Din on his feet, ever moving, thinking, planning. Yet in the still moments,
where he paced an alley or gazed down from a rooftop, he almost swore he saw you dart
around a corner, so deep was his imagination. Chasing your image was fruitless and resulted
in little else than his own empty heart.

Yet now, here, held in his embrace, Din could finally feel a part of himself sink down from
the sky and settle deep into his soul once more as if grounded by the gravity of your weight
in his arms. The fear, the anger, the desperation seemed to fall from him like a shroud, and in
its place Din could feel the weight of it replaced by the overwhelming feeling of relief, of
gratitude to the stars and to the heavens that you and the child were safe, whole, with him
once more.

Though the remaining Mandalorian forces milled around in the aftermath of the battle, for a
moment they were beyond Din's perception. For what mattered to him now was you, here,
tucked so that your sleeping head lolled against his chest plate in well-deserved rest.

You were alive. You were alive, whole, and though you had not escaped from the ordeal
unscathed, you had clawed your way back to Din, fighting tooth and nail to survive. Din
would have been impressed if he wasn't struck by the strength sapping relief of your
expression slackening into slumber, lips barely apart with the softest of breaths as you dozed.

For a moment Din was struck by how your now peaceful face contrasted with the ferocious
determination, the fear and the bravery that so often held your expression. The beauty of your
suddenly vulnerable visage startled him in some ways, strange to him and yet not unwelcome
by any means. With several strands of hair falling into your face, eyes still and body
completely limp in his hold, the urge to hold you closer, to never let you go again seemed to
overwhelm him, and Din was held fast by the force of it.

A small whine echoed in front of him, and Din's sudden fixation on your sleeping face was
interrupted by the child toddling away from the Mandalorian medic who had watched over
him in the battle, one who was now focused on the incoming injured. The child scampered
over quickly, making a small sound of distress as he reached Din's kneeling figure with you
still in his arms. Plaintively, he placed a small hand on your form, upturning wide worried
eyes to the Mando before him.

"It's okay." Din replied, voice quiet, afraid to wake you. "She's just sleeping."

Din swore he almost felt the relief roll off the figure of the little one in front of him, like a
stone dropped into a still pool of water. It was a small reminder of the child's strange abilities,
able to touch the parts of Din that weren't physical, somehow extending himself in a way that
the Mando couldn't understand.

You shifted slightly in your sleep, as if too sensing the odd ripple from the child. Din was
reminded once again of the strange bond you and his charge shared, something that lay
beyond his understanding. It begged many questions, all of which Din had no means to



answer. How the child knew your name, how you both and he had come to be in this exact
place at the exact time that he and the other Mandos had attacked, somehow reuniting you, all
felt beyond his comprehension. If he tried to grasp it, to reach out and seek the answer, his
only reply would be a soft mist slipping through his fingers, just barely out of reach.

Yet at the same time, it was...strangely captivating. There were those that believed that such
events happened for a reason, that it was indeed the galaxy at work, pulling the invisible
silver tethers that connected the stars. Din did not consider himself to be one of those people.
To think that some great unknowable force connected events in such a way was a luxury that
those struggling to survive in the aftermath of the Empire could not afford. It was wishful
thinking, one reserved only for those who did not have the strength to fight by their own
accord, who needed something greater to carry them through.

And yet...

It seemed that with every new step in this journey that he had untaken with the child, with
you, that...that belief had slowly begun to crumble at the edges.

It was the same with you as well. It seemed that every time Din had finally begun to
understand you, had grasped the person that you were, that you surprised him once more. On
the waystation he had been taken aback by your fierce defense of the child, with your body
curled around him even as a blaster pressed against your scalp. After, on the desolate moon
you three had taken refuge on, he had seen the vulnerability as you confessed your past,
seeking answers to the universe that Din had in some ways sought out as well. On Hypori
your attempts to aid him, to stumble past the Razorcrest’s ramp despite teetering on death's
door had shaken him to the core, unexpected in that anyone would go so far for him.

More than anything, Din could not forget the blaze in your eyes as you faced down the
Clawdite on Rishi, as if the brilliant flame there could burn away the infinite darkness
between suns.

Now, to see how you had managed to again survive despite the impossible odds, made the air
in Din's chest stutter. No longer could he reconcile the image of your form hurling the armed
grenade in a gravity defying arc with the image of your scared, despairing face upon being
discovered in the Razorcrest's hold after your escape on Kadak.

Ever evolving, Din refused to take his eyes away from the radiance of it all, the enthralling
unfolding of this persona you had grown into with every step of your journey. He had never
seen anything quite like it, almost like watching the collection of wandering cosmic dust and
nebulae condense, collect to form the birth of a new star.

Strange, unexpected, captivating, mysterious, and yet between it all...beautiful. Yet Din knew
that somehow, this was only the beginning of your journey, that you would continue to defy
the odds and show him this person you would continue to be, to change into; and Din...

Din expected nothing less.

The child before him grunted as he managed to haul himself up, tugging on your clothes to
maneuver himself into your lap. As Din watched, the small green toddler observed your face



for a few moments, as if to reassure himself you truly were only asleep. He leaned forward,
bracing himself as he ever so gently put his hand on your face in typical fashion. The sight
made a small smile appear under Din’s helmet. Then, gently, the child lowered himself so
that he lay down across your front, ears drooping in fatigue as he settled himself.

"Sleep well, kid." Din smiled, and he could hear a final, mumbled coo in response before the
child stilled, curled onto your stomach.

For a moment that nightmare, that specter of the child, of you, laying prone in the vast
underworld of Coruscant, so far beyond his reach, surfaced again within the depths of his
mind. Like a dark shadow, the reminder that he had almost lost the both of you, that he could
have never seen either of you again made his shoulders tighten, his jaw clench. His gentle
touch around your shoulders fisted into your sleeves, knuckles white with a fierceness
previously unknown to him. Behind his visor, Din's shaded eyes flashed dangerously with the
urge to fight, to defend, to protect the two of you with everything he had.

The image brought forth a relentless protectiveness that prowled across Din's thoughts,
unwittingly tightening his hold on you both. Din felt his chest constrict, that same responsive
anger rising in defense, in the Mandalorian instinct to protect, to defend. Like a loth-wolf,
Din could feel a growl surface within him, as if daring the stars themselves to try and take
you both from him once more.

He was never going to let you go again. Of that, he swore.

"Djarin?"

Din looked up, jarred from his thoughts by the voice above him. There Paz stood, helmet
tilted to observe the trio below him. The older warrior still had a hand braced on his side,
where a fresh bandage hid his torn flight suit. A mild patch of red still remained under his
hand, but Paz seemed to pay it little mind, focused instead on the sight before him. Din could
see his visor shift to observe the two asleep in his arms, where he huffed an almost inaudible
laugh.

"Sleeping?" He inquired, voice dipping as if it would be a discourtesy to intrude upon your
restful dreams, and Din nodded in reply. "They deserve it."

Din couldn't help the small smile that crossed his lips, hidden underneath his helmet.
Wordlessly, he shifted the two resting creatures in his arms so that the child balanced,
sprawled, across your front, and his arms cradled your shoulders and dipped beneath your
legs so he could carry you. With a small grunt, he stood, taking you both with him. Your head
lolled gently against his chest, and for a moment he felt a warm wash of affection at your
delicate but vulnerable state.

"Here-" Paz offered, extending an arm, only to halt at Din's sudden glare from behind his
helmet. Instantly the younger warrior felt his body radiate tension, feet shifting wide to dart
back if need be, almost like a skittish animal. Din felt a guardedness, a trace of hostility
broiling under his skin, pointing his gaze at Paz as if he dared the other Mando to take
another single step forward.



The older Mando looked almost sheepish for a moment, realizing his mistake in trying to take
you both out of Din's arms so soon after your reunion. The Mandalorian instinct to protect
one's clan, to defend one's own simmered deep in Din's chest, and Paz seemed to recognize
that in Din's sudden tight grip on your sleeping form. The arm that had automatically
extended retracted quickly, which in turn was met by Din's softening stance, knowing that no
one would be able to force you from his hold just yet.

Yet with Paz now here, Din's mind began to fog with questions once more. How was he
alive? On top of that, to be standing, to be able to fight despite the injuries Din had seen on
him last was something that defied all possibility. Din had grieved for his Vod as much as he
had wished you were with him once more for all those days you had been gone. Yet against
all possibility, you two had found each other, had recovered your wounds and fought your
way to safety. The fact alone that somehow, in the vast immeasurable depth of the Coruscant
underworld, you and Paz had managed to find and ally yourself seemed like nothing less than
some sort of divine cosmic chance.

Though, knowing you, it was entirely possible.

Paz trailed at Din's side as he walked through the wreckage of the battlefield. Din felt himself
relax with the steady presence of his Vod at his side. Rivals though they were, they were
together honor bound by creed. Despite the fact that Din and the older warrior had their
differences, that they butted heads on more than one occasion, that they had even come to
blows in one of their recent exchanges, Din could feel himself slacken with the knowledge
that he trusted his comrade with his life. Now, in the aftermath of all that had occurred, he
could trust him with his tiny clan as well.

Paz lingered as they walked, taking his time in checking in with other Mandalorians, making
sure that the injured were accounted for, reassuring younger warriors that had yet to see
action of this kind since the escape from Nevarro. Din waited for him each time, trying not to
mind the ache in his arms and shoulders from carrying your form. You and the child seemed

Fortunately, Paz ensured his interactions were brief, promising to speak at length once the
Covert had safely arrived back at their compound.

After he was done, Din led the way past the broken murals, the carved fallen columns, the
cracked tile, out into the brimming dawn. A soft pink haze pierced the underbelly of the
