central district.

Din had landed the Razorcrest a ways away from the battlefield, not wishing to let the sound
of the engines alert the Black Sun of the incoming battle. Those who were able lifted off on
jetpacks, hovering for a moment in air before setting their sights beyond the shanty rooftops
and taller buildings reflecting the scant light of sunrise, back towards the compound.

Those too injured to fly had already begun to gather at the ship, where they had erected a
small triage of tending to those laid flat by the turret, those knocked unconscious, and the
ones too broken to stand. Din had no doubt they would all recover, knowing the warriors of
his Covert to not shy at pain, to embrace it as an existent part of their battle-worn culture. Yet



the sight of his comrades in varying states of injury and pain unsettled him, made him grip
your body a little closer. If somehow, that had been you…

He shook his head free of the thought, instead turning his attention to striding forward with
purpose, intent on the inside of the Razorcrest’s hold.

Upon his arrival to the landing platform, those present looked up at Din, or rather, the
sleeping forms in his arms. Din could feel their helmeted stares as he paced past them,
shielded eyes appraising, considering, passing silent judgement on Din, on the child in his
arms, on his tiny clan that had been through so much. Yet Din ignored them, gaze intent on
his empty bunk. His boots thudded heavy against the metal grate of the cargo bay, stopping at
the edge of the mat where he had lain to rest many times. There, he paused, realizing there
was no way he could lower you down onto the mat without disturbing the child curled on
your chest.

"Here."

Din craned his head, eyes coming to rest on the familiar figure of the warrior who had first
attempted to throw the grenade at the turret. She stood a step behind Din, voice soft as she
held out her arms expectantly to temporarily relieve him of the child. Slowly, cautiously, she
reached forward and took the child with gloved hands, careful not to wake him. Din made no
effort to stop her but stood rigid and still as she lifted the sleeping toddler from your form, for
a moment cradling him against her own chest plate.

Din turned his attention to you once more, lowering himself so that he could scoot into the
narrow space and lay you down gently against the mat. You shifted slightly as he did so, and
for a moment your eyes fluttered open at the sudden movement, hazy gaze resting on Din's
visor. Din could see the vague light of awareness flicker back into your eyes, a question half-
forming on your lips.

He paused for a moment, feeling a part of him stir at your gentle sleep laden eyes and slightly
parted lips. Mouth suddenly dry, he swallowed once before murmuring:

"Sleep, Cuyan. You're safe."

That seemed to satisfy you, as your eyes slid shut once more and muscles grew pliant so Din
could detach himself. With your arms then gently cradled by your head, body on your side,
Din withdrew quietly so as to not disturb you further.

Then he turned to the female Mandalorian that held the small but prodigal child against her
form, holding out with waiting hands and expectant breath. Softly, the child was returned to
him, and then reunited with the one who had kept him safe for all the time that Din could not,
nestled against your stomach as you both sank further into the embrace of slumber.

Again, Din was struck by the sudden fierceness in his chest, enough so that it briefly stole his
breath away from him. The sight of you two nestled against each other, safe within the arms
of sleep, drew forth an almost primal urge in him to defend, to protect, to keep safe at all
costs. He was nearly startled with the force of it, stirring heavy in his veins and winding the
sinew of his muscles tight within its grasp.



"Din." A heavy hand landed on his pauldron, shaking Din from the reverie he had trapped
himself within. A glance to the side proved that Paz had returned from his discussions with
those injured. Din could see a quiet resignation in the way Paz’s shoulders were set, the
slouch there born of a grief, an acceptance for that which was lost. Din felt a hardness form in
his throat, gaze sliding back over to your forms within the bunk.

"How many?" Din asked quietly, his voice dipping low more out of reverence for those
inquired than to not rouse you.

Paz stilled for a moment, as if he too was calculating, assessing, grieving. At last, he let out a
low sigh, voice nearly tinged on a growl.

"Four." He replied at last.

Four warriors. They had lost four warriors during the raid. Each a life snuffed out by the blast
of the turret, or perhaps the lucky shot of a Black Sun member catching past the beskar shield
they wore. Now their bodies lay among the rubble, to be carried back and honored for their
sacrifice.

Din grimaced under his helmet, jaw set hard. It was the most that the Covert had lost since
the raid on Nevarro. Four warriors from a barely surviving creed now lay somewhere beyond
the stars, having given their lives for their clan, and now reaping their celestial reward. It was
a blow just as devastating as losing the foundling slain by the Black Sun leader’s hand, for as
much as the future was important to the covert, so too was the experience, the history of its
warriors.

"It would have been more, if not for her." Paz spoke, following Din's gaze to your sleeping
form. For a moment, his gaze rested there, holding something still in his chest reserved only
for himself. Then he sighed, the hand on Din’s pauldron curling. "If she were Mandalorian,
her actions would have earned her jaig eyes on her armor."

Din looked at him then, truly. With his gaze now fully on his Vod, it became apparent that
there was something more to Paz’s words, a connection forged there in Din’s absence. The
truth of it made Din’s eyes flash in recognition, hackles rising territorially as he understood
the other warrior’s intentions.

Paz's eyes remained on your form, as if almost blatantly ignoring Din's inquiring stare. Yet
the hidden meaning in Paz's words did not escape Din's notice.

"If she were Mandalorian..."

Din felt something flutter in his chest, and he almost put a gloved hand there to quiet it. The
thought excited him, strangely. There was something about the thought of you adopting the
creed, of swearing the Resol'nare and being taken in by the Covert that made a spark of
electricity run along his skin, cheeks warm at the thought. To share that culture with you, for
your bond to be cemented in something other than experience and circumstance made an
ardent desire bloom in his veins, longing for the connection, the possibilities of that thought.

"Perhaps." He found himself mutter back, mouth dry with the word



Then, as Din watched, Paz turned to face him, dropping the amicable hand from Din's
pauldron and trying to stand his full height despite his injuries. Din blinked in surprise at
Paz's sudden change in attitude, almost as if he was once again challenging Din to stand
against him. Yet automatically Din rose in return, never one to be cowed by Paz’s superior
height and weight. Under his helmet his eyes narrowed, meeting Paz’s gaze head on.

"I mean it, Djarin." Paz dropped Din's first name once more, and just like that, they were
once again rivals, the brotherly reassurance falling away with an uneasy shudder.

"I know you have feelings for her, but if you don't act on them, I may be inclined to pursue
her myself."

Din had pressed himself up against Paz's chest without fully processing Paz's words, a growl
low in his throat at the threat of someone else staking a claim on you. Paz merely regarded
him, head tilted downwards to observe his Vod almost nonchalantly.

Din was at a loss for words, anger and defensiveness the only emotions he could summon to
Paz's remark. Yet there was an uncertainty there, one he wouldn't admit to. Having yet to
understand his feelings towards you, he couldn't necessarily object to Paz's words.

Paz seemed to realize this as well, and Din swore he could almost see the smirk under the
older warrior's helmet.

"That is...unless you decide to act first, Vod." The last words were emphasized with an almost
taunting lilt. Din felt his entire body radiate tension, coiling like a viper ready to strike. Yet
again, words failed him, a silent snarl threatening to overtake his features.

Paz let out an almost imperceptible huff, and Din could hear the smile behind it. Yet just as
quickly as Paz had caused himself to tower over Din, he relented and stepped away. As Din
watched he walked outside to help escort the remaining wounded into the ship, settling them
down anywhere Din had space in the cargo hold. Those present had begun to look less at Din
and more amongst themselves, hands reaching out to reassure those barely clinging to
consciousness, to aid in settling down those too broken to stand.

Eventually, when it appeared all were aboard, Paz hit the lever for the hatch, nodding back at
the ship's captain and pilot. Din didn’t offer a return nod, merely holding the other warrior's
gaze for a heavy, angered moment before turning to ascend the ladder to the cockpit. Before
he did, he cast one final, lingering glance at you and Grogu, at his tiny clan, before removing
himself from the hold.

Paz remained below with the others, leaving Din alone in the cockpit with his thoughts. As he
lifted the Razorcrest off the platform, angling it back in the direction of the Covert's
compound, his mind began to churn much like the steady rhythm of the ship's engines.

Paz's remark had unsettled him, angered him, and the knowledge of that alone sat heavy in
his bones. The thought that you, after all of your travels with Din, the events you two had
gone through together, would be swayed by someone else’s affections made his chest seize.



He didn't blame Paz for his interest in you. After all, you were quite something to behold.
With your quiet but dazzling beauty, your ferocity in protecting yourself and the toddler in
your care, the empathy to refuse in leaving anyone behind, and your warm but gracious smile
were all things that made that odd flutter rise in Din's chest once more.

Yet for Paz to voice an interest in that, to voice that in front of Din so soon after you had
reunited with him was less a remark and more a challenge. It was one Din automatically rose
to but in some ways didn't understand the repercussions of.

Yet the image of you on Paz’s arm, of holding his hand with the same delicate care you
extended to him in Din’s moments of vulnerability seemed to suck the warmth from his skin,
cold and empty like the void of space.

Din's intentions eluded even himself. It wasn't as if he was wanting for time to act on his
feelings towards you, he had plenty of chances prior to arriving on Coruscant. You didn't
seem unreceptive either, judging by how you had slowly let down your guard around him,
and had come to trust him with as much as your life.

That anxiety, the nervousness you had upon your first meeting had ebbed over the weeks you
two had been together, spending nearly every waking moment in each other’s presence. Din
had slowly grown accustomed to it, from your early, quiet attempts at conversation to more
recently, your blatant efforts in seeking him for comfort from your own fears.

The flash of your form tucked against his chest in the dark of night, of your gentle and quiet
snores echoing in the velvet midnight of Coruscant, of his hand guiding yours through the
Covert entrance resounded quietly in his thoughts. With it came the memory of your teary
eyes gazing up at him, lit by the starlight outside of the Razorcrest's cockpit, asking what you
had done to earn his quiet rejection of you.

"I was afraid." He had said then.

Afraid, yet of what?

Yet even now, that fear still lingered. Din had rarely been afraid of much in his life, but for
some reason the thought that if he spoke his feelings into words, that if he tried to advance
upon you, to reach out and touch that part of you that sang with him, that you yourself would
shatter like something beautiful but fragile. The feeling of never being able to act, to let those
feelings mount but eventually die away, that Din could ignore. Yet the thought that had he
confessed to you, that you in turn did not have the same feelings, that thought tore at Din
from the inside out.

It wasn't the rejection alone. It was the thought that somehow, by trying to find a piece of
himself within you, only for you to keep him away, that he would ruin everything. Nothing
would be the same. Those quiet conversations in the shadows of the Razorcrest’s hold, the
fleeting touches that spoke silently of something more, the shared gazes that said words that
could not be spoken, those strange and yet warm encounters between you both would be
soiled by Din's selfishness, the need to have you meet him halfway down this path both of
you tread.



Even then, Din didn't have a name for the emotions tied within him. It was almost as if
putting titles to them somehow soured their meanings. And yet...

They remained.

It was the urge to protect you as much as it was to fight alongside you, to keep you beside
him during his travels and abate the emptiness within the cold hull of the ship, to retain those
quiet midnight conversations deigned only for you and him.

He wanted to be with you, beside you, at your side. He wanted you to abandon the idea of
finding a quiet core world to settle upon, alone but alive. He wanted you to stay, to never
leave again. He wanted to see this marvelous and endlessly fascinating person you were
evolving into, to keep with him the image of your form standing amongst the flowers on
Rishi with the breeze ruffling the hem of your clothes, of your arm arched gracefully
throwing the grenade at the towering tank that rained hellfire down on your both.

He wanted you.

It was then that he finally comprehended the odd feelings within his chest, the fascination of
your personal evolution, the captivity of your quiet but brilliant beauty, the awe of the
determined blaze within your eyes. Much like witnessing the cosmic birth of a star within
your own evolution, the realization of Din’s own emotions burst like a supernova, painting
the background of the galaxy with dazzling, ethereal colors.

He had been right. He couldn't look away. Now he knew the reason.

It was....almost as if he loved you.

Chapter 33: Part Thirty Three: The Rematch
Chapter Summary

"Do you really not know?" She asked, surprise now evident in her voice. When you
shook your head she regarded you, a huff of disbelief sounding from under her helmet.

A loud clang rang out as Din threw his head forward under Paz’s grip, connecting his
helmet with Paz’s in a Keldabe strike.

"Paz said if Djarin didn't make a move on you, he'd court you."

Gaze shooting back to the Mando beside you, you blinked at her, and distantly you
could hear the faint, tinny sound of your brain trying to process the information she had
just given you.

"He…WHAT?!"

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

"Oof!"

You blinked dazedly as you once again found yourself staring back up at the ceiling of the
warehouse, the makeshift practice mat pressed up against your back, arms sprawled on either
side of your body. Chest heaving, mouth agape with surprise and an effort to catch your
breath, you watched as the helmet of your sparring partner hovered far above you.

"Had enough already?"

You blinked in a daze, chest tight as your thoughts raced in an attempt to catch up with your
body.

It had been several days since you had woken back up in the covert. According to Din, you
had slept for nearly a full cycle, completely and utterly spent. How you were still standing by
the time you had wandered into the ruins was beyond him. You don't remember collapsing
into his arms after the ultimate battle, much less being carried back to the safety of the
Razorcrest, where you had remained with him and Grogu for the next standard rotation.

When you finally awoke, curled on Din's bed inside the ship, Grogu snoozing against your
stomach, it had taken a moment to orient yourself. For a heartbeat you feared you were still
on the streets, having collapsed after pushing yourself for so long and falling into an almost
catatonic sleep. Worse yet, you were afraid that, somehow, you had been found by the Black



Sun during your slumber and had been taken back to a hideout to await whatever fearsome
fate lay for you there.

Yet then you felt the coarse, worn fabric of one of the blankets from your own small bed
behind the cockpit, heard the snores of the child beside you, and smelled the familiar scent of
carbon scoring, weapon oil, and carbonite residue that belonged to the Razorcrest's hull.
Comforted by the familiar safety of the ship, you had crept from the bunk, only to discover
Din dozing just beyond, head tucked against his chest and back leaned up against the
bulkhead at the foot of the cot.

Even now the sight filled you with a warmth beyond words, awash in the deep-seated
affection you held for the Mando, in how he refused to leave your side even as you slept. You
had been touched deeply, but not enough to ignore the growl of your stomach after having not
eaten for close to a cycle. After you had reluctantly left for the kitchens, Din had found you
there, nearly frantic at your absence. Though you couldn't see his face, it was evident alone
from his body language upon finally finding you in the kitchens, as he stood stiffly in the
curtained entryway, that he was terrified at finding you missing again.

Even now he waited just beyond your sight, silently observing your instruction from the
female Mandalorian you had saved during the battle. Leaned up against the wall, arms
crossed, the dim overhead lights of the warehouse glinted dark against his visor.

You blinked a few more times, finally shaking your head to clear your unfocused thoughts.
You gave the female Mandalorian, Hana, a grin, eyes flashing as you summoned the answer
to her question.

"Not yet."

You could hear her huff a half-laugh, coming around to your front and extending a gloved
hand to assist you to your feet. You took it gladly, swaying for a moment upon standing
before finding your balance once more. Shooting your new friend a quick smile of thanks,
you rolled your shoulders a few times before once again settling into a defensive position as
she took her stance.

Hana had been one of the first to approach you after your stunt with the grenade. Apparently
your heroics had earned you a decent amount of respect from certain members of the Covert,
who admired your bravery. The muttered remarks and snide laughter that had whispered past
you before your capture had vanished seemingly overnight, replaced by polite nods and a
quiet acceptance of you into the Covert’s fold. You had been somewhat surprised by it at first,
a little taken aback by how quickly the consensus on your presence had changed. Yet then
you realized that your single act, of saving one of their own in the heat of battle, had spoken
volumes to the Mandalorians, and had earned you a silent respect from the warriors.

It helped that Paz had begun to show you a considerable amount of favor as well. Though the
alor had been prickly towards you in the beginning, your journey together through the
underworld had replaced that trepidation with a familiar companionship, a relationship built
on respect and trust at having saved each other’s lives over and over again.



You often found your well-being inquired after by the older warrior, asking if you had
enough sleep, if you had eaten well, if you were recovering quickly from your ordeal. More
than once, you had found yourself accompanied as you roamed the compound, at mealtimes,
or simply tending Grogu. Though Paz's presence was certainly welcome, it surprised you
with the sudden frequency of his visits to you. It was almost as if his company was something
beyond friendship, an attention given only to you.

Din had noticed as well, and if he had hardly let you out of his sight before, he now remained
practically glued to your side at all hours. You could hardly breathe, eat, or sleep without Din
being nearby. In the beginning you didn't mind at all, happy to quietly be in his comforting
presence after having been away from his side for so long. After a few days, however, it had
begun to get a little stifling. Hell, you couldn't even use the communal showers without Din
respectfully waiting outside somewhere nearby.

That wasn't to mention whatever was going on between him and Paz. Though Din was never
more than a few steps away from you, Paz had only doubled his efforts to talk to you, to have
a conversation, to crowd into a table with you, Din and Grogu during mealtime, much to
Din's chagrin. At one point Paz regaled you with a tale of Din trying a jetpack for the first
time, a story which nearly had you in tears of laughter with Paz's natural affinity for
storytelling. Yet then you looked across the table to see Din grasping his mug with something
beyond a death-grip, emanating a silent violence in Paz's direction.

It was almost as if they were purposefully antagonizing each other over something, and
somehow you had found yourself caught in the middle.

Now, your eyes flickered over to the Mando leaning on the wall, simultaneously keeping one
eye on you, and the other on Grogu, who was playing with Umos and the other Covert
children.

"You ready, Cuyan?"

Your gaze focused back on Hana in front of you, stance prepared and ready to launch
forward. The female Mandalorian had taken it upon herself to repay her self-proclaimed debt
to you by teaching you basic self-defense skills, a lesson that you were quickly learning could
be quite painful.

Still, despite your winded and sore muscles, you nodded at her, signaling for her to begin her
attack. Without any preamble the deadly huntress launched at you in full force, holding
nothing back with her relentless assault.

To your credit, you managed to block her first few blows, using the width of your forearm to
hold back her strikes as she had taught you. Trying to put distance between yourself and your
attacker, you kept your hands close to shield your face, eyes moving quickly in anticipation
of her attacks. Hana’s barrage had little room for counter attack, her offense overwhelming.
Yet you managed to hold her back, having grown accustomed to her full-fledged assault.
Your mistake quickly became apparent, however, when you realized you were only tracking
her punches and attempts to grapple you at torso level.



You realized your mistake too late, as the Mando spun and with a single sweep of her foot,
kicked your legs out from under you and once again sent you sprawling to the ground, air
rushing from your lungs.

"You held out a little longer that time." She remarked idly, and how she wasn't even winded
was beyond your meager comprehension.

You huffed a laugh, still heaving for air below her.

"Can't you...hold back? Even a little?" You asked between gasps. Hana went silent for a
moment, and soon you found yourself assisted to your feet once more.

"If a bounty hunter comes after you, they won't be holding back. You have to be prepared for
that." She answered, voice serious. "Trust me, I'm doing you a favor by being so hard on
you."

The reassuring clap on your back made you nearly stumble with the force of it, and certainly
didn't help you catch your breath. Yet you shot your spar mate a chagrined smile nonetheless,
words absent but gratitude present.

"What's this, then?" A voice echoed from across the make-shift gymnasium, prompting both
you and Hana to turn to its source. Paz stood in the entryway, facing towards the two of you.
At his entrance, all heads present turned, including the gaggle of youngsters that were playing
and entertaining your young charge. At the sight of the warrior some of the children
abandoned their game and trotted over towards Paz gleefully.

Paz must have been in a good mood, because though he first pretended to not notice the few
kids surrounding him, he suddenly sprang and caught one of them around their middle. As
you watched he hoisted the young one into the air, man handling the child, much to her utter
delight. You recognized the little girl with the long braid that fell from under her helmet, the
same child that had called to Umos when you had first met him. Pretending to have captured
her, Paz gave a fake roar and held her high as she squealed and giggled. You hid your own
giggle behind a hand, not noticing the way Din's visor snapped towards the sound and
quickly looked between you and his Vod.

Umos, upon seeing one of his playmates captured by the warrior, valiantly reached upward
for her, jumping in an attempt to reach his friend. Paz growled and held her aloft just out of
reach as she giggled without restraint. In a playfully desperate resort Umos began to strike
Paz's armored middle with his small fists. Paz at once feigned injury, crying out as he
pretended to drop the girl before depositing her once more on the floor. Umos continued his
barrage even as the girl pretended to hide behind her rescuer, until at last Paz fell to one knee
and began to plead for mercy from the attack with a fake, wheezing voice.

Satisfied, Umos and the girl trotted back to the fold of the other youngsters, and Paz rose to
his feet before approaching you and your instructor. You were unable to hide your laughter
behind your hands, whereas Hana remained unamused.

"You indulge them too much." She chastised the other warrior upon his approach, and Paz
merely shrugged.



"It won't be long before some of them join the fighting corps." He replied, voice dipping to a
more serious tone. "I'll indulge them as long as I can before then."

Hana gave a small huff but didn't reply, and so Paz turned to you instead. You could see his
visor sink and then rise as he gave you a once over, noticing the thin sheen of sweat on your
skin and your muscles still coiled tight from training.

"It seems you're recovering well." He remarked, and you could hear the smile in his voice.
You returned it, though after a moment you winced and rolled your shoulders once more.

"Hana has been putting me through my paces, that's for sure." You replied. "And not being
exactly kind about it either." That prompted a scoff from your sparring partner, and a sharp
glance from behind her visor.

"If you think I'm being harsh, you should try taking on Vizsla here. I bet you won't complain
after that."

You widened your eyes at her, feeling your stomach sink at the prospect. It was one thing to
take on a skilled warrior roughly your size, but to take on Paz?

"No, no!" You interjected quickly, waving your hands. "I didn't mean it, I promise! I'm
actually enjoying this, see? I like the bruises, I-"

Paz's bark of laughter cut you off, and he crossed his arms before gazing down at you.
Despite his helmet you could almost see the glint of mischief in his eyes.

"Come on Cuyan." He teased. "You took on two Black Sun members and won, not to
mention fought off half an army while saving my shebs back in the Old Temple district. You
could take me."

You opened your mouth to object, only for Hana to interject.

"Actually, the more I think about it, the more it makes sense." She went on. "If you want to
learn quickly, it's best to practice against someone who poses as much of a threat as possible
to you if they were to try and capture you."

"See?" Paz turned to you once more, holding out a gloved hand as if Hana had proven his
point.

You looked helplessly between the two Mandos, quickly finding yourself out of protests
when faced by both of their visored stares.

"Allow me."

You spun, nearly colliding with Din behind you. Force, you hadn’t even heard him sneak up
behind you. He stared past you, gaze leveled directly with Paz's. You could feel your
shoulders sink with relief, a grateful smile rising to your lips upon realizing that by sparring
with Din, you'd at least be safe from any further bruises or bumps on your body. Yet before
you could voice your assent, Paz stepped forward and cleared his throat.



"I believe that it was said Cuyan here should practice with the one who could prove to be the
greatest challenge to her." He spoke, and you blinked upon hearing his voice dip, the
friendliness still there but now edged with a touch of warning.

"The practice is designed to defend against bounty hunters, Vizsla." Din replied, and though
his tone remained level, you could see that sudden tightness in his shoulders, the way his feet
widened under him. "I'm the only one who fits that description."

Paz seemed to sense Din's sudden tension as well, and even then he did not shy from it.
Rather, he tucked his shoulders back from his slack stance, towering to his full height and
staring over your head at the younger Mando. You found yourself stepping back, out of the
way of the two Mandalorian men.

"Is that what you are still, Djarin?" He asked, tilting his head as if studying your companion.
"A meager bounty hunter?"

You blinked, shocked at the sudden challenge in Paz’s words. You opened your mouth to
defend Din, only for Din to speak first.

"How about you ask the twenty-three Black Sun gangsters I killed while you were bumbling
your way through the Old Market district." Din replied back, fists curling at his side. His
voice was still even, not sinister yet, but the warning, the underlying threat was there.

Paz huffed, but the sound was anything but amused. "What's a bounty hunter to a
Mandalorian?" He queried, but even you could hear the growing snarl in his voice.

Din prickled, and his voice dipped to growl something in Mando'a that you couldn't
understand. "Ne shab'rud'niÖ."

Behind you, you could feel Hana stiffen, suck in a sharp breath. You had to stop your jaw
from dropping at Din's tone, shocked at how his voice suddenly dipped into that warning
growl you ever hear when you and the child were in danger, when he was trying to ward off
an enemy. To use it here, pressed up against Paz, chest to chest with the taller Mando, with
someone you considered to be an ally, a friend, was simply beyond belief.

"You might want to step back." Hana murmured to you, wrapping a gloved hand around your
bruised forearm and gently dragging you backwards. At first you allowed yourself to be
escorted, still bewildered by the sudden viciousness between the two Mandos. Then, as if
suddenly coming to your senses, you shrugged off her grasp and forced yourself between the
two of them.

"Enough!" You snapped, one hand placed on either chest as you separated the two. They
seemed to barely notice you, gazes still locked in silent confrontation. Still, they gave way as
you interceded, both taking a step back at you cutting between them. You gave them each a
sharp glance that went unnoticed, each palm splayed across their chest plates.

"Enough!" You said louder this time, finally gaining their attention. You felt Din startle for a
moment, as if suddenly realizing you were there. A gloved palm came up, hesitantly resting



on your hand touching him as if he wanted to remove it, but the urge faded into a gentle
touch. You gave him a stern glance, which he stiffened at.

"I don't know what has gotten into you two recently, but you need to sort it out." You
declared, craning your head to look up at Paz's visor as well. "Whatever it is can't go on like
this. You both need to figure out a way to solve this or cool off."

"C-Cuyan, I would-" Hana tried behind you, stopping as you sent a reprimanding glare her
way as well.

Paz had backed off a step, catching your hand as it fell from his chest plate, holding it
absently whilst continuing to stare at Din. He didn’t speak, and Din did not volunteer to fill
the silence, each of their stares never wavering between the other.

Then Paz tilted his head a mere inch, as if suddenly having a thought. In Mando'a he asked:

"Adik'akaanir?"

You blinked, unfamiliar with the word, so your gaze instead shifted to Din.

That made Din draw himself up, as if rising to the challenge in Paz's words. Giving your
hand a small, reassuring squeeze, he stepped away from you, eyes still locked on his Vod.
You followed them with your gaze, confused and unsure.

"Besbe'trayce?" He asked, voice shifting away from a growl, almost as if he was suddenly
negotiating. Paz considered whatever Din had spoken for a moment, before shaking his head
in a silent reply to the question. Din nodded at this. As if having come to a silent conclusion,
both he and Paz began to pace away several steps, now ignoring you.

"W-wait-" You called after them, concerned. Hana, however, stopped you. You glanced at her
sudden hand on your shoulder, brow creased with worry.

"Let them go." She cautioned, voice low. You wanted to shrug her off, but the indication in
her words prevented you from chasing after the pair, even as your feet itched to do so.

"What are they doing?" You asked, anxiety clear in your voice.

Hana leveled her visored gaze with you, and you could almost feel the sardonic stare
underneath boring into your skin.

"They're doing as you asked, Cuyan." She replied simply. "They're settling this."

Your worried gaze lingered on her visor, seeing your own expression reflected back at you.
When you next turned around, you found both Din and Paz carefully shucking off weapons,
pauldrons, armor and equipment a distance away from each other.

You blinked in surprise, too taken aback by seeing the two without their beskar to interrupt
them. Your confusion continued to mount as you saw Paz send a sidelong glance in your
direction before going to peel away his flight suit as well. Behind you, Hana snorted
derisively at some unknown joke.



Your eyes shifted to Din, who's gaze rested on Paz's figure removing his outer layer before
turning to your wide eyed, agape expression. You could make out an almost imperceptible
shake of his head before he too reached for the fastenings on his flight suit.

A small crowd had begun to gather after hearing the earlier commotion, lurking in doorways
and leaning over the railings of the upper level to look down into the training area. You,
Hana, and now the children stood off to one side as Paz and Din's figures made themselves
known to you.

You wanted to cover your eyes in vague embarrassment upon seeing both of their forms
revealed from under the layers of padding and armor they typically wore. For Paz that meant
a loose sleeveless shirt and his flight suit tied with the sleeves at his waist. The man was built
like a tank, and though the muscle on his form wasn't apparent, you knew that under the layer
of protective fat that he retained enough strength to easily overwhelm most of his opponents
with brute force.

Din had his back turned to you as he shimmied down to his pants under the suit, absent of
any type of undershirt. You tried not to gawk, and for a moment almost wanted to turn around
and avert your eyes out of respect. There was little use for that, however, when whatever was
unfolding in front of you was in such a public setting.

You traced the lines of muscle on Din's back, watching as they rippled under his shoulders
with his movements. There was a slight dip in the muscle where his spine was, and as he
rolled his neck you felt your mouth go a little dry at the motion. It wasn’ your first time
seeing him this exposed. You had seen him shirtless before, in the dark of night, a dim shape
against a lantern in a small room. Yet the image did little to reassure you, only serving to
increase the warmth on your face to a feverish touch.

You turned your flushed, bewildered face to Hana beside you, hopeless in trying to summon
the words to ask what in the stars was going on. The Mando regarded you for a moment
before snorting a laugh under her helmet, using a hand on your shoulder to balance herself as
she doubled over briefly chortling to herself. You were fairly sure you heard her say the word
'Di’kuta' under her wheezing breath.

The gaggle of foundlings and children that had gathered around you paid less attention to her
and more to the half-bare warriors settling into stances a ways away from you all, ooh-ing
and aah-ing over the pile of armor and armaments tucked off to the side of each. At your feet,
Grogu lifted his hands up at you in a signal to be picked up. Absently, you complied, and
when it became apparent you weren't going to get an answer from the Mando beside you, you
turned your attention to Din and Paz once more.

It was clear now that there was some type of spar going on, but for what reasons you still
couldn't understand. Hana had said that both Din and Paz were heeding your advice to 'sort
things out', but as to what that meant, you had absolutely no idea.

Now free of all armor and weapons, both Paz and Din sank in their respective stances as you
and the covert watched on.



Slowly, Din and Paz began to inch forward. You could already see in their movements the
differences in their approaches. Where Paz centered himself in his feet, using his height and
weight to focus his center of gravity into an unbudging mass, Din did the opposite. You could
see him balance on the balls of his feet, knees slightly bent, and arms held up but relaxed,
keeping himself loose and ready to spring into action.

Again, you tried to take a step forward to stop them, but Hana's hand on your shoulder
tightened, causing you to look at her.

"Don't." She spoke low, the previous mirth gone from her voice. Instead, there was a warning
there, a hard stare under her helmet. "They need this."

You blinked at her, and as if sensing your concern and confusion, the child in your arms made
a small murmur and turned his eyes up to you.

"B-but why?" You asked, brow furrowed at your friend.

You could hear Hana release a breath under her helmet, as if dismayed or perhaps frustrated
by your lack of insight.

Yet before she could answer, a rush of movement drew your attention back to the two in the
middle of the training area. Din had rushed forth, landing a series of rapid blows against Paz
before darting away again. Paz blocked them easily, reaching for Din in an attempt at offense
and coming up just short.

It quickly became apparent what Din's method was in this duel. He had no way of physically
overpowering Paz, so he was relying on his superior reflexes and speed to try and wear down
the older warrior with a series of speedy attacks. Whether or not that would work depended
on Paz's stamina, which seemed to be evenly matched with his opponent.

Paz advanced forward, rushing Din in an attempt to grab him, drag him into striking range.
Din managed to sidestep the rush, practically sliding around Paz's outstretched grip only to
withdraw out of reach once more.

Hana hummed beside you appraisingly. You cast her a sideways glance but kept your eyes on
the fight before you. Yet your churning thoughts were interrupted by her voice.

"It seems they each learned some lessons from their previous fight." She remarked, causing
you to finally look at her.

"What fight?" You asked, an eyebrow raised in curiosity.

"The one they had after you and the kid were captured by the Black Sun." She answered
nonchalantly. Yet her reply had your eyes wide and jaw falling open in shock. Instantly you
were scrambling for details, pressuring her for more information.

"Wa-wait, when?" You pressured her, turning to face her.

"After you were captured, I just told you." She replied casually, eyes still locked on the fight.
Din had launched another series of blows, and in it you saw a fighting style not unlike the



one Hana had demonstrated on you. "Paz tried to keep Din from marching into enemy
territory to go rescue you, and so Din challenged him to a duel, and won."

Your head spun with the realization. While you were shocked at Paz for trying to prevent Din
from coming to your aid, the fact that Din had gone as far as to attack his comrade so he
could come rescue you was...actually very touching.

A grunt made you look back towards the two fighting, where you saw Paz had managed to
seize Din by the inside of his arm. The two grappled for a moment, absent from any weapons.
Din landed a series of strikes on Paz, which the older warrior grunted under but did not
loosen his hold on Din as a result of. Finally Din managed to throw his weight enough to the
side to briefly make Paz lose his balance, allowing him to slide free once more.

"Wait, so then why are they still fighting?" You asked Hana, shifting your focus to the other
Mando once more but keeping your eyes on Din as he managed to take several steps
backwards, only for Paz to rush him and seize him around the middle.

"Oh, this is because of what Paz said while you were passed out on Djarin's ship." Hana
spoke, eyes never wavering from the duel in front of her. Your head whipped towards her,
face suddenly confused and wary. "They thought I couldn't hear, but I was right there. It was
impossible not to."

"Wait, what?" You asked, hands slackening to your sides. "What did he say? Did he insult
Din?"

Hana chuckled, shaking her head. "Your head must be as hard as beskar. I'm surprised you
haven't noticed yet."

That did nothing to quell your curiosity, and now you faced fully towards the Mandalorian,
face open with confusion.

"Notice what?"

That made Hana stop, shoulders stiffening as she turned her whole attention towards you
now.

"Do you really not know?" She asked, surprise now evident in her voice. When you shook
your head she regarded you, a huff of disbelief sounding from under her helmet.

A loud clang rang out as Din threw his head forward under Paz’s grip, connecting his helmet
with Paz’s in a kov'nyn strike. The strike itself didn’t rattle Paz, but he seemed to have been
caught by surprise with the action, head reeling backward enough for Din to bring a knee up
against Paz’s leg and catch him hard enough to force the other Mando to loosen his hold. Din
instantly sprung away, and for a moment you saw him reach for his gauntlet, recognizing the
motion as prepping the flamethrower that was absent from his wrist.

"Paz said if Djarin didn't make a move on you, he'd court you."



Gaze shooting back to the Mando beside you, you blinked at her, and distantly you could hear
the faint, tinny sound of your brain trying to process the information she had just given you.

“…Court?” You echoed dumbly, not understanding. “Paz…said?”

All at once you finally made sense of her words, and your confusion was replaced by pure,
unadulterated shock.

"He…WHAT?!"

Your yell momentarily distracted Din, who's helmet whipped in your direction at your sudden
shriek. That gave Paz the opening he was looking for, and with a roar he managed to grab
Din fully. He grunted loudly as Din tried to squirm, managing to fix his hold on Din’s thigh
and ribs. With a yell he heaved the Mando, raising him above his head. The crowd burst with
noise, yelling and shouting and cheering at their champion managing to best his opponent.

You gasped instantly, and the toddler in your arms whined worriedly at his caretaker’s sudden
helplessness, held aloft much like the foundling Paz had hoisted so high earlier. You could
see Paz’s arms bulging with the effort, but his voice was nothing less than triumphant as he
widened his stance, yelling in your direction.

"This is your partner, Cuyan?!" Paz asked despite Din squirming viciously. "He's weak like a
pup!"

You felt your face flush angrily on Din's behalf, and you took a half-step forward in an
attempt to defend your Mando, shaking off Hana in the process.

Din twisted above Paz, managing to get one leg free and bring his boot across Paz's helmet
with a resounding metal clang. Paz reeled from the surprise attack, grip loosening. Suddenly,
Din was tumbling to the floor, and you could hear the sound he made upon impact, harsh and
unforgiving.

He didn’t move.

"Din!" You shrieked, pushing a whining Grogu into Hana's arms so you could rush forward to
your Mando’s aid.

Paz had recovered from the younger warrior’s strike, but Din was still trying to raise himself
off the floor. As Paz approached you managed to slide between him and the smaller form of
the other Mando, arms spread protectively to prevent him from taking another single step.
Above you, a murmur ran through the observing crowd, shocked by your sudden
interference. You could hear Din try to protest behind you, breathless as he tried to regain
himself.

You didn't say anything, merely let your aggression and fear show through on your face,
challenging and yet warning Paz that if he tried to attack Din once more, he would have to go
through you.



You could see him pause, hesitate at your expression. Behind you, Din wheezed as he
managed to rise to his feet. Instantly your arms dropped so you could turn and assess him,
face falling into a look of concern at the forming bruises on his bare skin.

"I'm alright." He assured you, one hand briefly cradling his helmet before turning again to
Paz. He pushed you behind him, only for you to seize his arm roughly.

"Stop."

Din paused to look at you, and suddenly the gazes of both Mandos were on you.

Yet you didn't flinch under their stares. Rather, you remained steadfast, jaw clenched as you
gazed up at both of them.

"It's rude to interrupt a duel, Cuyan." Paz warned, voice low in his chest. You glared at him,
fingers tightening on Din's arm.

"I don't care." You snapped back, and the sudden venom in your voice actually made the
older warrior flinch. Then you turned your attention to Din, eyes softening into a pleading
stare.

"I don't know what you're trying to accomplish with this." You stated blatantly, and Din's
visored gaze remained clear on your face. "But you don't need to. You don't have anything to
prove to me, Din."

Din froze.

Every muscle in his body coiled, entire attention drawn to your face. You stared up at him,
eyes open and entreating, hoping that he had taken your words to heart, that he’d abandon
this foolishness and not hurt himself further. You knew the source of this now, knew that Din
was trying, in his own way, to protect you, to defend you. The truth of it smarted under your
skin, the idea that Din would fight for you and yet refuse to disclose his feelings to you,
keeping them locked away and hidden within him.

Din seemed to recognize this too, his arm on you twitching for a moment, torn on whether to
push you away or bring you closer still. You could feel the conflict within him from his touch
alone, could sense the tear within him.

He wanted you. He wanted you to stay. He didn’t know how to ask. He didn’t want you to
leave,

“I’m afraid.” He had murmured to you, low and in confidence aboard the vibrating hum of
the Razorcrest afloat in space.

He didn’t want things to change, and yet for his inaction to lead to this…

All at once, he understood.

You saw his shoulders sink, saw that telltale motion of surrender, of acceptance you had
come to know and love. With it came a small sigh, a dip of his helmet towards you in



deference. You didn’t understand it fully, didn’t understand that, in that moment, Din gave
himself into whatever lay ahead for him. Either way, you were right. This couldn’t continue.
You, Paz, everything had whispered signs to him that he was breaking apart inside as a result
of this fear, of this anxiety that somehow, inevitably, you would reject him. Yet to push you
away so he could try to physically fight through it instead of confiding in you...this...this
wasn’t right.

The thumb on your shoulder grazed the skin there absently, his gloveless touch calloused and
worn with years of experience. He retained a comfort from the motion, as if thinking to
himself that this would be one of the few remaining memories of being able to be this close
to you. With a bitter smile under his helmet, he raised his eyes to the warrior in front of him.

“I yield.” He spoke, voice steady and yet tinged with a regret that ached inside of him.

Paz tilted his head at the bounty hunter, weighing Din’s surrender. He still held himself taut
and tall above you both, but the posture was indicative less of aggression and more of an
attention, a respect.

You watched as something shifted inside of Paz, as if both he and Din had separately come to
a similar conclusion. Whatever silent battle they had been waging, Din had finally conceded.
Paz had made his point, and after struggling against it, Din had finally surrendered himself.
This wasn’t about the petty argument of who would spar against you. This debate ran deeper,
feelings hot and untouched and yet present all the same. Paz knew this.

“No.” He rumbled at last, voice deep. “I yield.”

And yet the words he spoke had a separate meaning entirely. His surrender was not to Din. In
some ways, he had surrendered to you instead, made his peace with your obvious decision
over who, in the end, you had chosen.

You were already Din’s, and silently, Paz made his peace with that.

You blinked, looking from him to Din, who’s hand still rested lightly on your upper arm. Din
considered his Vodfor a long, heavy moment, as if understanding the hidden meaning in his
words. In the stare that they shared with each other, Paz and Din seemed to come to an
accord, to an agreement.

In doing so, somehow the animosity fell away in the space between them. In ways beyond
how you could comprehend, both he and Din regarded each other as entirely equal, void of
status or ability, and simply as what they were destined to be: brothers.

Din was the first to move, raising the hand not placed on you and extending it to Paz, as if
reaching across the channel that had existed for so long, entreating Paz to meet him halfway.

Paz stared down at it for only a moment before clasping his own calloused palm against Din’s
in a gesture of truce.

Then Paz turned to you, letting the glint of his visor rest on you for an unbearably long
moment. You squirmed under his sudden attention, more self-conscious than uncomfortable,



seated with the knowledge that Paz had spoken of his feelings for you, and that you could not
return them.

“You’re a good match for him, Cuyan.” The warrior spoke at last, and though the words were
spoken in affection, there was an imperceptible touch of longing there that made you blink
back at him, surprised. Then your face melted into something more conciliatory, as if your
eyes could express the words you couldn’t say.

Before you could speak, however, Paz turned his back on you both and began to walk back to
his pile of armor and weapons. The gaggle of foundlings trotted over to him as he did,
surrounding him and peppering him with questions. The crowd that had gathered murmured
amongst themselves, as if disappointed with the duel’s outcome. Across the room, your eyes
caught Hana’s visor. She nodded to you once, and though she didn’t speak, you understood
nonetheless. She bent, depositing Grogu a distance away from you. Arms outstretched, the
toddler rushed in your direction. A small babbling coo escaped him as you lifted him up to
balance on your chest between you and Din.

The Mando’s helmet was bent to look at the both of you, and the feather light touch on your
arm grew solid as he swiped a thumb over your skin, not speaking and yet saying so much all
the same. Your chest warmed at the combined presence of both him and the child you cared
for, united as one tiny clan.

“I…” He began at last, and you shifted your gaze from Grogu to his visor. Din trailed off,
swallowed hard enough that you could see his throat bob without his cowl to cover it.

“I don’t have the words right now to tell you what I want to say.” He murmured, and your
chest seized with the vulnerability, the uncertainty in his voice. Your eyes softened up at him,
a gentle smile overcoming your features.

Din’s rough palm slid from your arm downwards, hesitantly reaching for and grasping the
edge of the hand you used to balance Grogu. At last, he continued.

“When I understand what I mean to say, will you listen?”

The plea in his voice, so soft and unsure, so unlike the Mando you knew, overwhelmed you.
You had an idea of the things Din wanted to tell you, and your own answer remained stuck in
your throat, waiting for the inevitable words he would speak to you. Still, to hear him like
this, to hear him speak as if he wanted your permission to confide in you…

Your chest ached.

Instead of replying, you simply took a step forward, using his bare chest to balance the
toddler against as your free arm wrapped around his middle and up to his sinewy back and
shoulders in an embrace. You could feel Din stiffen, hear him choke back a gasp as you did
so. Yet you didn’t relent. No, you held him tighter still, the ache in your chest fierce and
calling out to him in comfort.

Slowly, Din’s arms that were held aloft around you settled, fell to your shoulders and back as
he returned the hug at last. You melted into his arms at the touch, feeling your heartbeat



wildly between you but relishing the warmth of him all the same. Sturdy, steady, like an
ancient tree meant to shade and protect you. Yet in your grasp he softened, loosened in your
hold.

“I’ll be here.” You answered at last, and the breath that Din had been holding came out as a
sigh, muffled by his helmet. You closed your eyes, immersing yourself in his enveloping
presence around you, in Grogu murmuring softly between you both. Gently, just for the both
of them, you spoke the words he so desperately needed to hear:

“I’m not going anywhere.”

Chapter 34: Part Thirty Four: Stay
Chapter Summary

You couldn't deny it any longer. You wanted him. You wanted to stay with him. You
couldn't bear to leave him, to be left behind. You wanted him to hold you, to call you by
the wonderful name he had given you, to cling to him in comfort and respite, to whisper
the contents of your soul to him in the soft moments while the stars passed you by. You
wanted to be with him, to never leave his side again.

You…think you loved him.

Chapter Notes
