It was quiet by the time you finally made it to the showers that night, the evening soft and
dusky in the Coruscant underground.

After Din and Paz's match, Din had spoken softly to you, promising to see you later. At first
you thought that he was withdrawing again, taking one step forwards and two steps back. Yet
then, glancing around to make sure he wasn't being scrutinized, Din had leaned in and ever so
gently tapped the helm of his helmet against your forehead. You didn't understand the
meaning of the gesture, but recognized nonetheless that it was significant to him, something
to be shared just with you and the child in your arms. Then, in a murmured parting, Din had
left on some unknown mission, the gesture lingering in his absence.

The rest of your afternoon was spent either training with Hana, who seemed to approve of the
small gains you made in your efforts, and tending to Grogu. After dinner, getting him back to
the room, and gently tucking him to sleep in his carrier, you finally had a quiet moment to
yourself.

Din had yet to appear after his promise to see you later, and after some time spent waiting,
you decided instead to head for the communal showers now that all the female Mandos had
finished. You always waited until they did, recognizing the importance of privacy regarding



their helmets. Not to mention you enjoyed the privacy yourself, as it was one of the few
moments inside the crowded covert walls that you were well and truly alone.

Most of the Covert had retired or had begun to settle in for the evening. You could hear quiet,
muted conversations in the communal area on the second floor, spoken in a soft lullaby of
noise against the distant hum of traffic somewhere beyond the walls. It reminded you once
more that you were safe here, protected by Din and a whole clan of warriors just like him.

Except they weren't really like him, not in some ways.

You reflected on this in the shower, tilting your head up into the water stream and letting the
rivulets cascade down your form. With nothing but the sound of hissing water to distract you,
your thoughts wandered to Din.

Din was...different. Maybe not in identity, not in his values, or his skills necessarily. Of
course, he was certainly more skilled and morally sound than you had originally given him
credit for all those moons ago, during your original encounter. Still, it wasn't any of that. It
was that Din was different, to you

He was warm with you in a way no one else was, in a way that he wasn't with others in turn.
His protectiveness of you extended beyond your original contract, worrying not only for the
child you had been tasked with caring for, but for you as well. His trust and bond with you
lay in the small gestures, in the hand at the small of your back, his voice quiet and assured. It
lay in the silent trust he had given you, born quietly in the hours in hyperspace staring into
the blue array before you, with Din sitting in mutual companionship in the cockpit with you.

Then there were the closer encounters, the ones that left you breathless in his wake, that drew
a deep longing in your chest that you had yet to give words to. The memory of his arms
around you, embracing you and holding you tight, of the safety and comfort of his hold in the
darkest hours of night when nightmares pursued you, continued to haunt you.

Din's gentleness with you, the way he defended you so fiercely, the trust he had laid upon you
extended beyond the reaches of what you had originally considered your relationship to be.
You suspected the things he would eventually tell you, knew that his struggle in voicing it
was all too difficult for him.

But that left a question: Where did you stand?

You would be lying if you said you didn't soften under Din's gaze, at his mere presence
beside you. There was a comfort of being beside him that extended beyond the feeling of
safety, of trust. There remained an unspoken bond that neither of you had touched upon,
offering only stolen glances and lingering words that never seemed to breach the heart of the
matter.

All that time ago, you had told him you simply wished to come along until you found a
peaceful place to settle down. Away from the Empire, away from bounty hunters and criminal
gangs, living a quiet but fulfilling life by yourself, as you had always been.



Now the thought sent a strange pang through your chest, one that drew an ache there so fierce
that made your face sink into despair. The thought of being alone, of once again being on
your own was too great a burden to bear. You had been alone for so long, simply trying to
survive, to make it to the next day, and maybe the day after that. It was...heartbreakingly
lonely. To think that you once thought of leaving Din and Grogu made you want to sink to
your knees on the steel of the shower stall and let your heart cry out.

You couldn't bring yourself to say that to him. To say you wanted to stay here in the core
worlds, on a lovely peaceful planet while Din and Grogu went on without you...it was too
much to bear. No, you couldn't do it even if you tried.

It was because, with them, you were already home.

You had realized this long ago, but to whisper the idea softly to yourself made a lightness
grow in your chest, its faint but radiant light lifting you and keeping you buoyant with the
knowledge that you had found your place with them, found a place that you didn't want to
leave.

And Din, with his gentle touches and soft voice, his refusal to put you in harm’s way, his
desire to keep you safe, to speak to you in that voice he reserved only for you-

The warmth in your chest only grew, and in your bones you felt yourself call out to him,
wishing to hold him, to touch him, to keep him safe in turn, to comfort him in his loneliness
just as his presence comforted you.

That feeling that had first appeared on Rishi, standing together in the darkened hull of the
Razorcrest, both of you speaking and yet not saying nearly enough, had only grown since
then. It had been a quiet thing at first, uncertain and shy, unsure if your heart actually would
keep it, or if it would fade in time. Since then, it had only continued to blossom, growing less
in passion than in trust, in the quiet bond that you had felt with Din all this time. To name it,
to admit to yourself that it was true, could change everything.

Yet you couldn't deny it any longer. You wanted him. You wanted to stay with him. You
couldn't bear to leave him, to be left behind. You wanted him to hold you, to call you by the
wonderful name he had given you, to cling to him in comfort and respite, to whisper the
contents of your soul to him in the soft moments while the stars passed you by. You wanted
to be with him, to never leave his side again.

You…think you loved him.

And the knowledge of that stole your breath away, robbed you of the air in your chest. The
revelation of it all seemed not to shatter the world around you suddenly, without precedent.
No, instead it washed over you like a glorious dawn, painting vivid and radiant colors across
the previously lonely landscape of your heart. Like an aria accompanying the sunrise, your
soul sang out to him, wishing to bring the stars crashing down if it would mean one more
moment beside him, one more word spoken to you, one last night asleep in his gentle and
peaceful embrace.



You understood now, the silence and the beauty of it all. You didn't know when it had
occurred, but now you knew that you couldn't bear to live your life without Din or the child
you both cared for. You never wanted to be away from them again, and yet with Din you
wanted to be even closer, closer still, until you couldn't discern your fluttering heartbeat from
his steady breathing, the sound of him trusting you with every fiber of his being.

As the water above you finally petered out, you heaved a great sigh. Yet it wasn't one of
stress or disappointment, rather it was the sound of you reconciling with the great force that
lay inside you, of the desire and the love for the Mandalorian you had entrusted your life to.

You had to tell him.

You had spent enough time simply telling yourself you'd wait until later to discuss your
feelings, hoping that you would and wouldn't get the chance to say the things that had been
dwelling within you for so long. Yet the memory of being in the underground, not knowing if
you’d ever see Din again, not sure if you would ever be able to tell him how much he meant
to you, continued to haunt you still. If somehow, if tomorrow came and Din once more had to
leave your side for whatever reason, leaving without the knowledge of what lay inside you-
you would never forgive yourself.

You were dressed and walking to his room before you had even finished processing the
thought, clothes still damp and clinging to you in your hurry to find him.

The covert was fully dark now, lit only by dim lanterns interspersed through the hallways.
The blue midnight haze and orange glow of the lamps seemed to brush against you, leaving
misty smears of light in your wake as you walked with purpose down towards the men's
corridor. You didn't care if someone saw you, didn't care if you would get into trouble
somehow breaking the rules Paz had originally warned you about upon arriving at the Covert.
You needed to see Din. You needed to see your Mandalorian.

So distracted were you by your quest that you didn't hear the footsteps striding towards you.
As you rounded a corner, you found yourself nearly impacting a hard beskar chest plate,
stumbling away just in time to avoid it. Yet your sudden change of motion caused your
balance to teeter, and soon you were leaning dangerously far back, only for a hand to reach
out and steady you.

"Oh! I-" You looked up, blinking upon seeing the familiar visor above you.

"Din." You breathed.

"Cuyan." Din responded, his voice just as breathless. His grip on your waist relaxed a touch
yet didn't entirely disappear. "I couldn't find you upstairs, I-"

"Din." You spoke again, voice taking on a touch of urgency now. "I-I- There's something I
want to tell you."

Din let out a small breath you didn't realize he had been holding. The hand on your waist slid
up to your elbow, down to your hand. You glanced down at it, seeing the slow, gentle motion



Din used to cup your palm. A familiar flutter arose in your chest, and you looked back up to
Din's visor, imagining the eyes you couldn't see.

"I have something to say as well." He spoke, and his voice sounded...almost unsure of
himself. Hesitant.

"But not here."

Without any further words, you felt Din abruptly shift and turn, keeping your hand with him
as he began to lead you down the corridors. He moved quickly, and yet didn't drag you along,
simply escorting you swiftly through the hallways towards his destination.

You could feel the warmth of his hand through his glove, the way his grip held loosely onto
yours, fingers intertwined. It touched a familiar part of you, the depth of your soul you
wanted to confess to him, letting the words spill out like a dam broken.

None too soon, you found yourself standing in front of the familiar door of Din's room. Din
released his hold on you, and your hand fell limply back to your side as you watched him
slide open the door with quiet care. Din glanced inside for a moment, checking on something,
and then with a small nod of his head, gestured you inside.

As you entered your eyes landed on a familiar baby carriage, closed shut and still with the
sleeping child inside. Din must have retrieved him from your room while you were in the
shower. Shoulders softening, your mind conjured the thought of Din holding the sleeping
infant, making a bubble of warmth grow in your chest. You smiled at the image of the
intimidating Mandalorian always so soft and careful with the babe.

You turned to him then, seeing his silver armor reflect the orange haze of the lantern atop the
storage container beside him. It flickered like firelight, washing Din in warm vibrant colors
that glinted against his visor.

"Din." You whispered, momentarily struck by the sight. Din's visor, which had rested on the
bassinet, turned to you.

Shaking the distraction away, you turned to fully face him, hands soothing your still damp
arms. The words you wanted to say lingered on the tip of your tongue, and yet you didn't
know where to begin.

"I-" You started, only for Din's quiet voice to cut you off.

"Let me go first." He offered abruptly, and with a gentler touch: "Please."

You blinked at him, a little surprised with his unexpected forwardness, but then nodded for
him to continue.

Yet then he hesitated, as if he too struggled in where to begin. You saw him falter, then
suddenly straighten, as if remembering something. As you watched, he reached for
something strapped to his belt, struggling for a moment in the dim light before producing a
small blaster in his hands.



Your blaster.

You sucked in a breath upon seeing it, having nearly forgotten it's absence since you
originally lost it to the two Black Sun members who had kidnapped you. How Din found it,
you had no idea, but the sight of it made a smile stretch broadly across your face.

"How did you-, when?" You asked in a whispered rush, reaching for the weapon and
delicately taking it in your hands to examine it. The weight of it once more in your grasp was
comforting, a reminder that it was Din who had originally given it to you to defend yourself
and the kid. Now it was back with you once more, and you couldn't be happier at its return.

"I tracked down the Black Sun member who captured you." Din replied in a low tone, and
you glanced back at him upon hearing the touch of anger in his voice. His visor lowered just
enough to catch a dangerous glint from the lantern. "He will never hurt you or the child
again, I made sure of that."

You shuddered. You couldn't help it. The restrained fury in Din's voice, not directed at you,
reminded you again just how dangerous this man could be. Yet the thought that he did that to
defend you, to keep you safe...

It reminded you just how much you admired and cared for him.

"Cuyan I-" Din spoke, sounding almost choked for a moment, pausing to settle himself
before continuing.

"When you and the child were taken I... blamed myself. I should have never left you alone. I-
" Again, his voice caught in his throat, and you could hear him swallow the emotion there
unsuccessfully. You felt your own chest seize with the raw vulnerability Din was offering
you, caught between the hurt and the affection to see him so open with you, pouring out
words you thought you'd never hear.

"I never want that to happen again." Din went on, and he had settled now, his voice almost
even, and yet not absent of the vast array of emotion inside him. He took a breath before he
continued, letting it settle in his chest before breathing it out as a sigh. "The thought of you
leaving it...I can't make sense of it. I-"

Even in the darkness you could see the way Din's body held taut, like a chord pulled too tight.
His fists at his side drew his shoulders up defensively, as if closing himself off to you even
while he spoke. You held yourself back, wanting nothing more than to step forward and hold
him in comfort, reassuring him that you were right here, that he had nothing to fear. Yet you
knew Din had to say these words without your help, for both your sakes.

It took a moment, but Din eventually released himself, as if the one holding his strings
suddenly let go and allowed him to stand on his own. His shoulders loosened, hands falling
open at his sides. He took a deep inhale, letting it fall out of him as a sigh that seemed to ease
the tension from his form. In that singular moment, cradled in the vast expanse of your
lifetime, every moment grievously short and yet so full of wonder and awe, Din surrendered
himself to you. His walls came crashing down not with the chaos of a fortress shattered, but



as if he had been the one to open the door, allowing brilliant sunlight to stream inside and
bathe his form.

Then, he looked at you. Looked at you as if he was seeing you for the first time, as if you
were the stars and he was a moon, cradled aloft in space together. Speaking quietly, he said:

"I want you to stay. With us. For good." And after a breathless moment: "Please."

Time stood still. The hum of the lantern, the far-off sounds of Coruscant's heartbeat, even the
thrumming inside your own chest seemed to silence themselves. The neon lights of the city,
the orange flicker of the lamp beside you both, and the darkness in between seemed to flood
with colors you had never seen before. All at once, and yet ever so softly, the world became
silent, bright, painted in the aura of your own emotions as they mounted rapidly in your
chest.

You felt your lips part in wonder, eyes glinting in the darkness with the beginnings of tears.
The cool air of the room didn't touch you, damp hair still wetting the back of your shirt and
cheeks warming with a heartfelt feeling you did not yet fully understand but was familiar all
the same. The emotions you had been holding since your revelation seemed to bubble over in
your chest, up your throat in a ragged intake of breath to steady yourself against the force of
Din's words.

He wanted you. Not just because you were his partner, the child's caretaker while he was
away, able to protect him while Din couldn’t. No, Din wanted you. As you were, with all
your past burdens and scars and haunting nightmares. He wanted you to stay, and the
knowledge of that seemed to birth a new galaxy in you, one born of a hope so desperate you
could feel it catch in your throat and warm at the corners of your eyes.

Loneliness. You knew the name of that now, knew just how true it held for you. When you
had lived your whole life without a single person to call a friend, no one to hold you safe and
shelter you, the term made little sense, as you had never experienced anything other than
loneliness as your only true companion. Yet now, with Din standing before you, open, almost
desperate in his plea, you could feel the past weight of grief open up a well inside you, and
you felt yourself nearly sucked down by it.

You couldn't help it then, couldn't help the sudden sob that escaped you. The relief, the hope,
the desperate desire to tell him everything flowed out of you as a quiet cry, a small sound
against the dark expanse of the velvet midnight.

Din seemed to panic then, growing stiff as you nearly folded in on yourself with your grief,
your relief, your hope, your fear, you desire to simply stay. You didn't even notice his
reaction, too caught in your whirlwind of emotions so vast and deep that for a moment you
thought you would drown in your tears.

It was as if you had been clinging tightly onto hope for so long, clinging to it desperately,
praying to some higher being that life would not always be this way. That someday,
somehow, you would find someone who accepted you for who you were, who you could be,
with all your sins and the fault lines in between. You had been holding tight for a lifetime,



past the point of your fingers drawing blood and the great chasm of despair threatening to
swallow you up.

Now, with the words Din had spoken, you could let go, caught in the safety of his feelings for
you.

"Cuyan-" Din started, reaching for you. You caught him by the insides of his arms as he
approached, slightly bent over as you tried to catch your breath from the force of your ragged
sobs. Your fingers curled into the fabric of his sleeves, damp hair falling over your eyes. You
clung to him like he was a tether preventing you from being pulled out to sea, wishing he
would be even closer, would hold you like you wanted him to so desperately.

"Do you know?" You finally spoke, voice broken and choked. "How long I've wanted you to
say those words?"

Din jerked, then soothed again under your grasp. You needn't have said more, for he
understood, knew the origin of that hurt in you even without you voicing it.

"I'm sorry, Cuyan." He murmured. "I should have told you sooner."

You choked a sob then, shoulders shuddering under the effort and the failure to maintain
yourself. Your fingers dug into the fabric of Din's flight suit, eyes closed and tears salty
against your lips. Yet the desire within you seemed to burn brighter with every breath, the
pressure, the need, the greed to tell him about the weight in your heart that had lifted you,
that had kept you alive in the Coruscant underground and fighting your way back to him.

At last, you spoke, with a breathless, choked voice, whispering the thing you wanted to say
for so long.

"I want to stay. Din. I- I want to stay."

Yet Din didn't fully relax, visor still tilted down to observe you with worried, anxious eyes.
You shook in his grip, trembling, struggling to stay upright with the pain and the heart
clenching relief of everything you had just experienced. With your voice cracked in your
throat, hands shaking against his touch, it took everything in you to summon the needed
words from your soul.

Finally swallowing down the choke in your throat, you looked up at him, eyes shining with
tears that, to Din, appeared as starlight.

"With you. I want to stay with you."

At that, Din sank his shoulders in a silent but profound relief, and you heard the sigh, the
breath held tight in his chest dissipating into the quiet hours, delicate yet sincere, carrying
beyond the anthem of Coruscant's midnight soul and into the heavens beyond.

"Cuyan I-" He began again, face turned down towards you. You looked up at him with a
teary, hopeful smile, feeling your heart expand a hundred times over at the knowledge that
this man wanted you too, that you were no longer alone, that you would never be again. The



thought that together you would be a safe harbor for the other, trust abundant in the space
between your two forms, seemed to shed the past like a heavy cloak from your shoulders,
revealing you to him for the first time.

"Ni kar'tayl gar darasuum."

You blinked then, tears still spilling from your eyes, not knowing the meaning behind the
language he spoke. Yet you didn't have a moment to question it, for suddenly you were being
brought forward, and Din's arms were closing fast around you in the embrace you so
desperately had longed for. Your heart seemed to fly up to your throat, a surprised gasp
tearing past your lips as your hands fluttered, unsure where to place themselves on Din' broad
form. Yet Din only held you closer, head bent to fully encompass you, just as he had that
night when he had chased away your nightmares.

Yet now, instead of a soft, half sleep- spoken promise, his voice spoke quiet but true, telling
you:

"I- I love you."

You sank into him then, legs nearly buckling under you. With your face buried into the soft
fabric of his cowl, you let a shuddering sigh escape you, releasing all the tension, the worry,
the fear and anxiety loose from you for what felt like the first time in your whole existence.
You surrendered yourself to it, arms wrapping around your Mandalorian and holding fast to
him even as the remnants of cries bore forth from your chest. Din held you through it, and
soon your hands found purchase on his cape, as if holding onto it could bring him closer still.

"I love you too." You whispered, voice high in your throat and new tears growing hot in your
vision. The words seemed to soothe the inside of your throat like warm honey, sweet and
curative to your aching heart. Even then they alone did not truly express the depth of your
heart, could not describe the feelings you felt as Din gently pulled on the tether that
connected your two souls. "I love you, Din Djarin."

Din held you tighter still, his arms firm and secure around your form, head tucked against the
side of yours. The cool touch of his helmet brushed against your temple, and you found
yourself leaning against it, face scrunched in relief at being where you finally belonged. This
close you could hear his heartbeat, fluttering rapidly against his throat, hopeful and expectant.

Here, in the safety of his embrace, with his wide palms tucked against your back, the worries
of the world couldn't hurt you. Here, there were no bounty hunters, no Empire, no gangs or
thugs chasing your debts, only Din; only your firm, kind, capable, fiercely protective Mando
who you cared so deeply for.

The words he had spoken to you remained steadfast in your chest, and it took every breath
not to let them claim you, let them sweep you out to see in a tide of emotion.

You shifted, drawing back just enough to be right in front of his helmet. Once again, it ached
inside you how much you wished to see his face, how you wanted to see his eyes. Your
imagination ran wild, summoning the images you saw as you drifted off to sleep in his arms
all that time ago.



Then, Din leaned forward all of an inch, so that the cool beskar of his helmet tapped against
your forehead. Just as he had earlier, Din took in a deep breath, letting it settle inside him
before releasing it in a dusky sigh. You closed your eyes, grounding yourself in him. With his
hand at your back, the hard touch of Beskar pressed gently to your skin, the coarse fabric of
his cape under your fingers, you tried to immerse yourself in Din's gravity, letting it sink into
your senses and become a part of you.

"What does that mean?" You found yourself asking quietly, words spoken in a whisper only
Din could hear. "That thing you just did?"

Din huffed a breath, but underneath you could hear the smile in his voice. "It's
mirshmure'cya." He murmured back. "A greeting for Mandalorians."

You hummed breathing in the same way Din had a moment ago, mimicking the motion. "I've
never seen you use it with Paz or the others though." You returned. "Why me?"

Din grew a little stiff then, and in his next breath you could hear him clear his throat.

"That's..." He began, voice a little higher, somewhat nervous. "It's a greeting...mostly
for...courting or...coupled Mandalorians."

You opened your eyes then, leaning back so you could see your mildly surprised face
reflected in the dimness of his visor.

Is that what we are, Din? You asked silently, but instead simply smiled warmly at him.

"So, then it's a Mandalorian kiss." You supplied, voice a touch louder, an impish but pleased
smile spreading across your features. Yet the wetness in your eyes and stains in your cheeks
seemed to make the comment half-hearted, a question more than an answer to yourself.

Din's hands fidgeted, for a moment feeling as if they'd loosen their hold on you. You kept
your hands tight against his cape, however, and after a moment Din relented, realizing you
wouldn't let him escape so easily.

"Y-yes." He answered at last.

You felt your form soften against him, relaxing into his hold. Yet a part of you strained,
quietly crying out for that desire once more. You wanted to see him. You wanted to touch
him, to feel him, to understand him. Yet you knew that there may never be a day where Din
would bare himself to you, and that you must make your peace with that.

And yet...

"I wish I could kiss you." You breathed, as if the words were a prayer.

Then you blinked, realizing that you had just spoken aloud. Din froze, not moving, and you
felt regret crawl up your throat, words trying to form themselves half-spoken. Then Din
pulled away from you, and panic truly began to take hold of you as your arms slid from his
back, falling back down to your sides.



"Din- I-I didn't mean-"

Yet then Din took those hands, the ones you had used to save him, had touched him so gently
with, had taken care of him, and he raised them upwards. Your words died in your throat as
your palms came to touch the cool beskar of his helmet, and in his visor you could see your
eyes shining in the dim lantern light.

"Close your eyes." Din whispered, and you blinked at him several times before a concerned
look crossed across your face. Yet before you could ask, Din murmured to you once more.

"Do you trust me?"

Your eyes slid shut before your brain even finished processing your answer, the reply an
instinct already ingrained deep in you. So, you whispered your answer, now blind with only
your ears and hands to guide you.

"Yes."

Your breath held tight in your chest, unmoving, as Din's hands came to close over yours, the
suede fabric of his gloves soothing your freshly scrubbed skin.

Then, Din's hands pressed down on yours, turning your feather light touch firm against his
helmet as he brought it up with a small hiss.

You didn't breathe, didn't move, and certainly refused to open your eyes as Din's hands, your
hands lifted up his helmet from his face, revealing the expression you couldn't see
underneath.

The edges of your fingers skimmed along curly hair as Din helped you lift the helmet all the
way from over his head. The breath in your chest finally escaped you, able to be held no
longer, and you could hear the stuttering exhale as the helmet vanished under your grip.

There was a small thunk as Din placed it on the storage unit next to you both, leaving your
hands hovering in the air beside his face.

In your next inhale you drew them closer, finally allowing the pads of your fingers to cup
your Mandalorian's face for the first time. You could hear Din's sharp intake of breath, then
felt that same breath release itself from his nose, ghosting over the skin of your wrists. Your
nails raked gently against his jaw, feeling the tell-tale scruff there. You traced his jaw up to
his hair, ghosting over the curly locks soft against your touch.

Din was patient as you explored him by touch, his own hands coming to rest against your
own face, gloves soft against your cheeks. Neither of you spoke, as you tried to understand
the map of Din's face, and Din let his own eyes take in the awe painted across your face.

At last, your thumb grazed across Din's bottom lip, and you both drew in a breath at the
motion, remembering the words you had spoken only moments ago.

"Din." You whispered, and now the name came with so much more than a sight, a feeling.
Now the sound of his name brought forth the feeling of your touch on his face, with his



messy helmet hair and the softly smiling curve of his mouth as you whispered his name once
more. "Din."

"Cuyan." Din whispered in reply, and suddenly, gently, you were being brought up, towards
him, to where his lips parted to meet yours.

He was gentle, more so than you imagined. The hesitant touch of his lips on yours was small
at first, chaste and almost shy. His hands against your face were delicate yet firm, cupping
your cheeks and letting your head fall into his hands. You felt your own gasp tickle your skin
with how close he was. Yet his mouth did not stray from yours for long, as you reached up to
follow the contact. Without your sight it was a slight miscalculation, yet you could feel Din
smile against you with the motion, amused and soft with his love for you.

"Din." You whispered again, as if his name alone would keep you safe, would bring you
comfort, would draw him closer so he could kiss you again.

And he did, leaning down and kissing you with intent now. As if now realizing you wouldn't
back away, that he was allowed to touch you, he chased his own need against your lips. You
eagerly let him, trying to return in kind whilst reaching your hands up to press him
downwards, fingers raking through his hair.

Din kissed you as if you with softness so delicate and yet so purposeful you felt yourself
reeling from it. Was this the same man who had executed someone for daring to lay their
hands on you and the child? The one who had ruthlessly cut down an entire gang when he
saw your withered, poisoned form collapsed on the ramp of the Razorcrest?

Yet the way his hands snaked down to your waist to drag you closer, his trembling breath
against your face trying to seize oxygen in between the graze of his lips against yours, was
the same. This was the man who had held you gently while you slept, who had carried you
from the battlefield, who had held you in the silence of the Razorcrest's cockpit as he
confessed his fears, his mistakes to you.

This man was your fearsome protector, your beloved friend, your trusted companion, and
now, so much more. This man wanted you as you were, opened the gates of his heart to you
despite his hesitations, and now embraced you so tenderly that it stole the air from your
lungs.

"Cuyan." He murmured, and the sound was almost choked, as if Din too realized that his
fears had amounted to nothing, that you weren't leaving, that you were here, in his arms, safe.
"Beautiful Cuyan."

You gasped then, and it only allowed Din to deepen the kiss, letting your bottom lip be
caressed by his own. The hand in Din's hair weakened for a moment under the intensity of his
attention, and you arched into him as his hand pressed against the small of your back.

Then, with a lingering touch, Din drew back. Holding you still, he didn't move, and your lips
parted, waiting for him to return.

"What is it?" You asked in a whisper, and Din chuckled, the sound low and warm.



"Nothing." He murmured back. "Just...seeing you without my visor...it..." You could almost
hear him swallow this close as he tried to summon the words. "You're so beautiful."

Your heart caught then, a small feeling that made the rhythm in your chest stutter for a
moment. When was the last time someone had said that towards you? Who had they been?
The memory of a dozen different individuals making lecherous remarks towards you
surfaced, and yet in all of them you couldn't find one who spoke to you the way Din did.

You believed him. You knew Din would not lie to you, would not say something so
emotional and profound without meaning every word. The knowledge of that made a breath
sink from you, stuttering with the weight of his affections.

Din brought you forward once more, tucking your head against his shoulder. You leaned into
it, feeling nothing but comfort and bliss, wishing for all the world that the rest of your days
could be spent here, in his embrace.

"I love you." You repeated again. "Din Djarin."

Din sighed, the breath tickling your hair.

"I love you too." He murmured in reply, voice gentle and sincere and so full of love. Then, in
a breath that was barely a whisper...

He spoke your name.

Chapter End Notes

No notes this time, only that I really hope you guys enjoy this chapter, and how far these
two have come. This is only the beginning of their story, there's still so much left to tell.
This has been my favorite chapter to write, and my heart is just bursting with love for
Din and Cuyan.

Chapter 35: Part Thirty-Five: Bounty
Chapter Summary

"I know." He breathed, and his voice suddenly took on a gentler touch, one that made
your own posture ease at the sound. Your expression softened from frustration to
concern, stance loosening against his gentle hold.

"It isn't that I don't believe that, Cuyan." Din went on, trying to keep his voice delicate.
"It's that it's still too dangerous. I'll be able to focus better knowing you're here, safe, in
the Razorcrest. I don't want to risk putting you in danger again.” Then, after a beat:
”Mesh'la”.

The affectionate name made your knees tremble for a moment with the utter tenderness
at which Din spoke the word in Mando'a, letting it roll off his tongue as if it was the first
word he had spoken as a child. His concern for you bled through in his voice. You
almost let his words wash over you and assuage your fears, let them win you over so
you'd surrender.

Almost.

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

"No."

"Please?"

"No."

"Din."

"Absolutely not."

You frowned up at the Mando through his visor, your displeasure clear in the beskar's
reflection.

"I can help." You insisted, voice hovering on the edge of desperation.

"You're still untrained." Din replied evenly, not budging even a single inch. Though his hands
remained loose at his sides, there was a tension in his shoulders you had come to recognize as
something akin to annoyance.



Your frown deepened at this, and you took a step closer to your Mando. Din's head declined
to see you, staring down past his chest plate to meet your eyes.

"My aim has improved a lot. Even Hana said so back at the covert. You saw how much I've
improved, I can help." You tried again, but this time you were only met with a steely silence
at your protests.

It was true, and Din knew that. Your weeks at the covert had been largely spent being flipped
on your back in sparring after sparring session, being closely supervised in blaster-arms
practice, and being disciplined in how to properly maintain the gear you had acquired,
scarce as it was. Din had played a large hand in your impromptu training, leaving a
substantial portion of the work to Hana, your newly acquired friend, but taking time to
oversee your progress as well.

Slowly, but with sure-footed strides, you had begun to make remarkable advancements in
your training. While you were by no means a Mandalorian, or even a bounty hunter, you had
managed to hold your own against Hana in your sparring sessions more than once. To be
able to fend off a Mandalorian, even for a short while, was no small feat, and Din had told
you as much at the end of one of your sessions. You had beamed at him, feeling your sore
muscles loosen under the warm gaze hidden behind his visor. You knew that with Din at your
side, you could face any opponent.

Things had been easier since that night, the one where you had tasted Din’s lips on yours and
let your breath echo against his own heartbeat. Though Din was not necessarily more
affectionate, or perhaps open about his intentions, he seemed…steadier. No longer at war
with himself, no longer trying to deny what was clearly there. Instead, his confession seemed
to bolster him somehow, like a heavy stone in the middle of a stream, unable to be moved.

At one point, when you both had been watching Paz instruct the covert’s soon to be warriors,
Din had even reached for your hand.

Hana, for her part, knew when to step in and when to sneakily slip away so that it suddenly
became only you and Din sitting cleaning your blaster in the darkened hours of the
Coruscanti midnight. It seemed the huntress's instincts were just as sharp as you had
expected, noticing the subtle but undeniable shift in between you and Din following his
confession.

In fact, it seemed that most of the covert knew, somehow. Your slow but sure acceptance into
the tribe had eased significantly following the midnight conversation you two had had in
Din's bunk. Not that it was spoken of, save for a sudden bout of questions from the foundlings
that alerted you that your relationship with the Mando was not as secret as you had
originally though it to be. You had answered their questions as carefully as you could,
ignoring Umos's question about ridurrok which made your entire body warm to the touch and
stomach swoop at the thought.

You enjoyed your time at the covert, spending your days learning and training and enjoying
the comforting company of Din and the child, surrounded by other warriors where you knew
the three of you would be safe.



Yet eventually a narrow escape with one of the patrols and a bounty hunter snooping around
for you and the child had alerted you to the fact that it was time to move on. Staying in one
place for too long, even in the glittering metropolis of Coruscant, just wasn’t safe.

So, you and Din packed your gear back into the Razorcrest, leaving much of your supplies
behind with the covert, knowing they needed it more than you. With a bear hug from Paz, and
a solid firm grasp of Hana's vambrace against your forearm, you three had lifted off once
more into parts unknown.

That had been several standard rotations ago. Now, with the remainder of your scarce
supplies dwindling, Din had found it pertinent to find an assignment on a backwater planet
within the core to earn some much-needed credits.

Which led you to here and now, where you were practically chest to chest with the
Mandalorian, arguing that you would not be left behind.

Din stared down at you, the 'T' of his visor expressionless. Yet you could feel the tension
radiating in his form, spreading from his fingertips up to his shoulders. You didn't move,
staring up defiantly at him, the child in your arms worriedly looking between you both.

At last, Din sighed, the breath releasing the tension from his form. His hands rose up to hold
your arms carefully against your sides, gloved hands firm yet soft against your sleeves.

"I know." He breathed, and his voice suddenly took on a gentler touch, one that made your
own posture ease at the sound. Your expression softened from frustration to concern, stance
loosening against his gentle hold.

"It isn't that I don't believe that, Cuyan." Din went on, trying to keep his voice delicate. "It's
that it's still too dangerous. I'll be able to focus better knowing you're here, safe, in the
Razorcrest. I don't want to risk putting you in danger again.” Then, after a beat: ”Mesh'la”.

The affectionate name made your knees tremble for a moment with the utter tenderness at
which Din spoke the word in Mando'a, letting it roll off his tongue as if it was the first word
he had spoken as a child. His concern for you bled through in his voice. You almost let his
words wash over you and assuage your fears, let them win you over so you'd surrender.

Almost.

After a moment you shook your head, as if clearing your thoughts, turning your gaze back up
to him with a look of determination that made Din's hands tighten on your upper arms.

"No." You replied, voice unwavering. "I won't stay behind. I'm not doing that again."

To your credit, Din nearly took a surprised step backwards, body subtly rocking away from
you for a moment before resettling. You tried to pin him to the spot with your stare, pressing
forward and shortening the already close distance between you both as if it would help you
plead your case.



"Besides-" You went on, as Din's grip began to anxiously fist the fabric of your jacket sleeves.
"You aren't considering how I feel about this. You know how much time I spent in that
hellscape on Coruscant, thinking about how I'd never see you again? And you expect me to
just sit here and watch you march off into danger again? Without me?"

Yet then you softened, let your shoulder roll loose and felt the gravity of Din's grasp on your
arms.

"I know you want to keep me and the child safe. I know it's the last thing you want to put us
both in danger." Your brow creased as you spoke, eyes gentle and pleading up at your
Mando. "But the last two- three times you left us alone, terrible things happened. We were
kidnapped, I was stabbed, I almost died on Hypori when you left for help.” You sucked in a
sharp breath, trying to keep your voice steady despite your frustration. “We aren't as safe
here as you think."

Din paused, then shifted on his feet, the motion carefully rocking his weight from one foot to
the other as he considered your words. You stared hopefully up at him, trying to school your
expression into one of stubbornness, and failing easily.

Din remained silent, still, utterly frozen as he gazed down at you. His visor seemed to gaze
almost through you as he debated within himself whether to surrender. In your arms, Grogu
made a small babbling sound, almost out of concern, as if he understood the context of your
conversation.

"Fine." Din bit out at last. Yet his stance didn't ease at all with the word, instead further
tightening with the anxiety of his decision.

Before you could let the relief wash over you and light a smile on your face, Din cut your
thoughts off.

"But." And you paused, staring up at him anxiously as he continued. "You follow my
directions. If I don't like the situation, you get out of there as quickly as possible. If I say you
run, you run. If I say stay put, you don't move. Understand?"

You tried not to let your happiness bleed through onto your expression, nodding seriously at
Din's finger wagging in front of your face. Yet inside you couldn't help a thrill of excitement
at going on your first official bounty hunt with Din, something you had been working and
training for ever since you had woken up at the covert all those moons ago.

Din released his other hand from you, letting it fall to his waist, where it balanced as he let
out a suffering sigh, helmet averting away from your gaze. You could tell he was already
beginning to regret his decision mere moments after he had spoken it, and normally you'd try
to comfort him. Now, however, you were practically bouncing on your heels in excitement.

This was the life you had only dared to dream of as a mechanic on Kaddak. A life of
adventure and thrill, dashing off to daring expeditions in a crew of experienced travelers and
skilled pilots. Though this wasn’t exactly the crew you had imagined, the reality of your
wildest dreams coming to fruition electrified you nonetheless. The enthusiasm seemed to
lighten your feet, draw a light into your eyes at the thought of accompanying Din on his hunt.



Yet you also knew that this was a dangerous task, and that Din's concerns were entirely
justified. On Coruscant, Din had spoken to you in quiet hours as the child slept about hunts
gone wrong, about being nearly electrocuted, shot to pieces, stabbed, dismembered at the
hands of his quarry and other bounty hunters. There was a reason only the strong survived
this profession. Those who couldn't handle the challenge were either killed, disgraced, or
never heard from again. Din was right in being worried about your presence there.

Yet that danger felt like nothing compared to the thought of being left behind again. The idea
that cycles could pass without hearing from Din, that you'd be waiting in the cold empty
Razorcrest with the child hoping and praying he'd come back soon was far worse than any
threat from a bounty or fellow hunter. While Din was sure he was the one protecting you, you
had vowed to yourself long ago that you would do anything to protect him too.

That was the thought that finally settled you, let the excitement bubbling in your veins still
into a steady stream of focus.

Din gave you another glance, letting his gaze rest on your serious, determined expression
before heaving another small sigh.

"Get your gear." He announced curtly, turning. "We're heading out as soon as you're ready."

- - - - -

Daro was just as dense as Rishi, with its tumbling sloping forests and craig like mountain
ranges. However, while Rishii's heat prickled deep under Din's skin and made his flight suit
stick to him like a second skin, Daro's arid, cool winds tickled the small bit of exposed skin at
the nape of Din's neck in a sweet whisper. The dappled shade of the tall trees and pebbled
paths made the planet a lovely sight, encouraging Din to hike to the zenith of some of the
densely wooded mountains and take in the breath-taking views from above.

If he had to pick a place to lay low and avoid bounty hunters, Daro was a pretty strong
contender out of the places he had visited.

Which was probably why his quarry had decided to camp here.

Din had found the bounty posting a few parsecs over as he was spending the last of his
credits on restocking the Razorcrest. In the darkened corner of a market stall Din had used
his helmet to filter the sounds of the discussion loud enough for him to hear. In a stroke of
luck, the employer had yet to post the bounty. With a careful introduction and few convincing
words, Din had managed to grab it before the posting could make its way back to the guild.

Luck wasn't something Din necessarily had faith in, but he did admit it had been his friend as
of late.

The quarry was an ex-stormtrooper captain, one who had deserted towards the end of the
empire's reign of terror and had attempted his hand at spice running. With the logic they
instilled in the Empire's finest, the captain hadn't gotten far before he was in over his head,
and now had debts too large to pay back with mere credits. Unfortunately, the man's poor



decisions were about to catch up to him. As the saying went: for bounty hunters, one man's
misfortune is another man's payment.

It hadn't taken much to track the man down. Din didn't even need a tracking fob for that. He
had simply looked to the closest backwater planet in the sector, checked with some local
mechanics about fuel purchases to confirm his suspicions, and taken off with the Razorcrest.

It was only now, in the dense forests of Daro, with its bubbling streams and forest full of
fallen logs, did Din begin to encounter the true challenge of his hunt. Without a tracking fob,
it would require searching the entire planet for a single ex-stormtrooper to flush out Din's
prey. Fortunately, Din's years of experience allowed him to guess where he might find a trail
on his bounty: Near an old stormtrooper training base that had pinged against the
Razorcrest’s scanners.

With only so many supplies, the deserter would have to eventually rely on what he could find
on the planet. Din didn't put it past him to go for the easiest option, raiding the facility and
retreating into the woods to cover his tracks from other hunters. As much as the Empire liked
to put on a show, their stormtroopers were surprisingly simple-minded.

The cold steel of the facility walkway echoed under Din's boots, with yours echoing shortly
behind him. Normally Din would be laser focused on this hunt, easing quickly into the rhythm
of only him and his prey. However, with your presence close by, it was harder to keep his gaze
narrowed on the task at hand. The anxiety of suddenly being shot at, of some horrible mistake
resulting in your injury or worse had been quickly locked away as soon as the three of you
had set out. Yet the call of it rattled in the back of his mind, like a strange noise on a ship, one
he couldn't pinpoint.

You paused behind Din as he held up a hand, using the other to switch on a filter for his visor
to let him track footprints. Kneeling, he began to scan the grime laden floor, searching for
even the smallest remnant of life in the abandoned corridor. In the rubble and dust of the
bombarded facility, it was hard to pick out any patterns on the floor. With the burst windows,
leaves and debris had blown in, leaving the entire hallway to become overgrown and overrun
with nature slowly reclaiming its dominion over the base. Yet there, at the far end of the
hallway, a neon smear against the blue static of his vision alerted Din to the presence of
someone who had walked this hallway not too long ago.

Looks like his gamble had paid off.

"What is this place?" You asked from behind him, and Din's shoulders hiked at the sudden
noise of your voice. He cast a glance over his shoulder, knowing you couldn't see his warning
stare from past his visor, and held a finger to his lips in a silent caution.

To your credit, you understood his message almost instantly, stiffening and stance widening
in readiness. Beside you, the cradle hovered silently at your side, the child inside inquisitive
but also silent.

Slowly, Din stood. Switching off his filter, he cast another glance about, letting his senses
immerse into the silence of the abandoned base. Outside, against the structure built into the
mountain, the wind wafted through the shattered glass and carried the sound of birdsong.



Inside the facility only the artificial noise of durasteel walkways and corridors greeted him,
echoing in their desolate and abrupt emptiness.

Then he turned back to you, having made sure that at least this area was safe. At his shift
towards you, you relaxed, realizing that there was no immediate threat. Internally Din felt a
murmur of pride at how quickly you had picked up the subtle but distinct language of his
body, knowing when to be alert and when to stand down.

"Stormtrooper training base." Din answered at last in reply to your question. "From the early
days of the Empire."

You raised your eyebrows at that, looking around as if the added information could yield new
secrets to your surroundings. After a moment Din saw a shudder run through you, one you
tried to clamp down on and failed at.

"I like it better without the stormtroopers." You intoned dryly but couldn't entirely hide the
undertone of apprehension in your voice.

Din agreed silently, turning back to the task at hand.

"Whoever came through here is long gone." Din observed, standing and crossing his arms
sourly at the aged footprints. "But, I have an idea where they might be."

With that, he turned and strode back towards you, past you, feeling you turn after him as he
started back in the direction of the entrance. After a pause, you trotted to catch up, the low
whir of the bassinet following behind you.

As you both entered back into the rim of the forest, Din paused. You settled beside him,
staring into the woods ahead of you and watching him from the corner of your eye.

"Remember what I said." Was all Din offered to you, voice low in warning. In the silence that
followed, he knew you understood. Then, like a Nexu stretching low in the underbrush, Din
began to make his way into the forest with you at his side.

The forest on Daro was much quieter than Rishi, Din noted. Or Endor, or any of the other
many forested moons and planets he had tracked on. Normally bird song from high in the
treetops, alien creatures in the tangled roots of trees, and wind whispering through the
branches spoke a language that only the wilds knew on this planet. Here, however, everything
was muted. It seemed as if the forest here held its breath, afraid to speak. No doubt the
presence of the Empire, with its brutal and punishing regime, would stifle the presence of a
planet so thick with life. Even years afterwards, it still held a silence that spoke of a
treacherous past, one that left scars to this day.

You seemed to feel it more than Din did, shoulders hunched and eyes bright with focus on the
trail in front of you. Each foot you put down lay silently across the forest floor littered with
leaves and fallen branches, being extremely mindful of your presence.

It wasn't too long before Din began to pick up a trail, and as he followed it, it began to
intersect with other paths as well, as if this person had tried to approach the base at different



angles so as to confuse their pursuers. Not that it mattered much, when all the trails ended at
the same location on the other side.

Din paused just long enough to draw his blaster, and at the sight you did so as well, holding
yours in a white-knuckle grip from under your gloves. Knowing you were right behind him,
Din followed the freshest prints down a mossy slope, where they continued faintly on the
other side of a small stream.

Soon enough, the prints began to appear fresh, speaking silently of the trespasser that had
traveled through these woods, betraying their secret to the hunter. Din could also see the
signs where someone had dragged a crate or some sort of container and gave a small smile
at how easily he had guessed his bounty's plan to raid the base for supplies and retreat to the
forest, just as he thought.

The tracks followed up a shallow slope, then further to the ridge above. At this Din paused,
knowing that if his quarry had made his base on higher ground, it became all the more
difficult to approach without being detected.

Quickly, he turned, gesturing for you to come closer and duck down with him. You followed
instantly, eyes sharp and following his gesture intently.

"Stay here." Din whispered, voice low through his modulator. "Stay low."

You nodded, both hands still clasped tightly on your blaster pointed at the ground. With a
small press of a button, Din watched as the cradle closed shut, keeping the child inside safe

“-Do not ever do that again.”

Then, turning his attention to the quarry still pinned under you, Din drew himself taut, used
his shadow to blot the sunlight from the man’s gaze.

“You were lucky it wasn’t me who found you.” Was all he spoke, watching the man’s face fall
despairingly and shoulders tremble in fear and pain.

“Get him up.” Din instructed you. “We have a long hike back to the ship.”

- - -

It was only once the bounty was safely encased in carbonite that Din let his head loll against
the bulkhead of the Razorcrest, listening to the metallic thunk his helmet made with the
durasteel. The chill of the carbonite still stuck to his armor, burning a cold imprint through
his flight suit.

“Din?” You asked anxiously from the ladder to the cockpit.

Din’s head turned towards you, weary gaze taking in your figure shifting your feet restlessly
as you tried to get his attention. Din could see your face, sour yet contemplative as you
scuffed your boots against the Razorcrest’s floor.

Sensing your unease, Din rolled his shoulders to push himself off the wall behind him. His
slow, purposeful footsteps echoed heavy on the metal grating of the Razorcrest’s hold as he

Din stopped just short of you, head bent to look at your face. Even then you didn’t meet his

Gently, his hand curled, and with a single finger, he lifted your face to gaze up at him. Your
eyes were open with your thoughts, anxious and yet hesitant to offer the words you likely
expected him to hear. In the time he had known you, Din had grown to read you just as easily
as any member of the covert he had ever known.



You wanted to apologize. You didn’t regret what you did. You thought he was still upset. You
didn’t want him to be angry.

You cared about him.

Din breathed through his nose, letting the air tickle the scruff of his jaw on the inside of his
helmet. Then, ever so gently, he offered:

“I’m not mad. Not at you.”

Relief instantly washed over your features, posture loosening and hands ceasing in their

cheekbone. The motion made that familiar flutter rise inside him again, and for a moment he
was reminded of your wild eyes and crouched form in the forest. The image made his heart
beat faster, summoning a foreign but not unwelcome desire deep within his stomach. The idea
that you had come so far in your skills, had become so capable and yet retained that almost
feral, protective urge did something to him that he didn’t quite understand yet.

Din had to bite down on the sudden, strange urge to kiss you.

“I didn’t mean to worry you.” You provided at last, voice gentle, drawing his attention back
beyond his thoughts. “I just…I know that this bounty was important. Know that it’s hard to
find work. I…wanted this to work out for you.”

Din felt something inside of him ease, like a window being blown open by a soft breeze. As
much as he still wanted to be upset over your sudden disappearance, over ignoring his
instructions designed to keep you safe, he knew you didn’t do it out of malice; and that- that
was because you cared for him.

He sighed, and the sound seemed to release the remaining tension in his body. You looked up
at him, and again Din felt a wash of affection come over him at the care in your gaze. Stars,
how he had managed to somehow end up with you at his side, it seemed to defy all of the
possibilities he had ever conjured for himself.

“I know.” He answered, voice dipping low. “I just…when I came back, when I saw you were
gone- Cuyan. I-“

The familiar fear at your absence rose within him once again, the same fear that had stalked
him every step of the hunt prior to that horrifying moment when an unfamiliar blaster shot
shattered the peace of the tranquil forest.

You nodded, the motion familiar against his hand pressed to your face. “I’m…sorry.” You
spoke at last, voice hesitant with the apology. “Not for getting the bounty, but…for doing that
to you. Especially after I argued with you about the same thing before that.”

Any sense of triumph at receiving an apology from you was muted by the solemnity of your
words, earnestness bleeding through your voice and chipping at the walls Din was built for
himself.



Yet with you, always with you, those walls began to crumble, letting the warmth of your
beautiful soul pierce through Din’s defenses.

As if in a final, deadly blow, you reached forward, letting your arms slide around his
midsection and meet in the back. Din at first flinched at the embrace, the gesture foreign and
unfamiliar to him. Yet you persisted, keeping him steady against his own hesitations. Here, in
the place between words, you could convey those feelings that you had spoken to Din in the
midnight of just you two.

And Din, Din was helpless against it. Helpless against your firm but gentle touch, your
determination to uncover him piece by piece, your assurances that, with you, he wasn’t alone.

Carefully, Din’s arms settled around you in return, eyes closing in surrender at this
comforting but familiar presence, at the place where he loved you.

There would be more to discuss later, words to be shared in the silent blue hum of
hyperspace. Yet for now, all was forgiven, and once again he was with you, just as you were
with him.

Maker, Din sure knew how to pick the planets you stopped on.

You weren't sure if this planet even had a name, or if it was much like the nameless moon you

Chapter 37: Part Thirty Seven: The Cantina
Chapter Summary

Motion caught the corner of your eye, and you glanced towards one of the tables where

that same burly Trandoshan who had caught your eye earlier seized her arm. The woman

waitress shakily deposited a tray of drinks before trying to hurry off. Before she could, that
