and several patrons started towards the scene, only to hesitate when the mercenary's fellows
let their hands drift towards their weapons.



 

A wave of nausea washed over you at the sight of the girl's eyes, terrified and furious all at
once at being handled in such a way. In what seemed to be pure coincidence, those same eyes
caught your gaze, looking across the bar pleadingly.

 

The memory of your own pure, unfiltered terror at being chased down like prey, your ankle
grabbed in a bruising, burning grip seemed to seize you. The air in your chest stifled, hands
shaking and throat drying instantly.

 

You stood.

 

The motion seemed to settle a silence over the bar, and even the mercenaries seemed to
pause, take notice of you.

 

You faltered for a moment, suddenly aware of the two dozen or so eyes on your form. Yet
you didn't look at any of them, still staring at the young woman whose arm remained in the
Trandoshan's reptilian grip. You swallowed thickly, feeling that same liquid courage give way
to a new type of bravery.

 

"Let her go."

 

The Zabrack leader who was bent over the edge of the bar seemed to perk up at the sound of
your voice, as if mildly surprised you'd speak out. He straightened, turning to you, eyes
disinterested yet appraising. Then his gaze flicked to the Trandoshan member of his crew, and
he gave a small nod before the reptilian released the girl's arm. The waitress was quick to
scurry out of the way, sending you a concerned but grateful look as she cradled her arm and
ducked behind the bar.

 

You turned your attention back to the Zabrak leader, who continued to regard you with a mild
interest from across the cantina. The tension had not vanished from the atmosphere, and you
no found yourself to be at the center of both his and his crew's attentions. Yet you stood your
ground, swallowing hard before speaking clearly:

 



"Thank you."

 

You thanked the stars your voice didn't waver. However, neither did the Zabrak's attention
falter from you. You tried not to squirm under his stare, uncomfortable at his sudden
inspection of you. Briefly, you considered sitting down and letting the matter be. Before you
could, however, the mercenary spoke in a low, accented voice.

 

"Aren't you a little...foolish? To be a bounty hunter?" He asked, and the question made a
ripple of laughter run through his crew. You stiffened at the accusation, shoulders drawing
back defensively. You realized that’s what you appeared as, in your gear, with your blaster
strapped to your thigh, gloved hands clenched at your sides. For a moment you were grateful
that the pirate didn’t notice your face from any bounty boards. Yet your tongue seemed to be
sharpened by your prior indulgences, because before you could stop yourself you shot back a
retort.

 

"You're a pretty ugly for a guy who walks around like he owns the place."

 

Behind you, Din sighed.

 

A flicker of annoyance passed over the Zabrak's face before it was schooled into that same
indifference from before. He didn't reply, not at first, regarding you for a moment longer
before nodding to the Trandoshan, who stood. The chair under him squeaked against the floor
as he did, his breath rattling with a hiss as he towered to his full height.

 

You gulped.

 

"Greenhornssss always need a lesssssson or two." The Trandoshan hissed as he began to
make his way towards you, then paused.

 

You felt a familiar presence behind you, coming to stand just behind your back and glaring at
the Trandoshan over your head. A small sigh rose up your chest in relief with the knowledge
that Din was right there beside you, ready to intervene and offer his aid without you even
needing to summon him. A glance at Grogu found him climbing into his carrier, able to spot
trouble a mile off as result of his travels with you two.



 

"Take it easy." Din spoke, and you recognized the tone as one of negotiation, trying to de-
escalate the situation before it got even further out of hand. "We're just passing through. We
don't want to start trouble."

 

That wasn't entirely true. Not on your part. The anger at seeing someone mistreated, at being
insulted still boiled hot in your veins. Your fists were clenched at your sides, teeth grinding
and heart beating entirely too fast. Logically you knew it was safer to walk away, but the
alcohol had dampened your restraint, and you found yourself itching for a fight that you
knew wouldn't serve anyone.

 

"A Mandalorian?" The Zabrak asked, almost amused. "I thought your kind were extinct."

 

Now you felt Din tense, and you could imagine the almost imperceptible tilt of his helmet.
"Not all of us."

 

The leader hummed, and a wry smile crept onto his lips. With a snap of his fingers his crew
rose up as one. You couldn't help but take a step back, your body colliding with Din's sturdy
frame. Yet your Mandalorian remained unmoved, even when you glanced up at him in
concern.

 

"Too bad." The leader spoke, drawing your gaze. "I hear the price of beskar is pretty good
nowadays." and with that the crew began to advance on you.

 

Your breath seemed stuck inside your chest, a gasp to shallow to swallow down. The sight of
five different mercenaries stalking towards you and Din was something that even the liquid
courage in your bones didn't anticipate, and you couldn't help but be remain frozen to the
spot.

 

Yet just as Din was about to push past you, unholster his blaster and do what he had to,
movement made your eyes flicker past one of the burly mercenaries.

 



A young man, one of the ones who had been standing by the door, now stood behind one of
the gangsters with a look of determination shining past the fear in his eyes. You could see
him hesitate for a moment, take a step and then pause. Yet then his eyes locked with yours,
and you saw him draw himself up to his full height. In a single, fluid movement he hoisted
one of the chairs he had been perched on and spoke to the slighter pirate in front of him.

 

"Hey."

 

You watched as the pirate turned halfway, a curse almost past his lips when the farmer
brought down the chair across his back in a devastating blow, the wood shattering upon
contact. The pirate collapsed to the floor, groaning and crumpled. You stared wide-eyed, open
mouthed at the young man who stood over his form, breathing heavy, eyes wild.

 

"Holy sh-"

 

With that, all hell broke loose.

 

As if that were some type of cue, the farmers and townsfolk in the cantina seemed to surge as
one, standing and launching themselves at the nearest member of the mercenary group. In an
instant the cantina's terse atmosphere boiled over, exploding into shouts, yelling, the sounds
of people and furniture crashing against the walls.

 

From your step up in the corner boot you could see the entire scene unfold. A burly older
gentleman smashed one of the late-reacting mercenary's faces into the wood table he sat at,
only to be struck across the jaw by one of his victim's comrades. Two women, as if sharing
the same exact simultaneous thought, launched themselves at one of the pirates, a Twi-lek
who had withdrawn his blaster. While one grappled with his firing arm the other yanked at
his lek, making the man howl in pain.

 

A blaster shot pinged off the wall mere inches from your head, and automatically you ducked
and rolled away from the incoming fire. The cacophony of the sudden brawl was deafening,
and in just a heartbeat you found yourself lost, trying to find Din, Grogu, the exit to the
cantina, any type of escape route.

 



Yet then the Trandoshan tossed aside two of the scrawny farmer boys who had stood guard at
the entrance and locked his eyes on your ducked form. You didn't have time for your veins to
freeze in fear because soon the pirate was pushing and shoving his way towards you, sharp
teeth gleaming inside his mouth.

 

You grasped blindly for your blaster, anything nearby to try and defend yourself. The amount
of time it would have taken you to set your sights on the mercenary was overcome quickly by
his form hurling towards you, claws out and ready to rip you apart. You coiled and just as he
swung, dove out of the way blindly.

 

Now under a table you watched as the Trandoshan turned in search of you, his huge frame
taking up most of your vision. At that exact moment your hand landed on the neck of a bottle,
the glass cool against your sweaty grip.

 

When the Trandoshan caught sight of you under the table, he leaned down and reached a
claw to try and grasp at you. Yet in retaliation you swung the bottle as hard as you could,
listening to the shattering sound it made against his scales. His reptilian howl seemed to dim
all the other chaos in the bar for a moment as glass shards embedded in his skin. That gave
you just enough time to scramble from under the table and put some distance in between you
and him.

 

"Din!" You yelled as soon as you were standing, trying desperately to try and gain your
bearings. A glance proved he was no longer standing at the booth, but that Grogu's carrier
was firmly shut and pushed off to the side away from the fighting. Your relief at the toddler
being safe was short lived, however, because the table in between you and the Trandoshan
was suddenly violently knocked to the side, accidentally impacting a member of pirate crew
who had just begun to gain the upper hand on one of the farmers. He went down with a
groan, body collapsing into a crumpled heap beneath the wooden table.

 

You tore your eyes from his figure to the Trandoshan looming over you, bracing
automatically as his arm came swinging down at you.

 

Yet before it could impact and knock you violently, a familiar blaster rang out. The plasma
struck the Trandoshan square in the center of his shoulder, making him reel backwards and
teeter with his abrupt loss of momentum. A split second later another shot rang out, this one
managing to down the alien so that he fell at your feet.



 

Eyes wild, you turned to the origin of the shot, behind you and to the left.

 

Din. He had somehow made it closer to the door, weaving his way through the chaos in a
likely effort to try and find you. His visor caught the warm glow of the lanterns inside the
tavern, one hand on his blaster and the other brandishing his vibroblade to fend off any
attackers who came too close.

 

You had just enough time to smile in relief before Din's visor flashed, and you could see him
reach out-

 

Something struck you from the side, and you went spinning away from the collision, arms
reaching out in an effort to grab onto something, anything to anchor yourself. You could hear
Din call your name, only for the sound to be cut off with a grunt as he dealt with an attacker
of his own.

 

You shook your head, trying to clear away the sudden dizziness that clouded your vision. Just
in time, your gaze focused on a gloved hand aimed straight at your face. Instinctively you
raised your own hands, blocking in the way Din had drilled you to do over and over again. It
was clumsy at best, and the impact bruised your forearm. Yet it seemed to work, for your
attacker seemed to misjudge their next attempt at striking you. Instead, they managed to grab
you by your shirt, trying to drag you closer.

 

You grunted, wiggling and trying to dislodge them. A wild kick proved futile at besting this
person. Instead, it was all you could do to try and grab them back, trying to force them away
from you. Yet this person was stronger, their grip sturdier than yours. In a desperate attempt
you reached under their arm to their back, trying to grapple your way out of their grasp.
Somehow that managed to lift your attacker slightly off the floor.

 

As if it was a starship engine flaring to life, your muscle memory began to take over. You
planted your feet, turning and using the person's momentum to try and lift them even further.
It was a significant effort, but this person was slightly leaner than you, and soon you had
them halfway across your shoulder. The fire in your blood, burning ever bright in a furious
combination of adrenaline, fear, courage, and booze seemed to burst from your veins. With a
hoarse scream you pulled as hard as you could muster and sent the person flying over your
shoulder and crashing into a chair on the other side, flipping them onto their back below you.



 

For a moment you were consumed by your triumph, at successfully using the same technique
Hana had taught you at the Covert on Coruscant to defend yourself. You stood over your
victim, chest heaving, eyes wild, clothes askew, and fists clenched at your side. The man
under you, dazed and confused, could only stare up at you and blink in an effort to try and
regain himself. In a haze of battle-born confidence you leaned over him and yelled
victoriously, which seemed to only confuse and frighten him further.

 

You felt your shoulder grabbed, and just as you whirled to throw a strike at your next
opponent, Din's visor reflected your wild eyes and fierce stare.

 

"Get down!" He called out hoarsely, yanking you downwards along with him to the floor.
You yelped as you went down, only to feel one of Din’s arms settle atop you and push you
into his side protectively.

 

Within a mere moment Din's bracer erupted with a series of high-pitched whistles, and you
felt a gloved hand cover your head as they shot past and around you, the sound only adding
to the chaos. Yet they seemed to find their marks, as a chorus of yelps and pained shouts rose
up around you. You scrunched your eyes shut, pressing closer to Din's arm sheltering you.

 

The noise of fighting around you seemed to dim as the whistling birds found their targets,
who collapsed in a circle around you both. Yet it wasn't over, as several skirmishes continued
even as you opened your eyes. From where you knelt you saw two men finishing off another
mercenary, who's dazed expression merely gazed back at them blankly as he bled from a torn
lip. One farmer held him in place while the other rained a series of fatigued, weary blows
onto him. After one particularly devastating strike the mercenary's knees collapsed, and he
fell to the floor bloodied, beaten, and whimpering.

 

Din helped you to your feet, catching you by the elbows and steadying you as you glance
around to see the remnants of the brawl ending. Mercenaries lay strewn across every surface
from tables to floor, all in varying states of incapacitation. Some rolled to their sides, injured
and not getting up any time soon. Others, like the Trandoshan, remained completely still,
unmoving. Yet the battle seemed to be over, as you and the farmers were successful in
defending yourselves from the onslaught.

 



The farmers weren't exactly in great shape, and you saw many help others to their feet or sit
each other down to examine wounds received during the fighting. Broken chairs, busted
lanterns, and tossed tables littered the cantina. Your boots crunched shards of broken glass
under you. If you didn't know better, you'd have assumed someone had let a grenade go off
inside the establishment.

 

You took a step and wobbled slightly, only for Din's grip on you to tighten and ensure you
remained on both feet. You glanced up at him gratefully, eyes still shiny and lips parted from
the exertion you just experienced.

 

The crash of glass caught both your attention, and simultaneously you both turned towards
the bar. There, the mercenary leader wobbled to a stand, what appeared to be either spotchka
or blood dripping down one side of his face.

 

"You-" He slurred, turning and wavering on his feet as he tried to face you. "You made a big
mistake trying to- eurgh." He held a hand to his head, watching as it came away stained red.
"Karking-"

 

Unceremoniously, he unholstered a blaster at his side, raising it towards you both. Din
stepped in front of you, blocking your form with his beskar-clad body. Yet the mercenary
leader seemed to be too dizzy to focus, because his aim went wild as he tried to stare Din
down.

 

"We're the...Dantooine Dusters... you can't-"

 

You saw Din's shoulders sink, and with a small, almost pitiful shake of his head he raised his
own blaster and fired off a single shot, making the pirate reel backwards and take out another
shelf of booze before falling unceremoniously to the ground, dead.

 

The farmers in the cantina who had watched this epilogue unfold watched the pirate fall, eyes
lingering for a moment before turning to Din and you. Likewise, you stared wide-eyed at the
deceased pirate, blinking for several long moments in shock.

 



The silence weighed heavily, awkwardly across your shoulders. You and Din glanced
anxiously at each other, both caught in the realization that your quiet evening out had turned
into a deadly brawl that had all but trashed the establishment you had deigned to drink at.

 

The sound of glass scraping along the floor caught your attention, and automatically you
tensed, expecting another adversary to emerge. Yet you looked to the doorway behind the bar,
where the bartender had appeared and now stared down at the body lying at his feet. Open
mouthed, he stared blankly before turning his gaze at you, eyebrows all but vanishing into his
receding hairline.

 

You cleared your throat awkwardly, stepping forward with an apology on your lips. Yet
before you could the bar tender's eyes abruptly flickered with a sudden enthusiasm, and he
tossed his hands up in the air with excitement.

 

"Drinks for everyone!"

 

The bruised crowd around you managed a series of tired but enthused cheers, and you
couldn't help but wheel around to look at the crowd, as if it would give you an understanding
as to what had just happened.

 

Beside you, Din also turned to examine the community of farmers surrounding you both,
more composed than you but bewildered all the same.

 

"I-I don't understand." You managed at last, looking back to the bartender. "I- we- it's our
fault this happened, so-"

 

The older gentleman in front of you waved a hand, cutting you off. His scraggly beard
upturned in a warm smile.

 

"That may be true, but don't worry about any of that now. Sit down, have a drink. Are you
hurt? Let's see if we can get you patched up."

 



You and Din shared a long glance.

 

Then Din took a step forward towards the bar, fishing in one of his pockets.

 

"At least let us help you cover the damages." He offered. "My partner and I didn't mean for
this to get so out of hand, let us repay you for the trouble-"

 

Again, the bartender waved him off.

 

"Nonsense." He rebuffed. "Truth be told, those pirates have been a scourge upon this village
for some time now. It's been so long since someone stood up to them, taught them a lesson.
Your friend there reminded us that we're not simply folks to take that kind of transgression
lightly. Besides-" He winked. "If you really want to help, you can start by cleaning up the
mess you made."

 

You stiffened, shoulders going taught as you stood behind Din. Abashedly, you cast a
sidelong glance at the ruined seats and tables and broken glass scattered across the cantina,
and the townsfolk already going about trying to clear the wreckage.

 

It was going to be a long night.

 

Swallowing hard, you stepped up beside Din and gave a small, chagrined smile at the
barkeep.

 

"I'll uh, take that drink now."

 

----

 

"I am. Never. Taking you drinking again." Din grumbled from under the weight of one of
your arms, trying to keep up with your staggering, unbalanced gait as he walked you both
back to the Razorcrest.



 

It had been at least several hours since you two had begun to help restore the cantina to order
after the brawl that had taken place there. It had taken some time, and now you could see the
horizon beginning to lighten with the promise of dawn.

 

Din had helped send the remaining pirates packing after they had come to, piling them onto a
rusty farming wagon destined for the no-man's land well beyond the settlement. You had
done your best in helping toss our broken furniture, sweep glass, anything you could to make
up for your discourtesy of all but trashing the place.

 

Yet the townsfolk were good natured about it. Some were grumpy at receiving bruises or
gashes from their brawl with the pirates, but even they seemed to calm down after a bit of
being in the comradery, jovial atmosphere of everyone working together. Even those who
were still hostile about the whole situation seemed to lighten after being greeted by Grogu,
who you had allowed to wander about once the floor was clear of broken glass and debris.

 

At some point someone had popped open a bottle of...something from the top shelf. While
you had wrinkled your nose at it at first, you soon found yourself toasting with some of the
other patrons. After a few more drinks you had begun to lean on the walls to stay upright,
whereupon Din had collected you and a very sleepy Grogu to make your way back to the
ship.

 

You snorted beside Din, a tipsy giggle bubbling up your throat like champagne bubbles. Din
merely huffed at your drunkenness, which only worsened your inebriated snickering. The
road before you swam in your vision, the lanterns warm and dim against the darkness. They
looked almost like the glowing fungi on Coruscant, and you had the strangest urge to reach
out and try to touch them.

 

Din shifted, and you drew your attention back to his solid frame pressed against you. It felt
nice, being this close. With every step you could feel the strength in his arm that steadied you
at your waist, his gloved touch clear through the fabric of your shirt. At this proximity you
could hear his breath from under his helmet, slightly strained at having to walk and handle
you at the same time.

 

It brought back thoughts from earlier in the evening, the idea of Din handling you in different
ways, his breathing labored and sweet against your lips. Despite the evening not having gone



to plan, that desire hadn't faded. You still wanted to reach out, touch him, feel his skin under
his armor and remove the pieces of him that sealed him off to you.

 

" Yer' so warm." You slurred, flopping your head against Din's shoulder. " 's nice."

 

Din didn't reply, but you swore you could hear him swallow.

 

"Let's get you to bed." He answered at last, though it was less a reply and more of a
declaration.

 

You frowned, bottom lip hanging out in a pout. You didn't want to sleep. You wanted him to
touch you, to hold you and whisper your name. You wanted to kiss him, to smother him with
your love and the confessions on your lips. You wanted Din.

 

"Not sleepy." You protested, and Din huffed again. Yet this time it sounded less annoyed and
more amused, as if he was tired and humored by you all at the same time.

 

"You're going to need sleep, cyar'ika." He spoke, voice dipping gently. "I don't know how
you managed to drink so much, but it won't be pleasant in the morning."

 

"Shaaar-eeee-kaaaa." You echoed, letting the unknown Mando'a roll off your tongue. "Was'
that mean?"

 

Din made a sound under his helmet that sounded choked. He composed himself after a
moment, voice tight as he answered.

 

"It means...uh...someone you like." He managed, tensing as you gasped dramatically.

 

"You like me?" You asked, twisting in his hold to peer up at his visor, dark in the midnight.
"Really?!"



 

This time Din huffed a chuckle, tired but humored by your antics.

 

"Yeah." He replied, and the affection in his voice made your knees wobble enough for him to
tighten his hold on you. "I do."

 

You had to swallow back the sudden emotion bubbling in your chest, the intensity of it
suddenly severe enough to make tears prick at the corner of your eyes. You rubbed furiously
at them for a moment before pretending to flop against Din's side.

 

"D'awwww, I like you too, you big tin can." You answered, and this time Din's snort was less
than amused.

 

It wasn't long before the Razorcrest came into view, settled at the edge of the village. You
tried your best to stay upright as Din punched in the code to open the cargo hold, briefly
hanging onto Grogu's carrier to balance yourself before remembering the sleeping child
inside.

 

"Come on." Din spoke quietly, using a hand at the small of your back to usher you up the
ramp, while holding onto your hand with his other. "Let's get you to bed."

 

You followed obediently, trying your best to walk straight despite the incline of the ramp.
After what seemed like a mile-long trek your knees bumped against the compartment of Din's
bed, to which you raised your eyebrows.

 

"W-wait. This is your bed." You spoke, suddenly clear-headed enough to recognize the
gesture of Din offering you his bunk.

 

Din shifted behind you, helmet tilting in consideration.

 



"...It's better than the pile of blankets you have draped over the supply crates up there behind
the cockpit." He replied quietly.

 

You blinked up at him, then shrugged before ungracefully scrambling onto the cot and
flopping ungracefully, relishing the softness that you didn't get from your own 'bunk'. You
stretched out with a little whine, feeling the remnants of alcohol float through your veins.
Already the hangover headache seemed to threaten the back of your skull, yet you ignored in
favor of horizontal bliss.

 

Yet then Din turned away from the bunk, as if to climb the ladder up to your own sleeping
spot.

 

"Wait." You called after him, and Din paused to turn back towards you. You sat up, leaning
forward and bracing yourself with your hand in front of your knees. "You're not going to go
sleep in my bunk, are you?"

 

Din stayed still for a moment, then shifted uncomfortably.

 

"I...yes." He answered at last, hesitantly.

 

You frowned up at him. As comfortable as you were with taking Din's bunk for the night, you
also didn't want him to sleep on the lumpy, uncomfortable stack that you called your own
bed.

 

Then, a coy, flirtatious smile crept across your face.

 

You rocked back on your heels, gently rolling your neck into your shoulder as you directed
your voice casually at Din.

 

"Really? You're going to go sleep on that uncomfortable thing upstairs and let me sleep
alone?"



 

Din froze.

 

Your smile only widened as you went on. "After all, I've been thinking so much about when
we were on the beach, remember?" You peeked open an eye at him, stretching your arms
overhead languidly, like a Tooka stretching in the sun. "I was hoping we could...finish what
we started?"

 

"Mesh'la." Din breathed, and it sounded almost like a warning. The air in your chest caught
as Din turned to fully face you, his broad form blocking the entrance to him bunk. The dim
lights of the cargo hold overhead cast strange shadows onto his cuirass. "Don't say things you
don't mean."

 

You frowned, the playful act dropping at his words. Instead, you gazed seriously up at him,
vision still slightly fuzzed at the edges from the tipsy feeling in your stomach. "Din, I do
mean that." You replied evenly. "I-I've been thinking about it... a lot.” Now you began to
fiddle with them hem of your shirt, torn in between taking it off and letting it remain.

 

“I've been thinking about the way your hands were on my hips, about...the way you kissed
me. I-" Your eyes fell to your lap, and you swallowed hard. "I...want that with you."

 

Despite not being able to see him, you felt Din's entire body go taut like a bowstring. He
breathed in sharply, fists clenching and unclenching at his sides as he regarded your form,
kneeling before him, on his bed, in his ship, your eyes half-lidded and expression
embarrassed and desiring all at once-

 

It nearly undid him.

 

It was a heavy moment before his breath finally fell from his chest in a loose rush of air. You
looked up at him then, lips parted, and eyes concerned and wanting.

 

"Cuyan." He began, and his tone, bordering on what sounded like disappointment, made you
curl into yourself. He paused at that, and you felt that pleasantness in your stomach sour



under his stare.

 

Yet then Din reached out, a gloved hand coming to tilt your chin upwards, cup your cheek.
You sighed at the feeling, tilting your head into his palm. Din breathed gently through his
nose at the sight.

 

"I want that too." He spoke, and hopefulness blossomed once again in your chest. "But
tonight isn't the night for that. I want your- our first time to be something we can both enjoy
when we're clear-headed and haven't been drinking. Do you understand?"

 

Dejectedness filled you, but Din's words made sense. Drunk as you were, consent wasn't
something you could give in a clear state of mind. It didn't mean you didn't want Din, it just
meant that for now, it would have to wait. Shoulders slumping in surrender, you nodded,
trying to ignore the burn of disappointment within you.

 

You sighed, reaching a hand to press Din's palm closer to your cheek. Eyes closing, you
inhaled the scent of his gloves, thick with blaster smoke and leather.

 

"Okay." You agreed finally, opening your eyes to gaze up at his visor. "But for tonight...can
you stay? Just to sleep?"

 

Din's shoulders loosened, his entire form radiating a mixture of relief and affection. You
gazed up at him, eyes lingering on his visor with a loving gaze.

 

"Of course, Cuyan." He replied quietly, tenderly. "I can do that."

 

He withdrew his hand, sitting on the bunk beside you inside of the locked cargo hold, with
Grogu close by and sleeping soundly. Your hand traced against one of his pauldrons, and his
gloved hand seized it gently, giving it a firm but reassuring squeeze.

 

You pulled your jacket and vest off as Din went about removing sections of his armor. You
opted to keep your pants and undershirt on, seeing as Din kept everything save his flight suit



and helmet on him. Eyes roaming his body as he went about carefully piling his armor, you
couldn't help but notice his bare hands as h removed his gloves. The flesh there was tanned,
sun kissed. You could see callouses from years spent using blasters and weapons alike. In the
creases of his palms you could see your own face nestled there, breathing love against his
skin.

 

Soon Din turned to you, and you both jostled your way into a comfortable arrangement
within the tiny bunk. The memories of Din cradling you in his arms while you both slept on
Coruscant appeared within your thoughts, and as if on instinct you turned to face him, curling
into his chest. The sharp intake of breath on Din’s part nearly made you roll your eyes. Even
after all this time, your touch was still something that seemed to make him reflexively react,
so unused to people touching him. Yet inside a part of you ached at the thought, at Din being
close yet so distant from the people around him.

 

You could hear his heartbeat hammering inside his ribcage, a staccato out of rhythm as it
tried to synchronize with your own fluttering pulse. A deep inhale brought in the scent of
him, of the sharp iron taste of beskar, sweat, machine oil, Din. You raised your head just
enough to breath against the collarbone hidden under his flight suit, your exhale sinking into
his form like a part of you.

 

"You are warm." You murmured there, and Din's stiff body relaxed, his arms coming to settle
around you. You cozied into them gratefully, feeling the distant comfort of sleep become a
reality. "It's nice."

 

Din adjusted so the crown of your head was tucked under his chin. Then he let out a long,
easy breath, muscles loosening as he did.

 

"Cuyan." He murmured, and you made a sleepy sound of acknowledgement at him, tucked
within the confines of his arms, where the worries of the world couldn't reach you.

 

Din didn't answer for a long time, and you didn't press him. Instead, you began to drift off,
feeling the relief of slumber beckon you closer into its velvet embrace. Here, within Din’s
embrace, safe inside the ship with Grogu’s distant muffled snores close by, a deep
contentedness fell over you.

 



The thought that, out of all the places in the galaxy you could be, whether it was a tiny repair
shop on Kaddak, an Imperial holding cell, or some back water planet living peacefully, that
you were here, settled over you. You didn’t know what exactly you had done to deserve this
happiness, to be safe and protected, to be trusted and loved by someone you loved so dearly
in turn. Whatever it was, be it a past life or some deed you had yet to perform, you would
encounter it boldly, knowing that Din would walk beside you.

 

"I love you."

 

You blinked your eyes open, as if you could somehow see Din's face as he spoke those
beloved words to you. To see his smile, his gaze, the creases next to his eyes as he murmured
those words seemed a temptation beyond your wildest dreams.

 

"I love you too." You said instead, the emotion of it all threatening to crack in your throat and
bloom at the corner of your eyes. Nestling deeper into his warm, protective, comforting
embrace you sighed once more, offering a quiet prayer to the stars that this would be how
you spent the rest of your days.

 

Then, silently, you vowed to yourself that someday, somehow, you would get a chance to see
the look in Din’s eyes as he promised his love to you once more.

Chapter 38: Part Thirty Eight: The Disgraced
Chapter Summary

Something was wrong.

You couldn't tell definitively what it was, but you could feel the air within the Razorcrest
ripple with an unspoken murmur, a whispered warning. It sang to you deep in your
bones, humming out a call that felt so familiar and yet ever so distant. To you it almost
felt like the calm before a storm, when the dark clouds began to roll in with the
whipping wind, only to still for mere minutes until lightning seemed to split the sky
wide open.

Din had told you on the beachside planet weeks ago of great cataclysms known as
tsunamis, when the water rushed away from the shore only to return with devastating
force. You felt now as if you still stood there on that very beach, watching the water
recede as the wind carried the sound of catastrophic, rushing waves far off in the
distance.

Chapter Notes

Recommended listening for this chapter:

 

Section 2/??? POV: Moff Gideon's Theme

Section 3/Razorcrest door opens: Trilla Death Theme

See the end of the chapter for more notes

 

 

 

Few knew about the strange, luminous underground on the planet of Christophsis.

 

With its hanging platforms and walkways carved into the green crystal caverns beneath
Chaleydonia, the upside-down of the city was known only to the rare collection of bounty



hunters and other underworld informants that kept it secret. Home to more vagrants that
permanent residents, the underground appeared less than lackluster as compared to the
towering, glittering skyscrapers on the planet’s surface above. Instead, it was lit by the
strange, ominous diffusion of sunlight through the crystals, which illuminated the streets in
an exotic, turquoise glow.

 

Once the undercity had been home to refugees of the clone wars, driven underground as
clones and droids battled for control of the city streets. Later it had been known as the staging
ground for a rebel cell that birthed itself right under the Empire's unyielding control of the
city above. Now, with the Empire long since shattered, the undercity had devolved into a
haven for fugitives, bounties, and the ones that hunted them.

 

Such was the case for Din, who stood in the shadows of the dimly lit bar near the small
gathering of other hunters collected around the local bounty board.

 

Arms crossed, back leaning against the durasteel wall, the Mandalorian's visor tilted to
observe the flickering images of various bounties that rotated through the holo-projector.
Around him music filtered through tiny speakers built into the ceiling, and a projection of a
Twi-lek dancer spun around a pole near the bar, sticky with spilled drinks. The establishment
was as dingy as they came, and Din liked it that way. Fewer patrons, fewer eyes to notice
him.

 

His entrance had fortunately not caused much of a stir. Though it had been some years since
he had last hunted a bounty in this sector, those that frequented the undercity's streets were
much accustomed to seeing all types of strange and unsavory characters. Luckily, the few that
were in the bar were too focused on either their drinks, the bounty board, or the glitchy image
of the dancer to take stock of the Mandalorian who had wandered in.

 

Din hadn't wanted to stop here originally, but circumstances had necessitated it. Low on both
fuel and credits, he needed to pick up a job in order to keep the three of you on the run from
both the guild, Imperials, and any other hunters on your tails. Fortunately, Christophsis was
well out of guild territory, as well as being a lucrative hunting ground, if not a competitive
one. Its reputation for being a safe haven for fugitives and runaways meant that there were
just as many here hunting as those being hunted.

 

Din shifted, keeping his eyes on the listings of bounties and their corresponding rewards as
the list occasionally refreshed itself. Most of the bounties didn't pay enough to even bother



giving chase. They either were off-planet and required fuel which Din didn't have, or nearby
and likely being chased by a collection of hunters Din didn't care to entangle with. His best
hope was to wait for the board to refresh itself and offer a more compelling prey.

 

There was one bounty however, that had caught his immediate interest: yours.

 

Din wasn't surprised that the child's had not appeared. No doubt Greef Karga had preferred to
keep it so that the only ones who knew of the reward were those within the guild. The same,
however, could not be said for you.

 

Eight thousand Imperial Credits.

 

More than double your original price. For what, he did not know. Yet the fact that it had
grown since the bounty had been posted all that time ago told a story that Din couldn't help
but be compelled by.

 

You had sworn you had no idea as to why you of all people had such a high bounty, and an
Imperial one at that. Din had believed you based on the fear and confusion you radiated
alone. Still, the lack of an explanation as to why did nothing to negate the fact that you were
such a high prize, one that could easily buy any bounty hunter as much prestige as wealth.

 

It was for that exact reason that you and the child were bunked safely in the Razorcrest and
well out of sight of any other hunters. It hadn't taken much to convince you, thankfully.
Especially after Din had explained that he would be one of many hunters in the undercity
looking for an easy mark. So, you had stayed behind with the kid, finding ways to occupy
yourself in the time that Din had gone hunting.

 

As if to mimic his thoughts, the bounty board flickered again and soon reflected your own
bounty.

 

The image had obviously been grabbed from your time spent on Coruscant, a grainy filtered
picture of your wide-eyed stare looking at something just beyond the street camera that had
caught you in its sights. Even through the poor image and flickering holo-projector, Din
could see the grime on your clothes, the fatigue and heaviness in your shoulders.



 

Din had to stifle an errant pang in his chest at the reminder of you and the child lost, hunted
in the underbelly of Coruscant. Even though Paz had been there to assist you, it was hard not
to remember the thought that Din would never see either of you again.

 

The Mandalorian gave a small shake of his head, as if to rid himself of the thought. All that
mattered now was that you were both safe, with him, and out of the hands of those that
wished to harm you.

 

Yet that wasn't all.

 

Din was thankful for his helmet, for it obscured the small smile on his lips at the memory of
you, gentle and endearing with him and the kid, yet fierce and protective towards those that
threatened any of you. The duality of your fierce determination compared to your gentleness
with him and the child he had been tasked with made Din’s expression soften under his
helmet.

 

It had become nearly impossible to reconcile the person you were now with the one he had
found crouched, hidden in the Razorcrest when you had originally stowed away on his ship.
Where you had then been skittish, uncertain, you now stood bravely before the daunting
challenges ahead of you. The panic, the shine of fear in your eyes then had since transformed
into a glint of determination, of courage.

 

You had come so far in such a brief time, mere months since Din's original encounter with
you. Where you had once struggled to hit a boulder with your blaster shots, your skills had
now evolved to reflect the number of hours you had spent practicing and fine tuning your
aim. Once, you had run from those who wished to harm you, and now you stood bravely
against them, as if daring them to hurt you, Din, or the child you were both responsible for.
Even your self-defense skills had improved in the time since you had begun training at the
new covert on Coruscant, honed under Din's watchful eye.

 

Din had watched each of your steps raptly, tracking each small victory of yours as if
spellbound by your presence alone. It was mystifying, enthralling, this evolution that was
you. There were moments where Din couldn't tear away his gaze, stricken by the captivating
journey you had begun down, despite not knowing what lay on the other side. The vision of it
all was mysterious, riveting, and oddly beautiful.



 

Such as the image of you on the secret beach, balanced in his lap with your eyes scrunched
shut and lips open, gasps and small noises spilling past them. Your voice, the wind in the
trees, and ocean waves had coalesced into an orchestra that played in Din's mind still.

 

Din's mind began to drift at that thought, fed by the tune of that rhapsody he had coaxed from
you. Images of you filtered through his thoughts unabated. You, with your playful smile and
twinkling eyes staring at him over the table at the tavern. You, with your body tensed and
blaster drawn in the forest of Daro. You, with your tender, tearful gaze and lovely smile as
you stared up at him in the midnight dimness on Coruscant as you told him exactly how
much he meant to you.

 

You.

 

Din never imagined himself to be soft-hearted. Civil, yes, polite, even. Yet he was sure the
part of him capable of something as tender as romance had been lost long ago, hardened into
the beskar that made him strong. In Grogu he had seen himself, without a family, a child in
need of protection in an otherwise tumultuous, ever-changing galaxy. The regret and pain he
had felt for that childhood version of himself had manifested into the hands that held the
child against him as he rescued him from a certain demise at the hands of the Imperials.

 

Yet, with you, it was different. You never had anyone to protect you, and it had made you into
the person you were. Where others would have killed the compassion within them in the face
of such hardship, you had retained yours through the daunting challenge of mere survival.
Despite everything, despite all you had gone through, you were kind. You were kind in the
way that heroes were good, finding ways to help others even if it meant putting yourself in
harm's way. As much as you had evolved to ensure your own survival, you hadn't lost the
ability to reach out for others and take them with you towards something better, something
brighter. That kindness was a small, flickering light in a galaxy that constantly shifted with
shadows and the perilous darkness of the unknown.

 

And Din, for all that he was worth, found himself drawn like a moth to flame.

 

Now, now that he had confessed his feelings to you, and that you had spoken your own
emotions within that same Coruscanti midnight, that light seemed only to grow, to multiply



and illuminate the path before you. Where it led, Din did not know, but he could only hope
that, at least for now, he could walk it with you.

 

Din's smile tugged upwards at the mere thought of you waiting back at the Razorcrest, with
your beautiful smile and voice ready to greet him, the child held aloft and content in your
arms. The tempting image of your soft eyes gazing up at him for a moment made him want to
forget the bounties before him, and escape back to the Razorcrest, if even for a few moments,
just to be by your side.

 

Yet before he could indulge in the thought further, a small ripple of commotion caused him to
look up at the bounty board in curiosity.

 

-and stop dead in his thoughts.

 

Heart skipping, blood racing, muscles tensing, Din took in the bounty that had just been
posted with a widening, stricken gaze .

 

An Imperial officer, wanted for desertion.

 

Last seen in the undercity of Chaleydonia.

 

Even though Din couldn't see you, even though the Razorcrest was half a city away, Din still
spun in the direction that led to you, as if he could whisper a warning with your name:

 

"Cuyan."

"Damn it all."

 



The undercity streets were aglow with the strange hazy radiance of the crystal caverns they
were carved into, sunlight managing to find its way down to even the darkest of places below
the city of Chaleydonia. Yet it was within that same dimness that Gideon's former
intelligence officer found herself, shrouded within the shadows of an alleyway, peering out
towards the lift that led up to the shipyards. A loosely gathered crowd waited for the lift to
descend, allowing them to travel to the outskirts of the city above and away from the rotten
underside of the caverns below.

 

The officer had spent days down here, barely surviving, managing to survive on the few
supplies she had taken with her in her escape from Gideon's cruiser, and the even fewer
rations she had manage to scavenge along the way. It was a miserable existence, built on the
paranoia and adrenaline she had retained in her desperate quest for mere survival.

 

It hadn't been easy, the escape, but she had in the end been left with no choice. Despite
countless hours poring over reports, examining footage and feedback from the few remaining
Imperial probes at Gideon's disposal, and monitoring traffic from bounty hunter channels,
there had been no trace of the Mandalorian known as Din Djarin, the asset, or the one who
had originally stowed away on his ship.

 

The last sighting of them had been on Coruscant, deep into New Republic territory. She had
been unable to make contact with the few Imperial cells holding out within that sector. Truth
be told, she didn't think they even existed anymore. By the time she had managed to gather
enough information to post and updated bounty on the stowaway, it seemed the group had
fled the system. Since then, it had been impossible to find them, and despite her desperate
attempts, there was only so much the officer could do to dissuade Gideon's frigid, dangerous
anger.

 

After one particularly disastrous report, Gideon had issued a final warning: Bring him the
location of the three they were hunting or face the consequences.

 

Yet the task itself was impossible. With the bulwark once known as the Imperial Intelligence
Service now shattered, and its resources scattered to the wind, finding three individuals who
had experience staying hidden across a galaxy of millions of systems was a task that could
never be completed in the time Gideon had given her.

 

So, she had fled. Fled for her life, in the desperate yet futile hope of buying herself just a few
more days, another hour, just a few more scant minutes before another Imperial or bounty



hunter inevitably tracked her down and left her body to rot in a back alley.

 

Her hope was to make it to New Republic space, consequences be damned. Even if her face
was flagged and she was apprehended by an officer, it was better than the fate that awaited
her if she decided to stay where Gideon's hunters could reach her. At least she would still
have her life.

 

Still, the bitter sting, the utter disgrace of being reduced to a mere fugitive, a bounty,
remained.

 

She had been one of Gideon's finest, destined to rise the ranks of Imperial officers. She had
been among the top of her class at the Imperial Academy, receiving accolades and
recognition from both peers and mentors alike. Gideon had hand-picked her himself after
seeing her marks. It had been grueling to work her way up to an officer position, the learning
curve of navigating Gideon's infamous, unreadable, icy temperament had been steep. Yet she
had managed it all.

 

Then, the Empire had seemed to dissolve overnight. With the Emperor's death and
consequent series of defeats amongst the disjointed remaining Imperial forces, she had been
tasked with faking Gideon's death so as to preserve his life, and consequently, her own.

 

Now that destiny of medals, promotions, and promise of greatness stood as a tarnished and
destroyed prophecy, left behind in the rubble of the Empire's ashes. The only option she had
left was to run, to be chased by the same hunters she had once looked down upon from her
place at Gideon's side.

 

The streets were emptying as nighttime approached, passerby and pedestrians alike making
their way back to the surface or withdrawing into their own hidey holes carved into the
crystalline walls of the undercity. Now was her chance.

 

Checking again to make sure the way was clear, the officer darted quickly for the lift,
managing to push past a waiting bystander who cried out in offense. Yet within moments she
was ascending upwards, towards the part of the city ruined by the New Republic offense into
Imperial territory, long since forgotten by all except those who frequented the underground.

 



She could do it. She could make it to the shipyards, steal a starship, and hopefully have
enough fuel to keep her on the run as she bolted for New Republic space. She would steal
every mile, every inch she could if it meant keeping that much more between her and the
ones that chased her down in their sights.

 

The lifted whined to a shuddering halt, dim sunlight streaming through the cracks in the
warehouse that held the entrance to the undercity. As the lift stopped, several of those waiting
turned and murmured in surprise to see a stranger wearing an Imperial uniform of all things,
standing with her blaster drawn and eyes wild like a cornered animal.

 

With a wave of her blaster, the scant few present parted without much protest, ducking out of
the way of possible blaster fire. One nearby woman screamed in surprise, and for a moment
the officer considered shooting her then and there just to silence her. Yet it would only mean
she’d be wasting precious time and leaving behind a trail with which to track her.

 

No doubt she had left an impression, which meant hunters wouldn't be far behind. The terror,
the mere knowledge of the fact that she was being tracked, hunted, was enough to fuel her
mad dash towards the shipyards.

 

Any ship would do, but something light, something fast, would be her best bet. The perimeter
fence securing the shipyards was but a mere mark in the sand as she managed to deactivate
the ray-shield that stood between her and her goal. From there, her eyes raked over the ships
present, mentally noting her options.

 

A stock light freighter, a G 30 model, a Contispex crusader, a few shuttles, plus a Razorcrest-

 

The disgraced officer blinked, eyes moving back to take in the ship she had passed over a
mere moment before.

 

The Razorcrest.

 

The same model flown by the Mandalorian hunter.

 



The adrenaline, the frantic focus on escape seemed to skid to a halt inside her terrified
thoughts, much like a starship engine failing in the endless void of space. Instead she blankly
stared at the ship in the distance, brow creased in confusion, uncertainty as she tried to
process the image before her.

 

...It wasn't possible. The odds weren't just abysmal, they were practically non-existent. It
shouldn't have been within the same realm of possibility that her exact target was here, on the
same planet, just a mere sprint away from her.

 

Yet the sight before her spoke otherwise. It was the Razorcrest. With the same, unmarked
exterior, the panels showing their age from a time long since passed.

 

And it was right there. Just waiting for her.

 

The officer took a single, hesitant step forward, her scuffed boots crunching the dust and
debris under her step. Then, resolutely, she took another, then another, until she was at last
striding towards the ship, blaster drawn, eyes focused intently on her prey.

 

As if fate itself had decided to smile upon her, the universe had given her one, final chance to
redeem herself, to capture Gideon's asset, to bring him his prize. One more chance to prove
herself loyal to the Empire, to save herself from her wretched, miserable fate.

 

...and she would not waste it.

 

-------

 

"Dank ferrick." You muttered, frowning at the comm in your hands. A thin whisp of smoke
curled upwards towards the roof of the cargo hold from the wire you had just accidentally
melted. You sighed in frustration, switching off your soldering iron and pushing it away from
you on the tiny work surface you had managed to assemble out of the various crates and such
within the Razorcrest.

 



Fixing the other broken comm you had managed to dig out of Din's spare parts drawer should
have been easy for you. You had done the same task for others a hundred times before, but
now you'd have to replace the stupid wires in the device because of your slip up. Now it
would take even more work for both you and Din to have a set of working communicators to
use over long distances.

 

You cradled the bridge of your nose between your forefinger and thumb, willing your focus
to return to you. Yet despite your attempts, it remained just as woefully absent as it had all
day. As if whisked away by some pesky Jawa with a penchant for stealing, you doubted you'd
be able to find it any time soon.

 

You were distracted. By what, it remained unclear. Yet you couldn’t shake an overwhelming,
pervasive feeling that had plagued you for most of the day.

 

Something was wrong.

 

You couldn't tell definitively what it was, but you could feel the air within the Razorcrest
ripple with an unspoken murmur, a whispered warning. It sang to you deep in your bones,
humming out a call that felt so familiar and yet ever so distant. To you it almost felt like the
calm before a storm, when the dark clouds began to roll in with the whipping wind, only to
still for mere minutes until lightning seemed to split the sky wide open.

 

Din had told you on the beachside planet weeks ago of great cataclysms known as tsunamis,
when the water rushed away from the shore only to return with devastating force. You felt
now as if you still stood there on that very beach, watching the water recede as the wind
carried the sound of catastrophic, rushing waves far off in the distance.

 

You wanted Din back already. Perhaps this persistent anxiety was merely the absence of him
by your side after weeks of being so close together. The knowledge that he was out there,
contending against other hunters, made your stomach sink low and heavy with concern. You
wanted him back, here, with you and Grogu, safe aboard the Razorcrest as you curled into his
chest, caught within the grip of dreams illuminated by the blue light of hyperspace.

 

"Batuu."

 



You blinked, jolted from your reverie by the touch of the little one who was struggling to
crawl into your lap with a breathy grunt. You smiled down at the large eared, green toddler in
your care, assisting him until he was perched in your lap and gazing up at you with a curious,
brown eyed stare.

 

"Your dad has been gone a while, huh bud?" You asked softly, running a gentle touch along
his large ears. Grogu made a little snort against your touch, reaching up and batting your
finger away. You huffed a laugh, your features easing from concern into relaxation.

 

No matter how you worried, how you paced, Grogu always had the charm of being able to
make your troubles ease away, even for just a few moments.

 

It had been some time since the original meeting between you two, you reflected. Months had
passed since then, and truly it had come to feel as if you had known Grogu your entire life.
The strange bond you had developed shortly after your first meeting with the child had only
strengthened during that time. Now, it felt as if Grogu and you could almost communicate
unspoken. Between you and Din, you were always the first to know if Grogu was tired, if he
needed to eat (which seemed like every other hour), if he wanted to play, walk, or simply just
needed to be held. Likewise, Grogu was able to pick up on your own tumultuous thoughts,
coming toddling towards you at the first sign of distress. Even now, as your anxieties over
Din's absence whispered against the back of your thoughts, Grogu's small form cuddling
against your stomach made some of that apprehension quiet.

 

You gently stroked Grogu's back absently, eyes staring past the interior of the Razorcrest
towards something you couldn't truly see.

 

Months, you realized. Mere months and yet it had felt almost like a lifetime. Only months
ago, you had been on Kaddak, tending your workshop alone, doing tasks much like the one
before you now. In the cracked, warm, clay walls of your home you had been satisfied with
the meager life you had made for yourself, having scraped by and fought for the truly little
that you had.

 

Yet now your life was so much fuller, having expanded to places ad people you had
previously never thought possible. The friends you had made in your journeys, the people
you had met made that small, dim workshop on Kaddak seem like a mere shadow against the
brightness of the relationships you had forged. The villagers on Rishi, the covert on
Coruscant, Ankau and his family, Paz and the other Mandalorians...



 

...and Din and Grogu.

 

You had hoped someday to fall in love. Even though it seemed like the stars had already
written your destiny of living and dying alone, you had somehow found the two members of
your tiny family in a galaxy of others. Grogu, the strange child with whom you shared a
mysterious connection, and Din- who had, over time, become the other half of you.

 

Din had spoken of being raised by a clan, and at the time you had been envious, regretful in a
way that you had never experienced that. Yet now, in the constant company of your two most
important persons, you could now understand.

 

While you and Grogu had forged a solid, unspoken bond, your relationship with Din had
been nothing of the sort. You both had been silent for your growing feelings for some time,
naturally. It was built into the fiber of who you both were, having been alone for so long and
not wanting to trust the other. Yet it had taken the horrific experience of being separated on
Coruscant for you both to realize: You didn't want to be without the other ever again.

 

With Din you felt a safety and security you had never experienced before. With him you felt
as if, for once, you could stop running. Be it from your past, your nightmares, or even the
things about yourself you didn't understand yet. By his side you were whole. It was through
his strength that you had managed to grow so much in such a short span on time. Knowing
that he was there to support you, guide you, come to your aid...

 

You loved him. Loved his calm and steady presence, loved the way his voice dipped with that
tone he only reserved for you, loved his wry, dry humor and blade sharp intelligence. You
loved the way you could curl into his arms at night and keep the nightmares at bay, loved his
calm reassurances and the tenderness of him he displayed to only you and his son. You loved
the fact that this intimidating, cold blooded Mandalorian who had doubtlessly defeated
hundreds before him, had the ability to be so soft and gentle when you were alone.

 

Yet...

 

You had still yet to tell him about what had happened on Coruscant, in the moments between
wakefulness that had led you into the desecrated ruins where you had found Grogu, gazing up



at the moons as if they held answers you couldn't comprehend. The mystery of it all, the
dream you had, how you had learned Grogu's name, the strange power his had displayed in
saving Paz's life, how the mysterious vision you had received that had managed to blend in
seamlessly with the same image of your nightmares, had remained unsolved.

 

You had wanted to tell him, back in that moment on Coruscant, right before he had spoken
those words to you; asking you to stay, telling you of his love for you. Yet the words had
been forgotten in the light of his confession. Silently, you had tucked those questions and
secrets away, for another time, for a moment in which you had begun to understand so much
as ask him the things he likely did not know. Yet in the joy of the revelation between you
two, in the bliss of simply being Din's, and him being yours, those questions had been long
forgotten.

 

Now, in his absence, they seemed to murmur at the back of your mind with a phantom voice,
drawing your attention and deepening the well of anxiety in your stomach. You knew that if
you continued to leave it alone, to push those questions, that confession of what had
happened with your dream on Coruscant, it would only fester inside you.

 

So, in the dimness of the Razorcrest, with the child snoozing gently against your stomach,
you felt yourself call out to Din, as if willing him back to your side once more.

 

You sighed again, let the breath draw what anxiety it could away from your chest and float
somewhere beyond you, upwards into the darkening sky above the ship and beyond into the
stars.

 

Yet when the ramp of the Razorcrest lurched and groaned as it opened, you couldn't help the
little jump of surprise that jolted the child awake in your lap.

 

Grogu came to with a startled whine, hands instantly clawing at your shirt as you scooped
him into your arms. Strangely, you felt him give a small shudder as he tucked his face into
your shoulder as you stood. You didn't pay it much attention, face already brightening at the
fact that Din was back so soon, that you could finally gather your courage enough to confess
to him all those things you had held back. The image of his form standing before you,
bending to touch the forehead of his helmet to yours, welled inside you and pushed down the
growing shadow of doubt that begged for attention.

 



Soon enough, the ramp had lowered enough to reveal the form waiting just outside of it, and
your voice was cheerful as you greeted the figure there.

 

"Welcome...back..."

 

You froze, the excited words dying on your lips as you took in the person who stood opposite
of you on the other end of the cargo hold, their boots clicking neatly against the ramp as they
took a few steps into the Razorcrest.

 

"Finally." They breathed, voice shaking just as much as the drawn blaster in their grip. "I've
finally found you."

 

The air around you seemed to vacuum into silence, each and every atom hovering in a
deafening stillness that seemed to blot out every other detail in the entire world except for the
image of the woman standing before you.

 

An Imperial.

 

Not a stormtrooper, but an officer, dressed in the standard greys of the Imperial Navy. The
clothing was dirty, scuffed, as if she had been on the run for some time. Her dark hair was
loose, framing her ashen, pale face as she gazed at you with wild eyes. The blaster pistol in
her grip was pointed at the ceiling, and your eyes flickered towards it with a terrified, wide-
eyed stare.

 

The promise of Din's return, the joy at being by his side, of watching him hold the child in
your arms with such delicate care, all of it came crashing down around you, shattering into
the silence that engulfed the cargo hold with and icy grip. Your blood seemed to freeze in
your veins, and under you it felt as if your legs had stopped responding out of pure shock.

 

Against your shoulder, Grogu whined.

 



The sound was enough to startle you from your terror, and quickly you tucked him further
into you with one arm, the other reaching for your own weapon holstered at your side.

 

"Don't."

 

You stilled at the sound of a safety clicking off, eyes watching in horror as the muzzle of the
pistol drew downwards, aimed right at you and the infant in your arms.

 

"If you touch it, I fire." The officer spoke, and you couldn't contain a shudder at her tone.
Unbroken, even, cold. The clipped, posh accent trademarked by Imperial officers was
unmistakable, making the staccato in your chest intensify to what seemed like light-speed.

 

You swallowed, feeling the motion scrape the back of your dry throat. You tried to think,
tried to consider the possibilities, but it felt as if every neuron in your brain had been fried,
unable to respond to the most basic instructions. If you were shot, that was one thing. But
Grogu...

 

"Okay." You breathed shakily, raising your free hand away from your weapon. "Please...don't
fire."

 

That made a smile tug at the corner of the Imperial's mouth, and now, assuredly, she took
several more steps into the cargo hold. You managed to slide backwards, trying to put
distance in between the two of you as you tried to summon something, anything to think of a 
way out of this.

 

Maybe if you got near the ladder, near Din's bunk, you could somehow barricade yourself
inside just long enough until Din returned, protect Grogu and-

 

"Do you have any idea-" and instantly your attention was drawn back to the Imperial officer
advancing on you. "-how long I've waited for this?"

 



You had to keep her talking. You had to stall. That way Din had time to come back, to find
you and Grogu held in the line of fire.

 

"Who are you?" You asked, feeling your voice crack in your throat. "What do you want?"

 

The officer laughed, the sound was high, bubbling up from her chest. You couldn't contain a
shiver at the madness there, as if you were witness to a woman who had been broken one
times too many, desperate and frantic in her efforts to succeed.

 

"I'm the one who's been chasing you, you stupid girl." She hissed. "All this time, since the
moment you stepped foot on this ship, I've been trying to track you, hunt you down."

 

You tried to shift further away at her words, cradling Grogu closer to you and fixing her with
a hardened stare.

 

"You're the one who put the bounty on me." You murmured, muscles tensing and coiling
automatically.

 

"Of course I am!" The officer snapped, yet this time you didn't flinch. Instead, you fixed her
with a hard stare, summoning within you all the anger, all the frustration and anxiety you had
felt in that moment you had realized there was a price on your head, that you would be
hunted seemingly for the rest of your life.

 

"I'm the one who put a bounty on you, I'm the one who sent all those blasted probes after you,
I..." Her face, contorted in anger as if was, seemed to relax all at once. Her eyes, glassy and
yet vivid with their focus on you, seemed to transfix you with a new gaze.

 

"...I even know who you are."

 

Something within you shifted. That low, deep recess of your mind that had whispered to you
on Coruscant seemed to speak again, murmuring in words you couldn't understand. Yet you
managed to ignore it, instead summoning a wry smile in return to the officer's words.



 

"Me? I'm just a mechanic." You bit back, bitterness tinting your voice. "I don't have any
parents, I'm no one special. I just happened to stow away on a random ship that had a
Mandalorian and a kid on board."

 

"Don't lie to me!" The officer snarled, her voice rising and cracking like a whip in the air
between you. You flinched at the violence there, as if her voice alone had struck you. "You
stupid traitors, you're all alike. You think you can just trick whoever you need to into
forgetting you, into doing what you want."

 

Traitor? You wondered, the smile on your lips failing as you tried to process her words.

 

Yet the officer managed to regain herself, and after a moment reached up to carefully tuck her
hair back from her face. Now poised once more, she offered you a simple, triumphant smile
as she spoke.

 

"Oh well. It doesn't matter. Either way, I've finally done as the Moff has asked. When I return
to him with both you and the asset, he will no doubt rescind his fury and grant me the
position I've always deserved."

 

Moff? Asset? Your thoughts seemed to fly wildly as you tried to understand what the officer
meant. Yet as she took another step forward, you felt your heart beat deafeningly inside your
chest, the fear within it seeming to rip you at the seams. Carefully, you took another small
step backwards, only to feel your back bump against the exterior of Din's bunk.

 

"Give me the child." She spoke, extending a single, black gloved hand.

 

You shook your head immediately, all bravado gone now in the dread of handing over Grogu,
of his small, shivering form leaving your arms.

 

"Give me the child or I'll shoot." She demanded again, voice hardening with impatience.

 



“I’ll die before I give him to you.” You shot back, voice wavering. The Imperial before you
merely smiled.

 

“That can be arranged.”

 

Out of all options now, back against the wall with nowhere to run, you did the only thing you
could think of: You spoke.

 

"Why?" You gasped, letting the fear flow through your voice in full this time. Hands shaking,
heart throbbing violently, you stared at her with the full horror you felt inside of you.

 

"Why?" You asked again. "Why us? Why me? What would the Empire want with a mere
child and a simple mechanic from a back-water planet?" Your voice shook as you spoke, and
the words alone seemed to summon all the true fear within you; the fear of not knowing, the
fear of dying without understanding the reason you had been chased, hunted, pursued for all
this time.

 

That seemed to make the officer pause for a moment, and for a split second you saw a flash
of confusion flicker across her eyes. It was gone in an instant, however, as the woman's face
hardened back into that same look of fury. Voice deeper, fueled by a barely contained rage,
she growled out a sinister response.

 

"I thought you were done playing dumb." She seethed, voice trembling with the restraint it
took her to not scream belligerently at your tensed, terrified form. "I know exactly what you
are, exactly who you are."

 

You gave a small shake of your head, even now still not understanding, still not recognizing
the meaning behind her words.

 

You were going to die. Die and never learn the reason why.

 



"You're a traitor." The officer snapped, eyes frenzied, wide and uncontrolled in their mania.
Yet it wasn't the vision of her dangerous obsession that managed to chill you to the very fiber
of your being, but the words she managed to speak next.

 

"I don't know how you managed to survive out of your entire order-" And the confusion,
terror in your eyes seemed to at last coalesce with the whisperings inside you, rising to a
deafening cacophony that threatened to mute the voice of the crazed, disgraced officer before
you.

 

"-but I know that it was only a matter of time before we hunted down and killed you..."

 

Then, in a single word that rang out like a clarion against the very depth of you, reaching
inside and grazing that unknown silence like the cataclysm you had been anticipating all this
time, the officer hissed one, final, infernal sacrament:

 

"J e d i!"
