Chapter 39: Part Thirty Nine: Fractures
Chapter Summary

All at once it was no longer Din's helmet you looked at, but one of the images from your
nightmares. Eyes widening, you suddenly felt the burning, scorching heat of fire lick at
your skin, and the screams inside you suddenly shifted, rising in pitch to echo your own
name. The image of the visor before you transformed before your eyes, and suddenly
you were gazing into the dark, bottomless blackness of a different helmet, one that
belonged to someone who leveled the muzzle of their blaster at you, letting their finger
slowly push down on the trigger...

"NO!!"

Chapter Notes

TW for descriptions of panic attacks. Read at your own discretion

See the end of the chapter for more notes

"Jedi!!"

 

The sound, the word that had been hissed through gritted teeth, the one that seemed to strike
at the very core of you, rang out deafeningly through the interior of the Razorcrest, bouncing
off the walls in an endless repetition.

 

Jedi.

 

Those rumored to have strange abilities gifted by the stars themselves, to command the
unknown entity that was known as 'the force'. The same enigmatic, seemingly omnipotent
beings who traveled the galaxy to disperse peace, but in the end had been hunted down as
traitors of the Empire. You had heard murmurs of their kind, spoken in hushed whispers away
from the ears of Imperials and their sympathizers. To speak of the Jedi was to summon
misfortune. Those who spoke of the force and those who commanded it disappeared, never to
be seen nor heard from again.



 

Yet the woman before you, belonging to that same Empire that had wiped out that strange
coven of sorcerers, now accused you of belonging to that same extinct creed.

 

Your entire form began to tremble at her words, wavering like a sapling in a gale of that
which you didn’t understand. In your arms, Grogu too, shivered. The small ripple of fear that
ran from him to you and back again in a never-ending circuit seemed to at last awaken you
from the shocked trance you had found yourself in.

 

"Liar." You croaked at last, voice cracking, eyes wild with fear. Yet the word felt tight,
constricted. Your chest tightened in an effort to simply speak, to refute the accusation. "The
Jedi are a myth."

 

Yet simultaneously that pull within you, that same gravity that had beckoned to you on
Coruscant, spoke otherwise. That same unknown thread that tied you to those same
desecrated ruins where you had found Grogu, that same force that sucked you down into the
abyss within your nightmares, roiled within you in whispers you couldn’t understand.

 

It was impossible. You knew nothing of the Jedi other than the hushed whispers from those
who dared to speak of such sedition. The Jedi were extinct, hunted down, slaughtered and
executed as traitors. There weren’t any Jedi left as far as you knew. You had nothing in
common with them. You were just an orphan, one of many left behind by the clone wars,
destined to die or fight to survive in the face of the fledgling Empire. You didn't have magic
powers, you didn't possess the strange abilities the child in your arms did. You...

 

You were no one.

 

Yet the officer before you merely sneered at your wavering declaration, as if disgusted by the
lies you tried to tell yourself.

 

"Don't play games with me, survivor." She barked, voice hoarse from the days of being
forced to hide, to flee. "I'm not feeble-minded enough to fall for your foolish Jedi mind
tricks."

 



Traitor. Survivor. Fugitive. Nobody. Jedi.

 

Your thoughts seemed to scream inside your head, loud enough for you to want to press a
palm to your temple to quiet it. The motion drew the attention of the officer before you, who
raised her blaster high enough to make it glint in the waning light of sunset. You hardly
noticed, caught in the net of your own thoughts like a small, delicate bird trying to free itself.

 

This didn't make any sense. You? A Jedi? Someone who was chosen by the enigmatic power
of the Force? It wasn’t just impossible, it was so far from your realm of existence it would
have been laughable if the circumstances were different. You didn’t possess strange abilities,
you didn’t wield a laser sword. You were just a mechanic who found themselves in the wrong
place at the wrong time, aboard a vessel with someone who at the time wanted nothing to do
with you.

 

Of all the things to be wanted by the Empire for, you never guessed it would be for the one
thing you couldn't be.

 

Grogu shifted in your arms, shuddering with a whine. The motion brought you back to your
senses all at once. You blinked once, twice, before focusing back on the woman before you.
Your eyes caught hers, and for the briefest of moments your gazes were able to lock as you
managed to stare past the blaster muzzle, into the depth of her.

 

As your gazes stilled on the other, you saw once more that hesitation, that confusion flicker
across her eyes. It was gone in an instant, and once more she glared at you.

 

"That's enough stalling, Jedi." She hissed, leveling her aim once more. "Hand me the child, or
I'll drop you where you stand."

 

You stared at her, eyes betraying the horror that engulfed you. The threat of dying, of losing
Grogu seemed like nothing compared to the curse she had laid upon you, calling you
something that didn't even exist, that raged a silent, deafening war within the fibers of you.

 

"I'm not a Jedi." You spoke, voice barely audible. Yet your gaze didn't break from hers, not
for an instant.



 

The officer blinked, again hesitating for just a moment.

 

"Speak up!" She spat, and it only made your curl further in on yourself, withering under her
stare.

 

"I'm not a Jedi." You spoke again, voice shaking, barely audible to the officer in front of you.
Eyes unblinking, staring into the depths of her, you tried to summon every inch of truth into
your voice despite the conflict inside of you. "I'm not."

 

Yet she merely laughed, the sound almost deranged to the point of madness with the duress of
being hunted, pursued by the same bounty hunters she had once looked down upon.

 

"Of course, you're a Jedi, you stupid girl." She shot back venomously. "There's no use in
denying it now, not when you've finally been caught.” Then her voice deepened, sank to a
low, dangerous tone that, for a moment, you were sure would be the last words you’d ever
hear.

 

“You're foolish to think I'd let you go after everything I've fought for."

 

She didn’t believe you. You didn’t believe her, and you suddenly realized that this would be
the impasse that would lead to your doom. Neither of you willing to surrender, the result
being a crumpled, bloody form slumped against the metal floor of the ship you stood in.

 

Something rose within you then. Like a spark raging to life, you were at once consumed by
the fear, the anger, the frustration, the desperation of her failure to believe you, of not
understanding, of not knowing why denying the accusation seemed to render a part of you in
half.

 

"I'm not a Jedi!" You yelled, eyes closing, body hunching over the child in your arms, voice
shrill and ricocheting off the walls of the Razorcrest.

 



The silence that followed seemed like the end of all things, a final, moment's pause before a
shot rang out and ended your life where you stood. Yet, after several moments when the
silence only grew, when you didn’t feel a brief, horrifying pain followed by nothingness, you
at last looked up to the officer before you.

 

Her blaster had lowered just a few inches, pointed now at your feet rather than you and the
child in your arms. The sneer, the disgust and desperation on her face had faded, and in its
place you saw a confusion, an uncertainty that seemed more terrifying than her contorted
expressions from before.

 

"You..." She spoke at last, voice softer now, disconcertingly quiet, unsure.

 

You stared at her, lips parted, eyes threatening tears, chest clenched in an invisible, intangible
hope. Yet then the officer before you, ragged and desperate as she was, spoke in a voice that
shook the depths of you.

 

"You…really don't know...do you?"

 

PEW-!

 

You screamed at the abrupt sound of a blaster shot, sinking down to the floor and hunching
over Grogu, who cried out within your arms. You waited for the pain, for the moment in
which you felt the horrific burning, scorching wound of the blaster bolt through your side,
ripping apart your insides and rendering you a final, fatal blow.

 

Yet it never came.

 

Trembling, breathing hard, a whimper threatening your throat, you waited for several, long
moments before finally beginning to reconnect with the world around you once more.

 

You could hear the sizzling, smell the smoke of burnt flesh. The pungent odor of cauterized
blood seemed to seep into your clothes. Yet it didn't come from you. Nor did it come from the



tiny, trembling toddler in your hold.

 

At last, you looked up. Prying one eye open, then the other, you raised your gaze from the
floor to the officer who stood over you.

 

Her expression was stricken, horrified, pale and uncomprehending as the grip on her own
blaster loosened, wrist now slack and limp against her. You watched as her fingers slowly lost
all their tension, relaxing until the blaster slipped harmlessly from her hold, clattering to the
floor of the Razorcrest with a sound that seemed to be almost as loud as the blaster shot that
had rung out.

 

Terrified, you watched as the officer's eyes turned at last to you, catching you in her terrified,
glassy gaze. Her mouth moved, as if to issue one, final rebuke, to lay that fatal ultimatum
against your flesh just one more time.

 

Then her body fell, collapsing in a heap next to her discarded blaster. You heard her give a
single, lingering, shuddering exhale. Then she went still.

 

You froze, eyes impossibly wide, staring at the fallen form of your attacker. Grogu trembled
in your arms, tucked tightly against your chest, where you felt your heart beat in a deafening,
irregular rhythm. You felt as if you couldn't breathe, couldn't think, thoughts everywhere at
once and yet nowhere to be found. For a single, shattering moment, you thought you saw a
vision of yourself lying on that floor before you, hands still outstretched for the child in your
arms.

 

Then, a single, terrified, hoarse scream broke through the fog of your thoughts.

 

"Cuyan!"

 

Your eyes shot towards the sound, able to only observe the glint of beskar as a large, dark
shadow hurdled towards you both.

 



Though you flinched at the sight, taken aback by the large, towering form that jogged into the
hold of the Razorcrest, Grogu immediately perked up. His large green ears, which had
drooped in fright, now raised in attention as his head swiveled to take in the form of his
Mandalorian caretaker. Instantly he whined, reaching for Din as the latter knelt in front of
you, now obscuring the vision of the officer he had shot dead from behind.

 

In your extended surprise your arms had loosened around Grogu, and quickly the child was
scooped from your arms into Din’s, who held him against his chest plate with one hand while
tucking his blaster away with the other.

 

"Are you hurt?" He asked quickly, voice tinting with a concern he only expressed for you and
the child in his hold.

 

Your eyes looked up, caught the image of his visor staring down at you, tilted down so it
failed to catch the overhead lights in the cargo hold. Wordlessly, you stared at it, thoughts still
racing in an attempt to process what had just happened. You opened your mouth
automatically to reply but found instead that the only sound that escaped was a shuddering
exhale which rapidly developed into a series of hyperventilating, ragged gasps.

 

Din flinched, reaching out a hand to firmly touch your shoulder in an attempt to bring you
back from the edge of panic. Yet you were already far gone, doubling over and clutching at
your chest, gasping and heaving in an effort to simply breathe.

 

Din's call for you was distant, unable to penetrate the horrific ringing in your ears. It sounded
as if he was somewhere far away, as if trying to summon you through a vast, deep ocean. You
could hear his voice, but it was muffled, obscured by the soul gripping terror that refused to
release you from its hold.

 

When Din's touch vanished from you, you felt a stab of pain in your chest so swift it knocked
what little breath you had from inside you. You gripped the fabric of your shirt tight in your
fist, as if it could somehow dull the sensation. When you looked up to where Din had gone,
you saw the limp, slackened form of the Imperial officer's body tumble from view, down the
ramp of the cargo hold. Din stood above it, shoulders tight and form emanating a raw sense
of fury you had seen only a few times before. Then he turned, visor glinting as his focus
turned to you. With one hand he reached out and punched the lever for the ramp, and you felt
the ship shudder under you as it began to rise.



 

Then Din walked back towards you, steps careful and measured, as if he was trying to not
spook an untamed, injured animal. You could catch some of the words he spoke, one hand
skirting a touch along your shoulder once more.

 

"...I don't....we can't stay here....off planet...hyperspace..."

 

He paused after he was done, as if expecting a response. You managed a belated nod, still
trying to fend off the terrifying breathlessness that held you in its hold. That seemed to satisfy
Din, for at once he vanished from you towards the ladder that led upwards to the cockpit. You
could feel each step as he ascended the ladder, then a pause before the ship began to come to
life, humming and awakening around you.

 

Yet you remained, trying desperately to claw your way back, back from the all-encompassing
panic that had swept you out into a dark, bottomless ocean. Like a riptide, you felt the vision
of composure and reality slip farther into the distance, becoming dark and obstructed by the
haze of your thoughts. Your heart felt as if it would burst from your chest, and briefly you
wondered if it would, if you would collapse here inside the cargo hold as your body gave out
from the unimaginable pressure inside you.

 

The only thing that managed to pierce through the pure, primordial fear like lightning
flashing in a blinding storm were the words of the Imperial officer.

 

"Traitor...Survivor...Fugitive...Bounty..."

 

"...Jedi!!"

 

Your shoulders shook as you heaved, coughing and gagging in the simple effort to catch your
breath. It was so much, too much. It felt as if you were going to split into a thousand tiny
fragments to be scattered across the stars and never be reunited again.

 

The ship rose under you, hurtling upwards through the atmosphere of Christophsis towards
some unknown destination. You felt for a moment, weightless, as if held aloft within the



cradle of space surrounded by the whispers which had grown into a deafening, catastrophic
chorus that chanted those same cursed words at you in a never-ending mantra.

 

You didn't notice as the ship paused, hummed, and then lurched forward into the blue light of
hyperspace.

 

It wasn't true, you tried to think to yourself. It wasn't true. Whatever the officer had said, it
was simply in an effort to disarm you, a blatant attempt to confuse you so she got the upper
hand.

 

Yet the truth of it rang deeply in your bones, touching that same part of you that you had
brushed against in that hazy, dream-like vision on Coruscant. There, the stars had hummed a
tune you had known all your life. Now that music was warped, screaming out against your
efforts to deny the word, the title that had been laid bare against your flesh.

 

Jedi.

 

With the ship humming under you, you failed to notice Din's footsteps as they rapidly
descended the ladder, rushing back towards you, towards your aid.

 

You heard his voice, and if you hadn't been so caught by the strange panic that had seized
you, you would have been concerned at the fear in his tone. When his hands landed on your,
on either shoulder, you flinched. Yet they didn't move. Rather, Din held fast to you, using his
own strength to raise you up, bring you to a shaking stand and turn you towards his bunk
behind you. The distraction of movement managed to help you bring what little breath you
had under control, even as you tried to quell the pang, the pressure inside your chest.

 

The simple touch of the one you trusted, the person you had silently sworn yourself to, made
a part of you ease into his grip. Carefully, you managed to sit on the edge of the bunk behind
you, body trembling uncontrollably as Din's hands fluttered around you, lifting your arms and
bending your legs as he looked for a blaster scorch against your skin. Yet he found none.
Despite everything, you nor Grogu had been injured in the encounter. You hadn’t even
suffered a scratch before Din had appeared in the nick of time, saving you once again.

 



When Din was satisfied, he at last let his hands gently cup your face, turning your gaze
upwards, towards his visor. You shuddered a breath, unconsciously leaning into his palms to
relish in his touch, seeking reassurance in a galaxy suddenly full of the unknown.

 

Yet something shook inside you then, at the sight of the dark, reflective surface you had seen
a hundred times before. Whereas before you had looked to Din’s visor for guidance, for hope,
in love and in reassurance, the shape of it now seemed to warp before you, shifting and
changing into something different.

 

All at once it was no longer Din's helmet you looked at, but one of the images from your
nightmares. Eyes widening, you suddenly felt the burning, scorching heat of fire lick at your
skin, and the screams inside you suddenly shifted, rising in pitch to echo your own name. The
image of the visor before you transformed before your eyes, and suddenly you were gazing
into the dark, bottomless blackness of a different helmet, one that belonged to someone who
leveled the muzzle of their blaster at you, letting their finger slowly push down on the
trigger...

 

"NO!!"

 

You reached out, raising your hands and pushing the heavy form in front of you, hands
connecting with the smooth metal chest plate of the Mandalorian that had a split second ago
been hunched over you in deep worry.

 

Despite your terrified shove, Din remained unmoved. His sturdy frame rocked back at your
palms landing on his chest plate, but otherwise he simply froze, every muscle coiled in a
rigid, unrelenting shock.

 

In the horrible, tense silence that followed,  you realized you had made a mistake. Like the
endless, deep void of space, at once your thoughts seemed to come hurtling back to reality,
screaming into a stop so suddenly it made your entire body shudder. Your eyes remained
closed, as if to block out the lingering, shadowy images of the helmet from before, protecting
yourself from the remnants of your nightmare as it at last whispered into silence.

 

Heart still racing, but thoughts now eerily, startlingly silent, you carefully pried open your
eyes to look at the form in front of you.



 

Din stood stock still, hands still slightly raised, as if wanting to reach out to you. Yet there
was a hesitation, a hurt in his stance you didn't recognize, so foreign was it to the image of
the hardened hunter that appeared to you in your mind. Din looked at you, startled, surprised,
shaken that you had shoved him away with such resilience. Even without seeing his face you
could see the shock, the hurt inside of him.

 

You paused, face falling, eyes widening to look at your hands, the hands you had used to
push away your ally, your protector, your partner, your lover, Din.

 

"Din...I..." You spoke, and your voice was cracked, hoarse and dry from the hyperventilating
breathlessness you had just experienced.

 

Yet Din's form seemed to harden, falling in on itself just as much as he drew himself up.
Shoulders tightening, hands clenching at his sides, Din’s figure tensed at the seams. All at
once the form of Din seemed to contract, fortifying itself into the stance not of the man you
had grown to trust, had grown to love, but the one who came before him. Mando.

 

"You should rest." The Mandalorian bounty hunter stated evenly, voice tight and
indiscernible. "You must be tired."

 

Then Din turned abruptly, without hesitation, and began to ascend the ladder back up towards
the cockpit. You watched him, gaze following and failing to summon the words to get him to
stop, to wait, to let you explain. Each step up the ladder seemed to land like a nail hammered
into a coffin, sealing you in the guilt and shock of your reaction. Din didn't look back as he
vanished, leaving only you, alone, sitting on the edge of the bunk, suffering in the silence of
his absence.

 

Crestfallen, you stared at the place where Din had been, listening as the doors to the cockpit
opened and hissed shut with a sound of finality. The silence that followed was unbearable,
leaving you alone once more and lost within the depth of your own mind, and the guilt at
having struck one of the only people in the entire galaxy who had sworn to keep you safe.

 

A horrible, sick feeling rose within you. Empty and yet all consuming, it bubbled up your
throat unabated and erupted into a wrecked sob that threatened your voice. Eyes suddenly hot



with tears, you folded in on yourself, burying your face in your hands and letting your quiet,
distraught voice hiccup against the heel of your palms.

 

You hadn't meant to hurt him. You hadn't meant to push him away. If anything, you wanted
him closer now more than ever, to hold you as your cries fell against his chest and you could
be reassured by the heartbeat there. Yet instead, you were alone, caught in the riptide of your
own swelling thoughts.

 

Like a wave crashing over you, all at once the stress of being nearly killed, of being told
something about yourself you couldn't reconcile with, at hurting Din and then being left alone
sank down on you like the weight of the galaxy itself. Your gut seemed to twist and coil like
some strange serpent, and it was all you could do to muffle your sobs into your hands.

 

Suddenly, it felt as if you were a child once more. Alone, afraid, disturbed by the ever-
changing world around you, yet forced to face it by yourself. In the baked, dry, dusty streets
of Kaddak, you wept into the silence of the abandoned houses and shuttered structures where
you found shelter.

 

You wept. You wept for yourself, but also for the things that you wish you had. You knew it
would be a simple task to follow Din up, to apologize, to seek that comfort you so craved like
the child you were inside, but it felt hollow, useless. Even if Din and you did reconcile, the
bitterness, the sting of what had just transpired would remain.

 

It was too much. The distraught made your stomach weave itself into knots, twisting and
turning with crooked ease. Face now slick with tears, you doubled over and sniffled against
your chest, folding in on yourself almost protectively.

 

You called out. Not audibly, but within yourself, summoning a voice from the depths of you
in an effort to reach out a hand for comfort. To simply touch someone else, to have them
acknowledge you, to simply stay by your side as the weight of the words crested over your
shoulders.

 

Then, in a feather-light contact, a small hand pressed into your side. You paused, stilled,
trying to catch your breath in the midst of your messy, choked sobs. Then you lifted your
head, and with your vision blurred from tears, found the small but concerned form of Grogu
hovering by your side, standing on the mattress next to you.



 

The child looked up at you, and in his own eyes you could see the mirror of your own.
Distraught, confusion, concern, and beyond that, a silent plea to not be alone.

 

"Oh Grogu." You breathed, easily scooping the child into your arms and holding him against
your chest. Grogu hiccupped, and in the sound you felt your own sorrow coalesce into
something that connected the two of you. The fear of your nearly fatal encounter, the distress
of everything that had just transpired wove an invisible bond between the two of you, uniting
you in misery.

 

That same, sublime thread that had connected the two of you since your first encounter
seemed to sing quietly a song of sorrow. In it you could sense that same, strange call from
before, the one that lay at the core of the strange whisperings and gravity you failed to
explain even to yourself. Yet you ignored it, instead focusing on the touch, the comfort of
another being that you could hold close as your ragged exhales shook your chest.

 

You don't know how long you stayed like that, wrapped in each other's touch, relying on just
each other to bear the brunt of the emotions that came with the experience you had just
survived, and the wounds that came with it.

 

At some point you found yourself on your side, sprawled on Din's cot, with Grogu tucked
against your stomach like a purring loth-cat. Then, in a graceful, quiet blessing, fatigue and
emotional exhaustion overcame you, and you surrendered yourself to the fitful embrace of
sleep.

 

----

 

The stillness inside the cockpit was...unsettling.

 

Din was by now used to your curious presence beside him, staring at the star charts and
controls, gingerly reaching to point at the various buttons and indicators with a steady stream
of questions. Din was reminded each and every time you sat behind him that your experience
with space-faring travel was negligible at best. Though at first your persistent curiosity had
mildly annoyed him with your distractions, so used to the silence that he was, eventually it
became just another endearing fact about you.



 

Now, this part of the Razorcrest was eerily quiet, filled only by the constant purr of the
hyperdrive and occasional, consistent beeping of the controls. The flashing blue light of
hyperspace flickered off Din's beskar cuirass, dancing against his vision in a familiar yet
enthralling display. Arms crossed, he slumped in the pilot's seat, turning over the sight of
your terrified expression over and over in his mind.

 

You had never touched him like that.

 

In all the time you had spent together, months now spent almost entirely side by side, you had
never pushed at Din in such a way. Terrified, panicking, caught in the current of your own
fear, reaching out and rejecting his concerned advances.

 

It wasn't as if you three hadn't had close encounters before. Rather the opposite. It seemed
with every new destination, every new adventure, that trouble seemed to follow you. From
Hypori to Rishi, from Coruscant to Christophsis, you three had managed to escape every
time, each time a little closer than the last. Yet this was the first time that you had come into
contact with an Imperial, an officer of all people.

 

The thought of what could have happened ate at Din from the inside out, devouring his
insides and haunting his thoughts. If he had been a moment too late, if he hadn't shot first and
asked questions later, if he had somehow missed the bounty posting, if he hadn't sprinted
back to the Razorcrest...

 

The memory of your prone, injured body collapsed on Hypori seemed all too real now. The
thought that Din could have arrived to an entirely different scene, to the Razorcrest
hauntingly empty, with you and the child whisked away from him again, consumed him.
Worse yet, you could have been killed, left to bleed out and waiting, waiting for him to
appear so you wouldn't have to die alone. The memory of Hypori now seemed to coalesce
with Din's nightmare, painting a horrific scene right before his eyes.

 

Yet the worst hadn't come to pass. You and the child were safe below in the cargo hold,
unharmed except for the invisible scars left behind.

 

Even so, what had happened was close. Too close.



 

He shouldn't have been surprised then when you had pushed him away. You had rejected his
comforting touch, trying to reassure you that you were safe, whole, unharmed. You had
shoved him away, yelling in terror, eyes wild, confused, stricken with fear. He couldn’t
exactly blame you for your reaction to such an encounter, shoving him away even as he
sought to remedy his absence. After all, his words swearing to keep you and the kid safe, to
protect you both, in your time of need he had arrived almost a moment too late.

 

Din had no doubt you blamed him for what happened. Stars above, he blamed himself most
of all. Still, he couldn't deny your rejection stung to the touch. The place where your palms
had landed on his armor seemed to ache even now, burning an imprint that you had left
behind.

 

He couldn't hold it against you, this fear. Unlike Din, you hadn't lived a life of close calls and
near misses. Granted yours had not been an easy one, but to meet your end by the thing you
feared the most: killed by the people who sought you with no answers as to why, was too
cruel a fate to bear. Din understood why you blamed him, he just wished it didn't sour such a
bitter taste in his mouth.

 

Stars, would you decide to leave over this? Go back to your original plan of settling
somewhere quiet, peaceful and praying that the Empire never found you? Din could imagine
your solemn, quiet voice asking for him to drop you somewhere in the core worlds,
whispering a goodbye that would ghost across his dreams...

 

Abruptly, Din tilted his helmet back so he could run a gloved hand over his face in an attempt
to dispel the thought.

 

You wouldn't. You couldn't. Din would never forgive himself. If you left, if he let you go...

 

Din was standing before he could finish the thought, yanking his helmet back down to cover
his face and striding with purpose towards the door. Even if you were still reeling at what
happened, terrified and anxious and furious at Din for allowing you to brush that close to
death, he couldn't sit idly by as you resolved yourself to leave based on his mistake.

 



Din's boots rang against the rungs of the ladder, and each step seemed nearly deafening to the
silence of the cargo hold. You were no longer crying, he noticed. Instead, there was a solemn
silence that enfolded the hold of the ship, cradling you there in it's quiet embrace.

 

When he turned, he could see your legs dangling from the edge of his bunk, haphazardly
thrown across the edge of it. Din wanted to approach, to sit beside you and relish in the
proximity he only ever experienced with you. Yet the fear that you might reach out and strike
him again- in fear, in anger, he didn't know- made Din shift uneasily where he stood. Instead,
he gently directed his voice towards you, trying to gain your attention.

 

"Cuyan."

 

There was an uneasy pause following Din's entreating voice. Then, carefully, you shifted on
the cot. Though you didn't offer a response, the movement signaled to Din that at least you
could hear him.

 

Din tried to stifle the twisting sensation in his stomach at your refusal to speak to him,
grimacing under his helmet. His lips parted, but hesitation followed soon after. For a few
moments Din tried to summon the words necessary for forgiveness, to entreat you to stay, to
offer him reassurance that this would not be the thing that unbound you.

 

"I...understand what happened was difficult." Din spoke at last, voice halting and unsure,
scraping hard against the back of his dry throat. "Trust me when I say that if I had known you
and the kid were in danger, I would have never left."

 

Din swallowed, feeling his throat constrict uncomfortably as he spoke his next words in a
solemn, pleading voice.

 

"I'm...sorry."

 

Yet you didn’t respond. Far from it, you didn’t even move. As if doing so would give Din
some type of indication as to your thoughts, you remained frozen still, silent, unwavering.

 



"I...know that probably isn’t enough.” Din provided at last, feeling strangely discomforted by
the silence. “I promised I'd keep you safe, and I broke my promise on that. If...if you are
angry, I don't hold it against you."

 

Din clenched his fists at his side, helmet bending to look downwards in dismay as you again
refused to respond. The words had begun to build inside him now, and for once it felt as if
nothing could obstruct him from speaking what he felt.

 

"But you...you and the kid...you are both more important to me than you will ever know.”
There felt an almost phantom pain against his chest, in the place where your palm had struck
him. The sensation seemed to pierce through his armor, deep into the fiber of him, bringing
forth his next words as a mere, near desperate murmur

 

“I just hope you believe me when I say that there is nothing I wouldn't do to keep you two
safe."

 

Looking up once more to your still form, entirely absent of any indication you had ever heard
him at all, Din felt his voice nearly crack.

 

"So Cuyan...please..."

 

Again, Din was met with silence.

 

As if someone had twisted a vibroblade into his guts, Din felt his heart sink at your blatant,
solid refusal of his apology, of his oath to you.

 

"Cuyan." Din spoke again, voice strained.

 

For a moment he felt as if he should return to the cockpit, abandoning all hope of
reconciliation. Yet something whispered at him, urged him closer to your still, unmoving
form.



 

Din took a tentative step forward, and when you didn't react, another. Soon he was peering
around the bulkhead into the compartment where you were laying, expecting to see your
bitter expression staring resolutely away from him.

 

Instead, he found your features relaxed in sleep, brow still knotted in worry and lips parted
with soft breaths that fell against your wrist as your arm pillowed your head under you. The
icy refusal Din had expected was entirely absent, and its place was your gentle, restlessly
slumbering form with the child cuddled into your chest.

 

Din was quiet all at once, trying to make himself small and silent so as to not disturb you. Yet
he couldn't help but breathe a sigh of relief that the cold shoulder he had imagined from you
was nothing more than your thoughts being lost within the grip of sleep, unable to answer
him.

 

Tentatively, Din approached closer, hovering at the edge of the cot to observe your
slumbering figure.

 

You had tear stains on your cheeks, and the sight of them alone made something inside of Din
clench in regret. He almost felt the urge to reach out and smear them away with his bare
hand. Yet, afraid the gesture would disturb you, Din instead let his hand brush your hair in a
feather-light touch, simply struck by your features worried even in dreams.

 

Somehow, that gesture managed to rouse the smaller form beside yours. The child shifted
with a small whine, and after a moment opened his brown eyes to stare up at Din with a
sleepy gaze.

 

That clench inside of Din seemed to soften at the sight of the child before him, quiet,
peaceful, resting safely tucked into your figure beside him.

 

"Hey." Din greeted gently, reaching his hand out and brushing it carefully against the child's
face. With a careful murmur, he spoke. "Go back to sleep. You're safe."

 



The child murmured something Din couldn't understand, the sound babyish and garbled. Yet
he did as Din instructed, eyes fluttering shut once more.

 

Din took in the sight before him, feeling his previous anxieties briefly abandon him at the
vision of the two beings curled on his cot, tucked into each other within the cradle of sleep.
For a moment Din wished he was part of this scene, with you asleep in his arms, listening to
the sound of your snores against his chest, hands stroking the surface of your back in a
gesture to reassure himself that you were alive, whole. With the kid tucked between your two
larger frames, the three of you tangled in a mess of limbs that seemed to bleed together at the
seams into a single soul.

 

Din sighed, helmet tilting. Under his visor, a small, gentle smile tugged against his lips,
upward towards his softening gaze.

 

His partner. His foundling. Together, caught within the grip of dreams. Safe. Here. With him,
where the world couldn't hurt them.

 

In that moment Din felt something greater than himself swell inside of him. It seemed the
threaten the seams of him, feeling at once so great and grave it forced a heavy, unrelenting
sigh from him. The idea that he could have lost nearly everything important to him, that he
would have failed to protect it, momentarily shook him again at his very foundation. Tilting
his head back to stare beyond the ship's hull, out into the vastness of space, Din swore again,
silently to the stars:

 

He would never let anything hurt his tiny, beloved clan. Never.

Chapter 40: Part Forty: To Conceal
Chapter Summary

"Din.” You spoke, voice small and barely a whisper. “Please…kiss me.”

Din stiffened instantly, and you felt his form ripple with the shiver that ran through him.

The hand under your grasp, tucked against the corner of your face, vanished from under
your touch, raising and drawing across his body. There, he pressed a button on his
gauntlet with the faintest of beeps, causing something within the hold of the Razorcrest
to whine into nothingness.

The lights. You realized. He had shut off the lights so you couldn't see his face.

The disappointment at the realization was quickly replaced by surprise as Din's hesitant,
reaching touch sought you in the darkness. You caught his hand in yours, realizing that
he had also removed his gloves so his bare hands could feel you, capture what he could
not see.

"Here." You whispered to him, unable to see his figure but wanting to draw him even
closer. "I'm right here."

Chapter Notes

Recommended music for this chapter: "Goodbye" by Ramsey (Found Here)

See the end of the chapter for more notes

You knew the scene even before it unfolded.

 

In your dreamscape the vast array of stars before you had shifted into hazy, vague images,
seeming to play in slow motion before it engulfed you at once from all sides.

 

The screams.

 



It was always the screams you heard first. They sang against the depths of you, ringing out in
ways that you couldn’t hear, beating against your chest like a stabbing, phantom pain. It
sounded like a great cry out against the flow of life itself, futile and inevitable against the
wheels of fate. Each wail was accompanied with the hail of blaster fire, a bright blue flash
that flickered against your irises brimming with tears.

 

The stench always came next, stinking of smoke and acrid, burnt blood and plasma. It lodged
itself in your throat, and despite your gagging, coughing, it refused to remove itself. You
choked on it, feeling your own voice hoarse and desperate bubbling up in a horrible, horrific
scream of fear, of protest at the scene before you.

 

Then, the fire.

 

How it had occurred, you didn't know. On accident or on purpose, it didn't matter. All that
was truly important was the way it threatened against your back, the searing heat seeping
through your clothes and laying threateningly against your skin. Immediately, you tried to
draw away from it, to flinch at the scorching sensation, but instead found yourself rooted to
the spot, immobilized by a soul-gripping terror that you had never thought possible.

 

So, you stood, with the fire at your back, the acrid smell of death clogging your nose and
throat, and the screams of the already dead haunting you for the remainder of your short,
tragic life ahead of you. A mere child, innocent and cut down for a crime that had never
existed.

 

With the flames at your back casting a hazy, orange glow around your form, figures rushed
past you to their inevitable doom. There you watched the scene before you, as shapes and
obscured figures of your teachers, friends, family moved past you, around you, through you.
You stood, transfixed by their forms running, jolting backwards horribly as they were cut
down by blaster fire.

 

And again, as it had a thousand times before, someone pushed past you, clamping down a
hand on your small shoulder so it left a blood handprint there. You didn't know their name,
didn't see their face. The only indication they had ever existed was the phantom touch they
had left there, long lost to the sands of time.

 



You tried to close your eyes, tried to blot out your senses, but the truth of it all seemed to sing
a twisted orchestra within your veins, reaching into your mind and replaying those same
sensations over and over again until it echoed in a disastrous cacophony that you couldn't
silence. It ingrained itself into you, into your very existence. You knew that no matter where
you went, no matter how you tried, that this scene would haunt you for the rest of your days.

 

You knew what came next, how the rest of this vision would unfold. Instinctively you tensed as
you were caught by the sensation of weightlessness, then falling, falling, seemingly into the
void of space itself. Your body hurtled downwards, sinking like a stone into an unfathomable
darkness.

 

...All as a voice called out your name in a final, horrified, desperate plea of despair.

 

----

 

Your eyes shot open, body freezing as if stilling yourself could chase away the remnants of
the nightmare that lingered at the edge of your thoughts. You didn’t gasp or scream the way
you would have before, instead felt that self from your dreams descend abruptly back into
your own body and allowing you a moment of reprieve to collect yourself before wakefulness
washed over you. Breath caught tight in your chest, afraid to move, you carefully pried your
eyes open.

 

The world made itself known to you in soft, cautious steps, starting with the sensation of your
dry, cracked lips, and your body sprawled across a familiar sleeping cot.

 

You blinked once, twice, feeling your eyes still puffy and tender from your previous crying
fit. Your limbs felt heavy, awkwardly slumped and sore. An ache, a fatigue had settled over
you, as if you truly had been falling, running, fleeing like you had been in your dream. The
sounds of the Razorcrest began to filter through your uncoordinated thoughts, with the hum
of the engines in power save mode and thrum of the ship's life support systems churning.
Dimly, you realized Din must have at some point brought you out of hyperspace.

 

Din.

 



You felt your body curl into itself, as if trying to valiantly protect you from the emotional
suffering that followed the thought. Yet it was to no avail, as the regret, the hurt of what had
happened when you had shoved the Mandalorian away awoke within you like a sleeping,
hungry beast. Again, tears threatened at the corner of your eyes, throat thick with a sob even
mere moments after waking.

 

The thought that Din had been hurt, had been angered by what you did, ate at you from the
inside out. Yet more than that, the grief of not being able to experience the comfort, the
reassurance you had so desperately craved from him felt like a raw wound had been carved
deep into your chest where your heart lay.

 

You gave it a few moments to pass, riding it like a tide washing over you and then drawing
out to sea. Your shuddering breath chased out the wave. Once it subsided, you again opened
your eyes and slowly began to raise yourself upwards off the cot. Limbs heavy and
uncooperative, it took you more than a few moments to shake yourself from your stupor and
reconnect with the world around you. Tentatively, you scanned the cargo hold where you had
fallen into a fitful slumber.

 

...Only to find Din sitting mere feet away from you.

 

You nearly jolted at the sight, instead feeling yourself freeze and inhale sharply at Din's silent
but profound presence. He was watching you with a keen stare, entire body tensed, as if he
were the prey spotted by some unknown predator. He was frozen, entirely still save for the
single, gloved finger he held out towards the bassinet beside him. There, you saw Grogu's
small, three clawed grip holding the finger loosely as he slept.

 

Your gaze flickered back to Din, who's stare had not wavered from your form. He seemed as
shocked to see you as you were to see him. His entire figure was rigid, fixed in place as if the
mere rise and fall of his chest would spook you. He sat on a nearby crate, and you saw his fist
curled upon his knee as he simply observed you in surprise.

 

Your stares unbroken with each other, you were reminded again of the moment where you
had shoved him away, where you both had gazed at each other in shock. Now, that same
ripple of discomfort seemed to exist between you, filling the space where words did not exist.

 



You felt a phantom pang in your chest, born there out of the grief and anger at what had
happened earlier. You almost pressed a hand there to quell it, wishing it away as you
continued to gaze at Din with your eyes containing your sorrow.

 

Din was the first to break the stare between you, carefully shifting his gaze from you to the
child in the bassinet, tucked in his blanket and snoring gently.

 

An awkward, heavy silence fell between you two, filled only by the background noise of the
Razorcrest and the sleepy sounds of Grogu. You swallowed, and upon doing so, realized that
the sob that had threatened to bubble up moments ago had not entirely vanished. Still, you at
last managed to summon your voice enough to speak.

 

"Where are we?" You asked, wincing at how cracked and hoarse your voice was from your
earlier crying fit.

 

Din's gaze shot up to meet yours, as if surprised you would speak at all. You watched as his
shoulder's rose as if to respond. Then he paused, measured himself before at last providing:

 

"At the edge of as asteroid field." And when he saw apprehension flicker across your
expression: "Far away enough to not be in danger, but close enough to hopefully be mistaken
for an asteroid."

 

He watched your expression, watched as you nodded and shifted your eyes away from him.
Then, in a gentler, softer voice he supplied:

 

"We're safe."

 

That made you look back up at him, lips slightly parted at the tinge of remorse you found in
his voice. Your eyes traced his movements as Din slowly withdrew his finger from Grogu's
grip, then shifted on his seat to better face you.

 



Bent over, elbows resting on his knees, hands clasped together, and head bent, he let out a
sigh that rattled inside his helmet. This was unfamiliar to you, this trepidation that held Din
fast within its grip. His shoulders rose, as if to talk. Yet in the silence that followed, you
wondered if Din was going to speak at all.

 

In a small, cautious voice that barely pierced the discomforting quiet, you asked: "Din?"

 

Din's head jolted up to look at you, lingering there for a moment before his gaze returned to
his clasped hands. Yet he did not speak, not at first. Instead, he waited a few more, suffering
moments before offering his voice:

 

"I'm sorry."

 

His words made you blink at the abruptness in which he blurted them out, as if Din had
forced himself to take a great leap of faith within himself. Confusion flickered across your
gaze, dim and unsure. You opened your mouth to reply, to ask why, but Din's voice went on.

 

"I broke my promise to you." He continued, as if his apology were a loosened stone that now
let a flood of words pour forth, unabated. Yet instead of the desperate tone you had
anticipated, Din's voice was even, measured. It felt as if he was simply explaining a star chart
to you rather than attempting a reconciliation that he had burdened himself with starting. It
was uncomfortable, rendering Din seemingly even further away from you, detached and
untouchable.

 

"I told you that I'd keep you and the kid safe, make sure that you wouldn't get hurt, but-" Din
paused, and you swore you could almost hear him swallow thickly before continuing: "What
happened, it's...my fault for not being there.”

 

You stared at Din, silent in your bewilderment as you tried to decipher his words. You didn't
understand. Din had arrived just in time, had saved you and Grogu, had whisked you both
away to safety. Yet now he sat before you, helmet bent, posture hunched and closed off but
asking for forgiveness, as if he hadn't just saved your life again.

 



"I...understand if you are upset." Din went on, tone and stare indecipherable. You found
yourself speechless, trying to desperately understand how Din had concluded that you were
somehow mad at him, trying to understand how Din was so calm.

 

The push, you realized belatedly. He thought you were shoving him away our of anger, not
the all-engulfing panic you had held inside you at the accusation the Imperial officer had
levied at you.

You felt your words die on your lips.

Chapter 41: Part Forty One: The Outpost
Chapter Summary

Who had spoken such words to you? It felt like a dream now, misty and intangible,
coming to you only when your eyes were closed. Much like the vision of fire and ruin
that had haunted your childhood, you couldn't recall when such a thing had occurred,
couldn't grasp the supposed memory that lingered even now.

It was impossible for you to be the member of such an order, and you knew that. You
didn't wield a laser-sword, didn't possess enigmatic, omnipotent powers. You couldn't
even shoot straight until recently. You were a simple mechanic from Kaddack, a back-
water world with no real history, no grandiose metropolis or government like the core
worlds. Of all people to be blessed with gifts from the stars themselves, it seemed
absolutely inconceivable that you were one of them.

And yet...

There was a part of you that seemed to know better. That same hazy, indiscernible figure
you had brushed against during your strange vision in the ruins on Coruscant seemed to
whisper to you from afar. She spoke in your own voice, calling out in words you didn't
understand but still resounded in the depths of you, pulling you like some anomalous
gravity towards a truth you refused to admit.

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

 

 

At some point Din had fallen asleep atop of you, his heavy body pressing down on you and
grounding you from your own thoughts. Yet even with his comforting presence atop you, you

peace in his comforting, slumbering embrace.

 

Eventually you managed to wriggle yourself out from under Din’s heavy form, surprised that

wriggling he remained fast asleep. It was only once you were free of Din's body that he

You felt a phantom pain stab at you then, weak at the sudden influx of emotion at just how

In the small confines of the ship, the only other place to be alone with your thoughts was in

A Jedi.

 

A member of an order wiped out at the end of the Clone Wars, branded as traitors by
Emperor Palpatine and executed for crimes against the then Republic. They had been hunted,

As far as you were aware, there was not a single Jedi left in existence.

 

It had been less than a decade since the Empire had fragmented into irreconcilable remnants,

the regime had purged any and every mention of the so-called peacekeepers who once were
allies to the Republic.

 

You knew from an early age that to speak of the Jedi was to tempt death itself. Any whisper,
any murmur of the mysterious sorcerers who once roamed the galaxy invited a visit from
stormtroopers, a blaster bolt in a back alley where no one would hear you, or some dark
shadow in the night that would ensure you were never seen again.

 



"Be silent. Stay hidden. Do not speak, lest you invite their wrath"

 

Who had spoken such words to you? It felt like a dream now, misty and intangible, coming to
you only when your eyes were closed. Much like the vision of fire and ruin that had haunted
your childhood, you couldn't recall when such a thing had occurred, couldn't grasp the
supposed memory that lingered even now.

 

It was impossible for you to be the member of such an order, and you knew that. You didn't
wield a laser-sword, didn't possess enigmatic, omnipotent powers. You couldn't even shoot

no real history, no grandiose metropolis or government like the core worlds. Of all people to

And yet...

To admit to yourself that the Imperial officer's declaration may have had some truth, that

"You...really don't know? Do you?"
