It was the sudden, thought shattering blare of the comms system that startled you from your
ruminations. You briefly flailed in your seat, nearly falling onto the floor at the alarming



disturbance. Simultaneously, there was a noise from below, and you realized Din too, had
been awakened by the alert.

 

You fumbled for the comms as you heard Din grumble and begin to ascend the ladder
upwards from the cargo hod. With your finger on the button, you peered at the origin
coordinates of the transmission, immediately failing to recognize them as Paz's or from Rishi,
or any of the other planets you two had visited.

 

The door to the cockpit whished open, and you jolted out of your chair, realizing you had
been occupying Din's seat.

 

Despite once again donning his helmet, you could sense the lingering fatigue in Din's form as
it was revealed by the cockpit doors. Head slightly bent, shoulder's slouched, Din looked up
at you with a small tilt of his head, still drowsy from sleep.

 

"Din." You breathed, heart still hammering in your chest. "The comms- it's not Paz, I don't
know-"

 

Din placed a gentle, reassuring hand on your arm as he slid past you and eased into the pilot's
chair with a begrudging sigh. However, he paused upon reading the coordinates on the
comm's screen. You stood anxiously behind him, hovering just behind the chair as Din's hand
hesitated over the communications board.

 

Yet before you could ask, Din was accepting the transmission, and a glitchy blue image of an
older man with a scraggly beard and unkempt hair flickered to life.

 

"Mando, long time no hear." The man greeted, cheerful voice scraping hard with age. "Been a
while since you left us common folk for the guild."

 

Din didn't move as he listened to the recording, shoulders suddenly tense and hand clenched
on his thigh. You cast a glance at him worriedly, already discerning that, whoever this was, he
wasn't exactly a person Din considered an ally.

 



"I hope you've still got openings in that big bad bounty hunter schedule of yours." The
recording went on. "Truth is, I'm in a bit of a pinch. I've got a job lined up but I'm short a
man. I could really use your help with this one."

 

You heard the leather of Din's gloves creak under his grip.

 

"It pays well if it helps. Very well, in fact. I know that's probably not an issue for a hunter like
you, though."

 

You blinked, again glancing at Din's indiscernible expression. It was true you three could use
the money, especially with the way you had all been burning fuel recently traveling around
the Outer Rim. Yet you had no idea who this man was, if his word was even sincere at all.

 

"If I'm being honest-" Your focused whipped back to the flickering image of the man. "I was
hoping you'd do a former partner a favor. For old time's sake, yeah?"

 

You frowned, feeling a small twinge of jealousy at the word partner despite yourself.

 

"If you're interested, come meet me at these coordinates. Got a nice little place running here,
far away from the hyperlanes. Good folk too. Matter of fact, I'll put on some caf while I wait
for you to show up.” The man gave a small little wave in farewell before reaching to end the
transmission.

 

“Ran, over and out."

 

The holo-recording ended with a small crackle, and the blue image of the pot-bellied man
vanished into nothingness, leaving the cabin around you and Din conspicuously silent.

 

Din remained completely still in his chair, staring at the spot where the holorecording had just
been playing. You could feel the tension radiating off of his form, shoulders tight and hand
still clenched on his thigh. He didn't speak, leaving only the sounds of the ship's systems and
your own racing heartbeat to echo in your ears.



 

You swallowed thickly, trying to decipher Din's silence. Was he angry? It almost seemed like
it. Perhaps not the same fury you had seen on him when you and Grogu were in danger, but
instead a low simmering frustration that he tried to prevent from turning into something
worse. Yet there seemed to be a tension, a hesitation that made you wonder if Din was afraid.

 

"Din?" You tried at last, voice seeming too quiet and yet too loud in the otherwise low hum of
the cockpit.

 

Your voice seemed to jar him from his thoughts, for at once Din's helmet turned to glance at
you over his shoulder. Then, his shoulders eased, and he let out a tired sigh.

 

"Ranzar Malk." He spoke at last, and you belatedly realized he was referring to the man in
the recording. "He and I ran together for a few years when I was just starting out. We...didn't
exactly part on friendly terms."

 

You felt your brow furrow automatically at Din's explanation. You had more questions to
Din’s explanation than answers, and you couldn’t help but be curious about the obscure
reference to the details of his career before he met you. Even so, your original hunch had
been right after all. Despite the man's good-natured attitude, he and Din weren't exactly allies.
So then why would someone like that call unexpectedly for a hunter he wasn't necessarily on
good terms with?

 

Something soured in your belly, feeling a general wariness born from years of heeding the
low hum of warning in your bones.

 

"He mentioned a job." You responded, voice still quiet. "Are you...thinking about taking it?"

 

This time Din turned to look at you fully, shifting in the creaky pilot's chair so he could look
at your form standing beside him.

 

"I'm...not sure." He provided after a moment's hesitation.



 

You swallowed, mouth quirking as you considered your options. It was true that you couldn’t
claim to trust this man as far as you could throw him, especially with Din's explanation.
However, the fact remained that Din's cash supply was rapidly dwindling. With the price of
fuel what it was, and with three mouths to feed, plus the supplies you had donated to the
Covert on Coruscant...

 

Din seemed to read your thoughts. "We can find somewhere else to find work." He declared,
even as he himself seemed unconvinced.

 

You nodded absently. It was true. There were other bounty boards on the Outer Rim. Still, for
all you knew Din could pick up a dozen bounties and it may not play as well as this offer. Yet
the timing of it seemed too suspicious, too convenient.

 

Din seemed to be waiting for you to speak, as if weighing his decision on your input.

 

So, against your better judgement, you supplied: "We can always hear their offer and leave if
we don't like it."

 

Din gazed up at you in silence for a moment, and you couldn't tell if his sudden stillness was
in consideration or something else. When his gaze on you didn't waver, you felt yourself shift
somewhat self-consciously.

 

"Are you...alright?" He asked at last, voice softer now, concerned.

 

You felt your expression betray your thoughts for a moment, caught off guard by Din's
sudden query. His question was not about the transmission, not about the job prospect, about
your own input. Instead, it was as if Din could sense the lingering tension in your form, the
words unspoken from your earlier miscommunication, the fear left over from your encounter
with the Imperial officer. For a moment it felt as if Din could see through you.

 

"I-" You started, voice hesitating as you desperately tried to find the words to explain
yourself. Should you tell him? Now? Right before you two entered a den of thieves? Confess



to him the terrible weight on your shoulders and let it burden him too?

 

"I'm fine." You declared at last, sounding not the least bit convincing, even to yourself.

 

Din continued to regard you for several longer moments, and you felt that if he stared for a
moment longer, if he questioned you, that the whole lie would come crumbling down around
you into ruin.

 

Yet, for whatever reason, Din mercifully turned from you and towards the controls of the
ship.

 

"Take the kid and put him in my bunk." Din instructed. "His pram too. Just in case."

 

You nodded, letting your hand fall from the back of Din's chair as you turned.

 

Yet as Din maneuvered the Razorcrest away from the asteroid field and punched in the
coordinates to the outpost, you couldn't help but feel your stomach again twist with an
ominous, prescient warning.

 

-                           -                           -

 

You were busying yourself with your gear as you felt the ship lurch out of hyperspace. The
sudden jolt of the aging ship did nothing to calm your already fraught nerves. Even the
presence of Grogu in front of you, teetering at the edge of Din's cot and eyeing you curiously,
did nothing to calm you.

 

Your fingers fumbled over the clasps to your holster, and not for the first time you suppressed
a quiet curse in front of the kid. You needed to calm down. This wasn't the time nor place to
get distracted. Not with Din seeming to see right through you, not with you having to hide
Grogu away, not in front of a group of mercenaries Din didn't fully trust-

 



"Kriff." You hissed as you accidentally knocked aside the comm you had been repairing
before you and Grogu had nearly been shot on Christophsis. It clattered to the ground at your
feet, and for a brief moment you felt yourself seize with a sudden mix of fear, frustration, and
momentary irritation at what would normally be a momentary inconvenience.

 

You forced yourself to breathe through it,  closing your eyes and letting air settle in your
lungs before releasing it with a deep sigh. Grogu made a small, questioning noise as you bent
to retrieve the project, and soon you found yourself at eye's level with him.

 

"Hey buddy." You sighed, trying to let the tension ease from your shoulders, tucking away
the communicator and trying to gentle your voice. "It's okay. We're going to be just fine."

 

You tried to take heed of your own words, tried to let them bring you as much comfort as was
intended for Grogu. Yet your heartbeat still seemed too loud in your own ears, hands
trembling imperceptibly before the child’s wide, brown stare.

 

Grogu merely tilted his head at you with another coo. You smiled in response, but it felt
almost hollow in comparison to the child's trusting gaze.

 

"I'm going to need you to keep quiet, okay bud?" You murmured, reaching out to stroke one
of his long green ears. "No running off this time. It's too dangerous."

 

Be silent. Stay hidden. Do not speak.

 

You gave a silent shudder at the words, feeling unease again coil low in your belly. Yet Grogu
seemed to understand, his ears drooping solemnly at your instructions.

 

"Hey, don't worry." You tried to reassure him with a small wave, sensing his sudden concern.
"We'll be back in no time. You won't even know we're missing."

 

This seemed to ease the toddler's anxieties somewhat, for he again raised his gaze to you with
a small, babbling gurgle.



 

...and once again, in that faraway voice, you heard your name.

 

You tried not to let the sudden apprehension show on your face, merely summoning a forced
smile as you nodded at him.

 

“That’s right buddy.” You encouraged, trying to stay cheerful despite the strain in your voice.
“That’s me.”

 

You gave him one final, uneasy smile as you stood. As you did, you lifted up a silent prayer
that, somehow, Grogu wouldn’t have to see any of the danger you and Din were entering into.

 

Just as you felt the Razorcrest steady itself and begin to descend, you pressed the panel for
Din's bunk and allowed Grogu to disappear from sight.

 

The ship settled with a dull thunk into what you assumed to be a hangar, hissing as its
systems began to disengage. You turned your back to the panel of Din's bunk and briefly
pressed yourself there, closing your eyes and willing the ripple of unease to still in your
stomach.

 

It was going to be fine. Just fine. Din was an excellent hunter. You had his back, and he had
yours. You both had managed to escape everything so far. What was a rag-tag crew of bounty
hunters to a Mandalorian and his partner?

 

A sigh escaped your lips as Din's tell-tale footsteps sounded upstairs, and you watched as the
Mandalorian descended the ladder beside you one rung at a time.

 

You straightened as he turned, trying to school your expression and body language into
something resembling confidence. Yet it seemed to not convince Din, who did a double take
at your tense form.

 



"...Cuyan?" He murmured, voice quiet inside the motionless ship.

 

"I'm fine." You supplied immediately, wincing internally at how utterly unconvincing you
sounded.

 

Din stepped closer to you after a moment’s hesitation, and you felt your shoulders hike an
inch at his sudden proximity to you. Yet Din remained a steady, calm presence before you,
gazing down through the tint of his visor at your face.

 

"Cuyan." He spoke again, and this time your eyes softened at the way his tongue rolled his
name for you, the tenderness in his voice. The way Din spoke that name, that title for you
sang inside your chest, bringing forth a warmth that seemed to grow hotter each time he
spoke. For a moment you felt that tight, unrelenting anxiety release itself, replaced by the
deep affection you felt for the man before you.

 

If only you could be back on Rishi, you thought to yourself, in that beautiful alcove at sunset
with the white petals of flowers floating on the breeze. That moment, when Din's voice had
spoken to you with a hesitant but resounding amazement, his visor contemplating your form
as your clothes rustled in the breeze...

 

Cautiously, Din's hand reached out, brushing against yours. You grasped it willingly,
smoothing your thumb over the suede of his glove.

 

"I won't let anything happen to you." Din murmured, gaze still fixed on you and echoing his
words from earlier. "You or the kid."

 

You closed your eyes, letting Din's words ground you like the artificial gravity of the outpost.
Silently, you nodded and let your soft exhale fill the space between you.

 

This seemed to satisfy Din, who gently released your hand and turned towards the ramp of
the Razorcrest. You hovered at his side. As the ramp descended, you tried to summon the
cool, calm confidence Din seemed to exude as he shrouded himself into the mask of the
bounty hunter known only as Mando.



 

"Stay by my side." Din murmured as you both descended the ramp. "Let me do the talking."

 

You nodded, schooling your face into your best expressionless mask as you tailed close
behind the Mandalorian hunter.

 

The hangar around the ship was a flurry of activity. Mechanics filtered through like worker
bees, each bent on their designated task but managing to take a curious glance at the two
newcomers. Close by, a flurry of sparks from a welder reflected onto Din's beskar armor. You
tried to ignore it just as Din did, even as the engineers and hangar employees eyed Din with
both fascination and caution.

 

Din managed to hardly notice them, visor scanning the hangar much like a predator searching
for signs of life in a dense underbrush. Carefully, you watched him from the corner of your
eyes. Not for the first time, you were impressed by the ease in which he managed to don the
fearsome, notorious bounty hunter personality. It seemed like a second nature to him, the way
he seemed to grow just a little taller, broader, seemed to draw all eyes in the room to him with
his presence alone.

 

"Mando." A voice called, and Din turned, being careful to keep you just behind him as he
did.

 

Your eyes followed the source of the voice, blinking as the stout, potbellied man from the
transmission approached from nearby. The corner of his mouth pulled into a smirk, partially
obscured by his thick, scraggly, white beard that matched his equally unkempt hair.

 

"That you under that bucket?" The man asked, narrowing his eyes mischievously at the
Mandalorian.

 

"Ran." Din greeted simply, taking the hand that Ranzar Malk extended to him in a firm grip.
The man merely chuckled, jerking Din's hand up and down in an animated greeting.

 



"I didn't really know if I'd ever see you in these parts again." Ran declared, releasing Din's
hand, and shooting Din a lopsided grin. "Good to see you."

 

Yet then his eyes flickered over Din's shoulder, landing on you. Ran's thick eyebrows
vanished into his frizzy gray mane of hair as he took you in. You could see the surprise flash
across his face for a moment before he again let his smile that seemed just a bit too wide grin
at you.

 

"Well, well, well." He chuckled. "Who is this?"

 

Din shifted, allowing Ran to see you head on. You gave the mercenary a polite smile, trying
to mirror Din's cool confidence.

 

"My partner." Din announced, followed by your name.

 

"Well, I'll be!" Ran exclaimed with a surprised bark of laughter. His hands tugged at the front
of his jacket as he eyed you up and down in fascination. "Never pegged you as the type,
Mando. Thought you worked alone nowadays."

 

Yet before Din could respond, Ran stepped towards you with an open palm.

 

"Ranzar Malk, at you service." He announced as you shook his hand.

 

"A pleasure." You returned simply, managing to cast a cursory glance at Din, who remained
unmoved.

 

Razar held your hand for what seemed like a moment too long before dropping it and turning
back to Din. Discreetly, you wiped the clamminess of his hand off on your pants.

 

Ran began to amble further into the hangar with Din at his side. You tailed along behind,
pausing one more time to glance at the ramp of the Razorcrest. Yet when you didn't see a



familiar, small green form attempting to waddle free and explore, you turned and trotted to
catch up.

 

Din had paused to allow you to again hover at his side, a gesture that made Ran chuckle. He
didn't comment on it though, instead offering:

 

"You know, to be honest I'm pretty surprised you showed up here." A comment which made
Din again focus on the mercenary with intense scrutiny. Yet Ran's smile didn't falter, even as
he waggled his eyebrows at the Mandalorian.

 

"You know...because I...hear things." He went on with a drawl. "Like maybe…things aren't
working out in between you and the guild?"

 

Din paused, turning to face Ran. You yourself stopped just short, feeling your skin prickle at
Ran's words.

 

Of course. Of course, he knew. Word travelled fast in the bounty hunter community. How
could he not know? This was a bad idea, you should get back to the ship-

 

"We'll be fine." Din deadpanned, voice low with an unspoken warning.

 

Ran merely regarded him for a moment longer, hands fidgeting as he scrutinized the bounty
hunter. He nodded in thought to himself, eyes narrowed.

 

"Mm. 'Mkay." He mumbled before holding up his hands in what seemed to be a placating
gesture. "You know the policy. No questions."

 

"And you-" Ran reached out, clapping a hand on Din's pauldron. "You're welcome back here
any time."

 



Ran shot you a smile and a wink as he brushed past Din, a gesture that did more to unsettle
than to reassure you. Din cast a sidelong glance at you, as if to comfort you, before following
Ran deeper into the hangar.

 

You three ascended a set of stairs, up and to a walkway that was at eye level with the
Razorcrest's cockpit. Ran led the way, meandering forward and keeping one hand on the
railing.

 

"So, what's the job?" Din asked at last, voice a tad deeper and hoarser than you were used to.

 

"Yeah, one of our associates ran afoul of some competitors and got himself caught." Ran
replied, having to raise his voice over the sounds of the engineers and mechanics below. "So,
I'm puttin' together a crew to spring him."

 

He spared a glance at Din before continuing. "It's a five-person job and I got four. All I need-
" and he paused to turn towards the Mando, gazing over his shoulder. "-Is the ride, and you
brought it." He concluded, nodding towards the Razorcrest.

 

Din spun, following Ran's gaze before wheeling back towards the mercenary.

 

"The Razorcrest wasn't part of the deal." He bit back. Likewise, you felt a momentary panic
at someone else using the Razorcrest. After all, Grogu was still hidden inside. If someone
found him…

 

Yet you remembered Din's warning to you, biting your tongue and clamping down on the
words forming on your lips.

 

Ran gave Din a nonplussed look. "The Razorcrest is the only reason I let you back in here."
He declared pointedly, and with a tone that made Din turn as take a single step closer to him.
Yet Ran remained undaunted, leaning forward as if to examine Din, try to see through his
visor.

 



"What's the look?" He asked, feigning innocence. Then, he stepped up to Din's side, close
enough that you felt the urge to take a step forward, place yourself in between the two of
them. Yet Ran's features eased into a smile, albeit one that didn't reach his eyes.

 

"Is that...gratitude?" He questioned mirthfully, pausing before huffing a wheeze of laughter
and walking past the Mandalorian. Then, to himself: "Yeah, that's what it is. Uh-huh."

 

You shot Din a worried look, but it seemed to bounce off of him much like a blaster bolt.

 

Ran continued to chortle even as you and Din descended the stairs on the opposite side,
wandering towards what appeared to be some sort of workspace. All the while you stuck
close to Din's side, feeling a hyper-awareness of the various gazes of the workers around you.
You wondered how many of them had perhaps seen the bounty board recently, had seen the
grainy image of your face and embedded it in their memories.

 

You didn't speak, didn't voice your concern to Din, but you didn't need to. You could see the
tension in his body language alone. Despite keeping his eyes forward, following Ran, Din let
a single hand briefly graze against the inside of your wrist behind him before returning it to
his side.

 

"Hey Mayfeld." Ran called out towards a pale, bald-headed man bent over a worktable.

 

"Yeah?" The man replied, annoyed, before turning to face the three of you. As he did, you
could see the various blasters holstered to both sides of his chest, his hips, as well as the
automatic firearm strapped on his shoulder. As Ran introduced Din, the man, Mayfeld,
clicked a part back into his blaster, looking unimpressed as Ran detailed Din's previous
exploits.

 

"This is the guy?" He asked as he stepped closer. He made a small face of disappointment
before his eyes flicked over to you.

 

"Yeah, this is him. Met him way back when, when we were all young, tryin' to make a name
for ourselves." Ran drawled on, oblivious to the fact that he no longer held Mayfeld's



attention. "But running with a Mandalorian-" and he turned to Din with a small finger
waggle. "That's what brought us some reputation."

 

Mayfeld nodded absently, eyes still focused on you.

 

"And who's this?" He nodded, and Ran turned with a bit of surprise, as if he had forgotten
you were there.

 

"My partner." Din supplied again, with the smallest tilt of his head towards the gunslinger.
You could feel the way he tensed beside you, as if disconcerted by Mayfeld's keen interest in
you. You couldn’t help but feel similarly, wondering if perhaps Mayfeld too, had seen your
face once before.

 

Mayfeld nodded, eyes narrowing at you for what seemed like a moment too long before
stepping forward and offering his hand.

 

"Migs Mayfeld." He supplied with a grin, and despite the friendly gesture you felt as if
Mayfeld's interest in you was not entirely courteous.

 

Yet you still introduced yourself, giving Mayfeld's hand a single shake before dropping it.

 

"How long you been running with Mando here?" Mayfeld asked, nodding to Din beside you.

 

You caught Din's glance towards you out of the corner of your eye, as if trying to remind you
of his previous warning.

 

So, you shrugged noncommittally. "Half a year, give or take." You supplied, trying to sound
as effortless as you could despite your hypervigilance.

 

Ran let out a low whistle. "That's a while for the likes of him." He declared, nodding towards
the Mandalorian. "He must really like you."



 

You smiled despite yourself, feeling a small rush of satisfaction at the comment. Still, you
simply offered a small nod in return, trying to keep yourself scarce. Din shifted beside you,
and you felt the distance between you shrink almost imperceptibly. You glanced at him,
surprised by the motion, as if he was wordlessly letting the other man know his fixed gaze on
you wasn’t welcome. It didn't go unnoticed by Mayfeld, who raised his eyebrows at Ran
before again focusing on you.

 

 "Well, if you ever want to run with a different crew, sweetheart, we could always use another
pretty face around here." He offered with what you assumed was his best attempt at a
charming smile.

 

You tried and failed to not wrinkle your nose at the offer, feeling put-off by Mayfeld’s sudden
endearment towards you.

 

"I'll pass." You provided bluntly, prompting a bark of laughter from Ran.

 

"Let me know if you want to reconsider." The older man chuckled. "It'll sure beat having to
look at Mayfeld’s ugly mug all the time."

 

The gunslinger whipped his head towards Ran, his charming smile vanishing instantly at the
insult.

 

"Yeah? When was the last time you didn't have to pay a woman to sleep with you, Ran?" He
shot back, which only made Ran laugh harder. Still, the mercenary waved a hand to dispel the
lingering tension as his wheezing laughter tapered off.

 

"You know, I asked Mando one time what he got out of running with our little rag-tag group
back in the day.” He spoke, trying to change the subject. “You know what he said, Mayfeld?"

 

Mayfeld still looked mildly annoyed, and you began to wonder if that was just his natural
expression, but bit at the query nonetheless. "What?"



 

Ran leaned forward, tilting his head towards the gunslinger with a solemn expression that
you guessed was his imitation of Din.

 

"Target practice." He declared seriously, before again letting out a wheeze of laughter.
Mayfeld tossed up his hands with a face, feigning amazement at Din's answer. Din remained
still, but you felt his hand clench at his side, not appreciating being the subject of the other
mercenary’s humor. You gave him a side-long glance out of the corner of your eyes, not
entirely able to hide your own amusement.

 

"Target practice!" Ran wheezed again, leaning over the table in front of him. Glancing at Din,
he nodded appraisingly.

 

"Man, we did some crazy stuff back in the day, huh Mando?"

 

Din shifted beside you, somewhat nervous, before at last supplying: "That was a long time
ago."

 

"Well." Ran shrugged. "I don't go out anymore, you understand?" The he turned towards
Mayfeld, who's expression remained unimpressed and focused on Din. "Which is why
Mayfeld is running point on this one."

 

Mayfeld gave a vague little wave towards you and Din, and you tried not to narrow your eyes
at him.

 

Ran looked between the three of you before continuing. "If he says it, it's like it's coming
from me. You good with that?"

 

Din tilted his head at Mayfeld, as if trying to size him up. All the while Mayfeld gazed back
at him with a small, smug smirk tugging at his lips, likely a little conceited at being able to
give orders to a more experienced hunter.

 



"You tell me." Din replied after a beat, and you tried not to shudder at the veiled warning
there, unspoken but resounding nonetheless.

 

Mayfeld shifted, eyes narrowing and body language suddenly seeming hostile. Yet before he
could speak Ran again let out a wheeze of laughter, wagging a finger in Din's direction.

 

"You haven't changed one bit, you know that?"

 

"Yeah, well-" Mayfeld interjected. "Things have changed around here." and with that, he
gave Din a lingering glance of irritation before turning in the direction of the Razorcrest.

 

You followed him with your eyes as Ran rambled on again, talking about how Mayfeld was a
former Imperial sharpshooter, a fact that made that hyperawareness suddenly seem a little too
loud, too present.

 

"That's not saying much." Din replied bluntly, forcing Mayfeld to wheel towards him,
snarling.

 

"I wasn't a storm-trooper, wise ass!" He snapped loudly, enough to make you flinch. His gaze
flickered to you for a second, managing to take in your startled expression a heartbeat before
you could school your face back into that expressionless mask. His gaze lingered there for a
moment before he turned again, stomping off in the direction of the ship.

 

You, Din and Ran followed. Again, you peered past Din's figure, relieved to see Grogu still
had not wandered from his hiding spot. Din spared you another glance, nodding as if he too,
had the same thought.

 

You found Mayfeld standing at the front of the ship, looking up and wrinkling his nose at the
antique of a spacecraft.

 

"Razorcrest?" He scoffed. "I'm surprised that thing can still fly. Looks like a Canto Bight slot
machine."



 

You didn't know what that was, exactly, but by the way Mayfeld referred to it you couldn't
help but feel a little defensive on Din's behalf. You had repaired that ship, managed to fix the
loose wiring and the fresher and the panels inside-

 

"Alright-" Mayfeld's voice interrupted your thoughts. "That good lookin' fellow there with
the horns, that's Burg."

 

You followed Mayfeld's gesture towards a rather large, red devaronian who, upon seeing
Mayfeld, dropped the crate he was hauling with a low growl. He narrowed his eyes at you
and Din, and as he did your gaze traced over the deep, jagged scars that crisscrossed over his
face.

 

"This may surprise you but he's our muscle." Mayfeld went on as Burg circled closer to you
and Din.

 

Subconsciously you stepped a little closer to Din's side, feeling cowed by the hulking stature
of the devaronian despite yourself. He seemed even bigger than the Trandoshan hunter, his
footsteps making the floor under you shudder. Din made no motion to reassure you, instead
exuding a cool, collected swagger as Burg leaned in close to his visor. Din didn't flinch,
staring up at the other mercenary unrelentingly until the devaronian brushed past the both of
you with a low huff of laughter.

 

"So, this is a Mandalorian." He intoned, voice a deep, rough timbre as he circled around you
and came to stand beside Mayfeld. "I thought they'd be bigger."

 

Your fist clenched at your side, irritated even as Din seemed to let the jab bounce off of him.

 

Mayfeld let out a humorless chuckle before nodding at a nearby droid. "Droid's name is

"I thought you said you had four."

"Hello Mando."

Chapter 42: Part Forty Two: The Promise
Chapter Summary

"I don't...know what happened with the Imperial." Din began, voice hesitant, as if he
were trying to soothe a wild animal that would flee at any sudden movements. "I don't
know what she said to you, but…" and when Din's gloved hand brushed again yours,
you flinched. "I do believe you when you said you trusted me."

No, You thought to yourself desperately. You couldn't do this. Not here, not now. Not
like this. You couldn’t let him know. The sick, festering knowledge inside of you
seemed to prowl like an awakened animal searching for a way to claw itself free. You
began to shake, eyes wide and terrified at being cornered, at Din’s abrupt but gentle
inquiry of you, trying to work that secret loose from your bones. His request was soft,
concerned, and yet it felt as if you were being held at gunpoint all over again, forced to
reconcile things you didn’t understand.

And Din…Din, was the one holding the trigger.

His voice was hardly a whisper as he spoke:

"Why can't you tell me?"

You understood now, this constant dilemma Din had to face as a bounty hunter. No wonder

You weren’t ready.

 

He wasn't wrong, and it was the admission of that fact that made his words sting so badly. It

You still had the scars from the encounter with the Clawdite hunter, from the attack on

Now, as he tried to avoid the same thing from happening all over again, from you getting

Din's words hurt so much because they were true, and the knowledge of that made you want

The hurt, the guilt must have shown clearly across your face because Din jolted slightly upon

The silence between you two wore on long and hard, growing heavier with each passing

"I...said I would keep you safe." Din offered at last, voice sounding almost regretful. His

"Distracted." You echoed nervously, suddenly feeling a new wave of alarm wash through you

unconvincing response, now seemed to blot out any objection you had about the mission

Despite your best efforts, your voice trembled as you tried to question Din. "What do you
mean?"

 

The blank, expressionless T of Din's visor stared back at you as he lifted his head, as if he
already could see right through your facade of false pretense. The idea that, despite
everything, despite your best efforts, that Din somehow knew what you were hiding made it
feel as if the outpost’s gravity had suddenly been turned off, and that you were now caught

pretend you couldn't feel how Din's gaze seemed to pierce right through you.



 

This time, Din spoke your name as he stepped closer to you, forgoing his usual title for you.
You couldn't help but shudder as he shortened the distance between you, suddenly torn

trying to soothe a wild animal that would flee at any sudden movements. "I don't know what
she said to you, but…" and when Din's gloved hand brushed again yours, you flinched. "I do
believe you when you said you trusted me."

 

No, You thought to yourself desperately. You couldn't do this. Not here, not now. Not like
this. You couldn’t let him know. The sick, festering knowledge inside of you seemed to prowl
like an awakened animal searching for a way to claw itself free. You began to shake, eyes
wide and terrified at being cornered, at Din’s abrupt but gentle inquiry of you, trying to work
that secret loose from your bones. His request was soft, concerned, and yet it felt as if you
were being held at gunpoint all over again, forced to reconcile things you didn’t understand.

 

And Din…Din, was the one holding the trigger.

 

His voice was hardly a whisper as he spoke:

 

"Why can't you tell me?"

 

It took every ounce of strength in your bones to not shatter at the question.

 

You couldn't breathe, could hardly speak. You could see your own horrified expression
reflected in Din's visor, eyes bright with fear. Your hands shook in Din's grasp, body
trembling like a sapling in a gale at Din's quiet, honest question of you.

 

How? How were you supposed to tell him? Right now? Like this? Here, in the middle of
foreign space, surrounded by threats from all sides, before he once again thrust himself into



danger? Confess to him the gruesome, dreadful truth of what the Imperial officer had spoken
to you?

 

“You…really don’t know…do you?”

 

The truth of it all threatened to break you from the inside out. Like a dam cracking under the
weight of a flood, you felt the words inside you threaten to come rushing forth, confessing all
your secrets to the man you trusted, as horrible as they might be. You wanted to tell him,
needed to tell him, couldn’t bear to hold this secret on your own, fearing that it would come
to consume you if left untouched.

 

"I-" You spoke, voice cracking. "Din, I-I can't."

 

Din didn't speak, didn't move, hardly seemed to breathe at your words. His gaze remained
fixed on you, and the sudden, horrible, and selfish want to see his face bubbled up your throat
in a threatening sob. Suddenly, it felt as if your voice alone had wrought some gruesome,
irreconcilable distance between the two of you, even as your fingertips brushed against his in
a desperate search for reassurance.

 

Yet...

 

That figure, the same hazy and enigmatic reflection of yourself that had spoken to you on
Coruscant now seemed to wrap you in her embrace, whisper to you the strength you needed
to speak your next words.

 

"Not yet." You added at last, voice shaking as you forced the words free of your chest.
Trembling, you echoed yourself once more. "Not yet."

 

You scrunched your eyes shut, tried to stop your whole frame from trembling, shuddering at
the effort it took to say just those two words.

 



You knew. You knew that, despite everything, there would come a time to admit to Din the
horrible truth, the awful confession that you yourself tried to deny so valiantly. You couldn’t
do this alone. If you did, you were sure you would shatter, that fate would find a way to
reveal to Din your secret before you could tell him yourself. If that moment did come, you
knew the distance between you and Din might grow so far as to never be repaired.

 

But…not right now. To send Din into this mission with the sick knowledge you kept so close
to you would be tantamount to inflicting a raw, painful wound that you could offer no salve
to.

 

Despite the shaking in your hands, despite the tremble in your fingertips, the quiver in your
voice, you forced yourself to smile at your partner, at your Mandalorian through the crushing
anxiety, the fear of it all.

 

"I will." You promised, voice softer now. "I will, Din. Just not now. Not yet."

 

This seemed to relieve Din, for after a heartbeat you saw the way his shoulders eased, felt the
way his hand came to clasp around your trembling palm. For a brief, fleeting moment you
wanted nothing more than to wrap your arms around him, the unbearable weight of it all too
much, too painful, too raw for you to bear.

 

"Alright." Din conceded at last, voice quiet and yet oddly gentle despite the circumstances.
"If that's what you want, but-"

 

Din's other hand came to reach up towards your other arm, gingerly smoothing his thumb
across the place where he had grabbed you moments ago. His voice was soothing, trying his
best to reassure you upon seeing the way he had frightened you, had wrought such fear across
your gaze with his query. "You have to promise me to sit this one out. Just this one time. If
anything happened to you I..."

 

He didn't finish, but he didn't need to. You knew the fear that lay there, knew his desperation
at losing you again was just as great as the burden of your own fears.

 



You didn’t want to leave him, didn’t want to be left behind by him. The thought of him
leaving with Grogu, even for such a brief period of time, rendered a phantom stab of pain
inside your chest. It felt too much like the years of being alone, of having only yourself and
your shadow to keep you company. Yet you knew he was right. This was not somewhere you
could follow him. Not now, not with the way you were, and not with these people.

 

So instead, you took a breath, twisting you hand so you could wind your fingers through his.

 

"Okay." You agreed at last, surrendering with a soft, breathy concession. “I'll stay."

 

Din let out a relieved sigh, the sound obscured by his helmet but loud enough to fill the
distance between you, less now that you two had found space to meet in the middle.

 

"Okay." He agreed in turn, sounding still somewhat nervous, but at least temporarily satisfied
by your promise.

 

He gave you both a few more moments to settle, nerves frayed between the two of you but
repaired by the simple, fleeting knowledge of being here, together.

 

Then, Din straightened, nodded to himself, before at last releasing you. You felt a twinge of
disappointment at him not taking the opportunity to embrace you, to bend his helmet towards
your forehead in his gentle way of kissing you even with the helmet on. Yet you knew this
wasn’t exactly the place for such affections, not with the possibility of someone seeing you.

 

Din turned slightly, waiting for you to move to follow him back towards the Razorcrest and
its unwelcome visitors.

 

Yet then he paused, tilting his head at you in consideration. You blinked back at him,
confused for a moment, before he spoke:

 

"Play along."



 

You barely managed a 'Huh?' before Din again was dragging you back towards Ran and the
others, his grip looser but still firm on your other arm. You had a moment of confusion before
beginning to catch on to the idea, feigning a protest as loudly as you could to your partner.

 

"Hey, Mando! L-let go!"

 

As the group came into view, you pretended to struggle with renewed force, attempting to dig
in your heels as Din dragged you forward. The crew had wandered out of the Razorcrest once
more, likely confused by the delay your discussion with Din had resulted in. Mayfeld and the
others turned as Din hauled you over, looking both amused and surprised at Din handling you
like a misbehaving tooka-cat.

 

You tried to jerk your arm from Din's grasp, shooting him a dirty look as you neared the
others. Yet Din didn't let you go just yet, instead dragging you closer towards him so his
helmet bent towards your ear. Then, in a voice loud enough for the others to hear, he seethed
at you with barely contained irritation.

 

"You are going to stay here until I get back, and if you aren't here at the hangar by the time I
get back, I will tear this station apart to find you."

 

You blinked, momentarily lapsing in this charade between the two of you. It took you a
moment to realize that, although directed towards you, Din's warning was instead meant for
Ran and the rest of the crew. Din, in his own way, was letting you know that come hell or
high water, he would find you if you weren't here when he returned. He wouldn’t give up
until you were by his side once more.

 

You didn't doubt him for a moment.

 

Still, you did tear your arm from his grip, sneering at him and stalking back towards the
nearby worktable, where you pretended to ignore him, avoiding his gaze.

 



You could hear Mayfeld’s and Xi'an's small 'oooohh' of entertainment at the spat unfolding in
front of them. If they managed to see through Din's threat, they didn't show it, instead amused
by seeing Mando so visibly bothered by your behavior and apparent refusal to listen to him.
No doubt this was novel to them, and their sadistic glee at Mando’s outburst showed clearly
across their faces.

 

"Trouble in paradise, Mando?" Mayfeld quipped, unable to hide his delighted grin.

 

"It's nothing." Din shot back instantly, and Mayfeld held up his hands in a dramatic gesture of
compliance.

 

"Geez, okay, fine." He replied before turning towards the ship once more. "Let's get this over
with, yeah?"

 

The others followed his lead, shooting Din various looks of bemusement and glee at his
discomfort.

 

"Don't worry Mando." Ran supplied as the others began to filter into the Razorcrest. "I'm sure
we can find something to keep your friend here occupied until you get back."

 

Then, turning to you, he smiled. "You any good with starships, kid?"

 

You gauged Ran from the corner of your gaze, still trying to maintain an air of aloofness
about you.

 

"If keeping that rust-bucket in the air is any proof, then yeah, I'd say so." You replied snidely
after a moment, nodding to the Razorcrest.

 

That prompted a bark of laughter from Ran, who's broad hand clapped you across your back
so hard you nearly stumbled.

 



"Ha! Rust bucket!" He wheezed. "I like your friend here, Mando. She'll get along with
everyone here just fine."

 

Din didn't respond, merely shaking his head and turning to follow the others. Still, you heard
him mumble something about a ‘rust-bucket’ under his breath as he went. You had to contain
a snark at that, at Din taking actual offense to your pretended jab towards his ship.

 

"C'mon then, let's put you to work." Ran announced, brushing past you and walking off
further into the station. You followed him after a moment, letting him lead the way to some
unknown destination.

 

Yet...

 

You paused for a moment, footsteps stopping. Your hands clenched at your sides as you
turned to cast one, final glance towards the Razorcrest. There, Din stood atop the ramp,
gazing back at you as if the same thought had crossed his mind.

 

Your gazes locked for a moment in a final, silent goodbye, voiceless and yet somehow
profound.

 

"I'll see you soon." You thought to yourself, hoping that somehow, despite the distance, Din
could hear you, could sense the promise you made to both yourself and him.

 

"Coming?"

 

You turned and nodded at Ran with a polite smile, trotting to catch up.

 

When you glanced back again, Din was gone.
