Chapter 43: Part Forty Three: Shatter
Chapter Summary

"Din." You breathed into the device, trying, and failing to contain the quiver in your
voice. "I don’t have time to explain. Din, it's a trap. They're going to try and kill you.
You need to find a way to leave them and get back here, it's too dangerous. Ran-" You
swallowed, trying to catch your breath despite the rush of words that poured past your
lips. "Ran set you up. He's going to steal the Razorcrest, and if you- if you don't come
back he's going to try and turn me in, to send me-"

If you hadn’t been so frantic, hadn’t been so entirely consumed by the task in front of
you, perhaps you would have noticed the soft footfalls that entered the storage unit.
Maybe you would have been able to stop yourself, play off your desperate attempt to
warn your partner. Yet you didn’t notice the presence of the person who came to rest
beside you, not until their voice cut through your thoughts like a deadly vibroblade.

"What do you think you're doing?"

Chapter Notes

HUGE TW for: Claustrophobia, Nyctophobia (fear of the dark), Panic attacks, and
references to child endangerment (brief)

Please read at your own discretion

See the end of the chapter for more notes

 

 

Much like the complicated, twisted innards of the starship above you, your stomach seemed
to roil and churn with every second that Din did not return to the outpost with both the
Razorcrest and Grogu.

 

You couldn't remember the last time you had been away from the both of them at once. Din
had gone on hunts or gone to investigate alone, certainly, but even on Coruscant where you
had been separated from him at length, you still had Grogu with you. Despite the mere hours



that had passed since their departure, you found yourself longing for the intimate quiet
aboard the Razorcrest, with Grogu snoozing peacefully in your arms and Din’s quiet voice
providing small bits of conversation in the otherwise cozy silence of the cockpit. Now, absent
of them both, you felt a hole open up inside of you, empty and longing for their comforting
presences. That emptiness seemed to swallow whatever reassurances you told yourself, that
they would be back soon, that Grogu would stay hidden, that Din would be uninjured...

 

Yet that persistent awareness that had clung to you ever since you landed at the outpost
continued to shroud you like a second skin, a spider's thread that you couldn't rid from your
flesh no matter how hard you tried.

 

You attempted to busy your hands in the meantime, in hopes it would quell your rapidly
churning thoughts. Fortunately, there was a familiarity, and ease to the work of a mechanic
that managed to comfort you. The thought and patience that it took to re-route wires, to weld
pipes, to replace circuits allowed you at least some distraction from the situation at hand. You
supposed you should thank Ran for suggesting it, though you found yourself somewhat short
of gratitude when it came to the ex-mercenary.

 

Sweat beaded your brow as you lay on your back, goggles on and the undercarriage of a
gunship lofted above you. It was small, light, and as you worked on replacing one of the
many carbon-scored pipes inside of the panel above you, you couldn't help but wonder what
it would be like to fly such a ship.

 

Din had mentioned to you before how it might be beneficial for you to know at least basic
piloting skills but had yet to follow through on his offer to instruct you.

 

...If he made it back.

 

You frowned, brow furrowing again at the reminder that Din and Grogu were somewhere far
away from you, unable to be reached, unable to give you some type of indication whether
they were safe.

 

Sighing, you wiggled an arm to wipe the sweat from your forehead and briefly pushed your
goggles up into your hairline.

 



"You doing okay down there?" A voice came from beyond the undercarriage of the fighter,
partially muffled by your current position underneath.

 

"Yeah, I'm fine." You called back to the voice's owner, a young mechanic by the name of
Dash, though you doubted that was his real name.

 

Ran had all but dumped you on him earlier, telling you to do whatever he told you with a
vague little wave before vanishing deeper into the hangar. Fortunately, Dash seemed to be
pretty easy going, with a naturally relaxed smile and bright, curious eyes. His honest
demeanor was a nice break from the rest of the people you had come across in the outpost so
far, all of whom had regarded you with detached, cautious gazes. Out of everyone, it felt like
Dash was the only sincere person you had met so far.

 

"You don't sound fine. Want me to take a look at something?" Dash questioned, and you let
your gloved hands drop to your stomach with another sigh.

 

"I'm fine." You insisted, though your voice didn’t contain your usual stubbornness.
"Just...distracted."

 

There was silence for a few moments, though you didn't hear the sound of Dash's footsteps
moving away. He seemed to consider your words before nudging your boot sticking out from
under the fighter.

 

"Well, you've been under there too long at any rate, probably should take a break. I can take
over for a few."

 

You considered it, mouth pulling to the side in thought before at last awkwardly scooting
yourself from under the ship. You weren't going to say no to the offer, not when the underside
of the fighter was uncomfortably warm and humid from your own body heat. Besides, maybe
you could take the opportunity to ask Ran how the mission was progressing.

 

Blinking against the sudden contrast in brightness of the hangar, you rolled out from under
the ship and gratefully allowed Dash to pull you to a stand. The mechanic gave you a friendly
smile and a gentle pat on your shoulder, nodding off farther into the hangar.



 

"While you're taking five, would you mind grabbing me an accelerator conductor from the
third storage unit on the left? Should be unlocked."

 

You nodded, eyes following Dash's hand pointing out a corridor off deeper into the hangar. It
seemed as good a place as any to take a breather, try and collect yourself and your thoughts
before asking Ran about the mission status.

 

"Thanks, friend!" Dash called as he vanished under the fighter, his lanky legs awkwardly
sticking out from where the rest of him vanished from sight. You couldn't help a little huff of
amusement at the scene before turning in the direction of the storage units.

 

You could barely hear your own footfalls past the constant sounds of industry in the hangar,
with a dozen different mechanics and engineers working on various components or projects
around you. You side-stepped a shower of sparks from a welder, who barely even seemed to
notice your presence as you walked by. You shrugged, supposing it was better to be ignored
than to be given the less than friendly stares you had been receiving thus far.

 

It was only when you reached the storage corridor that things began to quiet, and the constant
thrum of the hangar began to dim behind you. Alone now, you murmured aloud to yourself
Dash's previous instructions:

 

"Let's see...third unit down...on the left...ah!"

 

The door was already ajar, and as you peered inside you couldn't see past the ceiling-high
shelves stacked with various parts and bits that seemed to resemble more of a Jawa’s junk
heap than a storage supply. It seemed that only half the shelves were labeled on top of it all,
making the simple errand of finding a part into a whole task that would likely consume most
of your 'break'.

 

Yet just as you were about to let out a groan of disappointment, you blinked upon hearing the
sound of hushed voices whispering further into the storage closet, as if trying not to be heard.

 



You almost brushed it off until you heard whispered the tell-tale sound of "Mando."

 

That made you freeze mid-step, shoulders tensing and muscles coiling automatically at the
mention of what could be your Mandalorian.

 

Why were they talking about a Mandalorian at all, if not for the one who had just visited the
outpost? Beyond that, why so discreet? Why in such a hidden venue, away from the eyes and
ears of the other mechanics?

 

You didn't know, but you sure as dank ferrick were going to find out.

 

So, silently, carefully, you began to creep closer. Keeping your body hunched and hidden,
treading silently on the durasteel floors, you drew closer towards the two voices hidden
behind a stack of crates, intent on learning the true nature of their discussion.

 

The two speaking didn't seem to notice your form, obscured by the bins of various supplies.
Instead, they continued to speak in low, hushed voices, unaware of the keen ears that now
overheard their conversation.

 

"Are you sure?" One of them asked, his voice quiet.

 

"Positive." A second voice supplied, deeper than the first and rougher with age. "Don't trust
me? Go look at the holo yourself."

 

"No, I trust you. I just don't understand why Ran hasn't done anything yet. If it really is true,
then he should have already started making moves by now, right?"

 

From where you were crouched, your brow furrowed. Ran? A holo? What was this about?
What did it have to do with Din?

 



"He's probably waiting for the crew to make it back." The second voice provided. "Just to be
safe. You know Ran, he doesn't really take chances."

 

"Can't blame him. I only got a glimpse of the guy, but I have a feeling he might be able to
take on all four of them and come out of it."

 

They...weren't talking about Din, were they?

 

"They call them the strongest warriors in the galaxy for a reason, not that there's many left."

 

They...they had to be talking about Din. Yet it didn't make sense. What was this about him
taking on the other four? Why was Ran waiting to be sure?

 

The horrid, dreaded realization of it all began to pool in your stomach as your thoughts
processed what you were hearing.

 

Din. They had lured him into a trap. The other four, Mayfeld and the others, they were going
to attack him, maybe even try to kill him, and Din had walked straight into their ambush.

 

Alone.

 

You raised a hand to your mouth silently, afraid that your shuddering inhale would alert the
other two to your presence. This was the plan from the start, you realized belatedly. The plan
was to lure Din out here, to where bad blood ran freely between him and his previous
partners, to hammer the nail into the coffin and get revenge for whatever devastation he had
previously wrought.

 

It was a trap, and you had let him walk into it alone.

 

"So, then what?" The first voice asked, drawing your attention back to the conversation at
hand. "Mayfeld and the others do their job for once, they bring back the ship with no Mando,



how you think his 'partner' is going to react? I doubt she'll believe he sacrificed himself or
any other bullshit excuse."

 

"Hey, keep your karking mouth down, you want the whole station to hear you?"

 

"Sorry, but you have to be thinking the same thing as me, right?"

 

You could hardly hear them now, the drum of your own heartbeat in your ears seemingly loud
enough to betray your position and expose you.

 

Din...

 

He didn’t have any idea what he was walking into. No doubt Mayfeld, Ran and the others
knew, had coordinated from the start to catch him by surprise. For all Din knew, this was just
an unfortunate job he had to complete for your and Grogu’s sake, to earn enough credits to
keep you three on the run and out of reach from both the Guild and the Imperials.

 

He didn’t know.

 

You had to warn him, had to let him know. Even if it might be too late, you had to at least try.
Maybe you could sneak off to the communications table? Or send an encrypted message
while Ran had his back turned? Either way you had to get Din out of there, had to get him
back here, had to get the hell out of here as soon as possible before it was too late.

 

Yet a newfound terror began to open up inside you at the renewed anxiety that maybe Din
wouldn't make it back. He might be a Mandalorian, and a fearsome hunter at that, but he was
up against not only four other mercenaries, but New Republic security droids as well. Maybe,
somehow Ran's plan succeeded, and the Razorcrest would arrive back without its pilot. What
then? If Din wasn't there, would they try and take Razorcrest out from under you?

 

And Grogu- oh stars, Grogu, hidden away in Din's bunk and probably not knowing what may
have become of Din, suddenly amongst vengeful bounty hunters who might not hesitate to



hurt a child, to turn him over to the Imps...

 

You thought you had heard enough, readying yourself to quietly creep from your hiding spot
unnoticed so you could make a mad dash for the comms table in hopes that maybe, somehow,
you could get a message to Din before it all went to hell, could-

 

"Don't worry about her. Ran's got someone watching her. The second Ran gets the all-clear
from Mayfeld and the others she gets dropped where she stands."

 

You froze, breath stilling and heart stuttering inside your chest at the realization they were
now talking about you.

 

"Kriff, he's not going to kill her is he? Pretty sure the bounty said she's wanted alive."

 

The bounty.

 

Your bounty.

 

You couldn't move, couldn't breathe, couldn't so much as think now. The terror that you had
felt before at the pending ambush on Din was nothing compared to the endless void that now
vacuumed all your senses into void-like nothingness.

 

Oh stars...

 

They were going to ambush Din, trap him or even worse, kill him. Take him somewhere far
beyond you, where you would never see him again for the rest of your days. That thought
alone threatened to buckle you from the inside out, but as if it wasn't enough it meant that
Grogu would be alone, defenseless with the same mercenaries that took away Din...

 

And you...



 

The familiar terror of being handed over to the Imperials, accused of something you weren’t,
couldn’t be, now prowled against the back of your thoughts like a hidden predator. Not to
mention being handed over alive-

 

The significance was not lost on you. To die from the Empire was one thing, but to be kept
alive for a reason that only they knew, to be tortured and then cast aside, discarded after
you’ve lived your purpose…

 

You were so foolish. To let you and Din come here, to walk into this obvious snare like
waltzing with death itself. If only you had paid attention to your instincts, had steered far
away from here to start with, then maybe this wouldn't have happened. Maybe Din wouldn't
already be trapped, injured, beaten, worse. Maybe Grogu wouldn't be in danger. Maybe you
wouldn't again be facing down the barrel of an Imperial's blaster, hoping that against all odds
you would find a way out of this, that your luck finally hadn't run out.

 

"No." The voice off to the side of you brought your thoughts tumbling to a halt, senses once
again focusing in on the two you were hidden from. "Ran said she's needed alive."

 

Your heart beat a wild staccato in your chest as you again tried to understand exactly what
that meant. Why alive? Didn't Imperials execute Jedi on sight? Why in the world would the
Imps go through so much trouble to keep you alive? The possibilities of what that could
mean felt like a black hole looming on the horizon, inescapable and catastrophic.

 

You didn't have time to ponder the thought, not now. Your first priority was getting out of
here and finding a way to send an urgent warning to Din, maybe even find a way off the
station so you could rendezvous with him elsewhere.

 

Cautiously, you began to back away from the shelf where you had been crouching, careful to
not so much as breathe in case it alerted the two to your presence. Fortunately, they continued
to speak in hushed voices, unaware of your eavesdropping. Yet with every inch, every
heartbeat you prayed that you didn't somehow make a noise, that they didn't somehow sense
the eyes and ears tracking their conversation.

 



It was only once you were out of the storage unit that you managed to let your breath release
from your chest in a loud sigh of relief. You gave yourself all of a moment before quickly
walking away, out of the corridor and in the direction of the communications console you had
seen earlier near where the Razorcrest was docked.

 

It took every ounce of effort to not sprint towards it, keeping your gait easy and casual
despite your blood rushing in your ears, your heartbeat beating a frantic rhythm against your
ribcage. Yet your footfalls still seemed too quick, too heavy and purposeful to be disguised as
anything other than panic. You forced yourself to slow, to breathe easily, hard as it was. The
last thing you needed was to alert the other mechanics around you to your intentions, to any
sign that you had caught on to Ran's plan. You had only one chance at this, and you could not
afford to waste it.

 

Unfortunately for you, as you rounded the corner, you found that the communications table
was already occupied by none other than Ran himself. Though he had his back turned
towards you, you still couldn't help but suck in a sharp inhale and duck out of sight. Pressing
yourself flat against a nearby wall, you felt your face instantly fall into despair at your one
and only chance of contacting Din being snatched out from under you.

 

You could feel panic, cold and oppressive, begin to wash over you now, ensnaring your
senses into pure, unadulterated fear, incapable of thinking to think, to reason-

 

Gods, this was all your fault. If only you had been more careful, had told Din to steer clear of
this job, had kept a way to contact him on your person-

 

You blinked.

 

The comm device.

 

The one you had been working on just before the Imperial officer had forced her way onto
the Razorcrest.

 

The one in your pocket, shoved there as you were frantically packing your gear just before
landing at the outpost.



 

You patted your pocket, and sure enough, found the small shape of a handheld comm tucked
there against your hip.

 

You breathed, closing your eyes, and letting your head thunk on the wall behind you gently,
sending up a prayer of thanks to the stars above. Of all the things to randomly grab and stuff
in your pockets, it was the one thing you so desperately needed. If the Force did exist, then
truly it had decided to favor you in this moment, giving you the opportunity to save not only
yourself, but your tiny family as well.

 

"Thank the Force." You whispered to yourself, giving a small half-smile at the irony of it all.

 

Walking quickly away from the comms table now, you searched for a spot where you could
do the final repairs needed to fix the device, alone and secluded in a location where you could
contact Din without being overheard.

 

Decisively, you backtracked towards the storage closets, taking the first open door you could
find and shuffling your way as far back as possible so as to not be seen or heard behind the
crates and bins of various parts and supplies. Ducking down, you quickly retrieved the comm
device from your pocket, along with the soldering iron lent to you earlier by one of the
stations mechanics.

 

You tried to control your breathing as you worked, reminding yourself that you had done this
task a thousand times before, that you knew the repair even with your eyes closed. Yet it did
nothing to still the shaking in your hands, the tremble in your fingertips as you soldered the
remaining wires into place, gave the device the jumpstart it needed to flicker on with a small
green flicker of light.

 

Again, you sent a small thanks to the heavens above before trying to synchronize the device
with the pre-loaded communications ID-tag tied to the Razorcrest’s comms array. You
couldn't go as far as to contact Din directly without him having a comm as well, so you'd
have to hope and pray that somehow you managed to get through before everything went to
hell on the mission.

 



"Din." You breathed into the device, trying, and failing to contain the quiver in your voice. "I
don’t have time to explain. Din, it's a trap. They're going to try and kill you. You need to find
a way to leave them and get back here, it's too dangerous. Ran-" You swallowed, trying to
catch your breath despite the rush of words that poured past your lips. "Ran set you up. He's
going to steal the Razorcrest, and if you- if you don't come back he's going to try and turn me
in, to send me-"

 

If you hadn’t been so frantic, hadn’t been so entirely consumed by the task in front of you,
perhaps you would have noticed the soft footfalls that entered the storage unit. Maybe you
would have been able to stop yourself, play off your desperate attempt to warn your partner.
Yet you didn’t notice the presence of the person who came to rest beside you, not until their
voice cut through your thoughts like a deadly vibroblade.

 

"What are you doing?"

 

The remainder of your words cut off into nothingness, the air around you now abruptly still,
frozen by the sudden interruption. Eyes wide and unseeing, gazing down at the floor, you
began to process the voice that spoke to you, that had just heard-

 

Heart dropping down past your stomach, eyes impossibly wide, you slowly lifted your head
upwards towards the person who had just spoken, who had just heard you confess to Din the
entirety of Ran’s plan to ambush him, to take you captive. You could feel the blood in your
veins turn icy cold, washing you in a frigid, all-consuming shock as your gaze came to rest
on the person who had peered over the storage container you had tucked yourself behind.

 

Dash.

 

Yet not the Dash from earlier. Not the friendly, easygoing, genuine mechanic who had made
you smile with his lanky and awkward physique. No, the young man who stared down at you
now had his eyes trained on you like a mykal staring down on its prey. His entire form was
taut, rigid, but his eyes...

 

There was a fixated, almost demented intent there that made you shudder.

 



"You...weren't trying to contact the Mandalorian just now…were you?" He questioned, voice
deceptively innocent despite the almost crazed, unblinking stare he gazed down at you with.

 

Your voice wouldn't sound from your chest, every inch of your form frozen in fear at being
discovered. You didn't blink as you met Dash's eyes, unable to so much as breathe as your
thoughts rapidly tried to think of something, anything-

 

Except then Dash disappeared, darting from where he stood over you. The motion caught you
by surprise, expecting him more to lunge at you than to flee away from you. Yet that
moment's hesitation was all Dash needed as you heard him race for the storage unit door, and
you realized too late what his plan was.

 

"Dash, no-!" You yelled after him, launching forward as you tried to chase him towards the
exit. Yet it was too late, because the second you had him back in your sights again, Dash was
closing the door behind him, sending the storage closet into void-like darkness.

 

"NO!!”  You screamed, colliding with the door just as it shut, and banging your fists against
the steel surface. Your hand fumbled for the handle, but you couldn't find it before the tell-
tale clunk of the manual lock engaged, leaving you trapped and alone inside.

 

"Dash, NO!!" You shrieked, your voice bouncing off the metal door and into the darkness
around you. "Please! Let me go, Dash please!!"

 

Yet it was silence on the other side of the door, and even as you desperately tried to twist the
handle and yanked on the door you were met with no reply. It wasn't until a shattered,
wrecked sob of despair bubbled up your throat that Dash finally spoke from the other side.

 

"All you had to do was sit and be quiet."

 

You paused, breath coming in a series of ragged exhales that threatened to overwhelm you.
Yet you managed to swallow them down, tried to plead with him again-

 



"Dash, please!" You begged. "Let me out, we can find a way to-"

 

"-Work this out?" Dash finished for you, voice unflinchingly cold and detached. You jerked
away from the door for a brief moment, startled by the sudden change in the man you thought
was so friendly and sincere only minutes ago. "I don't think so, friend."

 

You couldn't speak, chest tight and too hot, tears threatening the corners of your eyes as a sob
formed in your throat. This couldn’t be happening, not right now, not when you were so
close-

 

"Look what you've done now." Dash continued. "You almost cost us this whole operation.
How did you even find out? Since when did you have a comm device?" You could hear him
sigh, the sound bitter and disappointed.

 

"Oh well. I'm sure it doesn't matter anyways since Ran blocked all outgoing transmissions."

 

The realization of what Dash had just said didn't process at first, so overwhelmed were your
thoughts of trying to escape, trying to find a way out, to contact Din, to-

 

"Wh-what did you just say?" You asked, voice cracking hoarsely, blinking in the darkness.

 

Dash let a bark of laughter from the other side of the door.

 

"You don't think he'd give you a way to contact the Mandalorian, would he? Didn't he tell you
he doesn't trust anyone? He blocked all transmissions the second they left. Your message
probably never reached him."

 

No. No, that couldn't be true. If...if that was true, then the message you had just sent to Din,
the one where you had begged him to come back, to find a way to come get you-

 

"You are never going to see him again."



 

Dash's voice was quiet, yet the words he spoke were sinister, sincere in their threat. That
same honest voice he had regarded you with earlier now spoke a truth that you couldn't
refute, a fact that now defined you in the dark emptiness where Din could not find you.

 

You stared unblinkingly in the darkness, trying to understand, still trying to find a way
beyond this, back to Din’s side where you belonged. Yet the reality of your circumstances
now made itself real to you. Din had walked into a trap, had left Grogu undefended on the
ship, had no way of knowing the ambush that awaited him; and you, you couldn’t warn him,
couldn’t reach him to recue him or provide aid. Instead, you were here, trapped with no way
out, surrounded by enemies who would hand you over to your darkest enemy without a
moment’s hesitation.

 

You had dreaded this nightmare for so long, and now in your waking reality, it began to
consume you.

 

Terror now began to manifest inside you, starting in your chest and creeping outward with icy
tendrils, intent on destroying every remaining ounce of hope that you so desperately clung to.
Even as you tried to refuse the idea, even as you tried with increasing panic to reassure
yourself otherwise, you couldn't deny Dash' words.

 

Your silence must have been the only response Dash needed, for you felt the door shift as he
pushed himself off of it, his muffled footsteps beginning to fade beyond your reach as he
tossed one lingering taunt over his shoulder:

 

"Just sit tight until Mayfeld and the others get back, okay? Be a good girl until then."

 

Then he was gone, leaving you alone in the pitch blackness of the storage room with nothing
but the indomitable terror that now threatened to eat you alive.

 

Din...Din was...

 



The darkness around you seemed to blot out every sound, ever sensation, every sense that
managed to filter past the horror that now roared inside you, screaming in a voice you didn't
recognize as your own. Hands trembling, limbs shaking, heartbeat racing, your legs crumpled
under you as strength faded from your limbs. You collapsed to your knees, hands still
flattened against the cool surface of the door that would not yield despite the futile pounding
of your fists.

 

"Dash!" You gasped, feeling panicked tears overflow from your eyes now, voice cracking in
your throat. "Dash, please!"

 

Yet the mechanic was far beyond your voice now, unable to hear your frantic cries as you
pleaded, begged to be released, to prevent your worst nightmare. To never see Din or Grogu
again, to be handed over to the Imperials for some unknown fate, to have no control over
your own pre-determined destiny, it...

 

It was all you could do not to shatter into a million fragments, as delicate and glittering as the
stars themselves.

 

"No-" You gasped again, trying somehow to contain yourself, to reason your way out of this.
Yet that part of you that could consider anything beyond the soul-gripping terror had faded
into oblivion, swallowed by the void of rising dread and despair that surrounded you just as
deeply as the pitch blackness encompassing you from all sides.

 

A ragged sob tore from your throat, and your fists curled against the door in anguish. You
couldn't reach Din, couldn't warn him, couldn't hold him and Grogu one last time...

 

The memory of his lingering glance, of your eyes meeting across the hangar in a silent
farewell, a promise to see each other soon now felt like an unbearable tragedy, a broken
promise.

 

"Din!" You cried, voice rising as you looked up in the darkness, tears spilling freely down
your cheeks and a wrecked sob escaping you. Silently, you begged the stars for one last
chance, one last opportunity to tell him how much he meant to you, to hold his hand, to have
him bend his helmet down to your forehead, to tell him how much you loved him.

 



Again, you banged your fist against the metal door, hard enough to feel a bruise form at the
impact. You did it once more, feeling something wet and warm blossom against your skin.
Yet the pain that came with was nothing compared to the ache, the grief inside you of losing
everything, of being stripped of all you had come to cherish so deeply.

 

This couldn't be the end. It couldn't. To leave Din like this, to have him leave you, to be
separated by space and time despite all the things you had survived together, all the trials and
tribulations you had conquered, it was too much. You couldn't stand it. Just when you had
finally found a family, found someplace to belong, it was now being stolen from you, and
there was nothing you could do to stop it.

 

"You will never see him again."

 

You sobbed, the sound broken and devastated. It floated up beyond the ceiling, somewhere
out into space along with your prayer that somehow you would find a way out of this, that
you could still…still see him just one last time.

 

Yet the heavens didn’t answer you, and the silent void of space offered no respite from the
tragedy, the horror of your own fate.

 

All at once, the fear, the despair, the anger and anguish of it all began to roil inside you,
simmering low like a dormant volcano. Yet with each passing moment that horrifying
scorching sensation began to climb higher and higher in your chest, burning hot and painful
with your grief. You tried to let it escape as a cry, but it remained stuck inside your ribcage,
straining against your heart and engulfing you in a sudden, unrelenting blaze of heat.

 

You screamed, hearing your voice echo in the darkness in a never-ending reverberation as if
shaking the foundation of the outpost itself. Yet that horrible, twisted realization that Din
might be dead, that Grogu had been taken, that you would be taken where they would never
find you only continued to build inside you, ceaseless and inescapable.

 

The pressure of it seemed to weigh against your bones, pull taut against your flesh and spasm
your muscles. You bent your head against it all, screaming now in the pain, the weight, the
unbearable force of your emotions swelling up against you.

 



It was too much, it felt as if you would split at the seams and much like a shooting star, would
combust into a final, dazzling spark before dying out.

 

The flames, the scorching horrible inferno from your nightmares now seemed to fuse with
reality, and now you could hear the screams, the blaster fire, smell the smoke from the
ancient tapestries consumed by the untamable blaze that burnt the temple from the inside out.
You could hear the cry of your own name, feel the splintering of glass before gravity took
you as you fell into nothingness-

 

And, distantly, you felt that same reflection of yourself from Coruscant, from your dreams,
from your nightmares reach out to you, washing over you with grace and serenity, offering
you a respite from the fear, the anger, the despair. Gently, she reached out, laying your palms
flat against the door before you, breathing a new strength into your bones. In a wordless
whisper, she seemed to speak to you in a voice you didn't understand, summoning that secret,
hidden part of you that you had kept secret since that fateful day.

 

And then, all at once, you felt something inside you shatter.

 

With a scream, you pressed your hands against the door before you, felt that enigmatic
gravity extend past your fingertips, flow into the metal and begin to bend it to your will. The
metal began to creak and groan under the pressure, resistance failing as your hands, as
something within you managed to inflict an unseen force upon it, crumple it inch by inch.
The hinges and lock whined, trying and failing to keep the door upright as the power within
you surged with every passing moment, building into an unstoppable cataclysm. You could
feel it roar to life, awakened from its long slumber and fueled by the despair, the desperation,
the need and intrinsic instinct to survive.

 

The door under your touch gave way with a final, ear-piercing creak, exploding and flying
away from your hands with a rush of wind, a sudden surrender that shook the ground under
you like an implosion of the outpost itself. Instantly, light streamed into the pitch-black
storage closet, forcing you to open your eyes and blink against the brightness. For a moment,
the world around you seemed to shake, felt as if it would rip apart from the force you had just
inflicted. Yet as your eyes adjusted it began to still, and the strange, feather light sensation in
your hands lifted up and away, leaving you breathless and braced against the floor in an effort
to regain yourself.

 



The world around you spun, suddenly dizzying and too bright, too overwhelming. Shaking,
you managed to lift yourself up despite gasping desperately for air, despite the tremor in your
shoulders as you threw your head back and forced yourself to breathe.

 

Inhales coming in uneven, ragged gasps of air you blinked, allowing your vision to adjust to
the sudden brightness beyond the pitch-black storage closet. You looked forward, to where
the door was. Yet you found it thrown more than a hundred feet in front of you, twisted and
mangled, destroyed as it lay against a now dented panel, far across the now eerily quiet
hangar.

 

You stared after the door, open mouthed and eyes wide, trying to understand exactly how it
had been sent flying such a great distance after you had merely put your hands against it,
leaned against it-

 

You felt a dozen pairs of eyes on you.

 

Blinking, you turned to look at the collection of mechanics, engineers, and deckhands that
now had their gazes locked on you, transfixed by what they had just witnessed. Terror,
confusion, anger, fear, all seemed to mirror your own emotions, staring back at you in a
mixture of awe and horror.

 

Your legs shook under you as you swayed to a stand, holding onto one of your now sore
arms, whiplashed by the terrifying ability you had just displayed. You took a single step
outside of the storage unit, staggering as your limbs trembled, your head pounded, and your
thoughts ceaselessly whispered in words familiar yet indecipherable.

 

"You..."

 

Turning, your eyes caught the form of Dash, having fallen backwards and away from you yet
still staring with a wide, horrified gaze at your figure.

 

"You- you're one of them." He choked out, voice cracking. "A- a Jedi!"

 



You flinched, nearly taking a step backwards at the forbidden title, the same curse that
Imperial officer had laid against your skin.

 

A Jedi.

 

A warrior, a member of a desecrated order, one that had been hunted to extinction, accused of
crimes they didn't commit. To be a Jedi was to be gifted powers from the stars themselves, to
use the enigmatic and forbidden power known only as the Force.

 

You looked at your trembling hands, fingers spread, and palms open as if they could provide
a clue, answers to the thousand plaguing questions that now rose within you. Yet the question
of how you had managed to escape, how you had rendered the door irreparably damaged,
how you had sent it flying across the hangar with nothing but your touch alone, that could
only be answered by one thing:

 

The Force.

 

A furious yell shook you from your reverie, forcing you back to the present with a dozen eyes
on you, and now a stout figure barreling towards your form, yelling obscenities about the
sudden explosion you had caused.

 

Ran.

 

"Stay back!" You screamed, instinctively grabbing your blaster from your holster, and
pointing it at the man. Ran slowly came to a halt a distance away from you, holding up his
hands placatingly as you leveled the weapon at him.

 

"Easy now." He spoke, keeping his voice even under that false pretense of friendliness even
now. "Put the blaster down, sweetheart."

 

You swallowed, feeling the remnant of your sobs choke your throat. The blaster shook in
your grip, but you managed to keep it level, point it directly at Ran's chest.



 

Motion caught your attention as Dash suddenly scrambled to a stand, withdrawing his own
blaster. Your aim swerved towards him, now torn between two targets as you desperately
tried to keep your eyes on both.

 

“D-don’t move!” You yelled again, voice wavering.

 

"Sh-she's one of them!!" Dash yelled, voice cutting off yours and echoing up against the
domed hangar ceiling. "She's one of those traitors!"

 

Ran side-eyed the young mechanic off to his side, giving him a mere second's glance before
letting his eyes return to you. You could see the thoughts process behind his gaze as he began
to understand the situation. It took him a moment, but then you saw a flash of realization in
his eyes, as if he suddenly understood what precisely had transpired, could see the truth you
so desperately tried to conceal. Yet of all the questions he could have asked next, questioning
you on your origins, your survival, your abilities, he instead asked the one thing you so
desperately feared:

 

"Does the Mandalorian know?"

 

You stiffened, thumb shaking against the safety of your blaster, chest heaving. You didn't
answer, too terrified to so much as move, but the fear in your eyes must have been all that
Ran required as an answer, for his eyes glinted in recognition.

 

Din- he didn’t know. How could he when you had been so uncertain of it until just moments
ago? You had promised to tell him, had given him your oath that you would confide in him
the bitter truth once he got back, once you two were reunited.

 

Ran took a single step forward, shifting as if he were about to speak. Yet before he could, you
finally found your voice, settling your feet further apart into a proper stance and trying your
best to stare the ex-mercenary down past the end of your blaster.

 



"You- you planned this from the start." Your voice still trembled, but the more you spoke the
surer you became, words low and dangerous with righteous anger. "To kill Mando, to take the
Razorcrest, to turn me in- and for what?"

 

Ran wasn't smiling anymore, instead returning your furious words with a cold, hard gaze. As
he spoke, you suppressed a shiver at the frigid, calculating rumble of his words, unflinching
in their honesty.

 

"For revenge." He answered simply, voice low and unyielding. “Mando screwed us over, left
one of our own to die and then left the rest of us to deal with the consequences. He deserves
what’s coming to him.”

 

You forced yourself to breathe past your fury, to not argue over Din’s honor and get
distracted. It wouldn’t serve you, not right now with your life on the line. Instead, you
shifted, adjusting the grip on your blaster as you again directed your voice at Ran.

 

“And me?”

 

"You were just an afterthought.” Ran offered coolly, nonchalantly. “I was hoping Mando
would come alone. Lucky for you, you had a bounty, otherwise I would have dropped you
were you stood once the Razorcrest lifted off."

 

A shuddering inhale caught within your chest, terrified at the possibility of being killed, of
dying beyond Din’s reach without him even knowing. Yet the sights on your blaster didn't
waver, still aimed perfectly at the center of Ran's body.

 

"That may have been the best outcome for you, if you think about it."

 

You blinked, distracted for a moment by Ran's words.

 

"W-what do you mean?" You questioned, trying not to be swayed by his sudden interjection.
Yet the idea that somehow, you were better off without Din, were better off dying made no



sense-

 

You swore you saw the ghost of a smile play against the corner of Ran's mouth, as if smug
that he had caught your attention.

 

"To be caught by the Empire is probably worse than dying." He supplied, voice lilting now in
that false friendliness that seemed vicious despite his tone. "-but that's probably not as bad as
staying with Mando if he finds out."

 

The tremble in your hands stopped, every inch of you frozen as you tried to process what Ran
was suggesting. You stared at him, eyes bright in confusion and dread as a sadistic smile
crept across Ran's lips, realizing he now had you right where he wanted you.

 

"After all..." He went on, voice almost gleeful with the devastation his next words would
bring.

 

"Mandalorians hunt Jedi."

Chapter 44: Part Forty Four: Leap
Chapter Summary

"H-he wouldn't." You tried, but your voice was again cut off by the ex-mercenary.

"You sure about that?" Ran asked, voice ringing out across the space between you.
"After all, you're his enemy."

"No-" You tried again, but your voice didn't hold the conviction you thought it did.
Instead, it was a desperate plea, a forced defense that you yourself didn't entirely believe
in.

Yet Ran's eyes seemed to stare into you, flaying you open for a dozen stares to see,
rendering your entreaties useless against him.

Then, recognition flashed across his features, and his voice dipped low, making your
entire form shudder at his next words.

"He doesn't know, does he?"

You froze, the shake in your arms and legs turning into an icy paralysis and rendering
your entire form taut, petrified.

No- He couldn’t-

"Shall we tell him?"

The trigger under your finger felt warm to the touch.

Chapter Notes

TW for:

Fire-related injury and death

Depictions of violence

(Unnamed) Character death

Threats of violence

Explosions

See the end of the chapter for more notes



 

 

 

 

Din's hands were still shaking, skin still itching and muscles heavy from the fight he had just
endured aboard the New Republic transport ship. He could feel freshly formed bruises
beginning to form along his flesh, trailing in an inconsistent pattern across his ribs and arms,
left there by his opponents. Adrenaline still coursed through his veins, thick and heady,
narrowing the entire world down to the tunnel vision that only seemed to show the flickering
blue light of hyperspace before him.

 

It had been an ambush. He had been so stupid-

 

He should have noticed the moment he boarded the New Republic transport- no, the second
he had turned away from you in the outpost hangar, your concerned expression haunting him
even now. Your form had stood alone in the middle of the bustling hangar, posture betraying
your anxiety. You had tried to tell him, had tried to warn him, but he had only tried to
convince you in turn.

 

He should have turned then, should have gone back to you, taken you away from there. He
should have held you away from the eyes that watched you both, immersed himself in the
simple comfort that was you.

 

Yet he didn't. Instead, he had gone forwards with the intent of proving himself, of providing
the credits and resources needed to keep you all safe, oblivious to the fact that danger stood
in his shadow. After all, he had sworn to keep you and the child hidden, protected from the
reach of bounty hunters and Imperials alike. To do so meant to face danger, to throw himself
into the thick of conflict if it meant protecting you both, to see you smile without the fear of
whatever cruel fate awaited you.

 

Yet now…

 



It hadn't been enough that Mayfeld and the others had tried to take his helmet, to show his
face,
to renounce his creed by force and make him Dar ‘Manda. No, as if that wasn’t enough,
they had threatened the kid as well, and had spoken of taking him away from Din as if
denying him some type of simple pleasure and not the right
he had to safeguard the child.

 

He should have killed them then, dumped their bodies into space, should have aborted the
mission and returned to you, creed be damned.

 

Yet he had walked into the attack blindly, distracted by the mere thought of your lonely figure
standing alone in the hangar, and of the child hidden aboard the ship.

 

Din could still remember the fear, the rage
when he had been knocked inside the holding cell,
had been left behind by the others with only the knowledge that Grogu, that you
were both in
terrible danger. If Ran had ordered Mayfeld and the others to do this much to him, he didn't
want to imagine
the fate that awaited you back at the outpost.

 

You could already be gone.

 

The following minutes after his escape from the cell had been a blur, obscured by a lethal
combination of instinct and barely restrained fury at Ran and the others for trying their best to
kill him, to take you both away from him. Hunter’s instinct, bred deep into his bones by his
training, had taken hold and blotted out any thought other than whatever violence was needed
to ensure he was again able to hold you safe in his arms once more.

 

Din had barely contained himself from killing the others, operating on nothing less than his
Mandalorian training and experience as a mercenary, driven by the need and desire to see
you, to make sure you and the kid were safe. Yet his patience had worn thin by the time he
had dealt with both Burg and Xi'an, and his focus had narrowed down to the fearful, paranoid
figure of the former Imperial sharpshooter, vainly trying to find him in the strobing light of
the corridor.

 

Mayfeld's eyes had betrayed his true terror when Din had attacked him from behind, held his
vibro-blade to his throat and demanded to know what Ran had planned for you. Din had felt
the sharpshooter’s throat bob against the blade, eyes wild and lips parted in a stifled plea. His
gaze had flickered in the light, the same flash that cast itself ruefully across Din's visor,
promising nothing except utter violence if Mayfeld failed to comply.



 

Mayfeld had only confirmed what Din had feared: Ran had planned this from the start, had
seen the opportunity to lure Din in and not only exact his revenge, but steal two precious
bounties away from him. With Din captured it would be easy to overwhelm you and to take
the child.

 

It wasn't until Din had pressed a razor-thin line of red into Mayfeld's throat that the
sharpshooter had told him about the all-clear signal Ran was waiting on from the Razorcrest
,
letting him know Din had been dealt with and allowing him the opportunity to catch you by
surprise.

 

Mayfeld's vision had gone dark after that, courtesy of a blow to the head from Din. By now
he was likely awakening to the inside of the same cell he had tried to trap Din in, along with
Xi'an and Burg. Quinn sat below in the Razorcrest’s hold, restrained and quiet, staring at the
fallen chassis of the droid that had aimed its blaster at the child.

 

The kid sat with Din in the cockpit, whining low soft sounds of concern, as if noticing his
caretaker's anxiety. Yet he refrained from his usual antics, as if sensing the urgency with
which Din forced the Razorcrest
to hurtle through hyperspace. With each passing heartbeat
Din could only hope that he wasn't too late, that you hadn't already been ambushed yourself,
subdued and taken somewhere far away from him.

 

It was the horror of Coruscant all over again, the idea that you would be stolen far away from
him, delivered into the hands of the enemy, that Din might never see you again.

 

Yet this time- this time it was his
fault.

 

He hadn't listened, hadn't heeded your anxiety, had forced you to stay behind as if that would
somehow protect
you.

 

The guilt gnawing inside his stomach was repressed only by the merge of anger and fear that
fed the adrenaline in his veins.

 



He had promised you he would keep you safe, and had been so afraid you would leave when
he had failed. Now, in the face of yet another failure, Din felt a part of him threaten to crack
open, spilling out his worst fears and anxieties like blood seeping into soil.

 

He had given you his word...

 

Now he had broken that oath, had tarnished that creed not once, but twice. This time his
failure seemed to open a void under his feet, swallowing down any hope that you would be
safe, unharmed, that he would somehow still be worthy
of you.

 

Yet beyond that, somewhere hidden inside, lay the fear that Din would never get to hear that
secret you were holding so close to you, the same one that seemed to terrify you and draw
your gaze somewhere far away, somewhere Din could not see.

 

Din had seen you scared before, had seen the way terror flashed across your eyes when he
had originally found you on the Razorcrest, when you had bent over him after he had been hit
by the pulse rifle on Rishi, hair falling into your face and eyes stricken. He had seen you
terrified before, and each instance, each memory brought forth a stab of phantom pain in his
stomach.

 

Yet the fear, the horror he had seen in your eyes after being confronted by the Imperial
officer, when he had asked you about the things you were holding from him-

 

Din never wanted to see you make that face ever again.

 

The fact that whatever you were holding on to was so deeply disturbing that it shook you
of
all people to your very core made Din himself shift in a deep-seated anxiety. You, who had
survived everything life had thrown at you, had faced down Mandalorians, mercenaries, and
bounty hunters alike, you... a survivor...

 

Now the possibility that he would never know, that he would never understand or be able to
comfort you, to hold you once again, brought forth such a fear and fury inside Din that he had
never experienced in his life.



 

You could already be gone.

 

Din could still feel the last moment you had spent beside him, when he had steadied you
despite the shake, the tremble in your bones after he had asked after what you had been
concealing. He could still remember that, despite your usual steadfastness, for a moment Din
feared you would crumple into him, would let everything pour past your lips like an
inescapable tide of truth.

 

Yet at the last moment you had rallied, had again held yourself together and offered him of all
things a smile
, to reassure his own anxieties despite yours mounting within you.

 

Now, it took everything in Din not to rip his helmet off in front of the child, to run a hand
over his face and sigh loudly into his palm with something that felt dangerously close to
panic.

 

Cuyan.

 

All too soon, and yet not soon enough the Razorcrest’s
system beeped a warning at the
Mandalorian, warning him of the imminent exit from hyperspace.

 

Beside him the child again whined, and abruptly Din felt a small tug on his sleeve. A glance
to the side showed that the kid was clinging onto his arm, his large brown gaze open and
concerned, ears drooping low.

 

"Hang tight." Din spoke, wincing at the sound of his own voice, stifled and hoarse in his
throat. "We'll get her back."

 

As if to emphasize his words, the Razorcrest
exited hyperspace with a lurch, and the outline
of the outpost became clear in the window of the ship.

 



Din took a deep breath to steady himself, let it settle in his bones, and then opened a one-way
channel to Ran's communication console.

 

"Ran." Din spoke, mustering every ounce of righteous fury and anger into his voice, growling
out the man's name in a low, dangerous warning. "I'm only going to play this message
once..."

 

----

 

"Mandalorians hunt
Jedi."

 

You stared at Ran, gaze wide and unseeing at his words.

 

Desperately, your mind tried to understand what he had just spoken, tried to process it
alongside the terrifying display of power you had just shown. Yet your thoughts were
devastatingly empty, sucked into silence following the shock, the overwhelming confusion at
everything that had occurred only moments ago.

 

Din, possibly dead. Grogu, in danger of being stolen from you. You, trapped and surrounded
by enemies, with no way out, no possibility of escape.

 

And you, you in possession of a power that you had dreaded to even exist.

 

A dozen eyes watched you and Ran face off against each other, and with a subtle shift of your

your form. No doubt they were terrified at what had just occurred, cautious and apprehensive

The shattered door, the one you had sent flying with nothing but your touch and mind alone.

 



Stars above, she had been right
.

 

"You...really don't know...do you?"

 

Now you understood, and the unbearable weight of the truth threatened to tear you apart like
a crushing, obliterating black hole.

 

Jedi.

 

You couldn't breathe.

 

The air seemed to be trapped inside your chest alongside your stuttering, asynchronous
heartbeat, stammering drastically out of rhythm and threatening to make your legs fall out
from under you.

 

Ran stared at you, gaze unflinching.

 

Yet you couldn't speak, couldn't summon the words needed to refute his claim. The truth of
your identity, the dawning realization of the origin of all those nightmares, the years beyond
the scope of your memory simmered low inside you, threatening to once again loose that
terrifying, unharnessed ability once more.

 

Orphan,

 

Mechanic,

 

Stowaway,

 

Traitor,



 

Jedi.

 

Survivor.

 

Cuyan.

 

"You're a liar." You croaked at last, voice cracking in your throat, hands shaking on the grip
of your blaster. It was all you could do to remain standing, staring down Ran's unblinking
stare over the sights of your weapon. Yet your voice trembled with your words, distraught
and confused, unable to understand, much less deny Ran’s statement. "Di-...Mando would
never hurt me."

 

The corner of Ran's mouth twitched for just a moment, long enough for your eyes to trace
over the smirk before it vanished.

 

"Maybe not." Ran spoke, and his voice was quieter now, but no less self-assured. "Maybe he
won't kill you or leave you for dead." He paused, and you saw him teeth his bottom lip in

tight, unable to suck in the air you needed.

 

"Maybe he'll just leave you behind or drop you off somewhere and leave you there." Ran
went on, and you couldn't help the stab of fury, of hurt
at how casual his words were, as if he
wasn't preying on your worst fear, of Din being taken away from you.

 

The image of the thing you had previously longed so hard for, of being dropped off at some
core planet, safe and protected by the reach of the New Republic, now seemed to haunt you.
All your days prior to meeting him you had dreamed of the safety and quiet of a simpler life,
free of gang wars and debts, settling down and perhaps living your life in peace. Yet now the
thought of living such a life without Din and the child brought forth a profound sadness
within you, cracking something fragile within you like the sound of something broken.

 



To think that Din might go as far as to abandon you there, to leave you behind despite all
your journeys together for the crime of your own identity…

 

It threatened to buckle you under the weight of your own soul, torn in half at the thought of
such betrayal.

 

Any comfort that you would normally find in the memory of Din's unwavering, grounding
presence seemed to only open up that dark well inside you further, swallowing the last bit of
hope that flickered dimly against the shadow of confusion and doubt that now towered
menacingly over your thoughts.

 

"H-he wouldn't." You tried, but your voice was again cut off by the ex-mercenary.

 

"You sure about that?" He asked, voice ringing out across the space between you. "After all,
you're his enemy."

 

"No-" You tried again, but your voice didn't hold the conviction you thought it did. Instead, it
was a desperate plea, a forced defense that you yourself didn't entirely believe in.

 

Yet Ran's eyes seemed to stare into you, flaying you open for a dozen stares to see, rendering
your entreaties useless against him.

 

Then, recognition flashed across his features, and his voice dipped low, making your entire
form shudder at his next words.

 

"He doesn't know, does he?"

 

You froze, the shake in your arms and legs turning into an icy paralysis and rendering your
entire form taut, petrified.

 

No- He couldn’t-



 

"Shall we tell him?"

 

The trigger under your finger felt warm to the touch.

 

You stared at Ran, eyes wide and unblinking, shivering where you stood. Ran's eyes were
locked onto yours, gaze unflinching and keen. Around you the mechanics and other
mercenaries seemed to be closing ranks, their shapes subtly shifting and rippling in the corner
of your eyes, their stares locked on your form and weapons drawn. Yet you kept your focus
locked on Ran, on the sharp and dangerous threat behind his gaze.

 

He would tell Din.

 

And Din...Din might...

 

Slowly, your finger pressed down on the trigger.

 

Yet it was the crackle and urgent beep of the comms board that made everyone in the hangar
jump, and for a moment you gasped, thinking the sound had been your blaster firing. Yet the

Ran shifted slightly, glancing out of the corner of his eyes at the source of the sound. Yet he
refused to take his eyes off of you and your weapon. Instead, he simply nodded to Dash
beside him, who pocketed his own blaster and trotted off in the direction of the

"Ran." He spoke only a moment later, voice quieter, urgent. "It's...the Razorcrest."

 

Despite yourself, your eyes shot over towards the mechanic, leaving Ran and allowing
surprise to get the upper hand on you. Ran kept his focus square on you, even as your blaster



tipped slightly downwards in your distraction. So caught were you in your shock that you
didn't notice him nod to someone behind you, didn't hear them begin to inch closer to your
form.

 

The only thought you could possibly think in that moment was: "Din."

 

"Play it." Ran barked at Dash, and after a moment's worth of static, you could hear your
Mandalorian's voice filter through true and clear.

 

"Ran."

 

You felt your heart jump to your throat, eyes flashing and lips parting in recognition of Din's
voice, tenored deep and dangerous, in that tone you recognized only as fury
.

 

"I'm only going to play this message once." Din spoke, voice bordering on a rumbling growl.
"You are going to let me land, you are going to hand over my partner, and you are going to
let us leave unharmed."

 

You couldn't help but let a smile ghost over your features in relief, imagining Din bent over
the controls, barely able to contain his anger but still rushing to your rescue.

 

Yet then Din's voice darkened even further, his words low and menacing.

 

"For every minute you do not comply, I will remove one of Quinn's fingers. In ten minutes, I
will remove his hands. In fifteen minutes, I will kill him, and then I will open fire on this
station."

 

A murmur ran through the crowd around you, whispers of shock and curiosity rippling like
running water at Din’s very sincere threat. They, as you did, likely did not doubt for a

now drew into a grimace as he continued to stare at you despite Din’s words ringing out

"I'm already counting."

 

With that, the transmission shut off, leaving you and the rest of the hangar in silence.

 

You could see Ran chew his lip in thought, could see him consider your figure before him
and the transmission he had just heard. In his gaze you could see him begin to weigh his
options, could see him try and plot his response as pilots charted their course through the
stars.

 

You saw the moment that realization flashed across his eyes, could see the wicked smile
creep onto his lips as he turned towards Dash and spoke:

 

"Ask him if he knows his partner is a Je-"

 

You fired.

 

The sound managed to pierce straight through Ran's voice, cutting him off with a choke and
thundering across the hangar in a deafening reverberation. The jerk on your blaster in your

There was a split second where you saw the profile on Ran's face, saw his eyes widen in
shock, saw his body lurch gruesomely before he stumbled. You saw him begin to turn

before his legs caved under him and brought his body into a free fall.

 

Ran's body hit the ground, and the heartbeat of dreaded silence that followed gave way into
unbridled chaos.

 



You ducked on instinct, just as a blaster fired right behind you and a red flash passed where
your head had been less than a second prior. Wildly, you kicked out a leg behind you, feeling
it connect with something solid and the person who had been a mere step behind you lost
their balance. You twisted, catching the mercenary's surprised expression in your gaze a
moment before you squeezed off another round directly at him.

 

Everyone around you was yelling now, caught in surprise and shock at the death of their
leader. You could see multiple forms quickly advance upon you, each with as much deadly
intent as the last. You raised your blaster towards the first but were stopped when someone
else's blaster fired in your direction. You, along with everyone else in the hangar, ducked at
the sound, and now you could see several hangar-hands and engineers scattering at the
blaster-fire, trying to find safety within the scattered remains of starfighters.

 

You dove out of the way of the first person who tried to wrest you to the ground, your body
colliding harshly with the durasteel floor and leaving a bruised imprint along your elbows.
Beyond you, someone yelled to get the weapons systems online just as another mercenary
loomed over you, hands outstretched.

 

With a terrified scream, you kicked wildly upwards, knocking the person's hand aside but
managing to get your foot caught by their other hand. For a moment you felt your body
hauled sideways, nearly upside down as the mercenary tried to subdue you. In desperation,
you fired your blaster again, letting the shot go wild but startling the person enough to let
your foot go. You yanked it free, knocking them across the hip in the process and sending
them stumbling backwards.

 

You managed to get to your feet, but not before someone else managed to attack you from
behind, wrapping their arms around your torso and pinning your arms to your sides.

 

You screamed in a mixture of surprise and anger, twisting, and thrashing in an attempt to free
yourself of their hold. Yet whoever it was only managed to squeeze you tighter, force the air
from your chest in a desperate yell of shock.

 

That awareness, the one you had always had, the one that had saved your life far too many
times now, whispered urgently to you once more. You felt your gaze drawn to a nearby
container, felt recognition at the label in Aurebesh flash across your thoughts.

 



Coaxium

 

You arched your back, holding tight to your blaster and managing to lift it in the direction of
the canister. Struggling, you yelled as you used all your strength to lift your arm against the
person's hold, pointing in the direction of the fuel and sending a prayer for your aim to be
true.

 

The sound of your blaster was drowned out by the sudden and explosive ignition of the
canister, erupting with enough force to knock you and the others around you to the ground.

 

You were on your feet first, shaking off the hand that fumbled for your ankle as you launched
yourself towards the entrance of the hangar, towards safety.

 

Around you, the hangar had dissolved into true anarchy, with many engineers flocking

from the still erupting blaster fire that rained down in your direction. Yet a split second after

You ducked behind a steel beam as a blaster bolt whizzed past you, landing on a scrapped
fighter off to your left.

 

All the while, your breath came in rapid, harsh intakes of air, eyes wild and darting, searching
for a place to hide, to escape. You saw one mechanic rush past you, ignorant of your form

catch him in the chest, and he let out a cry as he fell onto his back at your feet.

 

He stared up at you for a moment, eyes wide and confused, before they became glassy and
distant and he let out a desperate, final groan.

 

You stared down at his fallen form, horrified, before having to duck again at a blaster bolt
pinging off the steel beam behind you.



 

You had to get out of here.

 

You could try and run for the escape pods, but it seemed that the idea seemed to be a popular
consensus among the mechanics, who were increasingly abandoning the futile effort of
containing the now spreading fire you had caused. Even if there were any escape pods left by
the time you got there, you'd have to fight off not only the other mercenaries, but the
desperately fleeing mechanics and engineers as well.

 

That only left one option.

 

Fumbling for the repaired comm you had used earlier, you lifted it to your lips and spoke a
desperate plea.

 

"Din!"

 

For a moment, your heart felt suspended aloft, able to drop at any second should the
transmission not go through or Din not able to receive your call.

 

Yet then there was a crackle of static before Din's blessed voice responded to yours.

 

"Cuyan?!"

 

You nearly sobbed with relief, clutching the comm in both hands and whispering a prayer of
thanks to the stars above.

 

"Cuyan! Cuyan, are you there? Where are you?"

 

"I'm here." You croaked into the comm. "I'm here, on the station. Ran is-"



 

"I can see flames, what is happening? Are you hurt?"

 

You swallowed, feeling your throat clench around a bubbling sob. Yet you managed to raise
your voice enough to be heard over the utter discord around you.

 

"I-I'm unhurt. The station is burning, and I can't get to the escape pods. I-I need you to come
around to the hangar. Don't land- it's too dangerous."

 

"Don't land?"
You could hear the confusion, the fear, and the anger in Din's voice now, and
could feel his desperation let loose on you. "How are you going to get off the outpost!?"

 

You smiled then, you couldn't help it.

 

"I'm going to jump."

 

"You- WHAT?!"

 

"Promise you'll be there to catch me, Din." You spoke into the comm, voice tender and
hopeful despite the tremble of fear there. "I'll see you soon."

 

"Cuy-"
Din tried, but you shut off the comm and pocketed it.

 

You took a breath to settle yourself, closing your eyes for a moment letting the artificial
oxygen settle in your bones as your shoulders trembled. Your heart fluttered wildly inside

Yet you managed to stifle it, knowing that at this moment a single breath of hesitation could
mean the difference between safety- of your tiny clan and of Din’s arms wrapped around you

Stars above, protect me
. You prayed, lips falling open with the silent plea upwards to the
heavens.

 

The sudden lurch of the outpost made you nearly sprawl across the floor of the hangar,

In your mind’s eye, you again felt as if another scene now played before you, familiar and yet

Yet you had no time to entertain it, not with the alarms on the station now blaring loud
enough to deafen you and the growing fire beginning to stretch outwards with bright,

Summoning both your courage and your strength, you managed to rise and look towards the

Another explosion rocked the floor beneath you, followed by an agonized scream of another

With the flames growing hot at your back now, you began to race towards the opening of the

You jumped over a coiled wire, feet clearing it by mere inches as it began to hiss and spark

station was falling apart at the seams now, set adrift by the huge, bright blaze at its center, the
one created by your hand like some creature of anarchy.

 

Your feet pounded the metal floor under you, each step seeming slower than your own racing
heartbeat. Yet with each footfall you felt as if the fire was reaching out towards you from
behind, extending a blazing grasp towards your back in an attempt to drag you backwards
into it- into your own hellish nightmares.

 

A low whine began to sound above the fire, distant but louder with each passing moment,
turning from a low hum into a trumpeting vibration that you had long since engraved in the

The Razorcrest
.

 

The ship appeared all at once, passing once by the mouth of the hangar in a flash, its silver
coating reflecting the ominous glow of the raging maelstrom that outlined your form in

You clambered over a fallen panel, wincing at the scorch the heated metal left on your palm.

closer towards you with every precious heartbeat.

 

Din managed to ease the back ramp into the hold of the hangar, even with the fire threatening
other crafts and making the whole station list dangerously off to one side.

 

Yet even so, the ramp began to descend after a moment, not fully extending and merely
opening far enough for a figure to appear at the top.

 

Din.

 



You felt the air in your chest, held tight and hot against your ribcage, whoosh out of you at

yellow flames further into the hangar, his visor catching the light in a way that made him

In one hand he held his rifle, prepared and at the ready to shoot down any and all who would
deign to chase fruitlessly after you. Yet in the other he held the arm of someone you had

You didn't have any time to question who the man was, for Din shoved him forward with
enough force to make him stumble and roll off the partially extended ramp. The Twi-Lek's
body hit the hangar floor with a thump
hardly audible above the roar of the Razorcrest's
engines and the inferno drawing ever closer with each passing moment. The bounty, you
assumed, raised himself to his feet and looked up at Din pleadingly for a moment, only to get
a jerk of Din's head in return. Din nodded to a nearby, somewhat intact craft that was still

"Din!"

 

The Mandalorian's visor snapped towards the sound of your voice, rifle hauled into his hands
as he prepared to intercept any pursuers. Yet finding none, he shouldered the rifle and stepped
forward to the very edge of the ramp.

 

"Cuyan!!" Din roared, his voice able to be heard despite the deafening discord all around you.

 

"Din!!" You screamed again, the last of your air spent letting loose his name at the top of

Under your feet the station shuddered, let out a horrific groan and began to tilt violently. For

knees. To your horror, the outpost began to shift backwards, the floor rising under you and

"Jump!" Din's voice yelled from above you, muffled now by the catastrophic groaning and
grinding of the outpost now in its death throes.

 

As you watched, he spread his arms wide, feet planted and ready to catch your form the
moment you launched upwards towards him.

 

You took one last deep breath, steeling yourself despite the tremor in your hands, the shiver

You jumped.

 

As you did, it felt as if your body suddenly became lighter than air, floating farther upwards
than you had intended, as if you were ascending towards the stars themselves. For a moment

careening speeder onto a desperate gamble for safety. Yet even then, you felt the memory
extend further back, to a moment far before this journey had truly begun.

 

Suspended on all sides, the rush of stifling, hot air and flames and destruction around you,

night, atop a tower overlooking a sprawling ecumenopolis, you had been thrown, pushed out
into the hot night air as someone had screamed your name in one, final, desperate plea. Held
aloft for just a moment, clothes flapping in the wind, you stayed there for a single heartbeat
before falling downwards into something unknown, a darkness within your mind you
couldn’t recall, with naught but your own name trailing after you.

 

Now, a different voice called you by a different name, one you knew all the same. The one
who had bestowed upon you that title, survivor, now stretched forward, arms spread wide
towards you as you descended like a shooting star from the galaxy above, arching like an
arrow of light straight into his embrace.

 

Din's arms fastened around you tightly, enough to squeeze the breath from your body as your
arms wrapped tightly around his armored form. Your breath released in a shuddering sigh
against his neck, face buried there as you once more held onto your beloved protector,
partner, your Mandalorian.



 

Yet as much as you wanted to take the moment to immerse yourself within him, there was no
time. Not as the station creaked, groaned, and began to list away from the Razorcrest
. The
shield threatened to veer away from the ramp, sucking you both out of the hangar and into the
endless void of space.

 

So, you tore yourself away from Din just as he punched the button for the ramp, watching as
it began to ascend slowly, much too slowly, up into the cargo hold. All the while the station
