Coaxium fuel burned bright and ethereal, glowing with colors not its own in a strange, exotic
chemical reaction.

 

Just as the ramp closed you heard the hiss and scream of the oxygen beginning to be drawn
from the cabin, ruffling the hem of your clothes, and forcing the breath from your chest. Yet
then, mercifully, the door pressurized with a hiss, and the void of space was repelled beyond
the  bulkhead of its interior.

 

It was Din urgently brushing past you towards the ladder that reminded you that you all
weren’t safe yet- the threat of the station exploding and damaging the ship still very present.
You raced after Din, following him up towards the cockpit.

 

“Strap in.” Din barked at you, over the sound of Grogu whining insistently at your sudden
arrival. His small arms raised towards you pleadingly, eyes wide and worried. You managed
to scoop him into your arms and plant yourself in the seat behind Din without so much as a
hello, hands shaking and breath catching at the very present danger still posed to you all.

 

Yet to your utter surprise, the sensors of the ship began to beep insistently, and a glance
proved that there were two more ships about to enter the vicinity of the outpost.

 

“Reinforcements?” You squeaked out to Din, who merely shook his head as his fingers flew
over the controls and the Razorcrest began to angle away from the burning station. Your gaze
was drawn to the viewfinder, to where the radar signaled the origin of the incoming ships to
be coming from.

 



Yet it wasn’t a mercenary vessel or an Imperial cruiser that appeared before you, but two
New Republic X-Wings, flying in close formation, that dove in  towards the Razorcrest.

 

“Din?” You questioned nervously as they began to approach, afraid that perhaps Din’s
entanglement with the prisoner vessel had led to a pursuit.

 

"They're not here for us." Din replied quickly, punching in coordinates into the hyperdrive
navigator.

 

Sure enough, the two X-Wings darted past you, diving in towards the adrift station and the
collection of escape pods and debris that remained littered around it.

 

“Hang on.” Din instructed, and soon the ship began to lean backwards as the array of stars
before you distorted, and the blue light of hyperspace soon engulfed the Razorcrest as it
lurched forward beyond the reach of the station, well out of danger with all of you safely
aboard.

 

The hum of the hyperdrive failed to muffle the collective sigh of relief that ran through the
cockpit. Yet what followed was not a rush of questions or movement, but the quiet, profound
silence that it took to process such a narrow escape from disaster.

 

Bruised, battered, and slightly burnt as you were, you were alive. More than that, so was Din,
and the child in your arms as well. Again, despite everything, you had survived, had clawed
your way to safety, back to Din’s side.

 

Slumping in your chair, you smoothed a hand over Grogu’s back, feeling his tiny grip clasp
against your clothes as he buried his face against your stomach with a stifled, worried whine.
You closed your eyes and let a breath escape you, trying to calm your still racing heartbeat
and trembling grasp.

 

You could see Din’s shoulder sag, his form nearly crumpling in on itself with a quiet,
profound respite from the terror, the fury, and the dreaded anticipation he must have felt as he
raced to your rescue.



 

You yourself felt the same, figure still shaking from head to toe at the leftover rush of
adrenaline caused by the unfiltered horror that your escape, that Ran’s death, that the
revelation of your identity had caused.

 

Your eyes shot open.

 

Oh stars…

 

In your escape you had nearly forgotten it all, the lingering feeling of energy flowing through
your hands, of the door that had buckled under your grip, of Ran’s keen, malicious gaze
peering at you from across the hangar.

 

Mandalorians hunt Jedi.

 

You abruptly doubled over, nearly squishing the squirming, concerned child in your arms.
The motion caught Din’s attention, and he spun towards you as nausea began to rise thick and
vile in your throat, pushing down any relief you felt and replacing it now with a newfound
fear. You could hear the fear in his voice as he called for you, but the sound was distant,
warped by the cloud of your own thoughts, violent and sickening.

 

Jedi.

 

The word that you had dreaded so terribly now rose within you, undeniable and singing out
against your own soul.

 

Gods, it was true. It was all true. Everything that she had said, that officer had uttered before
her body had stumbled, fallen as Din’s blaster, aimed well and true, had pierced through her
flesh.

 



And you, you had tried to deny it, had fought so valiantly against the truth only for it to
reveal itself in dazzling, irrefutable veracity.

 

More than that, what Ran said haunted you even now, even after you had shot him, dropped
him where he stood to keep the truth from being wrenched from your grasp.

 

Din couldn’t know. If he did, if he knew, if what Ran said was true, then it would mean that
Din truly would leave you. He would abandon you somewhere and leave, unable to kill you,
an enemy, but unwilling to compromise his creed to keep you by his side.

 

You had sworn to him that you would tell him

 

He couldn’t know.

 

Yet there was no denying it now, no denying what it was you truly were.

 

You could still feel it, the light of something beyond your understanding rising within you,
bubbling upwards and breaking all the barriers you had constructed to force it down, to
contain it for your own survival. It threatened to split you at the seams, like light spilling
outwards and illuminating all that you had tried to hide from.

 

Hands landed on your shoulders, trying to shake you from your stupor. Yet even though you
could see Din’s helmet in your vision, your eyes looked past him, to the scene you had just
escaped.

 

The flames inside the hangar now seemed to merge with the core of your memories, of that
day when your fate had changed so drastically, forever altered by events beyond your control.
The blaze that had ripped through the temple, which had set everything ablaze, the sound of it
muffled only by the screams of your fallen friends and family in a never-ending wail of grief
that rang out within you, carving a place inside your chest, never forgotten despite the years
that had passed.

 



Again, Din’s voice melded with the one in your nightmare- no, your memories- as it
screamed out one final, horrific plea against the stars as you were held aloft for all but a
single moment before descending down, further, further into the all-consuming darkness that
silenced all your thoughts.

 

You slumped forward, head lolling and vision fading even as Din’s voice desperately echoed
your name.

Chapter 45: Part Forty-Five: The Memory
Chapter Summary

"It's...okay." Din offered after a moment, confusion still tinting his voice. "You're okay.
I'm here."

You sniffled, burying your face deeper into his shoulder as if you could hide from your
own thoughts there.

He was right. He was here, for now at least, here until the moment your secret would be
unveiled, and then gone the next. For all you were worth you couldn't help but cling to
him despite the dreaded guilt of doing so, of partaking in the temptation of holding him
while you still could. Here, in his tender embrace, you had found yourself safe from all
that tried to hurt you. Yet now that threat whispered softly in your ear, coaxing hesitant
words of comfort, all while your mind ran wild with the implications.

It seemed that, despite everything, not even here were you safe.

Chapter Notes

TW during flashback for: Situations similar to public shooting, explicit reference to
genocide in canon, child endangerment, and acrophobia

See the end of the chapter for more notes

 

 

Dreams did not plague you as you slept. Not this time.

 

Instead of the flames and screams of your childhood your senses awoke to a stillness, a
silence that felt just as unsettling as your nightmares.

 

The muffled hum of the Razorcrest's engines remained absent as your eyes slowly fluttered
open to take in the space around you. Yet the thing you noticed first besides that was the
sharp, sudden ache that awaited you, body clenching at nothing and releasing with a shiver.



Your hands smarted at the touch of chill on your skin, and you winced, glancing down to see
that your scraped and bloodied hands had been carefully wrapped in gauze, evidence of a
caring touch.

 

Your eyes began to adjust to the room around you, and you realized with dawning certainty
that Din must have set you three down at an inn on a backwater planet somewhere, likely
trying to stay under the radar as much as possible. Where, you weren’t certain, but if the chill
in your bones was any indication you would have guessed some frigid, isolated colony with a
mere scarce smattering of sentient life so as to avoid your pursuers.

 

Above you, a domed ceiling curved up far above your form. From it hung a variety of
tapestries and cloth, all woven together and wavering ever so slightly from a draft you
couldn't see. The whistle of the wind drew your attention off to your side, to where a set of
aging, frosted doors opened onto a small overlook. Beyond it lay a towering, steep mountain
range, the peaks reaching up to scrape against the stratosphere.

 

Across from you, flames flickered in a small fireplace, the smoke wafting and curling
upwards into the chimney. The sight of it made you shiver, as if suddenly reminding you just
how frigid the room was. Blankets had been piled atop you on the small bed where you lay,
heaped on top of you as if someone had been ceaselessly worrying at your bedside. Beneath
them you could feel you had been stripped of your scorched outer layers, leaving only your
shorts and thin undershirt underneath.

 

You frowned, a bit puzzled. You hadn't remembered taking off anything before you fell
unconscious. Granted, you didn't remember even landing on a planet at all, nor being
transported to the strange room you found yourself in.

 

Yet the one who was the answer to all these questions remained conspicuously absent.

 

Din.

 

You curled further into the blankets, too cold and too warm all at once, uncomfortable at the
very reminder of the Mandalorian. Conflict roiled in your stomach, dark and ominous, the
memory of what had happened at the outpost a dark reminder to your current circumstances.
Yet beyond that lay a relief, a sag of comfort at the silence around you, devoid of the horrible
creaking and groaning of the destroyed outpost.



 

Din had saved you, you realized belatedly. He had saved you, again, as he always did. Time
and time again Din came to your aid, as if destiny itself had guided him there, back again to
your side.

 

You could still remember the moment Din's voice rang out across the chaos of the destroyed
hangar, calling out desperately for you above the carnage you had created; of the feeling of
his arms closing around you, catching you as you launched yourself to him, into the safety of
his embrace.

 

Yet the memory of Ran's words, of his eyes, cold and calculating, remained burned into the
inside your thoughts.

 

"Mandalorians hunt Jedi."

 

A shudder ran through you, and for a moment it felt as if the chill was not around you, but
within you, lurking under your skin.

 

A Jedi, you realized. A survivor at that, the truth of your identity lending new credence to the
title Din had bestowed upon you all those moons ago. How you had survived you did not
know, but there was no denying it now, not after everything that had happened. The proof
was irrefutable, lingering in the display of your powers, of the memories turned nightmares,
of the sinister words hissed to you by the slain Imperial officer.

 

An enemy.

 

That reminder of Din's arms fastened around you now seemed to torture you instead,
whispering to you in a cruel temptation in which you could no longer indulge.

 

"Shall we tell him?"

 



You curled further into yourself, burrowing and wrapping the blankets around you as if they
could shield you from both the chill and the haunting reality of your current circumstances.
Again, Din's voice seemed to haunt you even now, echoing an uncertainty that you had no
way of answering.

 

"Why can't you tell me?"

 

It had been spoken so quietly then, in the scarce privacy behind the Razorcrest, with Din's
voice dipping low and almost pleading with you to share your burden with him. You had
promised him then that you would, that soon, very soon, you would reveal the truth that the
Imperial officer had lain against your skin, cursing you and your existence with her dying
words.

 

How could you? How could you tell him now, after all that had happened with his absence?

 

Even now, the lingering feeling of what you had done in the outpost hangar made you
shudder in awe and terror. You could still hear the sound of the door caving in on itself,
creaking and groaning horrifically before at last flying out from under your fingertips. The
light revealed to you then by your own destruction seemed to now illuminate the truth within
you.

 

It was true. You were a Jedi.

 

With that acknowledgment alone came the reminder of your nightmares, of how they had
haunted you all this time, ever since that fateful day in which you screamed out against the
force itself, wishing for nothing more than to forget-

 

And you had. All these years you had forgotten, had lived a life that was a lie. Those
memories still dwelled within you, haunting you, yet you had seen them as something no
more than a ceaselessly repeating nightmare, something you could not possibly have lived
through. Instead, you had pushed it down further, into the deepest recesses of your mind,
trying to be anything but the identity you had nearly been killed for.

 



Yet even within all those years the force had never left you, had remained by your side. It had
kept you safe, allowing you to run faster, to hear better, to react quicker, to sense danger
around every corner. You understood now why you had survived among so many other
orphans who had not, why you alone had managed survival against all odds.

 

Even now you could still feel it, could now sense that strange mystic power reawakening
within you. It pulsed through your veins, echoing that strange cosmic chorus that coordinated
with your own heartbeat. Muscles that had long lay unused now seemed to swell with
strength, roused from a long, dormant slumber. Even the room around you seemed to seem
sharper, seemed to whisper with the traces of those who had been there long before you.

 

Your skin felt abruptly not like your own, as if some stranger had descended to inhabit your
body and take hold. The reality of what you had done, of what you could do sank into your
bones, just as deep as the icy cold chill that lay outside the windows. If you had managed to
destroy a locked vault door, you didn't want to possibly imagine what you could do to another
living being.

 

Unprompted, the memory of your hands colliding with Din's chest plate as you had pushed
him away in panic now rose within you. With it came the sensation of the door in the outpost
flying out from under your hands. Stars, the idea that you might unleash that power upon
Din, or maybe even Grogu made terror slink in your stomach and coil there, sinking you
down further into despair.

 

If that did come to pass, even if you did keep your identity a secret, would Din be so merciful
to you then? With a power you did not know how to control? You did not know the reason
Mandalorians hunted Jedi, but you knew if you ever harmed Grogu, Din would not hesitate to
defend the child he was charged with, even if it meant defending him from you.

 

If you did tell him, would Din see you as a threat even then? Even if he himself didn't hunt
Jedi? Would he leave you behind as you feared, abandoning you, and with you all that the
two of you had gone through together?

 

You sniffled, feeling the weight of a sob clog your throat. You tried to swallow it, but the
motion only brought forth tears to your eyes, too warm against the cold air. Yet it was to no
avail, for they abruptly spilled from the corner of your eyes and fell down your cheeks as you
began to cry.



 

You didn't want to be alone.

 

You had survived so much, had forgotten all you had lost in a desperate bid for survival, and
even that had not guaranteed you happiness. You had been alone even then, in your workshop
on Kaddack, staring up at the stars at night and longing for a peaceful place to call home.

 

Against all the odds you had found it, had found your home inside the confines of the
Razorcrest, where Din's soft voice greeted you and Grogu cooed and wiggled happily within
your embrace. Din had asked you to stay with him, in the twilight midnight of Coruscant, had
let his lips fall to yours with a silent oath.

 

Yet the reality that Din might abandon you for who you were, leaving you for the same
reason the Empire hunted you, was too much to bear.

 

You wept, crying underneath your blankets as if hiding from the world, from Din, from the
Empire, from everything you stood to lose for the simple injustice of your own existence.

 

You didn't want to be alone again. Not after you had lost so much, all those years ago in that
fateful midnight where you had survived, forgotten the unbearable grief of losing all you
knew and loved. The weight of again being on your own, of wanting nothing more than to
find a place to belong threatened to crack you in two, shattering the hope you had dared to
dream in your time with Din.

 

Yet the burden of this secret, of the true reason the Empire had begun to chase you, had never
stopped chasing you all these years, threatened to buckle your shoulders from the horrific
gravity of it all. You knew to keep this secret was to let it fester and rot inside you, growing
into something you could no longer hide until at last the very truth of it would be ripped from
your soul.

 

You couldn't tell him. He could never know. You didn't want to be alone, yet...

 



Footsteps outside echoed down the hallway, heavy footed and sure in their direction. You
startled at the sound, sitting up quickly and feeling your body tense in readiness. When your
visitor approached the doorway, you silently felt a murmur, a whisper of that hidden strength
run through you, always prepared to fight, to flee, to do whatever necessary for your own
survival. You clamped down on it, praying that it would not unleash itself once more,
wouldn’t hurt anyone.

 

Yet, as the door swung open you were met with a familiar helmeted gaze, turning with his
shoulder pressing the door wide enough to let Grogu's bassinet to pass through before letting
it close once more.

 

Din turned, and at your wide, startled expression he froze, muscles tensing as if he had just
spooked an animal in hiding, not moving for fear it would flee.

 

"...It's just me." He offered after a few tense moments of silence, his voice quiet and
reassuring.

 

Yet you didn't respond, couldn't force yourself to relax fully, not with the haunting reminder
of Ran's words ceaselessly repeating in your mind.

 

"Mandalorians hunt Jedi."

 

Din shifted, as if disconcerted by your refusal to let your guarded gaze leave his form. Beside
him Grogu sat up, looked between you and Din with a small whine, his eyes pleading with
you as they always did for you to come and hold him. Something fierce and sharp stabbed
inside your chest, painful and tender all at once.

 

"I...brought you a change of clothes.” Din murmured quietly, almost as if offering a treaty, a
truce to break the silence. “-and some food.”

 

Your eyes darted down to his hands, holding a tray of something warm, the steam curling up
off the plate. As if on cue, you felt a low growl of hunger rumble low in your stomach.

 



Din chuckled, and the sound of his laughter alone sent a pang of guilt through you. You
wanted so desperately to enjoy this moment, safe once more with the man you loved, but the
undeniable weight of your secret, of the knowledge you had of your own identity seemed to
smother that affection into silence.

 

When you didn't respond Din took a tentative step forward, and then another when he
realized you wouldn't flee from him. Ever so gently he approached you to your side, at last
delicately resting the food tray on a nearby table, and beside them a bundle of clothes dug
from within the Razorcrest. Grogu hovered behind him, his ears drooping upon realizing he
was not the sole center of your focus.

 

You swallowed thickly, feeling the remnant of a sob still clog your throat.

 

"Thank you." You offered at last to Din, voice hoarse.

 

Din only nodded, but after a moment he turned and carefully set himself on the bed beside
you at your feet, the mattress shifting under his weight. Yet he didn't speak, at least not at
first. Instead, you saw him fidget with his hands for a moment, head bent in thought.

 

"Are you hurt?" He asked at last, voice tentative, quiet.

 

You curled into yourself, knees coming up towards your chest as you shook your head in a
silent response. Yet it seemed to reassure Din, as you saw his shoulders sag an inch upon
your reply.

 

"...Ran set us up." Din spoke again after a moment of hesitation. Again, you nodded, eyes
cast down to your hands.

 

"What happened after I left?"

 

You blinked, memories cut short by the fear, the hint of fury in Din's voice. It made
something within you shift, and you realized after a heartbeat that the sensation was one of



fear.

 

"Did...did he try to hurt you?" Din asked upon seeing the flicker of fright on your face, voice
nothing but worried, concerned, wanting you to be alright.

 

You shuddered visibly, suddenly recalling the horrid sensation of complete darkness, of
banging your hands on the metal door of the storage closet until they bled, of screaming your
voice hoarse in a desperate plea to be released.

 

Your silence must have been enough for Din, for you heard rather than saw his gloves creak
under his clenched grip, shoulders going taut with anger.

 

"I..."

 

You swallowed, voice still hoarse from crying. Yet Din shifted, turned to look at you, the
gaze behind the helmet gentle, open.

 

"I killed him." You murmured, shoulders hunching at the reminder. "I killed Ran."

 

Din, for what he was worth, did not react, at least not visibly. He didn't move, didn't seem to
breathe at your confession. Yet at last he reached a hand forward, let it rest upon your knee in
a silent gesture of comfort.

 

"You did what you had to."

 

You blinked, lips parting slightly and eyes wide as they stared at Din through his visor. Your
heartbeat seemed to echo too loudly in your ears, a loud and off-beat staccato rhythm that
seemed dyssynchronous with the world around you.

 

You did what you had to.



 

Not just in killing Ran. No, not just that. You did what you had to, when you had nearly died
at the hands of the Imperial Officer defending Grogu, when you had confronted that gang in
the cantina, when you had gone after Din's bounty in his stead, when you had thrown the
grenade at the Black Suns, when you had crash landed that speeder in the Coruscant
underground. Even before that, when you had sliced yourself open in your fight against the
Clawdite hunter, on Hypori when you had shot the pirate in the hold of the ship. Even when
you had stowed away on the Razorcrest, a fugitive with nothing to her name, you had done
what you needed to.

 

Even in forgetting, in absolving yourself of the memories that gave you your identity, you
had done what you needed to in order to survive. All this time you had done whatever it took
for one more day, one more hour, for the smallest glimmer of freedom in the distance.

 

And now, you would do it again.

 

"...Cuyan?"

 

You blinked, and in doing so suddenly felt the rush of warmth falling from your eyes and
streaming down your cheeks unabated. You tenderly raised a hand to your face, shock
flickering across your expression when your fingers came away wet with tears. Turning your
gaze back to Din, you noticed his hands half lifted towards you, posture rigid with surprise
and concern over your sudden tears. Even with the helmet you could imagine the distress, the
affectionate unease behind his visor.

 

And, upon imagining the image of Din's crestfallen face, you began to cry.

 

It was sudden, the choke of a sob bubbling up your throat like a geyser, erupting in a
wrecked, broken sound pouring from your lips. Your vision clouded over with tears, and soon
you were doubled over, shoulders shaking and chest heaving with the force of your cries. Yet
despite the sound you could hear Din again echo his name for you, voice unsure and worried
at your sudden change in behavior.

 

Din's touch, feather light and unsure, landed on your shoulders as he shifted closer.
Unconsciously, you leaned into it, wanting for a moment nothing more than to be held, to be



embraced by the one person you felt safe with in a universe of doubt and confusion.

 

At your movement, Din ushered you closer to him, shifting until your tear ridden cheek met
the coarse fabric of his cowl at his shoulder. One hand came to wrap itself around your waist,
the other hesitating for just a moment before settling itself on your hair.

 

You crumpled into him, sobs consuming you as you wept. Your hands came up to his chest
plate, one rising past it to wind the fabric of his cape in your fist, as if anchoring yourself
there.

 

"It's...okay." Din offered after a moment, confusion still tinting his voice. "You're okay. I'm
here."

 

You sniffled, burying your face deeper into his shoulder as if you could hide from your own
thoughts there.

 

He was right. He was here, for now at least, here until the moment your secret would be
unveiled, and then gone the next. For all you were worth you couldn't help but cling to him
despite the dreaded guilt of doing so, of partaking in the temptation of holding him while you
still could. Here, in his tender embrace, you had found yourself safe from all that tried to hurt
you. Yet now that threat whispered softly in your ear, coaxing hesitant words of comfort, all
while your mind ran wild with the implications.

 

It seemed that, despite everything, not even here were you safe.

 

Your hands tightened into fists, cries stuttering to a soft, uneven series of ragged exhales as
you gently pulled away from the Mandalorian holding you tenderly against his form.

 

"No." You managed, voice thick with tears and hoarse from your cries. "I-I can't."

 

You felt Din go stiff, unmoving against you. Yet it didn’t deter you, not even as you felt
something inside your chest ache hard enough to make you break all over again.



 

"Din." You spoke, voice cracking. "Din please, I-"

 

Din shifted away from you, holding you at arm's length so he could see your face. Yet it
remained downturned towards your lap, even as you trembled in his hold.

 

Something dark and rotten twisted in your gut, at the idea that Din was being so tender, so
gentle with you without knowing who you were, what you were. More than that, you hated
this, hated yourself for the knowledge that you would have to break his heart before
admitting the foul, awful truth of your own existence to him.

 

"Din." You whispered, voice cracking once more, and into that word you poured every ounce
of grief, of heartache, fear, and despair that you felt torture your own soul.

 

"I...want to be alone. Please."

 

For a moment Din didn't move, didn't breathe. Unable to see his helmet, you could only
assume the look of hurt that must have crossed his face, which colored his eyes behind the
darkness of his visor.

 

Then his hands tightened just an inch against you, dug for just a moment into the flesh of
your arms before releasing themselves once again.

 

"Cuyan..." Din murmured, and oh, you could hear the dismay, the ache in his voice, confused
and concerned and hurt all at once, unsure what to say or do to return you to his arms.

 

"Please." You echoed again, ducking your head even further from his gaze and forcing the
plea to tear from your chest. "P-please...just...just go."

 

Din remained frozen for a moment, and in that moment a part of you hoped he would
somehow stay, refuse to leave your side despite your wishes. If he stayed, if he held you once



more, then maybe…just maybe…

 

That same part of you fell, sank to your stomach when at last he pulled away, the feeling of
his hands lingering on your arms as he slid his touch from you. You felt the bed shift as he
stood, heard the quiet creak of the floorboards as he moved away from you. In his absence
you doubled over, as if you could hide yourself entirely from his gaze. Yet there, into the
cover, you felt tears spring to your eyes anew.

 

Din paused one more time, as if to cast a glance at you, before at last speaking softly to the
worried child in his pram.

 

"...C'mon kid. Let's...give her some space."

 

You waited until the door shut before shattering into ten thousand tiny fragments.

 

----

 

Din stood just outside the door, listening to the sound of you fall apart. Head bent to his
chest, he closed his eyes at the sound of your cries echoing out into the corridor.

 

The urge to return to your side, to usher you into his arms and hold you as if trying to anchor
you from your own emotions swelled within him. For a moment it was all he could do to just
force himself to breathe, to remain still, his back flush with the door behind him.

 

You had made it clear you didn't want him there.

 

Doubt, heavy and sour in his stomach, began to make itself known once more. That same
frustration, that same despair he felt upon realizing he had walked into a trap aboard the New
Republic transport, that he had put you in danger upon doing so, again rose within him.

 

He had made you a promise.



 

"I swear...that I'd die before anything happened to you or the kid."

 

He had spoken those words with his head bent to yours, in the quiet, familiar hum of the
Razorcrest, and with each word had summoned every inch of tender hope and affection for
you. Even now he could still remember his name falling from your lips as he braced himself
above you in the darkness, of his lips descending to yours in a gentle, beloved kiss.

 

"Din."

 

Yet that same voice had echoed his name just now not in love, but in a desperate plea, broken
and unsure. With your head bent to hide your tears, you had asked him to leave, to not stay
and comfort you even in your darkest hour.

 

Again, it was all his fault.

 

His fault for leaving you, for not listening, for failing you despite his oath, his creed.

 

Now he was forced to reckon with that failure, forced to listen to the sound of your own
emotions swell so violently against you that it now burst from the seams.

 

The sight of your form shuddering with sobs, of it shaking in his arms had made something in
Din threaten to crack, the ache even now lingering deep and heavy in his bones. With your
voice choked with tears, eyes red and cheeks stained from crying, Din had felt himself pause
in shock, rattled by the image of you falling away at the seams.

 

He could hardly reconcile that image with the partner he had known for what seemed like his
whole life by now. Were you truly the same survivor he had seen launch that grenade at the
Black Suns? The same partner of his that had flipped a pirate over your shoulder and brought
him crashing down through a cantina table? Were you still the same survivor that had
managed to keep yourself alive despite all the misadventures you had been through with him?
Offering him a tender smile even as your doubts began to consume you?



 

Yet your continued cries seemed to be evidence to the contrary, and the thought of that alone
made Din brace himself on the doorway and slide down towards the frigid wooden floor.

 

He didn't know what had rattled you so severely, he could only guess that something had
happened to you aboard the station, something that had caused you to shoot Ran and run. You
said you hadn't been hurt, and Din knew from stripping you of your scorched outer layers that
was true, but even he could not see the damage inside that Ran might have inflicted on you.

 

Yet it wasn't just that, he pondered. No, your strange and divergent behavior had gone back to
that moment on Christophsis, where he had found you cornered and terrified at the hands of
that Imperial officer. Din could still remember the sight of your form hunched over the child,
eyes bright with unshed tears and horrified at the sight of the officer's smoking corpse. You
hadn't even been able to speak past your breathlessness, hunched over and hyperventilating at
a menacing entity Din could not see.

 

He could still feel your hands press against him, shove him away in your panic.

 

Din had been so afraid then, so terrified at the thought he had failed you, that you were
furious at his inability to keep you safe. The thought of you being angry enough to leave him
over his failure had been all consuming, catastrophic against the silence of his thoughts. It
was only once he had chanced upon the sight of your sleeping form curled around the kid that
he had felt that desperation within him dissipate, able to be completely forgotten once you
had spoken to him with such tender assuredness he couldn't dare deny you.

 

“I’m not leaving. Even if you told me to, I don't think I ever could.”

 

Yet that had been before Din had led you into a trap alongside him before you had been left
to fend yourself alone against Ran and his crew. Why Din had left you there on the station by
yourself still failed him. You had all but begged to go with him, pleading to not be separated
again. Yet Din had denied you, even as your shook in his arms with whatever haunted you
even now.

 

He had failed you. Again. Now he was damned for it, cast out by your hurt and anger for his
own transgressions.



 

If Din had known this would be the result of your journeys together, he would have never
agreed to let you come with him all those moons ago. He would have never subjected you to
the fear, the chaos of the life he lived. Yet he had been so greedy, had wanted to see the
dazzling evolution that was you, until at last he wanted little else than to keep you at his side,
to hear you whisper his name again in that quiet, reverent voice of yours.

 

"Din."

 

If only he could go back, to the moment where he had asked you to stay with him and the
child, in that dark Coruscanti night where he had seen your shadowed silhouette with his own
eyes for the first time. If he had asked you then to stay with the Covert, to stay with the other
Mandalorians, then maybe now he wouldn't have to hear the sounds of your sobs echoing
past the door behind him.

 

You had wanted that, long ago, hadn't you? He remembered you telling him you wanted a
peaceful life, safe from the crime and chaos of the Outer Rim and the underworld, on some
serene Core world by yourself. Was it too late to go back to that? To spare you from this life
that tortured you so?

 

Yet that selfish part of him, that same one that looked at you, only at you, with tenderness,
affection, and desire all at once, refused the mere thought of that idea. Perhaps, if he could
just keep you at his side for a little longer, you would be able to conquer whatever demons
haunted you, would forgive him for his mistakes. If he could just see your smiling face, that
same face that had been dappled by sunlight amongst the crystal waves of that hidden
beachside planet, then all would be well once more.

 

He couldn't keep you. He couldn't let you go. Yet in between that fracture inside of him your
cries now eased into quiet, muffled sobs, weeping at something Din couldn't see.

 

If he could just hold you once more, could feel the warmth of your touch against his face...

 

Din sat in silence for a time, listening to the occasional sniffle or quiet sob echo from behind
the door, here in this place he had tried to make safe for you. Eyes closed, Din let himself



imagine those carefree days he had spent with you and the child, of your bright eyes and
smiling faces, safe from everything Din sought to protect you from.

 

When at last there was silence, Din opened his eyes, let himself stare at the raftered ceiling
above him.

 

"Cuyan?" He murmured, voice loud enough only for you to hear beyond the barrier. Yet your
voice was silent, not speaking or even whimpering with sobs.

 

That ache inside Din rose again, fast and sharp, hard enough to make him nearly grimace
through the force of it. Yet his voice remained steady, quiet and reassuring as he spoke once
more.

 

"I'm here, Cuyan. Whenever you need me. Always."

You eventually fell asleep once more, sinking deep into the well of your own despair with
nothing but your cries to fill the silence of Din’s absence. Exhausted, drained, and
completely, utterly spent you slept but did not truly rest, your mind and body falling further
and further just like you had all those years ago, back on that day that had changed
everything…

Everything had happened so fast.



 

It had been a normal evening, the ever-constant thrum of Coruscant easing as the night
darkened and folks went to their homes. The temple had an easy peace to it after dark, the
guardians and Jedi within its walls retiring to their chambers to meditate, padawans still bent
over ancient texts and data pads as they studied in the archives. Despite the war that raged
beyond its walls your home spoke of safety, a comfort which you had known your entire life.

 

Now as the night drew long, the lights of the ornate hallways and winding corridors
dimming, you sat in your communal area with your friends and classmates. Some still
chattered away to each other, some playing games, and those that were shy and relaxed
tucked themselves away in a corner to read or doze. You watch them from your perch on your
bunk, concentrating on trying to float the ball in your hand using the force.

 

You are among the first to notice it, the almost imperceptible shift in the force beyond the
walls of your communal area.

 

The low, protective hum of the temple sharpened, a low warning whisper calling out across
the dimly lit hallways. Snaking through the corridors like wavering shadows, it stretched out
from somewhere you could not see and murmured in a soundless voice of a hidden threat
slowly and inevitably descending down on you all.

 

You had no time to question it- for suddenly your creche master is at the door, her green
lightsaber already ignited and casting her stricken, fearful face with strange, dreadful
shadows. Soon you are all gathered behind her as you run your way through the temple,
through the screams and smoke and cries that seem to sing out inside of you. They cry out
alongside your own voice, choked with tears, at the horror, the futility, the inescapable fate
that had seized you all hopelessly unaware.

 

Your master is a force in herself, carving her way through the soldiers before her, all
decorated in the colors of the 501st legion. Huddled beside your friends you watch as her
weapon sings out in opposition, against the tragedy that befell you all, slicing through her
opponents in a desperate bid to fight off the inevitable.

 

Yet it was only that- a fate that drew darkly against you all, the strings pulled by an
unimaginable dark force that had lurked in the shadows all this time. As you witness it takes
the lives of your family- of the friend who held your hand during your attempted escape, of



the young boy just a year older than you that pushes you to safety, of your master kneeling
over the form of a fallen clone with her lightsaber embedded in his chest and with her last
breath pleading with you to flee.

 

So you do, tiny legs pumping under you and yet feeling for all the world like you are moving
through water, your flight a hopeless endeavor. As fast as you can sprint, the force racing
alongside you in a screech of peril, you bolt away from the classmates you had been raised
alongside, trained and played and learned with. Without a moment's hesitation you flee,
desperately trying to save yourself.

 

You don't know how you make it to one of the grand halls at the back of the temple, weaving
around blaster fire and fallen bodies, their eyes still staring up into the ceaseless heavens. A
shadow, deep and dark and unrelenting, propels you forward, and you know that the moment
you are ensnared by its void would be the moment your heartbeat would echo out one final
time in a choked, helpless plea.

source. A fire somewhere burns brightly, and yet seems to darken the edges of your
awareness all at once, consuming them along the lives of your friends and family, their voices
to never speak again.

 

So, you stand, with the fire at your back, the acrid smell of death clogging your nose and
throat, and the screams of the already dead haunting you for the remainder of your short,
tragic life ahead of you. A mere child, innocent and cut down for a crime that had never
existed.

 

With the flames at your back casting a hazy, orange glow around your form, figures rush past
you to their inevitable doom. There you watch the scene before you, as shapes and obscured
figures of your teachers, friends, family move past you, around you, through you. You stand,
transfixed by their forms running, jolting backwards horribly as they are cut down by blaster

You can’t concentrate, can't move. Your lungs burn with the smoke and ash, hair ruffled by
the blazing heat of the flames as you witness the utter destruction of what lay around you.

behind you. None try to drag your small form forward with them, too focused on trying to
save themselves. One taller individual, a padawan on the brink of knighthood, uses your
shoulder to push himself forward. His lightsaber ignites as he stumbles not to escape, but to
defend those who tried to flee the devastation around you, even as blood spills from his
wounds onto the tiled floor beneath your feet. His hand leaves a bloody stain across your
clothes. You barely even notice, eyes remaining locked on his form vanishing ahead of you,
the flames behind you licking at the hem of your clothes.

 

Heat, the scorch of it threatening to devour you whole. With it came the great roar of an
uncontrolled blaze, a world-ravaging inferno that wished to take you and burn you to ash. All
around you are the screams of those hurt, those shrieking for aid, the whimpers of the dying
coalescing into a bloody shriek that seems to shake the stars themselves.

 

There's nothing you can do.

 

You are powerless against this tragedy, a small form lost in a grand game of destiny, with
those that orchestrated it not knowing you were ever alive at all.

 

The dreams you had dreamt here in this place, of growing proud and strong alongside the
other children, of becoming something greater than what you are now are all in vain. They
too push past you, blurry and hazy shapes like phantoms.

 

Then, as the screams before you begin to die and the blaster fire sings out into silence, you
see him.

 

You think for a moment he's there to save you, clothed in the same robes of the fallen masters
around you, the blue of his lightsaber a sharp contrast to the vibrant red haze of the flames at
your back. Yet then you see the clones beside him, how they don't shoot him down like your
friends and family, how they hover silently behind him. You see how the darkness clings to
him as if he is its master and you know-

 

You run back towards the flames that threaten to devour you, leaping through them in an
effort to escape the bolts pinging off the ancient, decorated columns around you. Somehow
you ascend, climbing stairs up, upwards, as if into the sky and into the stars themselves as if
they can shield you, keep you safe.



 

Yet even there danger finds you, as you watch yet another Jedi hopelessly fend off the same
men who were supposed to be your steadfast allies. He screams at you, with your form
plastered to the wall behind him, petrified. Yet you heed his words, running, running,
knowing that it only buys you more time but does not negate the inevitable, that it was your
fate as well to die this way, your life cut short before it had even truly begun.

 

Why? You had never done anything worthy of this pain, this infinite chaos. Your days had
been peaceful ones, surrounded by your friends and allies. Even the darkest hours with them
had passed like a gentle rolling thunderstorm, with soft sunlight spilling through darkened
rainclouds after. None of it should have earned you the horrific soul defying grief that you
felt as another shot rang out, cutting off a sharp scream of terror.

 

Yet the truth of it all seems to sing a twisted orchestra within your veins, reaching into your
mind and replaying those same sensations over and over again until it echoes in a disastrous
cacophony that you can’t silence. It ingrains itself into you, into your very existence. You
know that no matter where you go, no matter how you tried, that this scene would haunt you
for the rest of your days.

 

At last, the force seemed to abandon you as you find yourself cornered against a window,
hands braced against the glass that stood between you and the abyss of the Coruscant
midnight. Before you is the one you hoped you would one day call master, her robes stained
through with blood even as she stands valiantly to defend you. Yet her form merely jolts as a
shot tears through her shoulder and her voice joins the same ones that would haunt you
forever.

 

They sing against the depths of you, ringing out in ways that you couldn’t hear, beating
against your chest like a stabbing, phantom pain. It sounds like a great cry out against the
flow of life itself, futile and inevitable against the wheels of fate. Each wail is accompanied
with the hail of blaster fire, a bright blue flash that flickered against your irises brimming
with tears.

 

A stray shot pierces the window beside you, and the glass shatters down onto your form,
feeling for all the world like hellfire- like stars raining down from the heavens to punish you
for the simple, defiant act of your own existence.

 



Yet as the window cracks, splintered like the fragments of your soul you feel yourself tilt
backwards. The rush of air cradling you for only half a moment, singing past your ears with a
sigh before gravity begins to take hold. In that moment you see her turn, that Jedi, and see
your shocked, horrified face at the moment you start to fall. Her lips part, your name a
scream that tears from her throat and sings to you as you begin to descend, further and
further, as if falling into the depths of eternity itself.

 

A single shot follows, and you know that she too was lost. Just like the rest of your family, of
your friends, of those you had always known and would know forever. They were forever
torn from you, taken by the unending wheels of fate that spun the thread of destiny.

 

You fall, and as you do you let a single wish echo out into the force itself, a single whimper
against the endless chorus of anguish that surrounds you. Blindly, you reach out for
something, anything to anchor yourself to. In that moment you are suspended in air on all
sides, hair and clothes fluttering as you descend. With the neon lights of the city all around
you, and the air rushing past you as you seem to take flight, you surrender yourself. You feel
your soul cry out against the stars hovering far above you, pleading ceaselessly to forget, to
never remember this tragedy, for one more chance at life.

 

If you could just someday be happy and live without this tragic, inevitable grief, and live in a
place where you could feel love once more, then...then maybe...

 

Maybe someday, this pain may have been worth it.
