Chapter 49: Part Forty Nine: The Gale
Chapter Summary

"Really, survivor?" She whispers, voice soft, almost distant. There's a sorrowfulness, a
scorn there you don't fully understand, as if she can somehow gaze into the things you
are too blind to see. "You're giving up?"

You blink.

Like snowflakes suspended in the layers of cloud above, it feels as if time begins to still,
that you yourself are cradled within it. A child of the stars themselves, you feel them
gaze down at you through the churning storm of your hopelessness, summon you back
to the time where you truly started this journey, all these years ago, when you'd yet to
understand the true path of your destiny.

 

"Stay alive."

Chapter Notes

This may be a jolt for those who are either re-reading or reading for the first time. I have
switched to using present tense in this chapter because I find it better conveys my
writing. Future chapters will be written the same way. Sorry for the sudden change,
hopefully it isn't too confusing. Enjoy!

See the end of the chapter for more notes

The storm was setting in now.

 

The whistling wind had heralds its arrival, a sharp cry from the snow dusted peaks as it
descends into the valley. Ice crystals form within the milky fog of the horizon, an ominous
grey that creeps across the hills with the threat of a freeze so deep it chips away at the outline
of the mountains themselves.

 

It's a death sentence for you to stay out here for much longer, the sinister shift of ice within
the atmosphere hovering, suspended before the storm breaks free, sets them hurtling down



towards the surface fast enough to slice through skin and bone.

 

It's a fate not much different from the one you faced now, you suppose.

 

You watch as flakes sifted downwards from the changing sky, the dove grey clouds fading to
ash, then to darkness as the sun sank deep into the well of the mountains beyond. The distant
rumble of clouds, churning with energy and ice, seem to echo within the groaning tempo of
the wagon under you, the creak of your frozen bones.

 

The fur cover that had been sloppily tossed over you prior, in order to conceal your prone
form, does little to obscure the freezing fangs of cold that gnawed against your limbs.
Sharpened, gleaming from the wind, they bite against your flesh, leaving rivulets of electric
blue ache tracing below your skin.

 

Normally you'd raise your voice, try to echo your disapproval to your captor even if it would
yield no result. Now, however, the sharp pang of frostbite offered a welcome respite from the
desolate shadows of your thoughts, the ones filled with sinking, spiraling despair at your own
fate.

 

He wasn't coming.

 

Nobody was.

 

He didn't know you hadn't left of your own volition. For all you knew Din was certain you
had abandoned him and Grogu, vanished into the velvet pink dawn with barely murmur to
him as he lay sleeping in the bed where he'd begged you to stay.

 

"Ni kar'tayl gar darasuum." Din whispered, and you recognized the words from his
confession on Coruscant, of his tentative voice back then, so hesitant to tell you of his love.
Yet you had echoed your own confession back to him, had felt his lips brush against yours in
an oath- a promise to stay by your side.

"I will know you forever." The words meant, and it only served to render your heart in two,
splintering at the seams. The thought that Din would remember you long after this, after you



saved yourself the heartbreak of his rejection by leaving him-

It was more than you could bear.

"I love you." You whispered back, voice choked full of tears as you curled yourself against
him, trying to remember every ridge of muscle, every silvery scar, every sensation of him that
you would carry forever and ever. "I will always love you."

 

And despite you loving him, despite the immeasurable affection you harbored for this man in
your heart, you had left him, blinded by your own pain and grief, confused and desperate by
the truth he held behind his mask.

 

A Jedi Hunter.

 

Then you, perhaps the last of your kind, a survivor of a bygone era. Something that should
have died long ago and yet somehow managed to survive, to thrive beside him, like a flower
grown from concrete, stretching valiantly up towards the sky.

 

Only to wither when faced with the shadow of the truth.

 

Just like that, you were alone again.

 

You'd cry if you had the strength. Let your tears freeze against your cheeks, mark your
sorrows against the planes of your face. Yet you can’t find the energy, the care within you to
even cry out against the injustice of it all. Instead, the drain, the fatigue of the cracked,
spilling anguish inside of you seems to poison your blood, force your body and mind into
limp, broken surrender.

 

You're exhausted.

 

Tired to the point of pain, tired of running, of lying, of fighting and struggling in a galaxy that
seemed intent on destroying your very existence. Tired of being alone, and yet unable to find
a place to go home to. Now the only person, the only place you'd ever belonged was tainted,
fouled by the secret of your own existence. Before your very eyes it had vanished into the



white haze of the blizzard surrounding you, his caped figure obscured by snow until there
was nothing left at all.

 

You were such a fool.

 

He would have never hurt you, and now he'll never know why you'd left- disappearing like
mist into the dusky pink hues of dawn, leaving only his broken soul to wither in your wake.

 

Now you're here, in the hands of an enemy, bound in body and in destiny, unable to alter the
course of your own fate. Even if you wanted to struggle, you can't, not when the stars have
set this path before you, the only path left to you: Surrender.

 

What will happen to you, you don't know. There was a reason the Empire wanted you alive,
after all. Din had mentioned once that Grogu's bounty had been the same, that he'd been
instructed to deliver him alive. When he'd found the child again, it had been with a scientist,
surrounded by whirring machines and equipment. Would your fate be the same? Treated as
nothing less than a specimen, used and drained until you had nothing left to give?

 

It doesn’t matter. Not anymore. If that was your destiny, then so be it. There was no other
place for you now. Now that you were no longer by Din's side.

 

You just...wish you could have seen him. One last time. To weep, to apologize, to whisper
tender words to him just once more.

 

"Ni kar'tayl gar darasuum." You murmured, echoing the same words he had whispered
against your skin the night before, engraving them forever in your memory.

 

"I'm sorry Din." You think to the heavens above. "I love you."

 

Yet the sky is silent save for the distant, ominous groan of ice that threatens to pierce your
hollow heart. It offers no respite, no sanctuary or absolution from the disaster of your sins.



 

Your captor is silent too. She's offered little conversation aside from your earlier interaction.
You hear her shift and grumble to herself, but the words she offers to you are scant. Even so,
you can sense her displeasure despite not knowing its origin. Most likely it's the worsening
storm, the sharp drop in temperature, or even the length of time it's taken to transport you.
You can hardly blame her. If being handed over to the Empire means being retrieved from the
brutal cold, then perhaps it's a welcome development.

 

Even so, it feels as if she's withholding her voice for a reason, sinking into contemplation you
can't ponder. You can't bring yourself to care beyond a passing curiosity, sinking further into
your form for warmth, for relief from the mournful, apathetic well of your own thoughts.

 

Far beyond the clouded sky, you think you hear the stars sing with sorrow.

 

It's the crackle of a communicator then, that draws you back down like gravity. The sound is
distant but familiar- the garble of wordless voices on the other side, the noise muted by the
snow. It forces you to open your eyes, frozen lashes blinking bright against your gaze.
Instantly, you recognize the sound for what it is.

 

You're here.

 

To echo your conclusion, the wagon under you shudders, at last draws to a grinding halt.
Even as it stills you still can feel the ceaseless shifting of the bed under you, turning and
tumbling your form like roughened ocean waves.

 

"Identify yourself!" A voice calls out somewhere beyond you, muffled by a helmet filter.

 

Stormtroopers.

 

The realization sends an instinctive jolt of panic through your limbs, just once before it settles
again into your bones. Your bred reaction to fight, to flee swells within you, only to be
dampened once more by the realization that even if you wanted to fight you can't. Not with



your hands and legs bound, your body frozen with whatever drug inflicted on you by your
captor.

 

The wagon tilts as your captor raises herself off of it, descends. Her boots crunch the snow,
her own filtered voice raising to be heard above the growing gale.

 

"Bree Cordis!" She calls out, and you can't help but blink at the utter confidence in her voice,
ringing hard and true like the toll of a belltower. There's a pride there you try to discern, a
story that's yet to be unfurled to you. "I have a package to be delivered to Moff Gideon."

 

You freeze.

 

Moff...Gideon?

 

You blink once, twice, trying desperately to understand.

 

Gideon is...dead. You heard the news of it in the months following the fall of the Empire.
Dead through the hands of the New Republic. Executed for war crime. Information spread
quickly through Kaddack, saturated as it was with off-world visitors. That had been years
ago. So how...?

 

Blinking, your mind summoned to you the words spoken by the Imperial officer who had
cornered you and Grogu aboard the Razorcrest.

 

“I've finally done as the Moff has asked. When I return to him with both you and the asset, he
will no doubt rescind his fury and grant me the position I've always deserved."

 

The Moff, you realized.

 

Gideon.



 

"Step away from the hover-cart." One of the troopers called out, his partner muttering
indiscernibly into his comm.

 

"Not before I get my reward." Your captor, Bree, she said her name was, replies testily, the
wind howling over her.

 

"Do as instructed!" The trooper demands, voice rising with irritation.

 

"You do as instructed, plastoid brain." Bree hisses back, words sharp. For the briefest of
moments, you can't help but be a little impressed by her spitfire. "You want your bounty
alive, don't you?"

 

As if to make her point, you could hear the Mando shift, feet inching closer to the bed of the
cart where you lay, a not so subtle threat.

 

"Stop right there!"

 

"Then tell your boss I want my money." She returned bluntly as you tried to incline your head
to see her.

 

The drugs had begun to wear from your system now, you realize after a moment, and the
loose, hazy dullness of the world around you now began to warm back to color. Yet it
remained muted by cold and the grey, ashen colors of growing darkness and storm. When you
try to move, the chill leaves a freezing afterburn in your muscles, a sharp stab of phantom
pain left behind by the poison of the drug stabbed into your veins.

 

"Hurry up." Bree snaps when only silence answers her. "Unless you want to be caught
outside when this storm turns deadly."

 



You can move, you realize dimly. Even though it hurt, even though every inch you shift
summons a scorching burn that traced up to your temples, you can at last wiggle where you
lay.

 

Yet the strength, the determination to do so is bled dry from you now, drained by the weight
of fatigue, of burden from inevitability, of futility. What use in escaping was there when you
had nowhere left to go? Even if you did escape into these mountains, you'd surely die there
from the incoming gale.

 

Dying, alone, on a planet you didn't even know the name of. Without him, without anyone
except the ghosts of a dead order that haunted you even now.

 

The wind howls in the emptiness of your heart.

 

You sink down into it, ignoring the sharp exchange of words over your head and instead
curling into yourself, tucking further and further into your form until the only thing you could
feel was the icy, forlorn chill of regret that dripped your heart. It reaches out with skeletal
hands, cradling you in a hollow embrace where all you could feel was the cold, the bite of the
ice laden wind. Here there was nothing. No pain, no guilt, no fear, just the depths of
emptiness that had waited silently for you all this time, waiting for your ultimate surrender.

 

Curled like a child, you feel the waves of it crest over you, drowning you in numbing, viscid
darkness.

 

Din wasn't coming. You are too tired to fight anymore, not after the betrayal you had just
committed. No after abandoning him, breaking his heart.

 

Let this be it, then. You think silently to yourself, eyes closing, form shuddering. Whatever
comes next, it doesn't matter. There's nothing left.

 

Footsteps, now that the conversation had silenced. The impact of snow crunching under
boots.

 



"Wait."

 

Bree's voice. The sudden cut of it seemed to slice through your thoughts, carving a singular
sliver of light that bleeds through the drowning darkness.

 

"Let me dose her again, just to be safe."

 

The words should send a stab of fear through you. Now, you could only hunch further into
yourself, as if trying to vainly shield your body from the pending imminence of your fate.

 

"Quickly." The stormtrooper snaps, and you can feel the cart dip as Bree climbs aboard,
rummaging for a moment before you feel her hover over your curled form.

 

Yet she hesitates, paused, as if taking in your shivering figure and your scrunched brow, the
tears pricking and freezing at the corner of your eyes.

 

When she doesn’t move, you at last open your eyes, turning and looking through the gusting
snow to where her helmet gazing down onto your face.

 

The owl-like visor of her helmet peers down at you, decorated in rusty oranges and sandy
whites. It's beautifully crafted, you can't help but think, and the pallet reminds you all too
much of Kaddack, the place where this story began.

 

No, you suppose. It began far before even that.

 

Now, Bree pauses, as if hesitating to turn the page in your tale, her hand gripping an injector
but her muscles frozen, gaze keen like a panther watching you, trying to gauge your next
move. You don't know what she expects of you like this, with your heart shattered and spirit
broken, your fate cupped within her hands. Yet she looks at you as if your destiny spills
between her fingers like the sands of time, a mystery she can't help but be mesmerized by.

 



"Really, survivor?" She whispers, voice soft, almost distant. There's a sorrowfulness, a scorn
there you don't fully understand, as if she can somehow gaze into the things you are too blind
to see. "You're giving up?"

 

You blink.

 

Like snowflakes suspended in the layers of cloud above, it feels as if time begins to still, that
you yourself are cradled within it. A child of the stars themselves, you feel them gaze down
at you through the churning storm of your hopelessness, summon you back to the time where
you truly started this journey, all these years ago, when you'd yet to understand the true path
of your destiny.

 

"Stay alive."

 

Where was it you had heard those words before? Spoken so long ago that they carved an echo
into the recesses of your memories, hidden down so deep they whispered into your bones?

 

You can hear them even now, the desperate, final plea of them choked to you by a dying
woman, her clothes stained by blaster fire, her eyes wild as they gazed into a forbidden
future, one that reeked of death and darkness.

 

"Run." She croaks, along with your name, her lightsaber embedded into the chest of a man
you once called a friend. "Survive."

 

You'd turned then, fleeing from her, from the bodies of your classmates, your friends, your
family. You'd fled into an uncertain future, letting her final sacrament embed into the fibers of
you, silently swearing to honor it until you no longer drew breath.

 

Survive.

 

So, you had. Running, fleeing, fighting, never giving in, never giving up, seeking out the day
in which you could at last stop running, could fall into the embrace of somewhere called



home. Falling from the tower on Coruscant, sprinting through the stary sky as it rippled under
you, wishing with every heartbeat there'd come a day where you could at last find a place for
your fragile, broken heart to perch. With every passing day you flung yourself forward, not
knowing yet that a day would come where someone would hold you, speak to you with a
beloved, cherished reverence.

 

Cuyan.

 

"What does it mean?" You asked him, all that time ago, watching the blue light of hyperspace
dance across his visor like enigmatic prophecies. You hadn't known then, how intertwined
your fates had already become, how even now it was his destiny's thread entangled with
yours that drew you back from the brink of surrender.

 

Mando paused for long enough that were sure he wouldn't bother answering. He stared at the
stars out the cockpit window, gazing at the endless abyss of space. The infinite blackness
reflected in his helmet visor. His thoughts were elsewhere, and you had no idea how far they
ventured. He seemed to forget you for a moment, head tilted and gazing at something you
couldn't see.

 

"Survivor." He said at last, voice in a tone you had never heard him speak before. "It means
survivor."

 

The path before you, one you thought was shrouded in darkness, stretches endlessly, lit by
radiant starlight. Cast in the ephemeral light of the heavens, you see him in the path ahead,
surrounded by a glow that cuts through the darkness of doubt lain into your soul, reignites the
flame there called hope.

 

He's there, at the end. Waiting, his voice a salve to your broken, wounded heart.

 

Din turns to you, he says your name.

 

 

 



"Hurry up!" The stormtrooper calls, tearing you from your thoughts with a heavy, unrelenting
phantom grasp.

 

You blink, and all at once the world around you feels sharper, clearer than it was before. The
harsh wind bites against your form and you realize you can feel the strength that's returned to
you, reinvigorated with the power of determination. The intrinsic need and desire to struggle
with everything you have, throw yourself endlessly towards your future with every ounce of
your might.

 

Because he's there, waiting for you.

 

That familiar gravity, the one that you inherited from the stars at the moment of your birth,
descends into you once more, trickling down from the sky and bleeding into your veins. That
power called the force flows through you, rises in you as you coil, draw it forward with a
shout that seems to echo off the mountains themselves.

 

You extend a hand, and blink as Bree is sent flying from you all at once, caught off guard by
your sudden animation. She doesn't even yell out her shock, instead colliding into a heap of
fresh snow as you sit up, fight past the lingering heaviness of the drug to kneel atop the cart.

 

The moments it takes the stormtroopers to realize what has happened are scarce, and it's in
that time that you turn to see them, their black visors a poor mockery of the soldiers they
were originally trained after, the ones that tried to hunt you down on that day. When they see
your head pop up from the cart they startle, turning to you and raising their blasters.

 

"S-stop!" One of them calls out. "Stop right there!"

 

You don't comply, instead rolling off the cart to the opposite side, putting distance between
you and the stormtroopers. Hands still bound, you rack your brain for options, trying to
remind yourself to think quickly, to improvise, to never ever surrender.

 

You need to run, before they can call for reinforcements, get away and into the growing
storm, find shelter before the elements kill you.



 

You need to find Din. To hold him, to apologize, to confess everything you’ve ever kept
hidden from him.

 

A blaster bolt fires over your head as you duck, the red of it streaking bright against the
growing pale of the landscape around you. It's above the howling wind that you can hear the
crunch of snow, the garbled voices over a comm as the stormtroopers begin to right
themselves.

 

"Come out with your hands up!" One yells out to you, his voice nearer than it was before.

 

Closer. You think, crouched, coiled, waiting.

 

You don't know if you can pull this off a second time, with the way your unsteady grasp of
the force clings to you. Still, it's your only option forward, one that you'll bet your chances
on.

 

It's only once you see the barest glimpse of the stormtrooper's outline that you spring
forward, harness your tenuous grasp on the force and push.

 

He stumbles, and it gives you the opportunity you need to barrel forward, tackling him into
the snow with a resounding yell.

 

The stormtrooper is so stunned that he struggles only reflexively when you try to wrench his
blaster from him. With the strength fueled by adrenaline flowing through your veins, it
doesn't take much to disarm him, level the barrel of the blaster right between his eyes-

 

-and fire.

 

He jerks, then goes limp under you.

 



The shot echoes out into the mountains, against the muffle of snow that falls against your
eyelashes.

 

Normally you'd pause, hesitate at this, at the act of taking a life. Now, however, you're too
focused on moving forward, escaping, the motion of survival imbued in your spirit. The flash
of red burns brightly against your thoughts, a stark contrast to the growing pale of the
landscape around you. You barely notice, rising, moving, pivoting on your feet to aim the
blaster at the remaining stormtrooper.

 

Before you can, your ears attune to a sound you recognize- a jetpack igniting.

 

Eyes widening, you turn just in time to feel a weight collide with you, throwing both you and
Bree into the slush as you struggle under her grip.

 

"Not bad, survivor." She breathes heavy from behind her helmet, trying to wrest the blaster
from your still bound grip. "Can't say I'm surprised, though."

 

You don't offer a reply beyond that of a yell, feet scrambling in the snow as she bends over
you, tries to subdue you. Panic begins to rise swiftly in your chest as Bree attempts to restrain
you, hands gripping at your wrists with a durasteel clasp.

 

"Let me GO!!" You scream, face contorted into a furious snarl, bucking under her. You
surrender the blaster only to twist, jab your elbow up into her visor and send her reeling back,
grunting from the impact.

 

That gives you the opportunity you need, and with a roar you push, send her careening off of
you long enough to scramble to your feet.

 

Too late do you notice the pinch under your forearm, raising your arm to notice the injector
hanging from the skin there.

 

Kriff-



 

There's more voices now, you realize, as stormtroopers begin to spill from the secluded hatch
into the mountainside. You see the shapes of them moving within the descending curtain of
snow, yelling orders beyond where the hovercart stands.

 

A new wash of terror rises within you. Outnumbered. Outgunned. Surrounded, and now once
more drugged. Even so, you refuse to surrender. You've come this far. If you stopped now
you'd be forced to say goodbye to Din and Grogu forever, and that is a future you refuse to
succumb to.

 

The wind howls at your back as you skid backwards, away from Bree who now stands with
her cape fluttering in the wind, fists clenched and from taut, stormtroopers at her back.

 

"Run." A ghost of the past echoes to you, the single word a prophecy unfulfilled.

 

You do. You turn, knowing capture bites at your heels with every step, sprinting with your
feet sinking into the growing snow, tripping forward even as Bree calls out behind you.

 

Somehow, her voice sounds like a warning.

 

You realize it for what it is a moment too late, as you put one foot forward into nothing but
air, feel your balance tip off center. In the snow you didn't see it, the sharp slope downwards
off the cliff where the secluded base entrance stands. The chasm yawns large and deep before
you, obscured by a white haze so thick you can't discern just how far down it goes.

 

You stumble, casting a glance over your shoulder to where your pursuers close in around you.
You can see Bree, with her orange armor bright against the snowy backdrop, reach out for
you with a single fist, readying her whipcord to launch forward and secure you.

 

You've been in this moment before, you realize.

 



Atop a tower in a burning building, the smoke of the temple curling around you acrid and
burning in your lungs. You can't see down past the glass wall behind you, horrified gaze
turning forward to where a single Jedi remains standing against the horde of approaching
soldiers before them.

 

You fell then. You fell as the glass shattered behind you and your body tipped backwards into
nothingness, air fluttering past you on all sides, suspended within the grip of fate. In that
moment you had entrusted yourself to the force, closed your eyes with a surrendering prayer.

 

You place a foot back, feel your toes graze the edge of the cliff.

 

Once more. You think in a desperate plea, offering a breath up to the heavens as the gale
howls around you, as snow encapsulates your form and you close your eyes. Once more, let
me live.

 

You take a step backwards.

 

Just like that day you feel air surround you, cradle you in its embrace. Bree's whipcord sings
in the emptiness left by your absence.

 

You fall.

 

You fall, and as you do you let a single wish echo out into the force itself, just like you did all
that time ago at the moment where this story truly began, when you wished to forget, to
refuse the memory of anguish and heartbreak so that someday you could be happy.

 

Once more, you let that wish rise upwards as you descend, air rushing past you as you seem
to take flight, as you surrender yourself. The snow around you flutters through your clothes,
your hair, and you fall through it to another unknown future.

 

Yet somehow you know. You know that this time too, your wish will come true. You know
this even as the wind whistles sharper, as you collide downwards against something that



sends hurt blooming across your gaze until there's nothing left but darkness.

 

You know you'll see him again.

Update 4-28-2023

I have NOT abandoned this fic!! I understand everyone is anxious for an update.
However I am currently in graduate school, juggling health issues, and have found
myself interested in other fixations. That does not mean this fic is dead. I appreciate all
the love, but please be patient with me while I try and get to a place where I can have
more space to think about this project. Thank you!

Update 6-17-2023

If you are wondering why comments are closed, it is because of a rising trend in
negativity within my inbox on this fic. I have been trying hard to summon the
motivation to continue this story, and it seems whenever I pick at my current draft for
the next chapter, I end up receiving entitlement, rudeness, hostility, or some form of
negativity that saps away at my passion for this story. As such, this fic is on hiatus for
the planned foreseeable future, hidden from unregistered users, and comments closed. If
comments open again it will be for registered users only, and comments will be
moderated.

I want to continue this story, but right now the thought of doing so just makes me
stressed and sad. I'm sorry.
